    "29d130138dc4142ea8a89e496fc271a892c6ddc06a7b972027bda98633d4d16a": "---\nname: amthor-workspace-governance-audit\ndescription: \"Audit workspace-wide skill identity and declared project prompt/workflow contracts from complete, pinned source snapshots and versioned registries. Use for workspace skill inventory, cross-project namespace preflight, skill-registration postflight, prompt-ecosystem baseline or targeted audits, repair-batch preflight/postflight, final workflow validation, and prompt-to-skill interoperability checks. Read-only: do not apply changes, publish pages, edit skills, run PF23, or automate PF10.\"\n---\n\n# Workspace Governance Audit\n\nAudit declared governance against observed reality without mutating either. Treat the Workspace Skill Registry as the single workspace skill identity model and a Project Prompt Contract Registry as the expected prompt/workflow model for one declared project.\n\n**WORKSPACE_GOVERNANCE_AUDITOR_REVISION:** 1.11.2\n\n**WORKSPACE_SKILL_REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSION:** 1.0\n\n**PROJECT_PROMPT_REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSION:** 1.0\n\n## Preserve the authority boundary\n\n- Remain read-only in every mode. Do not edit, install, publish, archive, retire, move, approve, or execute anything.\n- Distinguish Product Owner instruction, PF canon, approved registries, observed source state, plans, approvals, and completion evidence.\n- Treat missing or partial decisive evidence as `INDETERMINATE`, not as compliance or defect proof.\n- Never run or satisfy PF23 in this governance-auditor role. For the PO-authorized GCFPE integrated correction, route actual audit/triage/readiness execution to QA-10 in continuing Isis before QA-20. This auditor does not execute it. Actual PF10/PF23 publication remains Product Owner-controlled; informational pending publication is not an extra QA gate.\n- Never write, approve, publish, drain, or canonize PF10. When warranted, emit only a separate `Proposed PF10 Addenda` artifact for Product Owner review. Require substantive, non-proposal PF10 build-notes addenda from exactly the selected release's six qualifying semantic producers—CF-C-30, CF-E-30, IA-30, QA-70, RS-20, and ESC-40; this audit role checks those outputs and does not execute any producer.\n- Treat **PF10 addendum** as singular and **PF10 addenda** as plural. Do not use “PF10 agenda” as a generic term. Preserve “Agenda” only when reproducing the exact title or identity of a historical artifact.\n- Never use Universal Redline Apply on prompts. It remains available only for sufficiently large Markdown plans, specifications, and PF documents.\n- Do not provision or message sessions. Produce a bounded reviewer packet when an independent reader is required.\n- Do not invoke `skill-creator`, Flowmaster propagation, or any manager/writer to fix findings. Recommend the correct pathway only.\n\n## GCFPE current-release audit contract\n\nFor a GCFPE audit, resolve the currently selected release and exact member set from the Notion `GCFPE Membership and Release Register`, then resolve the selected catalog, `GCFPE-MGMT-10`, Flow Index, operating procedure, PE Metaprompt, active family hubs, and installed supporting skills. Never infer currentness from search rank, title suffix, modification time, predecessor evidence, or a candidate page. For the v2 repair successor, require `GCFPE-20260914.1 / 091426.1 / 55` only when the candidate snapshot or live selected register proves that exact identity; the live register remains authoritative for selection.\n\nWhen validating a candidate successor, require one complete impact disposition for every selected member and every affected control. Preserve the selected predecessor until the candidate passes complete readback, producer-consumer, graph, procedure, metaprompt, skill, hub, and archive-lineage checks. After authorized selection, verify each predecessor prompt moved intact to the existing scope-appropriate archive and was not deleted, overwritten, or treated as runnable.\n\nAudit these Alpha-feedback invariants:\n\n- Runtime planning files and off-repository planning artifacts are efficient, machine-readable Markdown in Google Drive directory `Glow / Ephemeral Planning Files`. Producers fetch back the complete artifact and return its actual Drive link. Opaque ChatGPT Library identifiers and conversation reconstruction are not valid durable handoff sources.\n- PFCanon authority is Markdown-only. Prove `Glow` → direct-child `Core Docs` → direct-child `PFCanon` and the selected Markdown item's direct parent. No current audit may open, fetch, inspect, compare, cite as authority, or use a Google Docs, DOC, DOCX, repository, export, archive, or alternate-store PFCanon file; failure to resolve and completely read one unique authoritative Markdown source is `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR` with no fallback and no manual-drain inference.\n- Every nonterminal final response contains exactly one fenced `text` `NEXT_PROMPT_HANDOFF` block that is itself a complete prompt the operator can paste into the receiving session. It begins by directing the receiver to the exact selected destination prompt by name, version, and direct Notion URL; names the receiving role/session and work identifiers; provides direct Drive artifact links; carries status, decisions, constraints, unresolved items, next action, and expected output; and contains no blanks, menus, or alternative destinations. Terminal results identify completion and the native Product Owner return.\n- No operative prompt, example, template, cross-reference, hub, procedure, skill, or validator requires a model/strength assessment, Analyzer, reasoning recommendation, eligibility/suitability/account check, capability appraisal, or configuration-based route or gate. Historical fixtures may be retained only as explicitly non-executable provenance and may not determine current validation.\n- GCFPE PR-30, same-session PR-35, interrupted PR recovery, and eligible RS-40 use `glow-hde-pr-development` as the sole primary workflow skill. `glow-hde-devops` is bounded environment/Railway/vendor/database/deployment/Ops/QA support only; `glow-merged-change-attribution-lock` remains read-only post-merge PR-40 evidence. Verify that PR-35 is one phase continuation inside the existing PR lane and adds no role, approval, authority transfer, Product Owner gate, Proceed, session, work unit, duplicate branch/PR/work vehicle, merge authority, R1 row, or cross-session route.\n- The exact ordered ten-field GCF-17 continuity list is: `WORK_UNIT_ID`; original Product Owner Proceed; dedicated PR-development session; workspace/worktree; branch; pull request; PR instruction; detailed PR plan; primary skill authority; continuous recovery/artifact lineage. Require PR-30 and PR-35 to share exactly one value for every field.\n- An authenticated ChatGPT GitHub connector is sufficient for operations it supports. Absence of a local `gh` binary is not a blocker when that connector can perform the operation.\n- PR-30 searches authorized workspaces, worktrees, branches, pull requests, and Drive artifacts for matching prior work before creating duplicates. It resumes the most advanced verified consistent state and never invents a session-inspection endpoint or unsupported platform limitation. PR-30 owns implementation/local testing/coherent initial publication and ends with `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED` plus one complete same-session PR-35 handoff.\n- One Product Owner `Proceed` authorizes the single PR-30/PR-35 work unit through genuine merge readiness, not merge. PR-35 owns review correction and current-head readiness. Local tests precede meaningful commits/pushes; changes are coherent; a draft may open after a locally tested checkpoint; known substantive findings precede paid CI; no fresh CI is intentionally triggered while they remain; a stale automatic run is cancelled only through a supported authorized interface; `[skip ci]` is forbidden without Nathan's direct specific authorization. `MERGE_PENDING` requires resolved current-head reviews/threads, passing required current-head CI or an exact valid waiver, verified remote-head identity and mergeability. Product Owner retains manual merge.\n- Exactly the selected approval surfaces that themselves record a qualifying approved rescope, escalation/remediation, material approved-Plan or QA-Plan delta, or in-flight Specification delta emit exactly one separate Drive `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM`. The six surfaces are exactly CF-C-30, CF-E-30, IA-30, QA-70, RS-20, and ESC-40. Initial approval, rejection/denial, `REVISION_REQUIRED`, pending, unchanged, editorial, and `IN_SCOPE_REPAIR` emit no empty addendum.\n- Every addendum states `status: READY_FOR_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `canonicality: NON_CANONICAL_PENDING_MANUAL_DRAIN`, and `drain_owner: Nathan / Product Owner`; carries the exact base, approval, overlay, affected requirements/dependencies/tests/Ops/docs/downstream work, exclusions, conflicts, unresolved items, return point, and stable `drain_verification_anchor`; and remains separate from the decision/handoff. The producer does not edit PF10, allocate canon numbering, or claim adoption. The approved base remains immutable. A pre-drain PF10 link is `PRE_DRAIN_BASELINE_EVIDENCE`. Nathan's manual drain is the canonicalization boundary, and the receiver freshly resolves/read current controlled PF10 before reliance.\n- Post-drain audit results are exhaustively `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_REQUIRED`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_MISMATCH`, or `DRAIN_VERIFIED`; source failure makes no assertion about drainage. A PR rescope records exactly `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION`, `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION`, or `PR-35`. After qualifying approval and manual drain, a prepublication branch resumes PR-30 directly with no open PR/RS-40; an open-PR branch uses RS-40 to resume the recorded PR-30 or PR-35 phase in the same session/workspace/worktree/branch/open PR/original Proceed. `REJECT`/`IN_SCOPE_REPAIR` return to the existing repair owner; `REVISION_REQUIRED` uses RS-30; `SPECIFICATION_CHANGE_REQUIRED` returns terminally to Nathan.\n- Selected PR-50 `Abort PR and Escalate` is manual-only for Nathan / Product Owner and must be unreachable from every agent, PR, IA, RS, QA, skill, automation, hub, and prompt route. An unrecoverable PR returns evidence and Product Owner control; it does not invoke PR-50, abort, delete, reset, or merge. PR-50 itself preserves workspace, branch, open PR, and evidence.\n- PR-35's `MERGE_PENDING` is historical pre-merge evidence. Nathan's later invocation asserts only that Nathan manually merged the identified PR; PR-40 independently verifies actual merged state and landed lineage. Never treat `MERGE_PENDING` as a current post-merge fact.\n- Preserve native QA selection, per-task scope/evidence/attempt/result/reviewer identity, substantive planning, engineering, independent review, Ops, evidence, closure, and manual Product Owner boundaries.\n\nThis skill remains read-only. It checks those contracts and runtime evidence but does not execute PR work, publish prompts, drain PF10, contact sessions, resume a paused Alpha, or repair the ecosystem. Route authorized correction to the selected GCFPE management surface and the appropriate authoring or skill-maintenance owner.\n\n## GCFPE role, approval, and flow preservation\n\nIA means Implementation Agent. Isis is Lead Developer. Thoth is Head of Development and owns the native Specification decision and remediation proposal lane. Kronos is QA-only. DevOps owns bounded Ops and QA execution, not PR-development workflow control. Preserve the selected release's exact native ownership, approvals, manual prerequisites, QA membership, recovery routes, and terminal behavior.\n\nIA-10 may author the whole-change Implementation Audit and Plan in one invocation; IA-20 remains a plan-only continuation for a completed valid Audit. QA-50 may author the QA Audit and Plan in one invocation; QA-60 remains a plan-only continuation for a completed valid Audit. Neither author approves its own Plan. Success hands directly to the selected IA-30 or QA-70 prompt with the complete native package. Exact-redline revision routes IA-40 and QA-80 apply to not-yet-approved artifacts; once approved, a Plan, guide, or specification remains the immutable base and qualifying in-flight evolution uses only the standalone PF10 addendum overlay/manual-drain contract.\n\nCL-40 remains the final managed scan and returns terminally to the Product Owner after its native prerequisites. Preserve its existing PF09-gap and CRD-candidate responsibilities separately from the new approval-triggered PF10 addendum rule.\n\n## Select one mode\n\n| Mode | Use | Required additions |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `BASELINE` | Establish complete pre-repair reality | Project profile, prompt registry, complete lane scope |\n| `BATCH_PREFLIGHT` | Test whether a proposed prompt batch is bounded and coherent | Exact targets and direct producer/consumer closure |\n| `BATCH_POSTFLIGHT` | Compare published results with one approved change set | Exact approved change-set identity and before/after snapshots |\n| `TARGETED` | Investigate one prompt, lane, interface, skill, or finding | Exact `TARGETS` |\n| `FINAL_VALIDATION` | Determine readiness for representative live workflows | Complete repaired suite and applicable skills |\n| `SKILL_NAMESPACE_PREFLIGHT` | Detect cross-project identity, trigger, scope, dependency, and write-authority clashes | Proposed skill record plus complete workspace registry |\n| `SKILL_REGISTRATION_POSTFLIGHT` | Reconcile a saved and validated skill | Exact installed source, validation receipt, expected registry record |\n\nRun `BASELINE`, `FINAL_VALIDATION`, and high-risk independent reviews in fresh sessions. Resume only from exact artifact and registry identities.\n\n## Require a complete run manifest\n\nRequire these fields before a decisive audit:\n\n```yaml\nAUDIT_RUN_ID: <stable unique identifier>\nMODE: <one supported mode>\nWORKSPACE_SKILL_REGISTRY_ID: <exact identity and version>\nPROJECT_PROFILE_ID: <exact identity or NONE>\nPROJECT_PROMPT_REGISTRY_ID: <exact identity/version or NONE>\nNOTION_SCOPE:\n  parent_ids: []\n  lane_ids: []\nSKILL_SCOPE:\n  installed_skill_names: []\nTARGETS: []\nAPPROVED_CHANGESET_ID: null\nPF_SOURCES: []\nPO_NOTE: null\nOUTPUT_DESTINATION: <durable destination or NONE>\n```\n\nRequire `TARGETS` for `TARGETED` and `APPROVED_CHANGESET_ID` for `BATCH_POSTFLIGHT`. Require a project registry only for project prompt/workflow modes. Never reconstruct expected state from memory.\n\n## Acquire and pin sources\n\n1. Resolve every exact source identity before interpreting content.\n2. Enumerate the complete declared scope, including duplicate titles and unexpected records.\n3. Fetch or read every source completely. Do not treat a search result, snippet, preview, title, path, or URL as content.\n4. Record source identity, kind, title/path/parent, exposed version or last-edited value, retrieval time, completeness, warnings, and exact retrieved representation.\n5. Place retrieved representations in a local run snapshot. Do not let deterministic scripts access the network.\n6. Run `scripts/build_snapshot_manifest.py` to compute raw SHA-256 and structural digests.\n7. Stop with `SRC-001 SOURCE_INCOMPLETE` when a decisive source cannot be retrieved completely.\n\nHash the exact complete representation returned by the source interface. Do not claim byte identity with Notion's internal storage. Preserve meaningful whitespace inside code, YAML, JSON, exact sentinels, and templates.\n\n## Validate declared state deterministically\n\nRun the applicable checks from the skill directory:\n\n```bash\npython3 scripts/validate_workspace_skill_registry.py Workspace-Skill-Registry.yaml\npython3 scripts/validate_project_prompt_registry.py Project-Prompt-Contract-Registry.yaml\npython3 scripts/detect_skill_collisions.py --registry Workspace-Skill-Registry.yaml --proposal Proposed-Skill.yaml\npython3 scripts/audit_workspace_governance.py \\\n  --run-manifest Run-Manifest.yaml \\\n  --workspace-registry Workspace-Skill-Registry.yaml \\\n  --snapshot Snapshot-Manifest.json \\\n  --project-registry Project-Prompt-Contract-Registry.yaml \\\n  --output-dir audit-output\n```\n\nOmit `--proposal` when checking only the registry and omit `--project-registry` for workspace-skill-only modes. Read [workspace-skill-registry-schema.md](references/workspace-skill-registry-schema.md), [project-prompt-registry-schema.md](references/project-prompt-registry-schema.md), and [rule-catalog.md](references/rule-catalog.md) before resolving validation failures.\n\nTreat deterministic trigger-overlap scores as collision candidates, not semantic proof. Resolve candidate overlaps by reading complete descriptions and recording a deterministic precedence rule or an open finding.\n\n## Perform maker/reader reconciliation\n\nFor every in-scope prompt or skill contract:\n\n1. Read the registry declaration and extract its function, inputs, outputs, owner, reviewer, mutation authority, approval effect, consumers, dependencies, and exclusions.\n2. Set the declaration aside and independently infer the same fields from the complete observed source.\n3. Compare fields explicitly. Preserve both readings when they differ.\n4. Check producer/consumer closure and exact interface names in both directions.\n5. Check role, authority, approval, artifact, evidence, mutation, session, and publication boundaries.\n6. Mark high-risk unresolved differences `INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and create a self-contained reviewer packet. Do not contact the reviewer.\n\nFor Glow HDE, enforce the project-specific invariants in [interoperability-contracts.md](references/interoperability-contracts.md). In particular, `IA` means Implementation Agent, Kronos is QA-only, `ASK OK?` requests approval, `ASK OK.` records approval only where the governing lane assigns that effect, actual PF10 disposition/publication is never automated, and the explicitly PO-authorized integrated QA-10 fresh audit/comparison/triage/readiness runs in continuing Isis before the Guide. Unapproved delegation remains prohibited; this auditor never executes that domain task.\n\n## Reconcile findings\n\nUse the finding model and rule IDs in [rule-catalog.md](references/rule-catalog.md). Do not silently drop an earlier applicable finding. Map it to a supported disposition, a superseding finding, or an exact repair proposal.\n\nUse severity consistently:\n\n- `BLOCKER`: identity, authority, completeness, or approval scope prevents safe continuation.\n- `ERROR`: complete evidence proves a material contract defect or contradiction.\n- `WARNING`: nonblocking drift or maintenance risk.\n- `ADVISORY`: optional improvement without a current contract failure.\n\nReturn exactly one verdict: `PASS`, `PASS WITH WARNINGS`, `FAIL`, or `INDETERMINATE`. `PASS` requires no open blocker, error, or warning.\n\n## Produce the run artifacts\n\nFollow [report-contracts.md](references/report-contracts.md). A full run produces:\n\n1. `WGA-{RUN_ID}-Audit-Report.md`\n2. `WGA-{RUN_ID}-Evidence.json`\n3. `WGA-{RUN_ID}-Proposed-Changeset.yaml`\n4. `WGA-{RUN_ID}-Proposed-PF10-Addenda.md` only when proposed addenda or unresolved PF10 questions exist\n5. `WGA-{RUN_ID}-Reviewer-Packet.md` only when independent review is required\n\nBegin the report with `WORKSPACE PROMPT AND SKILL GOVERNANCE AUDIT REPORT`. State the smallest next permitted action, but do not perform it. A proposed change set has no mutation authority.\n\n## Respect neighboring skills\n\n- Use `flowmaster-validate` for installed Flowmaster structure, embedded-core equality, and Flowmaster maintenance readiness. Use this skill for registry, prompt, Notion, cross-project, and cross-skill agreement.\n- Use `change-flow` to run or audit one actual Glow Change Flow. Use this skill when the question is conformance of its installed contract to the workspace/project registries or selected prompt ecosystem.\n- Use `tw-flowmaster` to run the Technical Writing Flow. Do not run it during governance audit.\n- Use `skill-creator` only under a separate creation/update request after namespace preflight.\n- For GCFPE, route authorized maintenance to its adjacent management prompt and Managing Prompt Engineer. Do not require the uninstalled future `amthor-workspace-governance-maintain` skill. If that separate workspace skill is later adopted, use it only within its actual authorization.\n\nRead [interoperability-contracts.md](references/interoperability-contracts.md) whenever a finding crosses one of these boundaries.\n\n## Verify the skill itself\n\nRun `python3 scripts/run_fixture_suite.py` after modifying this skill's scripts, schemas, or rules. Fixture success proves deterministic behavior only; it does not prove the operational correctness of a live prompt workflow.\n\n## Bounded rescope receiver compatibility\n\nFor the GCFPE v2 repair contract, RS-10/RS-20 accept supported planning, non-PR and merged-but-not-accepted work-unit findings using actual existing evidence. RS-20 remains the same IA bounded implementation-delta decision owner; preserve native product-intent and remediation approval boundaries. RS-30 retains the actual request/proposal type, author and decision owner, including a sourced Product Owner correction without inventing IA denial. An approved open-PR PR-30/PR-35 rescope enters RS-40 only after manual drain and fresh `DRAIN_VERIFIED`; a prepublication PR-30 rescope returns directly to PR-30 with no manufactured open PR. Other approved bounded deltas return to the native stage needed for remaining work then originating reviewer. ESC-40 `REMEDIATION_REVIEW` returns under its drained overlay to the recorded native delivery owner, including PR-30/PR-35; it never masquerades as RS-20 approval or creates duplicate review/addendum/Proceed. PR-30/PR-35/RS-40 with unrecoverable work or missing required source/owner/drain evidence returns terminally to Nathan, emits no continuation handoff, and makes no abort or closure decision.\n",
    "47a13f93a2b83edc6fefcff8f29c8d30fa148a5cd517004f920c90282cb0afae": "interface:\n  display_name: Workspace Governance Audit\n  short_description: Audit prompt and skill governance without writes\n  default_prompt: Use $amthor-workspace-governance-audit to audit this workspace or\n    project governance scope without making changes.\n  icon_small: assets/icon.svg\n  icon_large: assets/icon.svg\npolicy:\n  products:\n  - chatgpt\n  - codex\n  - api\n  - atlas\n  allow_implicit_invocation: true\n",
    "e9301497fa98ef56aaca7ede0857b9a18dc06c34040f0679c609a6bf49b1d38b": "<svg width=\"24\" height=\"24\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\" fill=\"none\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\">\n<path d=\"M3 13.5C3 12.1193 4.11929 11 5.5 11H9V21H5.5C4.11929 21 3 19.8807 3 18.5V13.5Z\" fill=\"#FFD400\"/>\n<path d=\"M15 7H18.5C19.8807 7 21 8.11929 21 9.5V18.5C21 19.8807 19.8807 21 18.5 21H15V7Z\" fill=\"#F75858\"/>\n<path d=\"M9 5.5C9 4.11929 10.1193 3 11.5 3H12.5C13.8807 3 15 4.11929 15 5.5V21H9V5.5Z\" fill=\"#FFA43D\"/>\n</svg>\n",
    "ed724dc4e557b01dbee129deaa75b101bedb96a5810ff5e1ce9bc2e24ead86d0": "# Behavioral fixture contract\n\nRun `python3 scripts/run_fixture_suite.py` after changing scripts, schemas, or rules.\n\n## Structural source fixtures\n\n- Complete snapshot with stable raw and structural digests passes.\n- YAML timestamp metadata is normalized to deterministic JSON text.\n- Incomplete decisive source emits `SRC-001`.\n- Changed content changes its raw digest.\n- Duplicate observed page title remains separately identified by page ID.\n\n## Workspace registry fixtures\n\n- Exact and case-insensitive installed-name collisions emit `COL-001`.\n- Reused UID or canonical key emits `COL-002`.\n- Trigger-overlap candidate without precedence emits `COL-003`.\n- Exact canonical-function duplicate in overlapping scope emits `COL-004`.\n- Overlapping non-read-only governed surface emits `COL-005`.\n- Reused source package emits `COL-006`.\n- Dependency cycle emits `COL-007`.\n- Ambiguous supersession emits `COL-008`.\n- Duplicate active mirror emits `COL-009`.\n- Reserved name colliding with an active record fails validation.\n- Shared skill linked to several projects remains one identity.\n\n## Project registry fixtures\n\n- Duplicate active page ID or prompt key fails.\n- Missing declared lane fails.\n- Active title without its lane-qualified key emits `NAM-001`.\n- Unknown direct prompt consumer emits `TOP-001`.\n- `ASK OK?` and `ASK OK.` remain distinct literals.\n- Source retirement cannot be inferred from a successor link.\n\n## Glow semantic fixtures for independent reading\n\nExercise these in a controller-level maker/reader pass: IA expanded as Implementation Analysis; Kronos assigned Ops; audit execution delegated outside the explicit same-Isis QA-10 authorization; actual PF10 disposition/publication automated; `ASK OK?` treated as approval; `ASK OK.` merely quoted; invented PR approval artifact; unapproved source retirement; proof used as substantive authority; Redline Apply used on a prompt; prompt/skill interface drift; conflicting canon; and missing evidence locality.\n\nThe deterministic suite confirms schema, digest, inventory, and collision behavior. It deliberately does not pretend that token or regex similarity proves semantic intent.\n\nFor the integrated correction, positive cases accept first-time QA-10 without prior READY or QA Plan; fresh audit and historical comparison, complete separate triage and evidence-grounded readiness; READY to Guide; and objective-failure handoff to Thoth. Reject dropped findings, invented ledger checks, historical-only debt or planned runtime verification treated as failures, missing evidence treated as READY, and an informational PF publication gate.\n\nExercise early and later QA/closure remediation: Thoth diagnoses/proposes, bounded discovery returns to Thoth, and Isis makes the single native ESC-40 decision on the exact bounded remedy. Preserve each approved Plan, Guide, and Specification as the immutable base. A qualifying approval creates exactly one separate PF10 addendum; the recorded native delivery owner relies on the overlay only after Nathan's manual drain and fresh verification, then returns to the actual originating reviewer. Initial, not-yet-approved Implementation Plan redlines alone use IA-40 and return to the same IA-30 reviewer; preserve the equivalent preapproval QA-80→QA-70 loop. Reject in-flight base replacement, generic repair approval substituted for a qualifying delta decision, old Isis-author/Thoth-approver roles, duplicate approval rounds, wrong-origin returns, fixed repair caps, retry reset, hidden dispatch and agent merging. A specifically Product Owner-requested Alpha QA-10 rerun is required before Guide; cancellation is not QA failure. Retain historical R1 checks separately; static tests do not prove runtime behavior.\n\n## GCFPE v2 repair interoperability fixtures\n\n- Accept one selected PR-30 → PR-35 continuation only when both phases share exactly one value for every field. The exact ordered ten-field GCF-17 continuity list is: `WORK_UNIT_ID`; original Product Owner Proceed; dedicated PR-development session; workspace/worktree; branch; pull request; PR instruction; detailed PR plan; primary skill authority; continuous recovery/artifact lineage.\n- Reject PR-35 if it creates a role, session, approval, authority transfer, Product Owner gate, second Proceed, work unit, duplicate branch/PR/work vehicle, merge authority, R1 row, or cross-session route.\n- Require PR-30 to recover before creation, test locally, commit coherently, publish deliberately, then emit `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED` with one complete same-session PR-35 handoff. Reject direct PR-30 → PR-40.\n- Require PR-35 to resolve then-known findings and retest before a coherent corrective push; reject waiting on or intentionally triggering fresh CI while substantive findings remain and reject `[skip ci]` without Nathan's direct specific authorization.\n- Accept `MERGE_PENDING` only with resolved current-head reviews/threads, current-head required CI or an exact valid waiver, verified remote-head identity and mergeability. Treat it as historical pre-merge evidence; separately require Nathan's later manual-merge assertion and PR-40's independent merged-state/landed-lineage verification.\n- Require exact rescope return phase `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION`, `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION`, or `PR-35`. Prepublication has no open PR and bypasses RS-40 after verified drain; open-PR phases use RS-40 and preserve the same vehicle and Proceed.\n- Require the exact six PF10 producers `{CF-C-30, CF-E-30, IA-30, QA-70, RS-20, ESC-40}` and the complete addendum/anchor schema. Reject empty addenda for initial approval, rejection/denial, `REVISION_REQUIRED`, pending, unchanged, editorial, or `IN_SCOPE_REPAIR`; reject QA-10, OPS-30, or CL-40 as producers.\n- Exercise all four drain outcomes independently: source-resolution failure with no drain inference, resolved source/absent anchor, related mismatched anchor, and exact verified anchor. Reject a pre-drain PF10 link as current post-drain authority.\n- Reject any prompt-, agent-, skill-, hub-, fixture-, or automation-originated PR-50 inbound edge. Only Nathan's direct identified-PR invocation is lawful.\n- Require Alpha state PR03 accepted-final and PR04 not started; accept a complete saved PR04 PR-10 handoff for Nathan, but reject executing PR-10 or beginning PR04 during repair validation.\n",
    "faa3bcaff47d1db63220ef766fd66fce976789fb5125319f4630f9aeed73da07": "## GCFPE Epic re-engineering effective contract\n\nApply the separately bound `epic-reengineering-correction.json` after the unchanged epic-alpha predecessor and immutable R1 layers. Target GCFPE-20260909.1 / 090926.1 has 53 prompt members, one Analyzer, 50 effective logical rows: 48 preserved predecessor rows plus conditional GCF-R01 / IA-50 and GCF-R02 / IA-60. Historical R1 still has 46 rows. Target metadata never establishes live selection; the owning Notion register does. Automation remains held. No active role session is contacted by maintenance.\n\nThe sole GCFPE-ASSESS-10 wraps every separate substantive invocation, including research, answer seeding, same-author recovery and correction intake; ordinary clarification and internal Audit/Plan phases do not add rows. IA-50 — IA Answer Seeder and IA-60 — Thoth Planning Research are both in Notion AI Prompts / HDE IA. Human answers are returned data. IA retains whole-change architecture ownership, Isis independent review and dedicated PR actors detailed engineering. Thoth's research lane accepts preapproval inquiries; ESC-30's remediation native inputs and returns remain unchanged.\n\nCorrection intake: an actual engineering answer or Canon conflict materially changing an approved Plan without changing objectives/exclusions first goes to existing same-Isis IA-30 with exact approved base/review/Specification and evidenced delta when no real correction instruction exists. Its actual PLAN_REVIEW_ID permits IA-40 and IA-30 return. Never invent a denial, Canon conflict, rescope or review ID. Actual rescope prerequisites apply only to actual scope changes; qualified ESC-40 equivalent Plan review retains every existing exact-Plan/reviewer/coverage predicate and does not require duplicate IA-30 approval.\n\nRecovery contract:\n\n| Paused state | Native continuation after IA-50 and the Analyzer |\n| --- | --- |\n| IA-10 Audit incomplete | Same IA-10; approved SPECIFICATION_ID plus exact incomplete phase checkpoint/envelope |\n| Audit complete, initial Plan incomplete | Same IA-20; SPECIFICATION_ID and complete IMPLEMENTATION_AUDIT_ID plus Plan/checkpoint/envelope |\n| Real IA-40 correction paused | Same IA-40; actual IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_ID and PLAN_REVIEW_ID, remaining corrections, envelope; preserve ordinary IA-30 or remediation ESC-40 return |\n| Approved Plan materially affected, no correction instruction | Existing same-Isis IA-30 correction intake first; real base/review/Specification and evidenced delta |\n\nThe envelope carries exact change, paused prompt/version/phase, author/session/reviewer, base/checkpoint identity/version/state/coverage, stable complete question, examined evidence/alternatives/unresolved fields/affected requirements/sections/ADRs/files, actual answer/finding with source/authority/limits, remaining work, return and real prerequisites. Partial answers affect only answered fields. A valid partial answer permits SEED_READY for bounded same-IA continuation when its native prerequisites are present; an unanswered decisive question still blocks later Plan submission, not that limited continuation. Applied duplicates reuse actual successor lineage. Stale/contradictory answers return the exact conflict to its owner. Scope changes use existing authority. No restart except explicit Product Owner instruction. IA authors complete successor artifacts; seeder/research do not approve or edit the Plan. A missing answer means an exact human question and recoverable pause, never a placeholder runnable handoff.\n\n## First substantive operation — PFCanon header inventory\n\n**Native duty owner: CF-E-10 kickoff worker only.** The following requirements describe that worker’s output and permitted actions. A controller routes and verifies this contract; flowmaster-validate and governance-audit only inspect it. They do not author, revise, approve, decide, publish or execute the worker’s task.\nAfter Analyzer entry and before any kickoff source interpretation (including the Epic Strategy Card), verify Glow / Core Docs / PFCanon ancestry and inventory its complete direct-child header-pair scope. No inaccessible-directory broad-search fallback is allowed. Pair by stable PF identity and verified directory membership, retaining exact file IDs, MIME types and current-representation selection evidence in runtime provenance. Inventory Markdown, DOCX and native Google Docs as their actual stored forms; do not report a DOCX comparison when only a Google Doc exists. Exports retain native source identity and representation lineage.\nCompare title/document identity, version, status and corresponding date/update-gate fields when present across the controlled Markdown and each actual document counterpart. Retain raw compared values. Normalize harmless whitespace only, preserving case, punctuation, numbers and meaning. Record MATCH, MISMATCH, INCOMPLETE, UNPAIRED, UNREADABLE or AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE; duplicate competing candidates never silently select the highest version. Header parity proves only header parity. Missing required identity/version/status fields are INCOMPLETE; a missing counterpart is UNPAIRED, not MATCH.\nFor each discrepancy record affected source use and correction/routing/explicit acceptance owner. Scoped acceptance names the exact allowed representation/version, scope and reason; retain the original unequal status and raw values. Block dependent source use where required, not unrelated kickoff work or whole-library repair. This comparison does not replace the existing controlled Markdown authority predicate or extend a live-Drive gate to authorized QA/OPS execution copies. Include the full inventory/provenance and dependency dispositions in the kickoff evidence and carry the material result in the sole kickoff handoff.\nThe installed Change Flow header helper may extract synthetic/local Markdown and DOCX and compare a faithfully exported native document header record using standard-library tools; it does not discover authority, establish ancestry, choose a canonical body or repair sources. If a real header cannot be extracted faithfully, report the limitation and inspect the actual representation with available tools.\n\n## Whole-change architecture and readiness\n\n**Native duty owner: IA-10, IA-20 and IA-40 authors only.** The following requirements describe that worker’s output and permitted actions. A controller routes and verifies this contract; flowmaster-validate and governance-audit only inspect it. They do not author, revise, approve, decide, publish or execute the worker’s task.\nOwn a viable whole-change implementation architecture before requesting Plan approval: component ownership, interfaces and exact important data shapes, invariants, cross-component dependencies, sequencing, failure/recovery behavior, acceptance allocation and decisive source feasibility. Use useful examples and diagrams where they make design reviewable. Dedicated PR authors retain detailed per-file planning; architecture, source-defined domain meaning and feasible evidence collection cannot be deferred as PR detail.\nTrace each requirement to the actual source clause, design decision, owned work unit, acceptance meaning and evidence deadline. An approved Plan governs its bounded change and approved decisions; it does not silently override unrelated Canon. Correct clear author transcription errors; classify genuine conflicts under the carried ADR contract. Resolve architecture/feasibility-determining questions before claiming submission readiness. Carry routine execution checks only to their legitimate stage, with exact owner/deadline; never weaken an upstream deadline. A complete Audit may contain explicit blocked dispositions, but that does not make an unresolved architecture ready for Plan approval. Save a truthful checkpoint and exact question when decisive evidence is absent.\n\nRecord decisive questions in the existing Audit/Plan, not a parallel approval system. Each entry carries stable question identity, complete question text, exact requirement and row/field, inspected source passages and provenance, known facts, remaining unknown subset, competing interpretations, proposed decision or exact unresolved exception, affected sections/ADRs/files, actual owner and required stage deadline. Extract conclusive facts even when other fields remain unresolved. No generic all-evidence-pending debt or assumed small unresolved subset is acceptable.\nFor mechanics development questions inspect current controlled PF08 and PF11 first. If inconclusive, verify Glow's direct HD Refs directory, read its Human Design Reference Index and retrieve the actual admitted source passages needed by the claim. The index alone is not doctrinal evidence. Use an available original PDF without requiring Markdown conversion. If bounded external inquiry is necessary, use only jovianarchive.com. An inaccessible original proves an access limitation, not absence of doctrine. If still unresolved, give the Product Owner the exact question, alternatives, inspected evidence, affected fields and practical consequences.\nFor engineering, inspect relevant current Canon and actual repository interfaces/files first; then use bounded primary technical sources. An advanced unresolved inquiry goes through the single Analyzer to IA-60 — Thoth Planning Research in AI Prompts / HDE IA. Prepare exact files/interfaces, constraints, alternatives, failure modes, decision criteria and requested finding. No approved Plan is required for this preapproval route. Preserve ESC-30's separate remediation intake and authority.\n\n## Independent substantive review and ADR decisions\n\n**Native duty owner: Existing native Thoth/Isis reviewers only; standalone approved-Plan addenda belong only to IA-30 or qualified ESC-40.** The following requirements describe that worker’s output and permitted actions. A controller routes and verifies this contract; flowmaster-validate and governance-audit only inspect it. They do not author, revise, approve, decide, publish or execute the worker’s task.\nIndependently compare the author's stated intent with the behavior a competent reader would infer from the actual complete artifact. Inspect canonical truth, Human Design fidelity where relevant, engineering quality, feasibility, coherence, source sufficiency and final handoff completeness. Apply PF13 and PF21 to outcome, coherent surface, boundaries, stewardship and applicable phase intent without symbolic stages or mandatory scores. A polished checklist or generic approval is insufficient when a decisive source or architecture claim is unsupported.\nReview each stable ADR against exact affected clauses, competing alternatives, rationale and implementation effects. Require NEW_CANON or CANON_RECONCILIATION, or a different class only with an already approved definition. Give every ADR an explicit APPROVED, APPROVED_AS_CHANGED with exact changed text, or REJECTED with reason disposition. Inclusion in a Plan is not approval. Preserve rejected proposals and original/changed text. Material new design returns to its author for a complete reviewable successor before approval.\nFor approved Plan decisions, preserve the existing standalone PF10 build-note addendum contract alongside exact approved Plan and proof: include every approved ADR's ID/class, exact decision, scope, lineage, drainage owner/target and authority boundaries. A coherent mixed approval batch may contain approved and approved-as-changed items only; retain rejected items in review evidence. All rejected means no empty addendum. Reuse a valid exact batch without duplication. Apply the same appropriate existing reviewer/addendum boundary to late findings; no new approver is introduced. Keep proposal, review decision, source-resolution, addendum preparation, Product Owner publication and permanent drainage states separate. Informational publication pending alone is not an extra gate; a decisive governing conflict remains evaluated on its actual resolution and scope. Never mutate PF10 or choose final numbering.\n\n## Semantic readiness before INSTRUCTION_READY\n\n**Native duty owner: PR-10 instruction author only.** The following requirements describe that worker’s output and permitted actions. A controller routes and verifies this contract; flowmaster-validate and governance-audit only inspect it. They do not author, revise, approve, decide, publish or execute the worker’s task.\nCompare the complete instruction, clause by clause, against the exact approved Specification, Implementation Plan and review, applicable classified/decided Canon ADRs, decisive current Canon/repository evidence and the full selected PR-20 contract. Keep a compact comparison record of source clause, intended meaning, instruction meaning, owned unit, acceptance and required evidence stage. Check numeric domains and zero/sentinel meaning, boolean exclusion where the integer domain excludes booleans, exact nested/closed object schemas, field ownership, separate PR ownership, acceptance-criterion meaning, dependency order and evidence deadlines. Do not copy historical example constants into this reusable contract.\nThe instruction must carry enough meaning and decisive source feasibility to plan the approved unit without reconstructing upstream intent. Preserve every obligation outside PR-20's Inputs heading: complete detailed engineering planning, implementation, security/code review, corrected-code coverage, findings and re-review, CI with scoped waiver conditions, manual-merge dependency handling and completion evidence. PR-20 may return its native AWAITING_PO_PROCEED only for a complete executable scoped plan; do not substitute an upstream PLAN_PENDING state or imply Proceed. The sole downstream native input remains PR_INSTRUCTION_ID and transport preserves its exact identity and complete source package.\nDo not mark INSTRUCTION_READY while a decisive comparison fails. Correct author transcription/instruction errors here without a fake Canon ADR. Return a genuine architecture/design/Canon conflict to the actual IA/reviewer or existing remediation/rescope owner with exact evidence and native inputs through the Analyzer. Missing source feasibility is an exact owned question before its source-required deadline, not an automatic postponement until mutation. The Analyzer only assesses the unchanged package and cannot repair this instruction or approval.\n\n## Actual final-response contract\n\n**Native duty owner: Each invoked native producer; Analyzer has its own worker-recommendation output.** The following requirements describe that worker’s output and permitted actions. A controller routes and verifies this contract; flowmaster-validate and governance-audit only inspect it. They do not author, revise, approve, decide, publish or execute the worker’s task.\nBefore sending the final response, inspect the actual final text against the actual result branch. State the result and usable artifact identities first, then the exact immediate next prompt name/directory, actor and retained or initial session, surface/model/reasoning and task-specific rationale, followed by the complete populated invocation. Advice here is for the Analyzer run; its own MODEL_HANDOFF advises the worker. A saved attachment containing the block does not satisfy final delivery. Unknown picker observations do not prevent concrete advice based on current applicable official support; disclose unobserved configuration separately. Do not guess inaccessible capabilities. A blocked branch gives the exact missing question/input/owner and recoverable saved state, without a fake runnable block. A real terminal branch returns to its native owner without an invented Analyzer. A human answer not yet received is a prerequisite, never a placeholder runnable seeder package. This check covers success, denial, revision, remediation, rescope, partial/manual-action, recovery and terminal results, including CRD paths. It is an output check within this invocation, not another stage.\nProducer and Analyzer schema include actual release and resolved source/destination runtime versions (truthful no predecessor version for OPERATOR_DIRECT_RECOVERY), native inputs, exact actor/session, artifact/approval/source lineage, real gates, full QA membership and per-task attempts/results/reviewers when applicable, capabilities, risks, package status and immediate-next recommendation. Predecessor recommends the Analyzer, Analyzer reads the entire worker contract/decisive sources and returns MODEL_HANDOFF plus unchanged worker invocation. Unknown picker does not prevent supported concrete advice. Official guidance remains dynamically appraised; no fixed worker table or measured-cost claim is added.\n\n## Verification and preservation\n\nValidate complete affected bodies and all-member dispositions, graph closure, exact native phase inputs, actual final outputs, both ADR classes and approve/change/reject batches, late addenda, source feasibility and historical semantic counterexamples. Static string presence is insufficient. Preserve actual QA membership/attempt rules, manual merge and Proceed, CRD compatibility, PF20/PF30 section-only outputs, PF09 substantive build-note addenda, bounded direct CRD candidate records and CL-40 terminal ownership. Header parity is Epic-only and not a new QA/OPS execution-copy gate. Permanent source drainage and pending informational PF10 publication are distinct from unresolved governing decisions.\n\nUse complete pinned snapshots and meaningful positive/negative fixtures; distinguish deterministic, isolated prompt-output and live evidence. Do not relabel historical counts or unresolved stalls as observed success. Require independent meaning/feasibility/role-boundary review before selecting published, fully read-back compatible candidates. Preserve old selected lineage until compatibility, archive original pages intact and verify guide pointers, installed persisted skills and selected identities. No Technical Writing or protected Primary-core change is authorized.\n",
    "138f6b90b5c915bdf54438c43dc615cedbaaf8a3b62840e809cf6bc11b9740c2": "# Interoperability contracts\n\nRead this reference whenever a finding crosses a skill, role, or workflow boundary.\n\n## Skill precedence\n\n- `flowmaster-validate` owns Flowmaster package structure, embedded Primary-core equality, self-containment, revision drift, and maintenance readiness.\n- `amthor-workspace-governance-audit` owns workspace registry, project prompt registry, selected Notion prompt ecosystem, cross-project collision, and prompt-to-skill agreement checks.\n- `change-flow` runs or audits an actual Epic/CRD Change Flow. Governance Audit checks the installed Change Flow contract against declared workspace/project interfaces but does not execute it.\n- `tw-flowmaster` runs the Technical Writing Flow and Redline Apply pathway. Governance Audit does not run it.\n- `flowmaster-propagate` copies an approved Primary core. Governance Audit may recommend propagation but never performs it.\n- `skill-creator` owns installed skill creation and source edits. Governance Audit supplies preflight/postflight evidence only.\n- `glow-hde-pr-development` solely owns GCFPE PR-30 implementation/publication, same-session PR-35 review/readiness, interrupted PR recovery, and eligible RS-40 continuation.\n- `glow-hde-devops` supports bounded environment and Ops capabilities. It is not the primary GCFPE PR-development workflow skill.\n- GCFPE maintenance belongs to its selected management prompt and Managing Prompt Engineer within current Product Owner authorization.\n- Session Branch and Session Relay may provision or contact independent sessions only in separately authorized work. Governance Audit prepares packets but does not send them.\n\nA specialized skill may streamline an existing native lane but must not add a stage, gate, approval, duplicate authority, or extra handoff. The sole GCFPE exception is one selected PR-30 → PR-35 same-session phase continuation inside existing R1 row GCF-17; it adds no role, approval, authority transfer, Product Owner gate, Proceed, session, work unit, duplicate branch/PR/work vehicle, merge authority, R1 row, or cross-session route.\n\n## Glow role contract\n\n- IA means Implementation Agent, never Implementation Analysis.\n- One IA session serves one Epic or CRD across its implementation lifecycle.\n- Isis is Lead Developer.\n- Thoth is Head of Development, owns the exact Isis-authored Specification decision, and authors remediation proposals through ESC-30.\n- Isis reviews the IA-authored Implementation Plan, Kronos-authored QA Plan, and concrete Thoth remediation through ESC-40. IA-40 and QA-80 may prepare exact-redline successors only while the respective artifact remains unapproved. Once a Plan, guide, or specification is approved, it remains the immutable base; no in-flight review or remediation reauthors it, and a qualifying approved delta follows the standalone PF10 overlay/manual-drain contract.\n- Kronos is QA-only: create QA tasks, analyze committed QA evidence, and issue QA acceptance review.\n- IA creates Ops tasks from the approved Implementation Plan and reviews the result. No separate pre-execution approval is invented for an IA-created Ops task.\n- DevOps executes bounded Ops and QA instructions. Ops may include database, provider, Railway, DNS, hostname, terminal, or other non-development work.\n- PR-30/PR-35 development uses `glow-hde-pr-development`; it may call DevOps support only for a specifically needed bounded environment, Railway, vendor, database, deployment, Ops, or QA capability. `glow-merged-change-attribution-lock` is read-only post-merge PR-40 evidence only.\n- Repository-producing Ops receipts point to committed evidence. Non-repository Ops receipts contain their native build-notes material for later appropriate manual drainage.\n\n## Approval, canon, and PF10 contract\n\n- `ASK OK?` means approval is requested and pending.\n- `ASK OK.` records approval only when the governing lane assigns that effect.\n- PR Proceed supplies the defined approval/execution transition; do not invent a separate approval artifact.\n- PF10 is never automated by these skills. The governance auditor never edits, numbers, publishes, drains, or canonizes PF10.\n- When a selected prompt itself records a qualifying approval, it emits exactly one standalone `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM` in Google Drive `Glow / Ephemeral Planning Files`. The six semantic producers are exactly CF-C-30, CF-E-30, IA-30, QA-70, RS-20, and ESC-40.\n- Each addendum contains exact change/work IDs, producing prompt identity, decision evidence, immutable base identity/lineage/link, prior addenda links, approved delta, affected requirements/dependencies/tests/Ops/docs/downstream work, conflicts, exclusions, unresolved items, return point, and stable `drain_verification_anchor`, plus `status: READY_FOR_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `canonicality: NON_CANONICAL_PENDING_MANUAL_DRAIN`, and `drain_owner: Nathan / Product Owner`.\n- Initial approval, rejection/denial, `REVISION_REQUIRED`, pending, unchanged, editorial, and `IN_SCOPE_REPAIR` produce no empty addendum.\n- Nathan's manual drain is the canonicalization boundary. Addendum production does not edit PF10, allocate canon numbering, or claim adoption. The approved base remains immutable. A pre-drain PF10 link is `PRE_DRAIN_BASELINE_EVIDENCE`. The receiving prompt freshly resolves and completely reads current controlled PF10; its exhaustive result is `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_REQUIRED`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_MISMATCH`, or `DRAIN_VERIFIED`. Source failure makes no drain inference. Only `DRAIN_VERIFIED` permits reliance and exact native continuation.\n- Universal Redline Apply is for sufficiently large Markdown plans, specifications, and PF documents, not prompts.\n- Publishing a successor never retires its source without exact source-disposition authority. An authorized GCFPE disposition moves the original prompt intact to the existing appropriate archive; no deletion, trash, overwrite, or copy-and-delete substitute.\n\n## Artifact and handoff contract\n\n- Reusable GCFPE prompt bodies remain in Notion.\n- Runtime planning files and off-repository planning artifacts are efficient, machine-readable Markdown in Google Drive `Glow / Ephemeral Planning Files`.\n- PFCanon authority is Markdown-only. Prove `Glow` → direct-child `Core Docs` → direct-child `PFCanon`, list direct children, and verify the selected Markdown item's direct parent. Never open, fetch, inspect, compare, cite as authority, or use Google Docs, DOC, DOCX, repository, export, archive, or alternate-store PFCanon files. Failure to resolve and completely read one unique Markdown authority is `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`; there is no fallback or drain inference.\n- Producers upload and fetch back the complete artifact, return its actual Drive link, and use that link in dependent handoffs.\n- Opaque ChatGPT Library identifiers and conversation reconstruction are not durable workflow sources.\n- Every nonterminal continuation returns exactly one fenced `text` `NEXT_PROMPT_HANDOFF` that is the complete pasteable prompt for the receiving session, not metadata or a blank form.\n- The handoff begins with the exact selected destination prompt name, version, and direct Notion URL and carries the actual receiving role/session, work identifiers, direct Drive artifact links, state, decisions, constraints, unresolved items, next action, and expected output.\n- Terminal results return to the native Product Owner boundary without fabricating a destination.\n- No operative prompt, handoff, procedure, skill, hub, validator, or fixture includes or requires a model/strength assessment, Analyzer execution or routing, reasoning recommendation, eligibility/suitability/account check, capability appraisal, or configuration-based route or gate.\n\n## QA selection and combined authoring\n\nSelection belongs to the Product Owner. Accept explicit QA step IDs/names, an unambiguous natural-language selection, a complete selection source, or ALL for every step in the exact approved QA Plan. Preserve an already supplied selection. If absent or ambiguous, show available IDs and short names and ask which tasks to run; never assume ALL or choose a ready subset. Author every selected valid task, including dependency-waiting members. Dependency readiness controls execution order, never assignment membership. Preserve blocked/defective entries explicitly. Reuse already-authored instructions as dependencies become ready; QA-110 returns them to QA-100, using QA-90 only for genuinely unissued selected instructions or the exact permitted retry. Never execute an unselected prerequisite or reset attempts.\n\nIA-10 performs the whole-change Implementation Audit and then Implementation Plan in one ordinary invocation in the dedicated IA session. QA-50 performs the independent Kronos QA Audit and QA Plan phases in one ordinary invocation. Preserve distinct complete Audit and Plan identities, mandatory audit-before-plan order, all source-native content, and existing concise supporting proofs. Neither author approves its own Plan. Success hands directly to the selected IA-30 or QA-70 prompt with the complete native package. A preapproval denial uses IA-40/QA-80; an approved-base-overlay denial returns to the exact overlay-proposal owner and never rewrites the base.\n\nIA-20 and QA-60 remain selected same-author plan-only continuations for a completed valid Audit, including interrupted and legacy work. They are not mandatory extra invocations. On interruption preserve finished phases and resume the first incomplete phase; a substantive source/scope blocker names the actual owner without fabricating approval.\n\n## PR-development contract\n\nBefore creating a workspace, worktree, branch, commit, pull request, or duplicate planning artifact, PR-30 inspects authorized roots, repository/PR state, and linked Drive artifacts, then resumes the most advanced verified consistent state. PR-30 owns implementation, local testing, coherent commit creation and initial publication. Its success is `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED` plus exactly one complete same-session PR-35 handoff. PR-35 owns review retrieval/correction, retesting, coherent corrective publication, CI economy, current-head proof and genuine merge readiness. The exact ordered ten-field GCF-17 continuity list is: `WORK_UNIT_ID`; original Product Owner Proceed; dedicated PR-development session; workspace/worktree; branch; pull request; PR instruction; detailed PR plan; primary skill authority; continuous recovery/artifact lineage. Both phases share exactly one value for every field.\n\nLocal tests precede meaningful commits and pushes. A draft PR may open after one coherent locally tested checkpoint. Avoid micro-commits and a no-publication stop. Known substantive review findings precede paid CI. Do not wait on or intentionally trigger fresh CI while findings remain; cancel a stale automatic run only through a supported authorized interface. Resolve then-known findings and retest before the next coherent push. Never use `[skip ci]` without Nathan's direct specific authorization. `MERGE_PENDING` requires resolved current-head reviews/threads, passing required current-head CI or an exact waiver, verified remote-head identity and mergeability.\n\nA PR-30/PR-35 rescope carries exactly `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION`, `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION`, or `PR-35` plus all actual vehicle/evidence lineage to same-IA RS-20. `REJECT`/`IN_SCOPE_REPAIR` return to the correct existing owner; `REVISION_REQUIRED` uses RS-30; `SPECIFICATION_CHANGE_REQUIRED` is terminal to Nathan. After qualifying approval/manual drain/fresh `DRAIN_VERIFIED`, prepublication resumes PR-30 directly with no open PR/RS-40, while open-PR phases use RS-40 and preserve the same vehicle/original Proceed.\n\nPR-35's `MERGE_PENDING` is historical pre-merge evidence. Nathan's later invocation asserts only a manual merge; PR-40 independently verifies actual merged state and landed lineage. No agent may present `MERGE_PENDING` as current post-merge fact.\n\nSelected PR-50 `Abort PR and Escalate` is manually invocable only by Nathan / Product Owner. It is unreachable from every agent, PR, IA, RS, QA, skill, automation, hub, and prompt route. An unrecoverable PR returns evidence and Product Owner control without invoking PR-50, aborting, deleting, resetting, or merging; PR-50 itself preserves the workspace, branch, open PR, and evidence.\n\n## Session contract\n\n- Use `DEDICATED_ONE_OFF` for one PR, audit, independent approval, or publication batch.\n- Use `CHANGE_LIFETIME` for one IA Epic or CRD.\n- Use `ROLE_CONTINUING` for Isis, Thoth, Kronos, and Prompt Engineering while their source set remains coherent.\n- Use `ORCHESTRATOR_RUN` for one Flowmaster or governance run.\n- Rotate on observed context drift, not a guessed token threshold, and preserve continuity through exact Drive artifacts and one complete handoff.\n\n## Final managed discovery contract\n\nCL-40 is the final managed prompt for both Epic and CRD cycles after positive closure, CL-20, and all actually selected managed maintenance/review work. Pending manual PF publication, memo delivery, and board administration are not scan prerequisites; preserve their actual state and include complete unpublished content. The original change remains closed.\n\nMissing recorded work produces complete PF09/task/subtask gap evidence in the substantive `CYCLE_GAP_SCAN`; it does not produce a `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM`, and CL-40 is not an addendum producer. Any later PF10/PF09 decision belongs to its native reviewer/manual owner. CL-40 returns terminally to the Product Owner without selecting or launching a new change.\n\n## Current-release validation\n\nResolve actual GCFPE selection from the register. Do not use legacy member counts, middleware fixtures, or historical correction layers as current authority. Historical files remain non-executable provenance only.\n\nFor v2 repair candidate/selected successor `GCFPE-20260914.1` at prompt version `091426.1`, validate exactly 55 prompt members (54 retained logical IDs plus sole PR-35); direct native transitions and exact terminal routes; Drive Markdown storage and Markdown-only PFCanon contracts; complete paste-ready handoffs; PR-30/PR-35 same-session skill/recovery/action-economy/review/CI/current-head behavior; exactly six PF10 producers `{CF-C-30, CF-E-30, IA-30, QA-70, RS-20, ESC-40}`; the immutable base/overlay/manual-drain/four-state contract; phase-aware rescope continuation; three-event post-merge chain; Nathan-only otherwise unreachable PR-50; PE metaprompt, procedure, hubs, Alpha record, contracts/fixtures and archive lineage; protected Primary-core byte identity and 46-row R1; and absence of active Library IDs, native-document PFCanon routes, invented endpoints, stale Alpha state, model/strength assessment, Analyzer, or configuration routing. Alpha remains stopped with PR03 accepted-final and PR04 not started; validation/promotion prepares but never executes the PR04 PR-10 handoff.\n\n## Bounded rescope receiver compatibility\n\nRS-10/RS-20 accept supported planning, non-PR and merged-but-not-accepted work-unit findings using actual existing evidence. RS-20 remains the same IA bounded implementation-delta decision owner; preserve native product-intent and remediation boundaries. RS-30 retains the actual request/proposal type, author and decision owner. A PR rescope carries exact phase. Only approved open-PR PR-30/PR-35 rescope enters RS-40 after manual drain and fresh verification; approved prepublication rescope returns directly to PR-30. Other approved bounded deltas return to the needed native stage then originating reviewer. ESC-40 `REMEDIATION_REVIEW` returns under its drained overlay to the recorded native delivery owner, including PR-30/PR-35; it never masquerades as RS-20 approval or creates duplicate review/addendum/Proceed. PR-30/PR-35/RS-40 with unrecoverable work or missing source/owner/drain evidence returns terminally to Nathan, emits no handoff, and makes no abort or closure decision.\n",
    "0994e8e2d488d21d9352271d8e5cb1ed26745197039e4891de2e87f091f0baab": "# Project Prompt Contract Registry schema\n\nUse this reference for a project's expected prompt topology. Keep one registry per governed project and bind it to one exact Workspace Skill Registry version.\n\n## Registry record\n\n```yaml\nschema_version: project-prompt-contract-registry/1.0\nregistry_id: <PROJECT>-PCR-<date>.<revision>\nproject_id: <stable project ID>\nstatus: DRAFT | APPROVED | SUPERSEDED\napproved_by: <identity or null>\napproved_at: <timestamp or null>\nworkspace_skill_registry_id: <exact registry ID>\nauthority_sources: []\nlanes: []\nprompts: []\nglobal_literals: {}\n```\n\nAn `APPROVED` registry requires `approved_by` and `approved_at`. Treat a draft as inventory and proposed expected state only.\n\n## Lane record\n\n```yaml\n- lane: IA\n  title: Implementation Agent\n  notion_parent_id: <exact parent ID>\n  active: true\n```\n\n## Prompt record\n\n```yaml\n- prompt_key: IA-10\n  notion_page_id: <stable page ID>\n  expected_title: \"IA-10 — <function>\"\n  lane: IA\n  sequence: 10\n  lifecycle: ACTIVE | REPLACEMENT_CANDIDATE | RETIRE_PENDING | ARCHIVED\n  function: <one falsifiable sentence>\n  session_class: DEDICATED_ONE_OFF | CHANGE_LIFETIME | ROLE_CONTINUING | ORCHESTRATOR_RUN\n  session_role: <role>\n  creator_role: <role>\n  reviewer_role: <role or NONE>\n  inputs: []\n  outputs: []\n  approvals:\n    request_literal: \"ASK OK?\"\n    approval_literal: \"ASK OK.\"\n    approving_role: <role>\n    effect: <exact transition>\n  mutations:\n    allowed: []\n    forbidden: []\n  evidence_contract: []\n  failure_contract: []\n  required_interfaces: []\n  controlling_sources: []\n  expected_parent_id: <parent ID>\n  supersedes: []\n  superseded_by: null\n  audit_assertions:\n    required_literals: []\n    forbidden_literals: []\n    required_regex: []\n    forbidden_regex: []\n```\n\n`audit_assertions` provides deterministic checks without replacing semantic maker/reader review. Attribute every assertion to a rule ID in the assertion object when a bare string would obscure authority.\n\n## Glow literals and roles\n\n```yaml\nglobal_literals:\n  approval_request: \"ASK OK?\"\n  approved: \"ASK OK.\"\n```\n\nFor Glow, IA means Implementation Agent; Isis is Lead Developer; Thoth is Head of Development and takes escalations; Kronos is QA-only; DevOps executes bounded Ops and QA tasks; continuing Isis executes integrated QA-10 audit/comparison/triage/readiness before Guide. Thoth proposes bounded remediation through ESC-30 and Isis decides it through ESC-40. Approved Plans, Guides, and Specifications remain immutable: a qualifying approved delta produces exactly one standalone PF10 addendum, and affected delivery resumes under that overlay only after Nathan's manual drain and fresh verification. IA-40 revises only an initial, not-yet-approved Implementation Plan for return to the same IA-30 reviewer; it does not prepare an in-flight Plan replacement or add another remediation approval. The Product Owner retains actual PF10/PF23 publication. Record the effective correction separately from immutable R1, preserve separate audit/triage/readiness identities, and reject an informational-publication gate at QA-50. Retired QA-15/ESC-20/ESC-50/ESC-60 functions remain in their declared replacements.\n\n## Invariants\n\n- Keep `prompt_key`, active `notion_page_id`, and active lane sequence unique.\n- Require an active prompt's expected title to begin with its lane-qualified key.\n- Require every active prompt to reference a declared lane.\n- Require outputs and direct consumers to close or record the unresolved external role.\n- Omit approval fields only when no approval boundary exists.\n- Do not infer approval merely because an approval literal appears in quoted or instructional text.\n- Do not retire a source because a successor exists.\n",
    "ba9919ba19b505c2997e1053f96344f262fcde30448fbee35ccfb4a3222c4c07": "# Report contracts\n\nUse this reference when creating or checking audit artifacts.\n\n## Evidence bundle\n\nStore the run manifest, registry identities and hashes, source manifest, deterministic check results, semantic findings, finding dispositions, and artifact hashes in `WGA-{RUN_ID}-Evidence.json`. Preserve raw and structural digests separately.\n\n## Finding record\n\n```yaml\nfinding_id: WGA-<run>-<sequence>\nrule_id: <catalog ID>\nseverity: BLOCKER | ERROR | WARNING | ADVISORY\nsubject:\n  kind: prompt | skill | interface | lane | registry | source\n  id: <stable identity>\nobserved:\n  summary: <complete-source observation>\n  evidence_refs: []\nexpected:\n  summary: <registry or authority requirement>\n  authority_refs: []\nimpact: <workflow consequence>\nrecommended_action: <smallest source-grounded correction>\nowner: <role or lane>\nrepair_batch: <batch or UNASSIGNED>\ndisposition: OPEN | ACCEPTED_DEVIATION | FALSE_POSITIVE | SUPERSEDED | RESOLVED\n```\n\n## Audit report\n\nBegin with `WORKSPACE PROMPT AND SKILL GOVERNANCE AUDIT REPORT`. Include run/mode, registry versions, snapshot identity, source completeness, inventory totals, lane counts, interoperability matrix, all findings and dispositions, repair impact, Proposed PF10 Addenda when applicable, independent-review requirements, the smallest next permitted action, and exactly one verdict.\n\nDo not claim publication, application, approval, acceptance, completion, or validation without exact evidence for that state.\n\n## Proposed change set\n\nRecord exact target, expected base identity/version/hash, requested operation, intended result, required approval, validation rule, owner, and source-disposition boundary. The artifact is a proposal only and has no mutation authority.\n\n## Proposed PF10 Addenda\n\nCreate only when a Glow finding exposes a noncanonical proposed addendum, decision, or drainage question. State evidence, the proposed addendum or exact question, the likely topic-owning document, and why no current authority resolves it. Do not write into PF10 or imply Product Owner approval. Use **PF10 addendum** as singular and **PF10 addenda** as plural. Preserve “Agenda” only inside an exact quoted historical artifact title.\n\n## Reviewer packet\n\nCreate only for a high-risk independent review. Include exact question, allowed source identities/hashes, prohibited assumptions, declared and inferred contracts, unresolved difference, required decision shape, and return route. Do not include the intended answer.\n\n## Verdict derivation\n\n- `INDETERMINATE`: any decisive source or authority is unresolved.\n- `FAIL`: any open blocker or error remains after complete evidence.\n- `PASS WITH WARNINGS`: no blocker/error, but at least one warning remains.\n- `PASS`: no open blocker, error, or warning.\n",
    "2ee514fc9b9e6296dbb7ef49836f9fe3f530d2612414fb3a606d0c79124ca722": "# Rule catalog\n\nUse these stable IDs in deterministic and semantic findings. Do not reuse an ID for a different meaning.\n\n| ID | Default severity | Meaning |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `SRC-001` | BLOCKER | Decisive source is incomplete or unavailable |\n| `SRC-002` | BLOCKER | Source changed after snapshot pinning |\n| `SRC-003` | ERROR | Snapshot identity or digest does not match the declared source |\n| `INV-001` | ERROR | Expected active record is absent from observed scope |\n| `INV-002` | WARNING | Unexpected active record is present in observed scope |\n| `INV-003` | ERROR | Duplicate active identity or live function |\n| `NAM-001` | WARNING | Active prompt title is not lane-qualified as declared |\n| `NAM-002` | ERROR | Prompt is under the wrong declared parent or lane |\n| `CTR-001` | ERROR | Declared and independently inferred function differ materially |\n| `CTR-002` | ERROR | Required input, output, consumer, or stop contract is missing |\n| `TOP-001` | ERROR | Producer/consumer interface does not close |\n| `TOP-002` | ERROR | Workflow contains a hidden bypass, dead end, or unreachable transition |\n| `AUT-001` | BLOCKER | Governing authority is conflicting or ambiguous |\n| `AUT-002` | ERROR | Historical or staging evidence is treated as permanent/current authority |\n| `APR-001` | ERROR | `ASK OK?` is treated as approval |\n| `APR-002` | ERROR | Approval role or effect is invented, broadened, or ambiguous |\n| `ROL-001` | ERROR | IA, Isis, Thoth, Kronos, PO, or DevOps duties are conflated |\n| `ART-001` | ERROR | Proof or receipt is used as substantive authority |\n| `ART-002` | ERROR | Required evidence locality or lineage is missing |\n| `MUT-001` | BLOCKER | Undeclared write, archive, retirement, or external execution is attempted |\n| `MUT-002` | ERROR | Universal Redline Apply is used for prompt mutation |\n| `SES-001` | WARNING | Session lifetime or independence contract is missing or contradictory |\n| `SKL-001` | ERROR | Prompt and installed skill disagree on an exact interface |\n| `SKL-002` | WARNING | Applicable specialized validator or maintenance route is unresolved |\n| `PUB-001` | BLOCKER | Publication lacks exact base, target, approval, or readback evidence |\n| `PUB-002` | ERROR | Runtime source and publication mirror differ without a drift disposition |\n| `COL-001` | BLOCKER | Exact or case-insensitive installed-name collision |\n| `COL-002` | BLOCKER | Canonical key or stable workspace ID is reused |\n| `COL-003` | WARNING | Trigger overlap candidate lacks deterministic precedence |\n| `COL-004` | ERROR | Canonical function is duplicated in overlapping scope |\n| `COL-005` | BLOCKER | Two skills claim write authority over the same governed surface |\n| `COL-006` | BLOCKER | Package/source path is reused |\n| `COL-007` | BLOCKER | Skill dependency cycle exists |\n| `COL-008` | ERROR | Supersession is ambiguous or has multiple active successors |\n| `COL-009` | ERROR | One installed source has multiple active Notion mirrors |\n| `COL-010` | ERROR | Project-local skill index competes with the workspace registry |\n\nDeterministic scripts may prove structural conditions. A complete-source semantic reading must decide material function, trigger, authority, role, and approval meaning.\n",
    "b79bd5197371109b17ba0626203c9c398c6fc3a9dee7662283dbe1decf900f91": "# Workspace Skill Registry schema\n\nUse this reference when creating, validating, or interpreting the single workspace-wide skill registry.\n\n## Registry record\n\n```yaml\nschema_version: amthor-workspace-skill-registry/1.0\nregistry_id: WSR-<date>.<revision>\nstatus: DRAFT | APPROVED | SUPERSEDED\napproved_by: <identity or null>\napproved_at: <timestamp or null>\nnamespace_root: amthor\nnotion_registry_page_id: <page ID or null>\nskills: []\nreserved_names: []\nproject_views: []\n```\n\nAn `APPROVED` registry requires `approved_by` and `approved_at`. A draft is usable for inventory and preflight, but it is not approved expected state.\n\n## Skill record\n\n```yaml\n- skill_uid: WSK-000001\n  canonical_key: amthor.shared.example-skill\n  installed_name: example-skill\n  display_name: Example Skill\n  namespace: amthor.shared\n  scope: WORKSPACE_SHARED | MULTI_PROJECT | PROJECT | EXPERIMENTAL\n  projects: []\n  lifecycle: PROPOSED | ACTIVE | SUPERSEDED | RETIRED | UNREGISTERED\n  canonical_function: <one falsifiable sentence>\n  trigger_contract:\n    use_when: []\n    do_not_use_when: []\n  mutation_authority: READ_ONLY | LOCAL_FILES | NOTION | REPOSITORY | EXTERNAL_SYSTEM | MIXED\n  governed_surfaces: []\n  precedence:\n    more_specific_than: []\n    less_specific_than: []\n  dependencies: []\n  conflicts_with: []\n  supersedes: []\n  source:\n    kind: INSTALLED_SKILL\n    package: <exact package or checkout identity>\n    revision: <declared revision or null>\n    commit: <exact commit or null>\n    sha256: <complete SKILL.md SHA-256>\n  validation_receipt: <identity or null>\n  notion_page_id: <mirror page ID or null>\n  publication_status: UNPUBLISHED | PUBLISH_PENDING | CURRENT | DRIFTED\n  notion_snapshot_sha256: <hash or null>\n```\n\n`governed_surfaces` and `precedence` make collision decisions explicit. They extend the approved core record without changing its meaning.\n\n## Reserved-name record\n\n```yaml\n- installed_name: amthor-workspace-governance-maintain\n  canonical_key: amthor.shared.workspace-governance-maintain\n  status: PROPOSED | RESERVED\n  canonical_function: <one sentence>\n  reason: <why the identity is held>\n```\n\n## Invariants\n\n- Reuse neither `skill_uid` nor `canonical_key`.\n- Compare installed names case-insensitively.\n- Keep one record for a shared skill associated with several projects.\n- Keep installed source as runtime authority and Notion as its publication mirror.\n- Do not create a competing project-local skill index.\n- Do not silently infer material trigger overlap from token similarity alone.\n- Do not treat registration as authorization to rename grandfathered installed skills.\n",
    "f7471bb398e1f3815868707eaa3fb7ba4946cd0bbdceb685af94e2e925e102fa": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Deterministic, read-only workspace governance audit helpers and CLI.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom collections import Counter, defaultdict\nfrom datetime import date, datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable\n\ntry:\n    import yaml\nexcept ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - environment failure\n    raise SystemExit(\"PyYAML is required to run workspace governance validators\") from exc\n\n\nWORKSPACE_SCHEMA = \"amthor-workspace-skill-registry/1.0\"\nPROJECT_SCHEMA = \"project-prompt-contract-registry/1.0\"\nMODES = {\n    \"BASELINE\",\n    \"BATCH_PREFLIGHT\",\n    \"BATCH_POSTFLIGHT\",\n    \"TARGETED\",\n    \"FINAL_VALIDATION\",\n    \"SKILL_NAMESPACE_PREFLIGHT\",\n    \"SKILL_REGISTRATION_POSTFLIGHT\",\n}\nSCOPES = {\"WORKSPACE_SHARED\", \"MULTI_PROJECT\", \"PROJECT\", \"EXPERIMENTAL\"}\nLIFECYCLES = {\"PROPOSED\", \"ACTIVE\", \"SUPERSEDED\", \"RETIRED\", \"UNREGISTERED\"}\nMUTATION_AUTHORITIES = {\n    \"READ_ONLY\",\n    \"LOCAL_FILES\",\n    \"NOTION\",\n    \"REPOSITORY\",\n    \"EXTERNAL_SYSTEM\",\n    \"MIXED\",\n}\nSEVERITY_ORDER = {\"ADVISORY\": 0, \"WARNING\": 1, \"ERROR\": 2, \"BLOCKER\": 3}\nTOKEN_STOPWORDS = {\n    \"a\", \"an\", \"and\", \"as\", \"at\", \"by\", \"for\", \"from\", \"in\", \"into\",\n    \"of\", \"on\", \"or\", \"the\", \"to\", \"use\", \"when\", \"with\", \"without\",\n}\n\n\ndef load_data(path: str | Path) -> Any:\n    source = Path(path)\n    with source.open(\"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        if source.suffix.lower() == \".json\":\n            return json.load(handle)\n        return yaml.safe_load(handle)\n\n\ndef dump_yaml(data: Any, path: str | Path) -> None:\n    with Path(path).open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        yaml.safe_dump(data, handle, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True)\n\n\ndef json_compatible(data: Any) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Convert safe YAML scalar types into deterministic JSON values.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(data, (date, datetime)):\n        return data.isoformat()\n    if isinstance(data, dict):\n        return {str(key): json_compatible(value) for key, value in data.items()}\n    if isinstance(data, (list, tuple)):\n        return [json_compatible(value) for value in data]\n    return data\n\n\ndef canonical_json(data: Any) -> str:\n    return json.dumps(json_compatible(data), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(\",\", \":\"))\n\n\ndef sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:\n    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef sha256_text(text: str) -> str:\n    return sha256_bytes(text.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n\n\ndef structural_digest(text: str) -> str:\n    normalized = text.replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\").replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\")\n    fences = re.findall(r\"```([^\\n]*)\\n(.*?)```\", normalized, flags=re.DOTALL)\n    features = {\n        \"headings\": re.findall(r\"(?m)^#{1,6}\\s+(.+?)\\s*$\", normalized),\n        \"links\":
