re.findall(r\"(?m)^\\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*):\", normalized),\n        \"fences\": [{\"language\": lang.strip(), \"content\": body} for lang, body in fences],\n    }\n    return sha256_text(canonical_json(features))\n\n\ndef issue(level: str, rule_id: str, subject: str, message: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {\"level\": level, \"rule_id\": rule_id, \"subject\": subject, \"message\": message}\n\n\ndef _required_mapping(data: Any, name: str, problems: list[dict[str, str]]) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", name, \"Record must be a mapping\"))\n        return {}\n    return data\n\n\ndef validate_workspace_registry(data: Any) -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    problems: list[dict[str, str]] = []\n    registry = _required_mapping(data, \"workspace_registry\", problems)\n    if not registry:\n        return problems\n\n    required = {\"schema_version\", \"registry_id\", \"status\", \"namespace_root\", \"skills\"}\n    for field in sorted(required - set(registry)):\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", \"workspace_registry\", f\"Missing required field: {field}\"))\n    if registry.get(\"schema_version\") != WORKSPACE_SCHEMA:\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", \"workspace_registry\", \"Unsupported workspace registry schema\"))\n    if registry.get(\"status\") not in {\"DRAFT\", \"APPROVED\", \"SUPERSEDED\"}:\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", \"workspace_registry\", \"Invalid registry status\"))\n    if registry.get(\"status\") == \"APPROVED\" and not (registry.get(\"approved_by\") and registry.get(\"approved_at\")):\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"AUT-001\", \"workspace_registry\", \"Approved registry lacks approver or approval timestamp\"))\n    namespace_root = registry.get(\"namespace_root\")\n    if not isinstance(namespace_root, str) or not namespace_root:\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"COL-002\", \"workspace_registry\", \"namespace_root must be non-empty\"))\n\n    skills = registry.get(\"skills\")\n    if not isinstance(skills, list):\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", \"workspace_registry\", \"skills must be a list\"))\n        return problems\n\n    seen: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {\n        \"skill_uid\": {}, \"canonical_key\": {}, \"installed_name\": {},\n        \"source_package\": {}, \"notion_page_id\": {},\n    }\n    known_names: set[str] = set()\n    active_records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n\n    for index, raw in enumerate(skills):\n        subject = f\"skills[{index}]\"\n        if not isinstance(raw, dict):\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, \"Skill record must be a mapping\"))\n            continue\n        record = raw\n        for field in (\n            \"skill_uid\", \"canonical_key\", \"installed_name\", \"display_name\", \"namespace\",\n            \"scope\", \"lifecycle\", \"canonical_function\", \"trigger_contract\",\n            \"mutation_authority\", \"dependencies\", \"source\", \"publication_status\",\n        ):\n            if field not in record:\n                problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, f\"Missing required field: {field}\"))\n\n        name = record.get(\"installed_name\")\n        canonical_key = record.get(\"canonical_key\")\n        uid = record.get(\"skill_uid\")\n        lifecycle = record.get(\"lifecycle\")\n        if isinstance(name, str) and name:\n            known_names.add(name)\n        else:\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"COL-001\", subject, \"installed_name must be non-empty\"))\n        if record.get(\"scope\") not in SCOPES:\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, \"Invalid scope\"))\n        if lifecycle not in LIFECYCLES:\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, \"Invalid lifecycle\"))\n        if record.get(\"mutation_authority\") not in MUTATION_AUTHORITIES:\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, \"Invalid mutation_authority\"))\n        if not isinstance(record.get(\"canonical_function\"), str) or not record.get(\"canonical_function\", \"\").strip():\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"COL-004\", subject, \"canonical_function must be a non-empty sentence\"))\n        trigger = record.get(\"trigger_contract\")\n        if not isinstance(trigger, dict) or not isinstance(trigger.get(\"use_when\"), list)   if not isinstance(record.get(\"dependencies\"), list):\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, \"dependencies must be a list\"))\n        if isinstance(namespace_root, problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"COL-002\", subject, \"namespace must use namespace_root\"))\n\n        source = record.get(\"source\") if isinstance(record.get(\"source\"), dict) else {}\n        package = source.get(\"package\")\n        digest = source.get(\"sha256\")\n        if record.get(\"lifecycle\") == \"ACTIVE\":\n            if not package:\n                problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, \"Active skill requires source.package\"))\n            if digest is not None and not re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9a-f]{64}\", str(digest)):\n \"skill_uid\": uid,\n            \"canonical_key\": canonical_key,\n            \"installed_name\": name.lower() if isinstance(name, str) else None,\n            \"source_package\": package if unique_values.items():\n            if value in (None, \"\"):\n                continue\n            if value in seen[field]:\n                rule = {\n                    \"installed_name\": subject, f\"Duplicate {field}: {value}\"))\n            else:\n                seen[field][value] = subject\n\n    for record in active_records:\n        for dependency in record.get(\"dependencies\", name must be a mapping\"))\n            continue\n        reserved_name = str(reserved.get(\"installed_name\", \"\")).lower()\n        if reserved_name and reserved_name in active_names:\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"COL-001\", f\"reserved_names[{index}]\", \"Reserved installed name collides with active skill\"))\n        if reserved.get(\"canonical_key\") in active_keys:\n identity\"))\n    prompts = registry.get(\"prompts\")\n    if not isinstance(prompts, list):\n        problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", \"project_registry\", \"prompts must be a list\"))\n        return problems\n\n    keys: set[str] = set()\n    page_ids: set[str] = set()\n    active_records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    for index, record in enumerate(prompts):\n        subject = f\"prompts[{index}]\"\n        if not isinstance(record, dict):\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"SRC-001\", subject, \"Prompt record must be a mapping\"))\n            continue\n        for field in (\"prompt_key\", \"notion_page_id\", \"expected_title\", \"lane\", \"sequence\", \"lifecycle\", \"function\", \"session_class\", \"session_role\", \"inputs\", \"outputs\", \"mutations\", record.get(\"prompt_key\")\n        page_id = record.get(\"notion_page_id\")\n        if key in keys:\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"INV-003\", subject, f\"Duplicate prompt_key: {key}\"))\n        elif isinstance(key, str):\n            keys.add(key)\n        if record.get(\"lifecycle\") != \"ARCHIVED\":\n            if page_id in page_ids:\n                problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"INV-003\", subject, f\"Duplicate active notion_page_id: {page_id}\"))\n            elif page_id:\n                page_ids.add(page_id)\n            active_records.append(record)\n        if record.get(\"lane\") not in lane_ids:\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"NAM-002\", subject, f\"Unknown lane: {record.get('lane')}\"))\n        if not isinstance(record.get(\"sequence\"), int):\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"NAM-001\", subject, \"sequence must be an integer\"))\n        title = \"expected_title does not begin with prompt_key\"))\n        approvals = record.get(\"approvals\")\n        if approvals is not None:\n            if not isinstance(approvals, dict):\n                problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"APR-002\", subject, \"approvals must be a mapping\"))\n            elif approvals.get(\"request_literal\") == approvals.get(\"approval_literal\"):\n                problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"APR-001\", subject, \"Approval request and approval literals must differ\"))\n\n    for record in active_records:\n        for output in record.get(\"outputs\") or re.fullmatch(r\"[A-Z]+(?:-[A-Z]+)*-\\d+\", consumer) and consumer not in keys:\n                    problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"TOP-001\", record.get(\"prompt_key\", \"prompt\"), f\"Unknown prompt consumer: {consumer}\"))\n\n    literals = registry.get(\"global_literals\") or {}\n    if str(registry.get(\"project_id\", \"\")).lower() == \"glow-hde\":\n        if literals.get(\"approval_request\") != \"ASK OK?\" or literals.get(\"approved\") != \"ASK OK.\":\n            problems.append(issue(\"error\", \"APR-001\", \"project_registry\", \"Glow approval literals are not exact\"))\n    return problems\n\n\ndef _normalized(value: Any) -> str:\n    return re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", str(value or \"\").strip().lower())\n\n\ndef _tokens(value: Any) -> set[str]:\n    return {token for token in re.findall(r\"[a-z0-9]+\", _normalized(value)) if token not in TOKEN_STOPWORDS and len(token) > 2}\n\n\ndef _scope_overlaps(a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:\n    if a.get(\"scope\") == \"WORKSPACE_SHARED\" or b.get(\"scope\") == \"WORKSPACE_SHARED\":\n        return True\n    projects_a = set(a.get(\"projects\") or [])\n    projects_b = set(b.get(\"projects\") or [])\n    return bool(projects_a & projects_b) or (not projects_a and not projects_b)\n\n\ndef _has_precedence(a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:\n    name_a, name_b = a.get(\"installed_name\"), b.get(\"installed_name\")\n    precedence_a = a.get(\"precedence\") or {}\n    precedence_b = b.get(\"precedence\") or {}\n    referenced = set(precedence_a.get(\"more_specific_than\") or []) | set(precedence_a.get(\"less_specific_than\") or [])\n    referenced |= set(precedence_b.get(\"more_specific_than\") or []) | set(precedence_b.get(\"less_specific_than\") or [])\n    return name_a in referenced or name_b in referenced\n\n\ndef _trigger_overlap(a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any]) -> float:\n    phrases_a = (a.get(\"trigger_contract\") or {}).get(\"use_when\") or []\n    phrases_b = (b.get(\"trigger_contract\") or {}).get(\"use_when\") or []\n    best = 0.0\n    for phrase_a in phrases_a:\n        tokens_a = _tokens(phrase_a)\n        for phrase_b in phrases_b:\n            tokens_b = _tokens(phrase_b)\n            if len(tokens_a | tokens_b) < 3:\n                continue\n            best = max(best, len(tokens_a & tokens_b) / len(tokens_a | tokens_b))\n    return best\n\n\ndef _collision(rule_id: str, severity: str, a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any], detail: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    return {\n        \"rule_id\": rule_id,\n        \"severity\": severity,\n        \"subjects\": [a.get(\"installed_name\", \"<unnamed>\"), b.get(\"installed_name\", \"<unnamed>\")],\n        \"detail\": detail,\n    }\n\n\ndef detect_skill_collisions(registry: dict[str, Any], proposal: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    records = [r for r in registry.get(\"skills\") or [] if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get(\"lifecycle\") not in {\"RETIRED\", \"SUPERSEDED\"}]\n    if proposal:\n        proposal = dict(proposal)\n        proposal.setdefault(\"lifecycle\", \"PROPOSED\")\n        records.append(proposal)\n    collisions: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n\n    for index, a in enumerate(records):\n        for b in records[index + 1:]:\n            if _normalized(a.get(\"installed_name\")) == _normalized(b.get(\"installed_name\")):\n                collisions.append(_collision(\"COL-001\", \"BLOCKER\", a, b, \"Exact or collisions.append(_collision(\"COL-002\", \"BLOCKER\", a, b, \"Canonical key is reused\"))\n            if a.get(\"skill_uid\") and a.get(\"skill_uid\") == b.get(\"skill_uid\"):\n                collisions.append(_collision(\"COL-002\", \"BLOCKER\", a, b, \"Stable workspace skill UID is reused\"))\n            if _scope_overlaps(a, b) and _normalized(a.get(\"canonical_function\")) == package_a = (a.get(\"source\") or {}).get(\"package\")\n            package_b = (b.get(\"source\") or {}).get(\"package\")\n            if package_a and package_a == package_b:\n                collisions.append(_collision(\"COL-006\", \"BLOCKER\", a, b, \"Source package/path is reused\"))\n            page_a, page_b = a.get(\"notion_page_id\"), b.get(\"notion_page_id\")\n            if page_a and page_a == page_b:\n                collisions.append(_collision(\"COL-009\", \"ERROR\", a, b, \"One Notion mirror is claimed by two active records\"))\n            surfaces = set(a.get(\"governed_surfaces\") or []) & set(b.get(\"governed_surfaces\") or [])\n            if surfaces and a.get(\"mutation_authority\") != \"READ_ONLY\" and b.get(\"mutation_authority\") != precedence\"))\n\n    names = {r.get(\"installed_name\"): r for r in records if r.get(\"installed_name\")}\n    graph = {name: [d for d in record.get(\"dependencies\") or [] if d in names] for name, record in names.items()}\n    visiting: set[str] = set()\n    visited: set[str] = set()\n    stack: list[str] = []\n    cycles: set[tuple[str, ...]] = set()\n\n    def walk(node: str) -> None:\n        if node in visiting:\n            start = stack.index(node)\n            cycle = tuple(stack[start:] + [node])\n            cycles.add(cycle)\n            return\n        if node in visited:\n            return\n        visiting.add(node)\n        stack.append(node)\n        for dependency in graph.get(node, []):\n            walk(dependency)\n        stack.pop()\n        visiting.remove(node)\n record.get(\"supersedes\") or []:\n            successors[predecessor].append(record.get(\"installed_name\", \"<unnamed>\"))\n    for predecessor, active_successors in sorted(successors.items()):\n        if len(active_successors) > 1:\n            collisions.append({\"rule_id\": \"COL-008\", \"severity\": \"ERROR\", \"subjects\": active_successors, \"detail\": f\"Multiple active successors for {predecessor}\"})\n\n    collisions.sort(key=lambda item: (item[\"rule_id\"], item.get(\"subjects\", []), item.get(\"detail\", \"\")))\n    return collisions\n\n\ndef build_snapshot_manifest(source_dir: str | Path, run_id: str, source_index: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    root = Path(source_dir).resolve()\n    indexed = (source_index or {}).get(\"sources\") if isinstance(source_index, dict) else None\n    if indexed is None:\n        indexed = [{\"source_id\": str(path.relative_to(root)), \"kind\": \"local_text\", \"path\": str(path.relative_to(root)), \"complete\": True} for path in sorted(root.rglob(\"*\")) if path.is_file()]\n    sources: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    for raw in indexed:\n        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not raw.get(\"path\"):\n            raise ValueError(\"Every source index record requires path\")\n        relative = Path(str(raw[\"path\"]))\n        resolved = (root / relative).resolve()\n        if root not in resolved.parents and resolved != root:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Source path escapes snapshot root: {relative}\")\n        data = resolved.read_bytes()\n        text = data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        record = {key: value for key, value in raw.items() if key != \"sha256\" and key != \"structural_sha256\"}\n        record.setdefault(\"source_id\", str(relative))\n        record.setdefault(\"kind\", \"local_text\")\n        record.setdefault(\"complete\", True)\n        record.setdefault(\"warnings\", [])\n        record[\"path\"] = str(relative)\n        record[\"sha256\"] = sha256_bytes(data)\n        record[\"structural_sha256\"] = structural_digest(text)\n        record[\"size_bytes\"] = len(data)\n        sources.append(json_compatible(record))\n    sources.sort(key=lambda item: (str(item.get(\"kind\")), str(item.get(\"source_id\"))))\n    snapshot_identity = sha256_text(canonical_json([{key: value for key, value in source.items() if key != \"retrieved_at\"} for source in sources]))\n    return {\n        \"schema_version\": \"amthor-workspace-governance-snapshot/1.0\",\n        \"run_id\": _finding(rule_id: str, severity: str, kind: str, subject_id: str, observed: str, expected: str, impact: str, action: str, owner: str = \"UNASSIGNED\", **extra: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    finding = {\n        \"rule_id\": rule_id,\n        \"severity\": severity,\n        \"subject\": {\"kind\": kind, \"id\": subject_id},\n        \"observed\": {\"summary\": observed, \"evidence_refs\": extra.pop(\"evidence_refs\", [])},\n        \"expected\": {\"summary\": expected, \"authority_refs\": extra.pop(\"authority_refs\", [])},\n        \"impact\": impact,\n        \"recommended_action\": action,\n        \"owner\": owner,\n        \"repair_batch\": extra.pop(\"repair_batch\", \"UNASSIGNED\"),\n        \"disposition\": extra.pop(\"disposition\", \"OPEN\"),\n    }\n    finding.update(extra)\n    return finding\n\n\ndef _issues_to_findings(problems: Iterable[dict[str, str]], kind: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    converted = []\n    for problem in problems:\n \"COL-007\"} and problem[\"level\"] == \"error\":\n            severity = \"BLOCKER\"\n        converted.append(_finding(problem[\"rule_id\"], severity, kind, problem[\"subject\"], _read_snapshot_text(snapshot: dict[str, Any], source: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:\n    root = snapshot.get(\"snapshot_root\")\n    if not root or not source.get(\"path\"):\n        return None\n    path = (Path(root) / str(source[\"path\"])).resolve()\n    try:\n        return path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):\n        return None\n\n\ndef   def unpack(value: Any, default_rule: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n        if isinstance(value, dict):\n            return str(value.get(\"value\", \"\")), str(value.get(\"rule_id\", default_rule))\n        return str(value), default_rule\n\n    for raw in assertions.get(\"required_literals\") or []:\n        value, rule = unpack(raw, \"CTR-002\")\n        if value not in text:\n            findings.append(_finding(rule, \"ERROR\", \"prompt\", str(record.get(\"prompt_key\")), f\"Required literal absent: {value}\", \"Required literal present\", \"Declared contract may not be implemented\", \"Review and repair the prompt\", evidence_refs=[source_ref]))\n    for raw in assertions.get(\"forbidden_literals\") or []:\n        value, rule = unpack(raw, \"CTR-001\")\n        if value in text:\n            findings.append(_finding(rule, \"ERROR\", \"prompt\", str(record.get(\"prompt_key\")), f\"Forbidden literal present: {value}\", \"Forbidden literal absent\", \"Observed prompt contradicts declared contract\", \"Review and repair the prompt\", evidence_refs=[source_ref]))\n    for raw in assertions.get(\"required_regex\") or []:\n        value, rule = unpack(raw, assertions.get(\"forbidden_regex\") or []:\n        value, rule = unpack(raw, \"CTR-001\")\n        if re.search(value, text, flags=re.MULTILINE):\n            findings.append(_finding(rule, repair the prompt\", evidence_refs=[source_ref]))\n    return findings\n\n\ndef audit_governance(run_manifest: dict[str, Any], workspace_registry: dict[str, Any], snapshot: dict[str, Any], \"semantic_review_complete\": semantic_complete,\n        \"findings\": findings,\n        \"verdict\": verdict,\n    }\n\n\ndef _render_report(result: dict[str, Any], project_registry: dict[str, Any] == \"PASS\":\n        next_action = \"preserve this receipt and continue only through the governing workflow; this audit performs no mutation.\"\n    elif result[\"verdict\"] == \"PASS WITH {counts.get('ADVISORY', 0)}\",\n        f\"- Smallest next permitted action: {next_action}\",\n        \"\",\n        \"## Verdict\",\n        \"\",\n        result[\"verdict\"],\n        \"\",\n    ])\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef write_audit_artifacts(result: dict[str, Any], run_manifest: dict[str, Any], workspace_registry: dict[str, Any], snapshot: dict[str, Any], project_registry:     "f0499082570ffc889d55dcc33b00e0b4ad9f6a63de3bf4ec1591ef4f8fcd4a16": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Validate a Project Prompt Contract Registry without modifying it.\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\n\nfrom audit_workspace_governance import load_data, validate_project_registry\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"registry\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    problems = validate_project_registry(load_data(args.registry))\n    result = {\n        \"valid\": not any(problem[\"level\"] == \"error\" for problem in problems),\n        \"problems\": problems,\n    }\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True))\n    return 0 if result[\"valid\"] else 2\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",
    "59307bd42eb4b0a80f90bc141de3713e887d5071d34e34d73f6a9a81ac2b1a5d": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Validate a Workspace Skill Registry without modifying it.\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\n\nfrom audit_workspace_governance import load_data, validate_workspace_registry\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"registry\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    problems = validate_workspace_registry(load_data(args.registry))\n    result = {\n        \"valid\": not any(problem[\"level\"] == \"error\" for problem in problems),\n        \"problems\": problems,\n    }\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True))\n    return 0 if result[\"valid\"] else 2\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",
    "28403f876c729170974a7a122ec5d3f776ce849e6be9b03b0927069f9341afb1": "---\nname: flowmaster-validate\ndescription: Validate the installed Flowmaster suite and the complete Glow Canonical Change Flow against the pinned immutable R1 oracle, including structure, raw-byte Primary-core identity, revisions, self-containment, all 46 Change rows, graph closure, actor/session/approval/lineage boundaries, prohibited architecture, deterministic fixtures, and maintenance readiness. Use after editing Primary or a specialization, before or after propagation, or when auditing suite currency. Read-only; do not run workflows or modify skills.\n---\n\n# Flowmaster Validate\n\nFLOWMASTER_VALIDATE_REVISION: 3.2.5\n\nMaintenance addition: register the self-contained human-design-reading-flowmaster domain\ncontract without changing the Primary core or existing domain/oracle checks. Its behavioral\ntests remain in that specialization and must be executed separately; a text contract check\ndoes not establish live provider, connector or Chat Pro target-surface availability.\n\nR1_ORACLE_PROFILE: GLOW_HDE_CANONICAL_CHANGE_FLOW_R1_20260831_1\n\nR1_CONTRACT_MATRIX_SHA256: faa7fb7d77066cc491bde957b6d2f7d3255c74833936e3952f97873da27ea2f1\n\nR1_ORACLE_SHA256: 52807e58c4a4659e6c1fc822749f6e50253ad7b01846c833f727ee266ca71d5e\n\nThis skill is a deterministic read-only validator. It never repairs a skill, propagates a core, invokes Change Flow, calls live Notion workflow components, mutates a registry, or converts a finding into an accepted deviation.\n\n## GCFPE release-profile validation boundary\n\nThe 20260914 candidate contract revision 4.0.5 binds the corrected complete raw-byte repair-plan and PF10 evidence, the corrected source manifest, and the preserved native recovery/owner graph. It checks QA-120 PASS by verified change class: Epic to CL-E-10 and CRD to CL-C-10, with separate Report/RCA and complete matching intake to continuing Isis. Validate the actual producer and both receiver bodies as well as graph/contract agreement; reject the wrong-class route even when all declarations agree. Missing or conflicting class or receiver evidence permits no closure handoff. Those pins describe the repair baseline; they never replace fresh runtime PF10 resolution. Deterministic agreement with these pins does not independently prove live Drive contents or semantic completeness.\n\nResolve the live selected GCFPE release only from its release register and selected catalog. The selected alias `references/gcfpe-current-direct-handoff-contract.json` must match that live binding. During candidate staging, validate the exact versioned successor through the paired `--gcfpe-contract` and `--gcfpe-candidate-root` arguments; a candidate pass never changes or proves production selection. The `GCFPE-20260914.1 / 091426.1` profile pins and re-reads a byte-identical candidate contract and 55-member frozen graph whose sole addition is PR-35 while the selected alias remains `GCFPE-20260913.1 / 091326.2 / 54` until promotion.\n\nValidate these active GCFPE v2 contracts:\n\n- Direct continuation has no model/strength assessment, Analyzer, reasoning recommendation, eligibility/suitability/account check, capability appraisal, or configuration-based route or gate.\n- Every actual nonterminal result has exactly one complete fenced `text` `NEXT_PROMPT_HANDOFF` containing the fully pasteable selected receiver prompt, not metadata, a menu, blank form, opaque ID, unlinked filename, `above`, or reconstruction instruction. Terminal results have no continuation block.\n- Off-repository runtime artifacts are machine-readable Markdown in `Glow / Ephemeral Planning Files`, are uploaded and completely read back, and travel by direct Drive link.\n- PR-30 and PR-35 are two phases of one GCF-17 PR work unit. The exact ordered ten-field GCF-17 continuity list is: `WORK_UNIT_ID`; original Product Owner Proceed; dedicated PR-development session; workspace/worktree; branch; pull request; PR instruction; detailed PR plan; primary skill authority; continuous recovery/artifact lineage. Both phases share exactly one value for every field. PR-35 adds zero roles, sessions, approvals, gates, Proceeds, work units, R1 rows, merge authority, work vehicles, or cross-session routes. `glow-hde-devops` remains support-only; `glow-merged-change-attribution-lock` remains read-only landed-attribution evidence for PR-40.\n- PR-30 owns recovery, implementation, local tests, coherent commits, deliberate initial publication, and its same-session PR-35 handoff. PR-35 owns review retrieval/correction, local retesting, coherent corrective publication, CI economy, current-head verification, and genuine merge readiness. Both recover the most advanced consistent matching vehicle before creating anything.\n- The exact PR-30 results are `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED`, `RESCOPE_PENDING`, `RECOVERY_PENDING`, and `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`. The exact PR-35 results are `MERGE_PENDING`, `RESCOPE_PENDING`, `RECOVERY_PENDING`, `REMOTE_EVIDENCE_PENDING`, and `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`. A compact `PR_REMOTE_ACTION_LEDGER` and durable checkpoints cover publication, coherent pushes, remote-only waits, interruptions, and rescope boundaries.\n- Local testing precedes meaningful commits and pushes. Complete tested authorized work is not stranded without a real blocker. Known actionable findings precede paid CI; stale CI is not a gate; unsupported cancellation and unauthorized skip-CI are rejected. `MERGE_PENDING` requires resolved current-head reviews/threads, passing required current-head CI or exact waiver, verified remote head, mergeability, and no unresolved material boundary.\n- Every PFCanon authority resolves only through `Glow / Core Docs / PFCanon` to one current controlled Markdown direct child. Google Doc, DOC, and DOCX records are metadata-only ignored candidates: no validator or fixture may open, extract, compare, or use their content. Native-only evidence yields `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`; no equivalence fallback exists.\n- Approved Plans, Guides, and Specifications remain immutable bases. The exact evaluated writer set is CF-C-20, CF-C-40, CF-E-20, CF-E-40, IA-10, IA-20, IA-40, PR-10, PR-20, QA-20, QA-50, QA-60, QA-80, and ESC-30. Each resolves current PF10 Markdown, applicable direct-link overlays, `AUTHORING_CONTEXT`, immutable-base distinction, and PF10 lineage.\n- The exact semantic addendum producers remain CF-C-30, CF-E-30, IA-30, QA-70, RS-20, and ESC-40. One qualifying approval creates exactly one standalone `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM` with `READY_FOR_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `NON_CANONICAL_PENDING_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `drain_owner: Nathan / Product Owner`, the complete required schema, and a stable anchor. Nonqualifying outcomes create none. Producers never edit/number PF10 or claim adoption.\n- Post-drain results are exhaustively `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_REQUIRED`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_MISMATCH`, or `DRAIN_VERIFIED`. Pre-drain PF10 is `PRE_DRAIN_BASELINE_EVIDENCE`; the receiver independently resolves current controlled Markdown and verifies the exact anchor, normalized delta, and absence of a later conflicting overlay. A source failure never proves that Nathan did not drain.\n- `PR_RETURN_PHASE` is exactly `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION`, `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION`, or `PR-35`. Prepublication has no open PR and returns directly to PR-30 after verified drain; the two published phases use RS-40 and preserve the same open PR. Reject/`IN_SCOPE_REPAIR` returns to the existing owner; `REVISION_REQUIRED` uses RS-30 and the same author/RS-20 owner; `SPECIFICATION_CHANGE_REQUIRED` is terminal to Nathan. No restart, base rewrite, duplicate Proceed, accepted-final replay, or automatic PR-50 route is lawful.\n- PR-50 has exactly one manual boundary: Nathan / Product Owner invokes `Abort PR and Escalate` for an exact PR. It has zero prompt-, agent-, skill-, hub-, or automation-originated inbound edges. Other actors return evidence to Nathan without invoking PR-50.\n- PR merges are Nathan / Product Owner manual actions. An agent never merges or enables automatic merge. PR-35 `MERGE_PENDING` is historical pre-merge evidence; Nathan's later invocation asserts the manual merge; PR-40 independently verifies actual merged state and landed lineage read-only.\n- Alpha remains `ALPHA_STOPPED_PENDING_CHANGE_FLOW_REFACTOR`, PR03 remains `ACCEPTED_FINAL`, PR04 is not started, the next intended stage is PR-10, the handoff is `NOT_YET_APPROVED`, and Nathan is the sole resume authority. Completion prepares and reads back the fresh PR04 PR-10 handoff but does not execute it or resume Alpha.\n\nThe versioned 33-case section-13 fixture suite must attribute every negative case to its exact expected rule and independently exercise combined negative variants. Static declarations and fixtures do not prove live Notion selection, Drive readback, repository state, archival, or worker behavior; inspect those separately.\n\nFor a selected schema-4 production readback, every prompt body must use the neutral lifecycle header `Selection status: REGISTER_CONTROLLED`, one generic `Notion URL: <direct URL>` binding, and the exact sentence `Selection authority: The GCFPE Membership and Release Register exclusively determines selected lifecycle; this page header makes no independent selection claim.` The contract alias, not the prompt header, carries `SELECTED_PRODUCTION`; the live register remains the sole authority for that alias claim. Production validation rejects candidate URL labels, stale member lifecycles, retained `candidate_page_binding` fields, and stale selection status in any designated prompt reference.\n\nThis validator remains read-only. It does not repair prompts, mutate skills, publish/archive pages, run workers, drain PF10, merge, resume Alpha, or activate automation.\n\n## Entry points\n\nFor the approved Technical Writing Alpha follow-up, the TW specialization revision is 1.1.6 (including Nathan's PF04 incident-name correction). Its selected-catalog profile requires pre-creation and pre-Apply assessments, no-redlines terminal handling and source-file header provenance. The structural assertion records those named contracts; scoped semantic/forward cases still establish their meaning. Only this compatibility assertion changes. Preserve the Primary core and immutable R1 oracle/runtime map; do not apply TW's profile to GCFPE or unrelated legacy consumers.\n\nRun the complete installed suite:\n\n~~~bash\npython3 scripts/validate_flowmaster.py\n~~~\n\nTreat warnings and advisories as blockers when validating an R4 candidate:\n\n~~~bash\npython3 scripts/validate_flowmaster.py --strict-warnings\n~~~\n\nRun one or more exact installed names:\n\n~~~bash\npython3 scripts/validate_flowmaster.py --target change-flow --target flowmaster-validate\n~~~\n\nRun isolated Change fixtures:\n\n~~~bash\npython3 scripts/run_change_flow_fixtures.py\n~~~\n\nUse SKILLS_ROOT or --skills-root only for an exact fresh checkout or isolated test root. Do not point the validator at a mixture of installed and candidate files.\n\nFor a bounded candidate-overlay audit of the installed skill tree, pass its exact versioned contract and the complete candidate snapshot root together. The suite always runs the selected-alias regression first, then additionally validates the candidate contract, frozen graph, recursively scanned 55-member prompt corpus, and all section-13 fixtures. These read-only options leave the selected alias untouched and prove candidate consistency only; the selected Notion register and post-promotion readback remain separate requirements.\n\n~~~bash\npython3 scripts/validate_flowmaster.py --strict-warnings \\\n  --gcfpe-contract /exact/change-flow-skill/references/gcfpe-20260914.1-091426.1-direct-handoff-contract.json \\\n  --gcfpe-candidate-root /exact/GCFPE-20260914.1-candidate-snapshot\n~~~\n\nRun the versioned GCFPE validator directly with the explicit candidate and required recursively scanned prompt corpus for a complete candidate pass:\n\n~~~bash\npython3 scripts/validate_gcfpe_20260914.py /exact/change-flow-skill \\\n  --contract /exact/change-flow-skill/references/gcfpe-20260914.1-091426.1-direct-handoff-contract.json \\\n  --candidate-root /exact/GCFPE-20260914.1-candidate-snapshot \\\n  --prompt-dir /exact/GCFPE-20260914.1-candidate-snapshot/prompts\npython3 scripts/run_gcfpe_20260914_fixtures.py /exact/change-flow-skill \\\n  --contract /exact/change-flow-skill/references/gcfpe-20260914.1-091426.1-direct-handoff-contract.json\n~~~\n\n## Authority boundary\n\nThe Change oracle is the bundled file references/glow-hde-canonical-change-flow-r1.json. It pins:\n\n- projection SHA-256 52807e58c4a4659e6c1fc822749f6e50253ad7b01846c833f727ee266ca71d5e;\n- the immutable R1 source and Contract Matrix Library identities;\n- Contract Matrix SHA-256 faa7fb7d77066cc491bde957b6d2f7d3255c74833936e3952f97873da27ea2f1;\n- frozen R1 snapshot SHA-256 5a6d89ed366f467ee75a5c71d23bf1a613dc79bb4d56791e812e20d53e53db67;\n- 26 core rows plus 20 material branch, loop, and utility rows;\n- exact row actors, sessions, approval and failure contracts;\n- normalized producer, consumer, artifact, and transition interfaces; and\n- active prohibited-pattern rules.\n\nThe validator must load that oracle independently and compare the specialization's declared mapping to it. It must never derive expected behavior from the current change-flow prose or bless the current skill merely because it is syntactically valid.\n\nThe bundled projection is maintenance evidence, not a new authority. Any future oracle update requires a separately authorized repair that proves a complete projection against the immutable or successor canonical source.\n\n## Suite structure checks\n\nFor every active Flowmaster package, verify:\n\n- one exact frontmatter name and a discriminating description;\n- supported frontmatter keys only;\n- agents/openai.yaml with display name, short description, default prompt, and exact skill invocation;\n- required scripts and references;\n- no unfinished placeholders;\n- dynamic discovery of every marked specialization;\n- exactly one Primary core marker pair and one parseable semantic core revision;\n- raw-byte equality of the inclusive core block with flowmaster-primary;\n- exactly one specialization marker pair and one specialization revision;\n- no specialization-only term in the generic core;\n- no active legacy overlap;\n- domain self-containment and required domain contracts; and\n- successful bundled self-tests.\n\nDo not normalize newlines before core comparison. A drifted core fails and identifies flowmaster-propagate as the repair route; validation itself performs no propagation.\n\n## Complete Change checks\n\nThe Change validator must emit 46/46 only when all of these pass:\n\n1. The exact oracle profile, matrix hash, and frozen snapshot identity are declared.\n2. All 46 row IDs occur exactly once in oracle order: 26 core and 20 material rows.\n3. Every row's actor, continuing-session contract, consumed artifacts, produced artifacts, next destinations, approval contract, failure contract, and full-source row digest equal the pinned oracle.\n4. Every destination is another declared row or an allowed special destination.\n5. Every required input is produced by one canonical upstream row or explicitly classified as an external governed input.\n6. Every output has at least one consumer or an explicit terminal disposition.\n7. No duplicate authoritative producer, bypass, dead end, orphan output, or unproducible required input remains.\n8. Both Epic and CRD start at Product Owner class selection, remain class-specific through formation, and converge only at GCF-08.\n9. The same Thoth session owns every Specification decision and exact-redline re-review; the same Isis session owns creation and replacement lineage.\n10. GCF-08 continues mandatorily through GCF-09 and GCF-10; the Implementation Audit precedes the change-wide Implementation Plan in one dedicated whole-change IA session.\n11. Isis owns the exact Plan review boundary; the same IA owns exact-redline replacement.\n12. One dedicated PR session plans and implements one work unit. Product Owner implementation authorization is only the PR Implementation Proceed invocation. The separately stated PR-40 post-merge verification interpretation supplies no agent execution authority, merge authority, or additional approval gate.\n13. No approval binding artifact or second binding act exists.\n14. Ops and QA execution belong to authorized DevOps/environment operators. Kronos creates QA artifacts and reviews evidence but executes neither lane.\n15. Rescope, lineage, documentation-before-QA, readiness, PF23, triage, manual PF10, QA planning/revision/execution, bounded rerun, escalation/discovery/remediation/re-entry, final QA Report plus RCA, Isis closure, memo/board drainage, ADR, and PF09 maintenance all close.\n16. No CRD-only, Epic-only, batch-only, skill-only, or partial-flow mode is active.\n17. Obsolete terms are rejected only when active. The validator permits them inside the marked explicit-prohibition block, in the pinned migration metadata, or in negative fixtures.\n\n## Findings contract\n\nEvery finding is machine-readable and contains:\n\n- rule_id: stable identifier;\n- subject: exact skill, path, row, or fixture;\n- severity: ERROR, WARNING, ADVISORY, or INFO;\n- evidence: deterministic path/row/detail fields;\n- disposition: BLOCK, REVIEW, or ALLOW.\n\nA pass has zero ERROR, WARNING, or ADVISORY findings. INFO findings may describe successful coverage and identities but do not waive any check.\n\nRepresentative stable rule families:\n\n- FMV-STRUCT-* — package, frontmatter, marker, file, or self-containment defect;\n- FMV-CORE-* — Primary revision, genericity, or byte-identity defect;\n- FMV-GCF-AUTH-* — pinned authority mismatch;\n- FMV-GCF-COVERAGE-* — missing row or partial-mode defect;\n- FMV-GCF-ROW-* — actor/session/interface mismatch;\n- FMV-GCF-EDGE-* — bypass or dead end;\n- FMV-GCF-PRODUCER-* — duplicate producer;\n- FMV-GCF-INPUT-* — unproducible input;\n- FMV-GCF-OUTPUT-* — orphan output;\n- FMV-GCF-ORDER-* — mandatory continuation or Audit-before-Plan defect;\n- FMV-GCF-SESSION-* — continuing-session drift;\n- FMV-GCF-APPROVAL-* — approval-owner or invented-binding defect;\n- FMV-GCF-LINEAGE-* — authorship or lineage drift;\n- FMV-GCF-ROLE-* — Ops or QA execution drift;\n- FMV-GCF-QA-* — QA/RCA/closure defect;\n- FMV-GCF-OBSOLETE-* — prohibited active architecture;\n- FMV-FIXTURE-* — fixture schema or expectation failure.\n\n## Fixture requirements\n\nThe isolated suite must pass positive Epic and CRD happy paths and positive probes for:\n\n- Specification denial, exact redline, replacement lineage, and same-Thoth return;\n- mandatory whole-change IA continuation;\n- Audit before change-wide Plan;\n- Isis review;\n- per-PR Plan and Proceed approval semantics;\n- rescope;\n- escalation plus discovery;\n- Historical baseline QA readiness/manual PF23/PF10, plus separate effective integrated QA-10 audit/comparison/triage/readiness → QA-20 Guide → Kronos intake. Informational pending PF publication is not a progression gate; actual governing scope decisions remain. Check early, later QA and closure remediation with Thoth proposal, conditional complete IA Plan preparation, one explicit Isis review, exact-author denial and actual-origin return. Final QA Report/RCA, closure and post-closure controls remain.\n\nIt must make every negative fixture fail for its expected stable rule:\n\n- obsolete Plan/IA-Plan/manual-hold architecture;\n- a held approved-Specification endpoint;\n- Plan before Audit;\n- different-Thoth return;\n- caller-invented lineage;\n- separate approval binding;\n- CRD-only or partial activation;\n- Kronos Ops execution;\n- Kronos QA execution;\n- missing RCA;\n- duplicate producer;\n- unproducible input;\n- orphan output; and\n- bypass/dead end.\n\nFixtures may not call live workflow components, run a runtime Change Flow, or mutate production state.\n\n## Result contract\n\nThe JSON result includes validator revision, authority identity, Primary revision and raw-byte SHA-256, per-skill status, complete findings, Change coverage, fixture totals, warning/advisory totals, and suite_ok.\n\nUse only these suite verdicts:\n\n- FLOWMASTER_SUITE_PASS\n- FLOWMASTER_SUITE_FAIL\n- FLOWMASTER_VALIDATION_FATAL\n\nA successful R4 validation requires FLOWMASTER_SUITE_PASS, 46/46 Change rows, all positive and negative fixtures behaving as expected, and zero blocker, error, warning, or advisory.\n\nIf Primary changed, validation alone is not propagation proof. Require exact per-specialization propagation receipts before a suite pass. If Primary did not change, record the negative decision and prove all embedded cores remained byte-identical.\n\n## GCFPE direct-handoff profile validation\n\nDuring candidate staging, the suite validates the selected 54-member `GCFPE-20260913.1 / 091326.2` alias and its predecessor fixtures first. When both explicit candidate arguments are supplied, it additionally validates `GCFPE-20260914.1 / 091426.1 / 55`, its recursively loaded corpus, its byte-pinned bundled contract and frozen graph, and all 33 section-13 fixtures. Candidate inputs never replace, redirect, or relax selected-alias validation, and the candidate validator proves the predecessor alias remains selected during staging. After promotion, the selected alias must resolve as the 55-member schema-4 production contract; the same release-aware validator and successor fixtures then validate that selected binding against the pinned semantic bundle.\n\nThe successor validator checks exact membership and Notion bindings, state/edge closure, PR-30/PR-35 continuity, result vocabularies, action ledger/checkpoints, current-head readiness, PF10 cardinality/schema/drain states, the 14-member writer set, phase-aware rescope, manual abort/merge boundaries, complete handoffs, Markdown-only PFCanon behavior, Alpha hold, protected Primary/R1 identity, and prohibited routing. The fixture report separates 33 required fixture IDs, independent variants, and exact contract-mutation rule attribution.\n\nHistorical validators and fixtures for prior integrated, final-scan, assessment-middleware, Epic-alpha, and Epic-reengineering layers remain provenance only. The active runner must not execute them as current GCFPE acceptance gates. Immutable R1 baseline checks and the ordinary Change Flow fixture suite remain active.\n\nFor a live release postflight, separately inspect all complete selected prompt bodies and their Notion readback, selected catalog/register/hubs, metaprompt, operating procedure, active skills, graph destinations, archive state, and Drive artifacts. Deterministic declarations are not runtime proof.\n\nThe final verdict is PASS only when every required current contract and live release check is satisfied with no unresolved mandatory defect. Otherwise return FAIL or INDETERMINATE with the exact missing evidence and smallest permitted recovery.\n\n## Bounded rescope receiver compatibility\n\nRS-10 remains optional proposal support. PR-30 or PR-35 produces the formal `RESCOPE_REQUEST`; the same whole-change IA decides through RS-20. RS-30 preserves the request/proposal type, author, and decision owner. A verified `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION` approval resumes PR-30 directly without manufacturing an open PR or RS-40 eligibility. A verified `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION` or `PR-35` approval uses RS-40 and resumes the recorded phase in the same session/worktree/branch/open PR under the original Proceed. Native remediation returns directly to its recorded delivery owner, including PR-30 or PR-35, and never masquerades as RS-20 approval. Missing source, owner, authority, or drain evidence returns the exact safe terminal/recovery result without invoking PR-50 or closing the change.\n",

    "57971dcd64b426cfc952a653ce10492a5d6840659f408a5e8fa5621444fb1042": "---\nname: change-flow\ndescription: Execute, resume, audit, or improve the self-contained complete Glow Canonical Change Flow for one Product Owner-classified Epic or CRD across Specification, mandatory whole-change Implementation Audit and Plan, PR and Ops work, QA, escalation, Isis closure, and post-closure drainage. Use when the user invokes Change Flow, supplies its run inputs, or asks for a Change Flow audit or RCA. Do not use for partial-flow activation, direct implementation outside the canonical gates, prompt repair, governance activation, or Technical Writing Flow.\n---\n\n# Change Flow\n\nCHANGE_FLOW_SPECIALIZATION_REVISION: 3.2.4\n\nR1_CONTRACT_PROFILE: GLOW_HDE_CANONICAL_CHANGE_FLOW_R1_20260831_1\n\nR1_CONTRACT_MATRIX_SHA256: faa7fb7d77066cc491bde957b6d2f7d3255c74833936e3952f97873da27ea2f1\n\nR1_ROW_COVERAGE: 46/46\n\nPRIMARY_CHANGE_REQUIRED = false\n\nPROMPT_REPAIR_PLAN_STATUS = RESOLVE_CURRENT_REGISTER\n\nAUTOMATION_STATUS = NOT_ACTIVATED\n\nInvoke this skill by itself. It embeds the complete Flowmaster Primary core and does not require flowmaster-primary, a workflow attachment, or another execution metaprompt at runtime.\n\nThe manual prompt set has recorded static completion; runtime behavior remains unproven and GCFPE establishment remains alpha. Read the current `GCFPE — Alpha Establishment and Change Management Checklist` at its verified Notion directory and `Glow HDE Prompt Flow Index` at its verified Notion directory above for current lifecycle evidence. This maintenance update does not activate automated orchestration. Execution requests still stop with STOP_RECOVERY_HOLD_ACTIVE until the Product Owner explicitly releases that automation hold with the required complete component evidence. A prompt publication, checklist completion, manual CRD test, or repaired skill alone is not an automation activation event.\n\n<!-- FLOWMASTER_CORE_BEGIN -->\n## Flowmaster core contract\n\n`FLOWMASTER_CORE_REVISION: 1.0.2`\n\n### Operating posture\n\n- Act as the controller and evidence keeper, not as a substitute for the worker sessions being orchestrated.\n- Execute external sends, writes, session creation, or configuration only when the user has asked to run or continue the flow and the governing specialization authorizes that action.\n- For an explanation, review, audit, RCA, design, or plan, remain read-only.\n- Never infer that permission for one flow, session, source, or mutation authorizes another.\n- Treat an unavailable capability, authentication gate, permission denial, CAPTCHA, ambiguous identity, or authority conflict as a stop condition. Request only the smallest necessary operator action.\n- Do not claim downstream completion from dispatch, startup, elapsed time, an artifact name, or an unverified link.\n\n### External confirmation checkpoints\n\nWorkflow authorization and a control-layer action-time confirmation are separate. A required checkpoint does not mean the operator's prior instruction was missing, unclear, or invalid.\n\n- Determine from the active control layer whether the exact imminent action requires a checkpoint. Do not assume that every browser or external action always requires one.\n- Prepare the transaction as far as the active policy permits, then request confirmation at the latest permitted moment. State that the prior instruction remains valid and identify the exact operation, destination, payload, and asset scope.\n- Bind a granted checkpoint to a confirmation action key containing the action key, target or destination, payload identity or hash, asset identities, and composer checksum. Any material change invalidates the grant; unchanged re-verification does not require another checkpoint.\n- Group checkpoints only when the active control layer permits it and every grouped action is imminent and fully specified. Never preconfirm an unknown future response, payload, destination, or generated relay turn.\n- Confirmation is not a send attempt. A request, grant, decline, or invalidation must not set `SEND_ATTEMPTED`, create a dispatch lock, or be counted as a send.\n- After a valid grant, reverify the exact destination and composer checksum, attempt the action exactly once, and only then apply the one-way send lock.\n\n### Authority and complete sources\n\nApply authority in this order unless the specialization establishes a stricter order:\n\n1. Current system instructions and the operator's latest explicit instruction for this run.\n2. The active self-contained specialization or, for a direct generic run, this skill.\n3. The validated run manifest and scoped operator note.\n4. The exact stage prompt, limited to its declared task.\n5. The current authoritative source or artifact designated for that stage.\n6. Directly observed session history and external state.\n7. The run ledger as a checkpoint only, never as independent proof.\n\nRead every decisive prompt, source, turn, and artifact as the complete required unit. A preview, snippet, search hit, summary, filename, ellipsis, cutoff, or content ending mid-unit is incomplete. Stop relying on incomplete retrieval, recover within the bounded-recovery rule, and redo dependent analysis after recovery. Retrieval failure is not evidence that content is absent.\n\nPin mutable stage prompts at first use by exact identity and complete content. If the same identity later resolves to materially different content and the pinned copy is unavailable, stop under prompt drift rather than silently switching versions.\n\n### Run mode and identity\n\nUse exactly one run mode:\n\n- `FRESH`: create a new ledger; do not retrieve prior Flowmaster conversations, broad personal context, or an older run ledger. Inspect existing worker-session history only for current operational facts needed for identity, duplicate prevention, capability state, and active work.\n- `RESUME`: recover only the exact retained ledger and exact session identities for the named run. Reconcile them against live sources before any new action. Do not perform broad historical reconstruction.\n\nDefault to `FRESH` only when the specialization permits a default; otherwise require the field. Derive a stable run identity from the supplied flow name or explicit run key. Never merge two runs because their names or targets resemble one another.\n\n### Separated state model\n\nTrack these layers independently for every managed session or target:\n\n- controller health;\n- tab ownership and visibility;\n- session identity and configuration;\n- composer state;\n- send state;\n- assistant-turn state;\n- source or artifact validation state;\n- task outcome; and\n- tab-close lease.\n\nDo not collapse controller failure into task failure, session invisibility into session absence, an empty text field into an empty composer, a send timeout into a failed send, or assistant startup into task completion.\n\nUse a one-way stage state machine:\n\n1. `SESSION_UNRESOLVED`\n2. `SESSION_VISIBLE_IDLE`\n3. `COMPOSER_READY`\n4. `SEND_ATTEMPTED`\n5. `DELIVERY_UNKNOWN_OR_RECONCILING`\n6. `DELIVERY_RECONCILED`\n7. `TURN_NOT_REQUIRED` only when the specialization explicitly declares a no-response endpoint, otherwise `TURN_UNKNOWN_OR_RUNNING`\n8. `TURN_TERMINAL` when a response is required\n9. `RESULT_VALIDATED` or `RESULT_BLOCKED`\n\nAfter `SEND_ATTEMPTED`, no transition returns to composition unless positive read-only evidence proves that no message was sent and the corrected-attempt rule permits one retry.\n\nBefore sending, pin the exact destination-history or external-state baseline needed to distinguish this action from any pre-existing identical effect. After the send attempt, establish `DELIVERY_RECONCILED` only from one new action-bound effect after that baseline. Unless the specialization explicitly declares that no assistant response is required, continue through the assistant-turn states. A no-response endpoint validates transport or delivery only and must never imply assistant startup, task acceptance, or downstream work completion.\n\n### Durable ledger and action identity\n\nMaintain compact current-run state. Use a durable ledger when the flow has multiple targets, spans multiple sessions or stages, resumes, encounters an ambiguous action or controller reset, or otherwise risks losing exact state.\n\nRecord only what is needed to resume safely:\n\n- run and manifest identity;\n- pinned prompt identities and content hashes;\n- authoritative source identities and versions;\n- session titles, stable session identifiers, and tab mappings;\n- configuration and session-scoped capability states;\n- stage, target, cycle, and dependency states;\n- composer checksum and dispatch identity;\n- pre-action destination baseline, delivery state, and exact new delivery-evidence identity;\n- response requirement and assistant-turn state;\n- confirmation requirement, confirmation action key, and outcome when applicable;\n- send, turn, validation, terminal, recovery, and cleanup states;\n- last confirmed action and next permitted action.\n\nDo not copy complete prompts, source documents, output artifacts, credentials, signed URLs, or unsupported conclusions into the ledger. Write a transition only after the corresponding state is directly verified.\n\nBefore any external send or write, form an action key from the run, stage, target or cycle, session, prompt identity, input identities and versions, and intended operation. Check both the ledger and live destination. If the action or its effect is already confirmed, do not repeat it.\n\n### Browser, tab, and session ownership\n\n- Inventory tabs before browser work without opening or inspecting the executing Flowmaster session.\n- Leave every pre-existing tab untouched. Never refresh, repurpose, navigate away from, or close a tab the flow did not open.\n- Use exactly one flow-owned tab per managed ChatGPT session and retain an exact tab-to-session mapping.\n- Verify the active site, project or workspace, exact session title, and stable session identity immediately before every state-changing action.\n- Never browser-open, inspect, configure, message, or verify the current executing Flowmaster session.\n- Do not assume a session-creation API exists. Use only currently available, authorized ChatGPT controls and verify the created session's type, project placement, title, and stable identity before configuration or work.\n- Prefer an existing authoritative session when the specialization permits it. Never create a replacement to escape controller-wide failure, an unresolved session set, or an ambiguous current-run send.\n\nSet `TAB_CLOSE_ALLOWED = false` whenever an active or possibly active turn still requires observation. Release the lease only after the specialization's required terminal result is visible, retrieved completely, checked, and checkpointed. Startup, elapsed time, controller unreadability, switching targets, or a stopped animation does not release it.\n\nClose each flow-owned tab when its required work is terminal and checked. Before final reporting or a flow-wide stop, attempt cleanup through every still-healthy route and report any tab whose closure could not be verified.\n\n### Control hierarchy\n\nUse the safest semantic control available:\n\n1. direct connector or structured control;\n2. exact URL or retained session identity;\n3. keyboard or inline command such as `/model` or an actual `@` picker selection;\n4. a semantic click when no safer route exists, including `Show in text field` or selecting an exact autocomplete result;\n5. coordinate-based interaction only when unavoidable and directly verifiable.\n\nVerify the resulting state. Do not press Enter to test focus or accept a suggestion unless the suggestion menu is visibly focused, because Enter may submit the composer.\n\nWhen a target-session task requires a ChatGPT skill, select the exact installed skill through the target composer's real `@` picker and verify the resulting skill chip before sending. Plain copied text that spells `@skill-name` is not sufficient evidence of activation. A skill active in the controlling session does not automatically carry into another session.\n\n### Composer transaction\n\nTreat the composer as one transaction across all visible surfaces: text field, prompt or file tiles, variable values, actual skill or connector chips, attachments or Library references, and session history.\n\nFor a long or stored prompt:\n\n1. Paste or insert the complete prompt exactly once.\n2. If ChatGPT converts it to a tile, use `Show in text field` once when available.\n3. Populate only declared variables with exact values.\n4. Select every required actual skill, connector, or Library reference through its supported picker.\n5. Verify all surfaces together: one prompt copy, no unresolved required placeholder, exact values, exact references, exact chips, correct target session, and no equivalent message already in history.\n6. Record a compact composer checksum containing the target, session, prompt identity, input identities, selected skills or connectors, and model/reasoning state.\n7. Send once.\n\nIf `Show in text field` is unavailable, retain the single tile and add one short ordinary-message block containing only declared overrides:\n\n```text\nAUTHORITATIVE VARIABLE OVERRIDES FOR THE ATTACHED PROMPT\n<VARIABLE> = <exact value>\n\nTreat these values as replacing the corresponding unresolved variables in the attached prompt. Do not infer or substitute other values.\n```\n\nNever paste a second prompt copy merely because the text field appears empty. Never add undeclared substantive instructions through the override block.\n\n### One-way send lock\n\nImmediately before sending, verify that the session is idle, the composer checksum is correct, no equivalent dispatch exists, the stage dependency is satisfied, and any required action-time confirmation remains valid for the unchanged transaction.\n\nImmediately when the final send action is attempted:\n\n1. set `SEND_ATTEMPTED`;\n2. set the composer and session to write-locked;\n3. record the action key and time;\n4. leave the session immediately; and\n5. continue to the next independent ready item or begin the read-only monitoring cycle.\n\nDo not linger in the same composer to prove startup. A timeout, blank text field, missing immediate assistant text, redirect, browser reset, or slow response is never evidence that the send failed and never authorizes another paste, send, interrupt, replacement session, or correction message.\n\nPermit at most one corrected send, through a materially different route, only after positive read-only evidence proves all of the following:\n\n- no new action-bound matching user message or external effect exists after the exact pre-action baseline;\n- no assistant activity corresponds to the action;\n- the session is idle;\n- no staged prompt tile, composer content, or selected attachment or chip remains; and\n- the first send was not applied.\n\nIf any condition is unknown, preserve `SEND_STATE_UNKNOWN`, remain write-locked, and report a blocker.\n\n### Monitoring and scheduling\n\nAfter initial sends, reconcile delivery read-only, then use round-robin monitoring for every response that the specialization requires. A monitoring timeout limits only the observation operation, never model generation.\n\nAdvance independent work by readiness. Do not impose a batch-wide barrier when one target's next stage depends only on that target. Preserve source order for first dispatches, then process terminal results as they become ready.
