Transport and readback are not approval.\n8. GCF-08 — Thoth approval binds the exact current class-specific Specification and hands it to one whole-change IA session. The two class-specific formation lanes converge only here.\n\nAn approved Specification never terminates the flow and never authorizes implementation. It must continue directly to the exact selected IA-10 destination with the complete native package when the required IA session is available; unavailable mandatory continuation is a blocker, not a valid held endpoint.\n\n### Mandatory whole-change IA: GCF-09 through GCF-13\n\nIMPLEMENTATION_AUDIT_PRECEDES_CHANGE_WIDE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.\n\n- GCF-09 — The dedicated whole-change IA performs the evidence-grounded Implementation Audit from the exact approved Specification, current repository, and applicable canon. If the Specification is insufficient, return to the class-specific Isis/Thoth loop with preserved lineage.\n- GCF-10 — Only after the Audit, the same IA authors the one change-wide Implementation Plan. The Plan contains planned PR and Ops work units, dependencies, acceptance evidence, migration, and rollback; it performs no work.\n- GCF-11 — The continuing Isis session reviews that IA-authored Plan and either approves it or issues an exact redline. After approval that Plan is immutable for the in-flight change; an approved remediation delta is recorded by ESC-40 only as an explicit PF10 overlay against that exact base.\n- GCF-12 — The same IA applies Isis's exact redline to a complete replacement Plan, preserves Specification and Audit lineage, and returns it to Isis. Repeat GCF-11 and GCF-12 until Isis approves.\n- GCF-13 — The same IA decomposes only the approved Plan into one PR Instruction per planned PR work unit and one bounded Ops Task per planned Ops work unit, with an exact dependency and lineage map.\n- GCF-13.PR and GCF-13.OPS — Each branch remains inside its approved work-unit scope. Task creation has no execution or approval effect.\n\nThere is no second IA planner, no independent approver role at this boundary, and no terminal state between Specification approval, Audit, Plan creation, and Isis review.\n\n### Combined Audit and Plan authoring\n\nIA-10 performs GCF-09 Implementation Audit and then GCF-10 whole-change Implementation Plan in one ordinary invocation in the dedicated IA session. QA-50 performs the independent Kronos QA Audit and QA Plan phases of GCF-21 in one ordinary invocation. Before any Plan, Guide, Specification, or permitted preapproval revision is authored, resolve the unique current PF10 Markdown plus every applicable active addendum and record their direct Drive links as `approved base + applicable PF10 overlays`. Preserve distinct complete Audit and Plan identities, mandatory audit-before-plan order, all source-native content, and existing concise supporting proofs. Neither author approves its own Plan. Success hands the complete native package directly to the exact selected IA-30 or QA-70 prompt. A preapproval denial returns through IA-40 or QA-80; a denial of an approved-base overlay returns to the exact overlay-proposal owner and never sends the approved base to a revision writer.\n\nIA-20 and QA-60 remain selected same-author plan-only continuations for a completed valid Audit, including interrupted and legacy work. They are not mandatory extra invocations. On interruption preserve finished phases and resume the first incomplete phase; a substantive source/scope blocker names the actual owner without fabricating approval. Historical logical rows and approvals remain; invocation consolidation adds no stage or permission.\n\n\n### PR, approval, lineage, rescope, Ops, and documentation\n\n- GCF-14 — Create one dedicated PR session for one planned PR work unit. That session validates the repository and creates the per-PR Implementation Plan. It performs no implementation before Proceed.\n- GCF-15 — The Product Owner manually runs PR Implementation Proceed in that same session against that exact plan.\n- GCF-16 — The invocation itself is the bounded runtime approval and execution authorization. There is no new approval artifact, token, object, signature, receipt, hash, ID, or second confirmation.\n- GCF-17 — The same dedicated PR session implements only that work unit across selected PR-30 and PR-35, validates it, and creates exactly one active branch and pull request. Any ordered lineage wording refers only to read-only historical landed-attribution evidence after manual merge, never multiple active work vehicles. PR-30 ends at coherent initial publication; PR-35 owns review correction and genuine current-head merge readiness. In-scope repair remains there. Out-of-scope work stops.\n- GCF-17.RESCOPE — PR-30 or PR-35 preserves the exact return phase and every vehicle/evidence field that actually exists and creates/reads back one complete formal `RESCOPE_REQUEST`. The same whole-change IA decides directly through selected RS-20. RS-10 remains separate proposal support, not a mandatory step. Rejection or `IN_SCOPE_REPAIR` returns evidence to the recorded existing owner with no base rewrite/addendum. Qualifying approval emits exactly one PF10 addendum; Nathan manually drains it; fresh verification then resumes prepublication PR-30 directly or uses selected RS-40 for an existing open PR, always under the original Proceed.\n- GCF-17.LINEAGE — PR-35's `MERGE_PENDING` is historical pre-merge evidence and supplies one conditional complete PR-40 invocation. Only after Nathan later asserts that the identified PR was manually merged may that invocation run. PR-40 independently verifies actual merged state and landed lineage read-only, then reviews the complete ordered lineage against the PR Instruction, authorized plan, Proceed invocation, and evidence. This is the single authoritative work-unit acceptance route; an attribution bundle is evidence only.\n- GCF-18 — An authorized DevOps/environment operator executes only the exact Ops Task and returns task-specific evidence.\n- GCF-18.RECEIPT — The same whole-change IA accepts or rejects the exact result. Evidence absence creates no `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM`; it returns through the native Ops repair, rescope, or escalation route with complete evidence.\n- GCF-19 — The final repository-documentation work unit uses the same ordinary PR plan, Proceed, implementation, and lineage route. Initial delivery must finish before QA readiness and does not perform PF canon drainage. Accepted PR/Ops/documentation remediation returns to its exact recorded QA or closure owner when readiness is unaffected; only initial completion or a materially affected readiness basis requires QA-10. Preserve all native acceptance/dependency predicates before that return.\n\nThe protected R1 projection that a material Plan change invalidates Proceed and restarts planning is historical for this selected GCFPE overlay. An approved in-flight base is immutable. A qualifying material delta uses its native decision, one PF10 addendum and the selected continuation; an active PR retains its original Proceed.\n\n### Integrated QA-10 audit, triage and readiness\n\n- One invocation of QA-10 in continuing Isis owns GCF-20.PF23 fresh audit and historical comparison, GCF-20.TRIAGE complete finding triage, then GCF-20 readiness. These are ordered phases of one operation, not independent dispatches. No prior READY or QA Plan is required. Preserve QA-10's complete approved Specification/Implementation Plan and accepted PR/Ops/documentation prerequisites.\n- Resolve the current audit/triage methods and applicable technical authority at runtime. Audit current implementation evidence first, then compare historical PF23 observations as new, persistent, resolved, changed/equivalent or unverifiable. Historical descriptions do not independently impose today's requirements. Reading code is not runtime QA success.\n- Save a complete Reality Audit Markdown and a separate `CHANGE_AUDIT_TRIAGE` Markdown containing substantive repository-wide findings. It is evidence for a later native decision and never a `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM`. State observed behavior, requirement/decision, impact, necessary action and material limits directly, without proposal framing or publication administration. Retain every finding's complete triage map, objective/owner/action/disposition, evidence, duplicate coverage and unresolved facts in the full Reality Audit. QA_READINESS links that accounting. Downstream actors read both substantive files; concise prose never substitutes for full evidence. When no new entry is warranted, still save CHANGE_AUDIT_TRIAGE with NO_ADDENDUM_NEEDED, the supported reason and complete Audit reference.\n- QA-10 has no PF10 addendum, live-ledger inspection, numbering, mutation, or publication authority. PF10 and PF23 publication remain Product Owner actions. Pending informational evidence does not block readiness, Guide or Kronos intake; any actual governing scope/approval prerequisite still applies.\n- GCF-20 decision: evidenced failure to achieve an applicable approved plan objective gives NOT_READY and an actionable early handoff to Thoth ESC-30, without an extra severity threshold. Cite the exact approved objective, expected outcome, observed shortfall and resolution evidence. Historical-only debt or future improvement does not independently block. Verification properly reserved for planned runtime QA remains an obligation, not a pre-QA failure or claimed achievement.\n- Missing decisive evidence remains an explicitly incomplete assessment with the exact evidence/recovery owner. Preserve completed phases; do not assert failure or READY. QA-10 checkpoints incomplete writes and inspects uncertain targets before retrying. Cancellation is incomplete work, not QA execution failure and consumes no QA retry.\n- READY_FOR_QA requires the whole readiness basis and routes the complete QA_READINESS, audit and triage to GCF-20.GUIDE / QA-20. QA-20 remains the Live QA Guide producer. One QA-50 invocation preserves Kronos's distinct QA Audit then QA Plan; Isis QA-70 approval and QA-80 same-Kronos revision remain separate.\n- Apply an explicitly required fresh QA-10 assessment only to the run and transition for which it was requested. Determine completion from the latest exact result; a fulfilled historical rerun instruction does not require every future cycle to rerun QA-10. Preserve earlier READY, cancelled work and accepted delivery as history.\n\n### QA selection\n\nSelection belongs to the Product Owner. Accept explicit QA step IDs/names, an unambiguous natural-language selection, a complete selection source, or ALL for every step in the exact approved QA Plan. Preserve an already supplied selection. If absent or ambiguous, show available IDs and short names and ask which tasks to run; never assume ALL or choose a ready subset. Author every selected valid task, including dependency-waiting members. Dependency readiness controls execution order, never assignment membership. Preserve blocked/defective entries explicitly. Reuse already-authored instructions as dependencies become ready; QA-110 returns them to QA-100, using QA-90 only for genuinely unissued selected instructions or the exact permitted retry. Never execute an unselected prerequisite or reset attempts.\n\n### QA execution and repeatable remediation\n\n- GCF-23 preserves Kronos task creation, authorized operator execution and Kronos evidence review for any finite caller-selected QA collection. GCF-23.RERUN still permits one bounded ordinary rerun only for correctable execution/evidence defects with the approved QA Plan valid. A second failure, behavior/scope/Plan change enters escalation; a remediation cycle cannot reset attempts.\n- GCF-23.ESC10 / ESC-10 remains Kronos's actual QA Escalation Report. Early QA-10 and closure findings enter ESC-30 from their own substantive decision evidence, without fabricated QA Plans, test attempts or Kronos decisions. Every entry preserves its actual stage, approved basis and originating return owner.\n- GCF-23.ESC20 and GCF-23.ESC30 / ESC-30 are Thoth's intake/discovery-selection and proposal phases within one substantive REMEDIATION_PLAN. The triage/discovery section is embedded in that record; no standalone Triage Receipt or separate triage prompt is required. Thoth establishes evidence-supported cause, dependencies, bounded work, owners, verification, risks and return point. Unproven explanations remain hypotheses.\n- GCF-23.ESC-DISCOVERY / ESC-25 accepts the actual REMEDIATION_PLAN_ID and an embedded DISCOVERY_TASK_ID, executes only that authorized bounded task and returns actual evidence to the same Thoth ESC-30. A historical TRIAGE_RECEIPT_ID is allowed only under an explicit in-flight transition. Repository discovery is read-only; a mutating task requires its separate actual authority.\n- When Thoth's proposal needs work decomposition or a material change to approved Implementation Plan content, represent that need as an explicit bounded overlay against the immutable base. Do not use IA-40 to create an in-flight replacement Plan. IA-40 remains only for a denied or pending preapproval Plan. The remedy records affected work and preserved content without fabricating a denial or rerunning the whole-change Audit.\n- GCF-23.ESC40 / ESC-40 is the same continuing Isis's substantive review. Its current artifact is REMEDIATION_REVIEW with exact APPROVE or DENY, reviewed proposal/version, immutable approved base, explicit overlay delta, application requirements and an embedded approved-work/pending-work return map. Preserve an actual legacy REMEDIATION_PLAN_REVIEW name only with verified equivalent semantics and lineage. It does not execute another role's work.\n- One ESC-40 record supplies the exact remediation decision only when it identifies the immutable approved IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_REF, explicit bounded delta and required evidence. On approval it emits exactly one PF10 addendum overlay. Affected delivery waits for verified manual drainage, then returns to the native delivery owner and originating verification owner. It does not approve or create a replacement Plan, and no duplicate IA-30 review of the same delta is added. Ordinary IA-30 initial/pending Plan review remains separate.\n- GCF-23.ESC50 is Thoth proposal revision mode inside ESC-30. Isis's exact proposal redline goes to Thoth. A denied pending preapproval IA Plan may use IA-40; an approved base never does. The corrected remedy/delta returns to the same Isis ESC-40. No self-approval or switch of reviewer is permitted.\n- GCF-23.REENTRY is the approved handoff function embedded in ESC-40, delivered to actual normal PR/Ops/documentation/QA owners. Native approvals, the original PO PR Proceed, code review, actual manual merge and IA acceptance remain. A material delta to an approved QA Plan is reviewed by QA-70 as an overlay; QA-80 revises only pending preapproval QA Plans. The controller never manufactures a destination approval from routing.\n- Ordinary corrections within an approved repair continue with the current authorized owner. Material changes to remedy, scope, approach, dependencies, risk or acceptance require Thoth's changed proposal, an explicit immutable-base overlay and Isis review of the actual changed work. There is no fixed remediation-cycle cap. Repeated failure without new evidence requires revised diagnosis/bounded discovery, not blind repetition.\n- A product objective or exclusion change uses the existing rescope proposal and PO decision plus a standalone Specification delta reviewed by the native Thoth prompt; approval emits one PF10 addendum without rewriting the approved Specification, and no affected continuation relies on the delta before verified manual drainage. The same drain-before-reliance rule governs material Implementation Plan and QA Plan deltas. Early findings may supply approved baseline and source evidence without a nonexistent PR Instruction. PR-originated rescope preserves its same-IA decision and one-addendum/manual-drain contract; after fresh verification, prepublication PR-30 resumes directly while an open-PR PR-30/PR-35 phase uses RS-40. Remediation cannot redefine success to erase a shortfall.\n- Accepted readiness repair returns to QA-10, which reassesses failed objectives and materially affected dependencies and refreshes affected audit/triage evidence. Later QA or closure findings return to the actual originating owner; revisit upstream readiness, Guide or QA Plan only where the repair affects their substantive basis. Preserve exact attempts, approved unaffected work and terminal evidence.\n\n### Final QA, closure, and drainage\n\n- GCF-24 — After the complete approved QA Plan reaches truthful terminal state, the same Kronos session creates both the final QA Report and an RCA, including for a clean pass.\n- GCF-25 — The continuing Isis session performs the terminal retrospective and decides close or not close. Isis alone owns closure. A QA PASS, Product Owner action, IA receipt, Kronos report, or memo cannot substitute.\n- GCF-26 — Only after a positive Isis decision, the Product Owner/operator manually drains any supported PF10 addenda still pending at closure and sends the closure memo to Thoth and Master Scrum; Master Scrum updates the development board. Earlier manual drainage that was a verified prerequisite for same-PR resumption remains preserved and is not repeated. This ceremony does not delay or create the already-made closure decision.\n- GCF-26.ADR — A supported ADR need is a separately authorized, optional post-closure maintenance task.\n- GCF-26.PF09 — Post-Epic PF09 maintenance is separately authorized, Epic-only, optional, and post-closure. It is never CRD input or a runtime terminal gate.\n\nA negative closure decision names the exact recovery owner and re-entry row. Optional maintenance failure does not silently reopen a closed change.\n\n### Final managed discovery: GCF-27 / CL-40\n\nAfter positive closure, CL-20 and every actually selected managed post-closure author/reviewer branch has completed or has its valid disposition, the same continuing Isis executes CL-40 for either class. Do not invent optional branches; an unfinished selected review/correction returns to its actual owner first. Pending manual publication, memo delivery and board administration do not block the scan: include their complete prepared content and preserve pending status. The controller's existing manual-ceremony reconciliation remains separate from scan eligibility and from already-decided closure.\n\nRead complete current PF10 and all its active parts, all seven PF09 phases, the complete existing CRD candidate list, and relevant available closure-linked development, delivery, QA, RCA, remedy, maintenance, board, incident, feedback and conversation evidence. Record actual coverage and inaccessible sources. Inspect relevant repository facts read-only when needed; preserve the tested historical baseline and do not run fresh QA or production operations.\n\nA PF09 candidate is missing recorded work that blocks successful application development; show the actual dependency and absence from current inventories. A CRD candidate is a functional/operational improvement or defect that does not block launch; support that effect rather than infer it from missing evidence. Either class may discover either kind. Check all phases, the existing list and known selected, in-flight, delivered or disposed work before adding anything. Do not duplicate an existing unfinished row, erase a deferral, fabricate an official CRD ID or classify unknown impact by guess. Report a contradiction of accepted closure evidence to its actual owner without silently changing historical closure.\n\nProduce a complete `CYCLE_GAP_SCAN` report with actual evidence/coverage, dispositions, supported PF09 gaps, required task/subtask content, actual CRD-list updates, and exact unresolved facts. This is gap evidence, not a `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM`, and CL-40 is not an addendum producer. Save the change-scoped report as efficient machine-readable Markdown in Drive `Glow / Ephemeral Planning Files`, fetch it back, and return its direct Drive link. Any later PF10/PF09 decision remains with the actual native reviewer and manual/governed owner. Gap entries state the missing obligation, blocking dependency, target phase/heading, full task/subtask substance and evidence needs; allocation fields remain explicitly unassigned when unknown. CL-40 invocation supplies only bounded in-place write authority to the existing Candidate-CRD-Items-List in Drive Glow / Ops / Assessments & Decisions. Preserve existing entries/decisions, re-read before writing, verify complete persistence, and inspect uncertain writes before retry. This is an explicit narrow exception for that ongoing noncanonical reference list, not registry, Canon, repository or board write authority. A repeated scan must not duplicate the same gap; no candidates means no list write.\n\nMissing decisive source coverage, undecidable impact or failed required persistence yields INCOMPLETE with preserved partial results and the smallest recovery owner/action. A supported COMPLETE result may contain no new candidates. CL-40 returns terminally to the Product Owner without selecting or launching another change. Candidate recording is not classification/approval for a new runtime change. The original change remains closed while the scan is incomplete; existing QA selection, attempts and automation hold are unchanged.\n\n\n### Failure and integrity rules\n\nStop at the first applicable row-specific failure in the pinned mapping. In addition, stop for:\n\n- STOP_RECOVERY_HOLD_ACTIVE\n- STOP_PARTIAL_ROUTE\n- STOP_CLASS_UNRESOLVED\n- STOP_COMPONENT_IDENTITY_OR_LIFECYCLE_INVALID\n- STOP_SESSION_IDENTITY_DRIFT\n- STOP_ARTIFACT_LINEAGE_DRIFT\n- STOP_APPROVAL_OWNER_DRIFT\n- STOP_DUPLICATE_AUTHORITATIVE_PRODUCER\n- STOP_REQUIRED_INPUT_UNPRODUCIBLE\n- STOP_ORPHAN_OUTPUT\n- STOP_BYPASS_OR_DEAD_END\n- STOP_CANONICAL_ROW_MISSING\n\nA blocker preserves all proven state and names the smallest owner/action needed. Never turn an open defect into an accepted deviation, bypass a manual control, or treat a receipt as substantive authority.\n\n### Explicitly prohibited and historical-only architecture\n\nThe text inside this marked section is negative control evidence. It must never be interpreted as an active instruction.\n\n<!-- FLOWMASTER_PROHIBITIONS_BEGIN -->\n\n- MANUAL_REVIEW_GATE_CONTRACT_REVISION is obsolete.\n- CHANGE_CONTEXT_LOCK_REVISION and the old dual-lane Change Context artifact are obsolete.\n- PLAN_V1_MANUAL_REVIEW_STATUS and IA_PLAN_V1_MANUAL_REVIEW_STATUS are prohibited substitute gates.\n- SPECIFICATION_APPROVED_IA_HELD is a superseded and prohibited operational state.\n- DEFERRED_QA_POLICY is prohibited because QA is mandatory in the complete flow.\n- Plan Author, Plan Reviewer, and IA Approver are obsolete role labels for the former architecture.\n- END CHANGE FLOW: IMPLEMENTATION READY is not a valid terminal result.\n- REQUIRE_APPROVAL_BINDING is prohibited; no separate approval binding exists.\n- ALLOW_PARTIAL_ACTIVATION is prohibited.\n- ALLOW_CRD_ONLY_OPERATION is prohibited.\n- KRONOS_EXECUTES_OPS is prohibited.\n- KRONOS_EXECUTES_QA is prohibited.\n\n<!-- FLOWMASTER_PROHIBITIONS_END -->\n\n### Immutable baseline and current effective projection\n\nBefore FRESH or RESUME execution, load the complete [bundled 46-row runtime map](references/glow-hde-canonical-change-flow-r1-runtime-map.json), SHA-256 `5574666e5975c104ccf13e77a13d94e0d16f37af37de7eb26d7e0f7b00f45b0e`, as immutable historical baseline evidence. Preserve its original rows and source digests.\n\nLoad [GCFPE current direct-handoff contract](references/gcfpe-current-direct-handoff-contract.json) as the current specialization overlay. Verify its selected release and member identities against the live Notion register and catalog before use; target metadata is not publication evidence. Apply its direct native handoff, Drive artifact, PR-development skill, PF10 addendum, and prohibited-routing rules without altering R1 actors, approvals, substantive destinations, or Product Owner boundaries.\n\nThe older integrated-readiness, final-scan, Alpha-feedback, assessment-middleware, Epic-alpha, and Epic-reengineering reference files remain immutable historical provenance. They are not executed as current routing overlays. Their retained byte identity supports audit history only and does not reintroduce retired prompts, middleware, selection advice, counts, or gates.\n\nStatic validation proves only declared contract consistency. It does not execute a worker session, resume Alpha, release automation, adopt PF10 content, or prove live behavior.\n\n### Completion report\n\nA successful final report identifies the run and class; every continuing session; the approved Specification and Thoth decision; the Implementation Audit; the Isis-approved change-wide Plan; every PR/Ops/documentation work unit; every Proceed invocation; recovered workspace and artifact lineage; purposeful commit/push checkpoints; review findings and dispositions; current-head CI and merge-readiness evidence; PR/Ops/documentation acceptance; integrated QA readiness; the approved QA Plan; QA evidence and escalation history; final QA Report and RCA; Isis closure; GCF-26 ceremony; optional maintenance disposition; every emitted `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM` and its manual-drain status; complete final CYCLE_GAP_SCAN and direct Drive link; ledger; and cleanup.\n\nReport no success while a mandatory row, branch, artifact, handoff, manual control, review finding, CI result, or exact consumer remains unresolved.\n\n## Maintaining this specialization\n\nTreat future workflow evidence, RCAs, and operator corrections as maintenance inputs, not runtime dependencies. Change-specific behavior stays between the specialization markers. Generic behavior stays only in the marked Primary block.\n\nAfter a future approved Primary update, use flowmaster-propagate and then flowmaster-validate. Increment CHANGE_FLOW_SPECIALIZATION_REVISION only for Change-specific behavior. Never edit the embedded core independently.\n\n<!-- FLOWMASTER_SPECIALIZATION_END -->\n",

    "617c8b6cc3799012996ec616912facfe48bd4768219ac139ad4ec94b9738aee3": "{\n  \"correction_id\": \"GCFPE-ALPHA1-FEEDBACK-20260907.1\",\n  \"predecessor_extension_id\": \"GCFPE-END-CYCLE-SCAN-20260907.1\",\n  \"predecessor_sha256\": \"495ffc9df997230c492e8d286758fe45a3b63fd741a62fe75246adef27a43ab8\",\n  \"selected_member_target\": 50,\n  \"effective_rows\": 48,\n  \"runtime_activation\": \"UNCHANGED_OWNER_CONTROLLED_HOLD\",\n  \"invocations\": {\n    \"IA-10\": {\n      \"ordered_rows\": [\n        \"GCF-09\",\n        \"GCF-10\"\n      ],\n      \"actor\": \"IA\",\n      \"outputs\": [\n        \"implementation_audit\",\n        \"implementation_plan\"\n      ],\n      \"review\": \"IA-30\",\n      \"continuation\": \"IA-20\"\n    },\n    \"QA-50\": {\n      \"ordered_rows\": [\n        \"GCF-21\"\n      ],\n      \"actor\": \"Kronos\",\n      \"outputs\": [\n        \"qa_audit\",\n        \"qa_plan\"\n      ],\n      \"review\": \"QA-70\",\n      \"continuation\": \"QA-60\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"output_replacements\": {\n    \"proposed_pf09_rows_if_supported\": \"pf10_build_notes_addenda_for_pf09_gaps\"\n  },\n  \"rules\": {\n    \"qa_selection\": \"EXPLICIT_PO_IDS_NAMES_SOURCE_OR_ALL_ASK_IF_MISSING\",\n    \"assignment\": \"ALL_SELECTED_VALID_TASKS_INCLUDING_WAITING_DEPENDENCIES\",\n    \"execution\": \"READY_SELECTED_ONLY_REUSE_EXISTING_TASKS\",\n    \"qa10_insert\": \"SUBSTANTIVE_REPOSITORY_WIDE_BUILD_NOTES_NO_PROPOSAL_ADMIN\",\n    \"qa10_full_accounting\": \"REALITY_AUDIT_WITH_QA_READINESS_LINK\",\n    \"cl40_pf09\": \"STANDALONE_PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDA_NOT_PROPOSALS\",\n    \"cl40_crd\": \"DIRECT_EXISTING_LIST_REREAD_VERIFY\",\n    \"pf_publication\": \"MANUAL_OWNER\",\n    \"audit_before_plan\": true,\n    \"independent_isis_review\": true,\n    \"no_retry_reset\": true,\n    \"status_reconciliation\": \"LATEST_EXACT_EVIDENCE_AND_EXPLICIT_PO_DECISION_SEPARATE_HISTORY\"\n  }\n}\n",

\"predecessor_correction_id\": \"GCFPE-STRENGTH-MIDDLEWARE-20260908.1\",\n  \"predecessor_sha256\": \"76b7cfc54cd2706f5d6e0b4ee7b734362055d2001242b63039121387a23313fb\",\n  \"preserved_layers\": [\n    {\n      \"file\": \"glow-hde-canonical-change-flow-r1-runtime-map.json\",\n      \"sha256\": \"5574666e5975c104ccf13e77a13d94e0d16f37af37de7eb26d7e0f7b00f45b0e\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"file\": \"integrated-qa-readiness-correction.json\",\n      \"sha256\": \"e94b0c8836210c934fe35fad69cf98cabe8688f86fb9c2346052c08383390949\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"file\":     "cd7acb3a7c72e08318606b91c3d3a011602c3cfb6cf553aadcbf382a06b6c5dc": "---\nname: glow-hde-pr-development\ndescription: Execute one Product Owner-proceeded Glow HDE PR work unit in its single dedicated development session across GCFPE PR-30 implementation/publication, PR-35 review correction/merge readiness, interrupted recovery, and eligible RS-40 continuation. Do not use for PR planning, Product Owner merge, PR-40 lineage review, QA/Ops execution, deployment, or Change Flow orchestration.\n---\n\n# Glow HDE PR Development\n\n`GLOW_HDE_PR_DEVELOPMENT_SKILL_REVISION: 1.2.4`\n\nComplete one approved PR work unit without losing prior work or wasting remote actions. PR-30 and PR-35 are two phases of the same native PR-execution authority, not separate work units. Keep the existing GCFPE actor, one dedicated PR-development session, one original Product Owner Proceed, scope, and manual-merge boundaries intact.\n\n## Establish the exact assignment\n\nRequire the complete selected invocation for the actual entry phase—PR-30, PR-35, or an eligible RS-40 continuation—for one work unit, including:\n\n- exact change and work-unit identities;\n- the complete approved PR instruction and detailed PR implementation Plan, with versions and actual Drive links;\n- the Product Owner's Proceed invocation for that exact Plan;\n- approved Specification, whole-change Plan/review, dependencies, repository identity, and any existing PR/commit/result lineage;\n- the immutable approved base, unique current PF10 Markdown direct Drive link, every applicable active PF10 addendum direct Drive link, and explicit effective overlay scope;\n- the dedicated PR-session identity, exact `PR_RETURN_PHASE` when rescope lineage exists, and known continuation state;\n- for PR-35, the complete `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED` result and same-session PR-35 handoff; for postpublication RS-40, the complete PR-30 phase result/checkpoint and, only when `PR_RETURN_PHASE: PR-35`, the PR-35 handoff; in either case require the exact workspace/worktree, branch, open PR and remote-head lineage;\n- for prepublication PR-30, explicit evidence that no open PR exists rather than a manufactured PR reference or RS-40 eligibility.\n\nResolve the currently selected prompt for the actual phase by its exact Notion name, version, and page identity. Do not infer currentness from title similarity or search order. Treat reusable prompts as workflow instructions; treat the supplied approved artifacts as the substantive scope. Resolve PFCanon authority only from controlled Markdown in Drive `Glow / Core Docs / PFCanon`: prove the `Glow` → direct-child `Core Docs` → direct-child `PFCanon` hierarchy and the chosen Markdown item's direct parent. Never open, fetch, inspect, compare, cite as authority, or use a Google Doc, DOC, or DOCX PFCanon item; there is no fallback. Failure to resolve and completely read one unique controlled Markdown authority is `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`, never evidence that a manual drain did or did not occur.\n\nProceed authorizes the bounded engineering lifecycle for the exact work unit: PR-30 implementation/local verification/coherent initial publication followed in the same session by PR-35 review remediation and current-head CI verification. It never authorizes merge, scope expansion, Ops, QA, deployment, Canon publication, or another work unit. An approved, manually drained PF10 addendum overlays the immutable base only for its explicit scope; continuation preserves the original Proceed and never requires or creates a second Proceed.\n\n## Recover before creating work\n\nAt every fresh, resumed, or uncertain entry:\n\n1. Resolve the authorized repository and read its complete `AGENTS.md` plus task-relevant repository instructions.\n2. Inspect accessible existing checkouts, worktrees, branches, worktree status, commits, PRs, and saved Drive artifacts that may belong to the exact change/work unit.\n3. Match prior work using evidence such as repository origin, work-unit identity, branch, commit ancestry, artifact lineage, and PR head—not a guessed directory name.\n4. Reuse the verified existing workspace and completed valid work. Reconcile partial or ambiguous external effects before retrying them.\n5. If several candidates conflict, preserve each and ask for the smallest owner decision needed. If no matching accessible workspace exists, create one only after recording what was checked.\n\nNever claim that prior work is absent merely because one location is inaccessible. Never invent a session identity, platform endpoint, inspection capability, or access limitation. Session history is not required when repository and artifact evidence establish continuity.\n\nFor detailed recovery and handoff cases, read [behavior-cases.md](references/behavior-cases.md).\n\n## Execute the two-phase engineering lifecycle\n\nRemain in the one dedicated PR-development session across both phases. `PR-30` owns recovery, implementation, local testing, coherent commit creation, and deliberate initial publication. Its successful result is `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED`, followed by exactly one complete same-session `PR-35` handoff. `PR-35` owns remote review retrieval, corrections, local retesting, coherent corrective publication, CI economy, current-head verification, and genuine merge readiness. The phase boundary adds no actor, session, work unit, work vehicle, Product Owner approval, Proceed, R1 row, or authority transfer.\n\nThe exact ordered ten-field GCF-17 continuity list is: `WORK_UNIT_ID`; original Product Owner Proceed; dedicated PR-development session; workspace/worktree; branch; pull request; PR instruction; detailed PR plan; primary skill authority; continuous recovery/artifact lineage. PR-30 and PR-35 share exactly one value for each field; the phase boundary may not duplicate, replace, omit, or transfer any field.\n\nThe PR-30 result vocabulary is exactly `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED`, `RESCOPE_PENDING`, `RECOVERY_PENDING`, or `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`. The PR-35 result vocabulary is exactly `MERGE_PENDING`, `RESCOPE_PENDING`, `RECOVERY_PENDING`, `REMOTE_EVIDENCE_PENDING`, or `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`. RS-40 continues the exact recorded PR-30 or PR-35 phase and returns only that phase's lawful result after the four-state drain gate. Do not invent another result, downgrade an external-evidence wait into completion, or treat a postpublication PR-30 rescope as if PR-35 had already begun.\n\nMaintain one compact `PR_REMOTE_ACTION_LEDGER` recording actual local checks, commits, pushes, PR creation/reuse, review reads, finding dispositions, CI runs and stale/cancelled status, remote head, mergeability, remaining useful local action, and next evidence action. Save and completely read back a durable Drive checkpoint at PR-30 initial publication; at PR-35 entry when repairing or advancing that publication checkpoint; after every coherent corrective push; before any extended wait for remote-only evidence; and at every nonterminal interruption or rescope boundary. Intent never proves a remote effect.\n\n### 1. Verify scope and baseline\n\n- Fetch current repository state before changing it.\n- Preserve unrelated user work and avoid modifying a dirty overlapping worktree.\n- Challenge the Plan against repository facts before implementation. Correct ordinary in-scope defects within the work unit; route a substantiated material boundary through the existing rescope path.\n\n### 2. Implement and verify locally\n\n- Make the smallest complete source change that satisfies the approved work unit.\n- Run the narrowest relevant local checks first, then the broader repository-defined checks required for the candidate.\n- Use current repository commands and CI definitions; do not invent a universal test command.\n- Fix local failures and rerun affected checks before committing or pushing.\n\n### 3. Commit and publish deliberately in PR-30\n\n- Create commits at meaningful, reviewable checkpoints after applicable local checks pass. Avoid both a no-commit stop and constant micro-commits.\n- An early draft PR is acceptable once there is a coherent, locally tested checkpoint. Reuse an existing PR for the same branch/work unit instead of creating another.\n- Before each push, confirm the intended branch, base, outgoing commits, and worktree state.\n- Bundle related implementation or review corrections into one locally verified push when practical. Never push merely to trigger another remote run.\n- Read back the remote head and PR state after publication. Freeze and reconcile an ambiguous push or PR result before retrying.\n\nWhen one coherent locally tested candidate is deliberately published or an existing matching PR is verified at that checkpoint, stop PR-30 with `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED`. Return exactly one complete `NEXT_PROMPT_HANDOFF` block that invokes the exact selected PR-35 in this same dedicated session with all repository, worktree, branch, PR, remote-head, artifact, test, constraint, unresolved-item, and original-Proceed lineage. Do not route PR-30 directly to PR-40, wait for merge readiness in PR-30, or create another PR/session/Proceed.\n\nNative `gh` is optional. The authenticated ChatGPT GitHub connector is a sufficient supported path for any repository, PR, review, workflow, or check operation it can perform. Do not block the PR work solely because `gh` is absent or separately unauthenticated. Use local Git for source history and the available authorized remote surface for publication and review operations.\n\n### 4. In PR-35, put review findings before stale CI\n\n- Read all applicable code and security reviews, inline threads, summary comments, and current check state after publication and after material updates.\n- Before another push, resolve every known substantive in-scope review issue locally and verify the affected behavior.\n- Do not wait for CI on a revision already known to require review corrections. If a CI run for that stale revision is active and cancellation is authorized and supported, cancel it; otherwise mark it stale and continue local remediation without treating it as a gate.\n- Push the coherent corrected candidate only after local checks pass. Then evaluate CI for that candidate revision.\n- Treat a review as clean only from the actual review content and unresolved-thread state, not from a generic `COMMENTED`, `COMPLETED`, or approval label alone.\n- Never use `[skip ci]` or an equivalent suppression mechanism without Nathan's direct, specific authorization for the identified push.\n- If CI starts automatically and later becomes stale because a substantive finding requires another candidate revision, stop treating that run as a gate. Cancel it only when a supported authorized interface permits cancellation.\n\n### 5. In PR-35, reach genuine merge readiness\n\nContinue in the same dedicated PR session until all applicable predicates are true:\n\n- approved implementation scope is complete;\n- required local checks pass on the candidate commit;\n- intended commits are pushed and the PR reflects the exact remote head;\n- applicable code and security review findings and required threads are resolved on the current remote head, or a truthful clean current-head review is evidenced;\n- required CI passes on the current candidate, or an actual scoped authorized waiver is recorded;\n- no unresolved material rescope, dependency, or repository-state conflict remains;\n- the complete PR implementation result and handoff artifacts are saved and read back.\n\nOnly then return `MERGE_PENDING` and say `Ready to merge` with the actual PR reference, verified remote-head identity, mergeability, current-head review proof, and current-head CI proof or exact valid waiver. This is historical pre-merge evidence, not a claim that the PR is already merged. Nathan / Product Owner performs the merge manually as a separate action. This skill never authorizes an agent to merge, enable auto-merge, schedule a merge, or keep polling for that manual action.\n\nUse `REMOTE_EVIDENCE_PENDING` only in PR-35 when an actual external review or required check result is unavailable and no useful local action remains. Save and read back the complete recovery checkpoint and return exactly one same-session PR-35 re-entry handoff. A normal short wait, unread review, unperformed local work, known substantive finding, or stale candidate never qualifies. Use `RECOVERY_PENDING` only for an exact same-session repository/artifact inconsistency that can safely be recovered without new authority, with one same-phase continuation; if the missing source, owner, or authority requires Nathan, use terminal `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED` and emit no continuation handoff.\n\n## Control remote-action cost\n\nOptimize for accepted completion, not activity:\n\n- prefer local diagnosis and testing before remote execution;\n- avoid duplicate PRs, redundant pushes, repeated review requests, and CI runs on known-stale revisions;\n- group related corrections without hiding meaningful review boundaries;\n- poll only when a pending remote result can change the next action;\n- preserve completed checks and review evidence across resumption when the relevant candidate and scope are unchanged.\n\nDo not impose a fixed commit count, push count, polling interval, or CI-cancellation requirement. Use the smallest remote-action sequence that still produces a reviewable, verifiable, merge-ready PR.\n\n## Route a real material boundary\n\nWhen repository evidence proves that the approved work unit cannot be completed without changing approved scope, architecture, requirements, or Plan authority:\n\n1. stop only the affected implementation work and preserve valid completed work;\n2. save a precise recovery/result artifact in the approved Drive folder;\n3. create and read back one complete formal bounded `RESCOPE_REQUEST`, record exactly one `PR_RETURN_PHASE` from `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION`, `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION`, or `PR-35`, then resolve the exact selected same-whole-change-IA RS-20 identity required by the selected route;\n4. return one populated, standalone, copy-paste-ready RS-20 review package containing the actual finding, affected boundary, change/work-unit identity, dedicated IA and PR sessions, immutable base plus current PF10/addenda, complete lineage, verified Drive links, completed work, tests, reviews and CI evidence, repository/workspace/worktree/branch state, open PR and remote head only when they actually exist, original Proceed, constraints, unresolved items, required same-IA decision, exact return phase, and expected `RESCOPE_REVIEW` output.\n\nDo not return a blank handoff template, routing metadata, or a title-only destination. Ordinary in-scope difficulty or review correction is not rescope. The PR session never approves its own rescope, rewrites the approved Plan/Guide/Specification, restarts work, or requests a new Proceed.\n\nWhen an approved rescope, escalation/remediation, or material Specification, Implementation Plan, or QA Plan change enters the work-unit lineage, preserve the responsible prompt's exactly one standalone `PF10_BUILD_NOTES_ADDENDUM` and its verified Drive link. It must state `status: READY_FOR_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `canonicality: NON_CANONICAL_PENDING_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `drain_owner: Nathan / Product Owner`, the exact approved base, decision evidence, complete overlay delta, affected requirements/dependencies/tests/Ops/documentation/downstream work, exclusions, conflicts, unresolved items, return point, and a stable `drain_verification_anchor`. Do not create a substitute approval, edit PF10, select final PF10 numbering, or claim that the addendum is canonical. Nathan's manual drain is the canonicalization boundary. No affected implementation may rely on any qualifying delta before exact verified manual-drain evidence exists; preservation, evidence return, and other work that does not rely on the delta may proceed under unchanged authority. Initial approval, rejection/denial, `REVISION_REQUIRED`, pending, unchanged, editorial, and `IN_SCOPE_REPAIR` outcomes create no empty addendum.\n\nFresh post-drain verification is exhaustive and mutually exclusive:\n\n- `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`: one unique current controlled PF10 Markdown could not be resolved and completely read; preserve evidence and make no assertion about whether Nathan drained the addendum.\n- `MANUAL_DRAIN_REQUIRED`: current PF10 was resolved and read, and the exact stable anchor is absent.\n- `MANUAL_DRAIN_MISMATCH`: related content exists, but decision, immutable base, or normalized approved delta does not match.\n- `DRAIN_VERIFIED`: the stable anchor and normalized approved delta match with no later conflict; only then resume the recorded eligible phase.\n\nA PF10 reference captured before Nathan's action is `PRE_DRAIN_BASELINE_EVIDENCE`, never current post-drain authority.\n\nFor an approved rescope with `PR_RETURN_PHASE` of `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION` or `PR-35`, require the same IA's actual `RESCOPE_REVIEW`, the existing open PR, and fresh `DRAIN_VERIFIED` evidence binding its one approved addendum to the independently resolved current PF10 Markdown. Only those open-PR branches use selected `RS-40 — Approved Rescope — Resume PR Implementation`. Resume the recorded phase in the same dedicated PR session, workspace/worktree, branch, open PR, current evidence and original Product Owner Proceed. The approved delta overlays the immutable base only for its explicit scope; do not reauthor the base Plan, create a duplicate work surface, restart the PR, or obtain another Proceed. An accepted-final PR remains final and must never be rerun.\n\nFor approved ESC-40 remediation returning to this PR, accept the actual current `REMEDIATION_REVIEW`, its bounded overlay, the original approved base and original Proceed, and fresh `DRAIN_VERIFIED` evidence. A legacy `REMEDIATION_PLAN_REVIEW` or other source-native alias is usable only when the actual artifact establishes its equivalent approval semantics and exact lineage. Continue under the recorded PR-30 or PR-35 phase as the native delivery owner, then return to the originating verification owner. A remediation review is not an RS-20 approval and cannot enter RS-40; do not request a duplicate decision or addendum, replacement Plan, or new Proceed.\n\nAn IA-30 approval of a material whole-plan delta is a separate `MATERIAL_PLAN_DELTA_REVIEW`. Carry it alongside the original `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_REVIEW`, immutable base and its one manually drained addendum. It does not replace the base review, authorize another work unit, or satisfy RS-40's RS-20 rescope predicate. Resume only the actual native stage within the existing authority.\n\nRS-10/RS-20 also serve bounded planning, non-PR, and post-merge-but-not-accepted work-unit discoveries through the same IA. Those branches preserve their original native owner and stage; they neither fabricate an open PR/Proceed nor use RS-40. A proceeded `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION` discovery returns after Nathan's manual drain and fresh `DRAIN_VERIFIED` directly to that same native PR-30 session/workspace/worktree/branch and original Proceed, without manufacturing an open PR or using RS-40. This skill does not execute other native stages.\n\nIf RS-20 returns `REJECT` or `IN_SCOPE_REPAIR`, create no addendum and return the decision and preserved evidence to the correct existing repair owner and recorded phase under unchanged authority, with no Plan rewrite. `REVISION_REQUIRED` creates no addendum: use RS-30 and return the repaired request/proposal to the same author and RS-20 decision owner. `SPECIFICATION_CHANGE_REQUIRED` creates no RS-20 addendum and returns terminally to Nathan for the native Product Owner decision and Specification-delta route. If repeated failure becomes unrecoverable, save a complete recovery/evidence record and return control to Nathan / Product Owner. Only Nathan / Product Owner may manually invoke the selected `PR-50 — Abort PR and Escalate` prompt. No agent, PR, IA, RS, QA, skill, automation, hub, or handoff may invoke or route to it. Never delete, reset, overwrite, close, merge, force-push, or rebase the preserved workspace, branch, PR, commits, or evidence as an abort surrogate.\n\nWhen this PR-30, PR-35, or RS-40 invocation is unrecoverable, lacks required source or owner identity, or lacks the required verified manual drain, preserve evidence and return terminally to Nathan for this invocation with the exact missing fact. Emit no continuation handoff. This ends only the invocation; it does not abort the PR, close the change, revoke the original Proceed, or erase completed work. Ordinary recoverable local failures and review findings remain work for the same session.\n\n## Store artifacts and hand off directly\n\nSave off-repository Specifications, Plans, reviews, results, recovery records, rescope packages, PF10 build notes addenda, and handoff files as efficient machine-readable Markdown under the verified Drive folder:\n\n`Glow / Ephemeral Planning Files`  \n`https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pRJ8R1a-p5dYQFY89a1YyJpDceYZ2MLc`\n\nKeep repository-controlled outputs at their exact governed paths. Keep reusable prompt bodies in Notion. Do not use provider-internal file IDs as runtime artifact references. After each Drive write, read back the saved file and retain its actual title, version, Drive link, and digest when available.\n\nEvery non-terminal return must include exactly one fenced `text` block whose first line is `NEXT_PROMPT_HANDOFF`; the remainder of that same block is the complete self-contained prompt Nathan can paste into the receiving session. It must instruct the receiver to run the exact selected Notion prompt by full name, version, and direct Notion URL; identify the receiving role and exact continuing/dedicated session; identify the change/Epic and work unit; supply every required direct Drive link and repository/PR reference; state current status, completed work, decisions, constraints, unresolved items, and preserved authority; and state the next required action and expected output. Populate only the actual branch. A metadata list, menu, blank form, filename-only reference, or instruction to reconstruct context is not runnable. A terminal return for this invocation emits no continuation handoff, including an operator return for missing required source/owner/drain evidence or unrecoverable work.\n\nAt PR-30 `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED`, return the exact same-session PR-35 continuation. At PR-35 `MERGE_PENDING`, return control to the Product Owner with the historical pre-merge result, PR reference and a complete conditional PR-40 invocation. The conditional text must instruct Nathan to use it only after Nathan has manually merged the identified PR; it must separately state the earlier `MERGE_PENDING` evidence, Nathan's later merge assertion, and PR-40's duty to independently verify actual merged state and landed lineage. For interruption, return the exact same-session same-phase continuation prompt and verified recovery evidence. For rescope, return the populated formal `RESCOPE_REQUEST` directly to the selected same-IA RS-20 described above; RS-10 is optional proposal support, not a mandatory in-flight step. For an approved and manually drained open-PR rescope, use selected RS-40 while preserving the recorded PR-30/PR-35 phase, original Proceed, and complete existing PR context.\n\n## Preserve boundaries\n\n- Use `glow-hde-devops` only for a genuinely needed environment, Railway, vendor, database, deployment, or bounded operational capability. It supports this work; it does not govern PR-30 or PR-35.\n- Use Change Flow controls for workflow selection and orchestration, not repository implementation.\n- Use `glow-merged-change-attribution-lock` only for its read-only post-merge evidence role.\n- Do not execute PR-40, PR-50, QA, Ops, deployment, closure, or Canon drainage from this skill.\n- Do not introduce model, strength, configuration, or reasoning-level assessment or routing.\n- Do not create hidden sessions or extra approval stages.\n- Do not invoke, select, recommend, or route to `PR-50`; only Nathan / Product Owner may invoke that terminal manual control.\n\n## Validate this skill\n\nRun after changes:\n\n```bash\npython3 scripts/validate_glow_hde_pr_development.py\n```\n\nThen run the personal-skill structural validator. Treat deterministic success as structural evidence only; representative Alpha use supplies behavioral evidence.\n",
    "54ed379fa4c573bb93b019d6814db56d0bd75865aa5c9335b1b07dfc4dd3eb8e": "interface:\n  display_name: Glow HDE PR Development\n  short_description: Run one Glow HDE PR through merge readiness\n  default_prompt: Use $glow-hde-pr-development to execute this approved Glow HDE PR\n    work unit through verified merge readiness.\n  icon_small: assets/icon.svg\n  icon_large: assets/icon.svg\npolicy:\n  products:\n  - chatgpt\n  - codex\n  - api\n  - atlas\n  allow_implicit_invocation: true\n",
    "8936b24f674a1250d999e2c2b5901374fb4240426f32bd1ae340c352a90d617d": "<svg width=\"24\" height=\"24\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\" fill=\"none\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\">\n<path d=\"M7 20.4524C6.225 20.4524 5.53333 20.2857 4.925 19.9524C4.31667 19.6107 3.84167 19.1357 3.5 18.5274C3.16667 17.9191 3 17.2274 3 16.4524V6.45239C3 5.67739 3.16667 4.98573 3.5 4.37739C3.84167 3.76906 4.31667 3.29823 4.925 2.96489C5.53333 2.62323 6.225 2.45239 7 2.45239H17C17.775 2.45239 18.4667 2.62323 19.075 2.96489C19.6833 3.29823 20.1542 3.76906 20.4875 4.37739C20.8292 4.98573 21 5.67739 21 6.45239V16.4524C21 17.2274 20.8292 17.9191 20.4875 18.5274C20.1542 19.1357 19.6833 19.6107 19.075 19.9524C18.4667 20.2857 17.775 20.4524 17 20.4524H7Z\" fill=\"#4D4D4D\"/>\n<path fill-rule=\"evenodd\" clip-rule=\"evenodd\" d=\"M7.95981 8.77245C8.22487 8.41907 8.72648 8.34735 9.07992 8.6123C9.43319 8.87741 9.50509 9.37903 9.24008 9.73241L7.79965 11.6523L9.24008 13.5723C9.50496 13.9257 9.43325 14.4273 9.07992 14.6924C8.72654 14.9573 8.22491 14.8854 7.95981 14.5322L6.16 12.1328C5.94667 11.8484 5.94667 11.4563 6.16 11.1719L7.95981 8.77245Z\" fill=\"white\"/>\n<path fill-rule=\"evenodd\" clip-rule=\"evenodd\" d=\"M12.6844 8.89452C12.882 8.49943 13.3625 8.33957 13.7577 8.5371C14.1526 8.73474 14.3136 9.21526 14.1161 9.61034L11.7157 14.4101C11.5181 14.8051 11.0375 14.9649 10.6424 14.7676C10.2473 14.57 10.0865 14.0895 10.284 13.6943L12.6844 8.89452Z\" fill=\"white\"/>\n<path fill-rule=\"evenodd\" clip-rule=\"evenodd\" d=\"M15.3202 8.6123C15.6736 8.34741 16.1752 8.41908 16.4403 8.77245L18.2401 11.1719C18.4533 11.4563 18.4534 11.8484 18.2401 12.1328L16.4403 14.5322C16.1753 14.8855 15.6736 14.9571 15.3202 14.6924C14.9667 14.4273 14.8949 13.9257 15.16 13.5723L16.5995 11.6523L15.16 9.73241C14.8949 9.37896 14.9667 8.87738 15.3202 8.6123Z\" fill=\"white\"/>\n</svg>\n",
    "06ba372111d8ea22cedeb16ed24ddec4a812c4ea57a952dad99e80a8e2bd46eb": "# PR development behavior cases\n\nUse these cases to check decisions after creating or materially revising the skill. They are acceptance examples, not extra workflow stages.\n\n## Fresh work unit\n\nGiven a complete proceeded Plan and no matching existing work, PR-30 inspects repository instructions and state, creates the bounded branch/worktree only after recovery checks, implements, tests locally, commits at a coherent checkpoint, and deliberately publishes or updates one PR. It then returns `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED` with exactly one complete same-session PR-35 handoff. PR-35 processes reviews, corrects all known findings locally, verifies the current remote head and current-head CI, and stops only at genuine merge readiness. An early draft PR is allowed after a coherent locally tested checkpoint. The phase split creates no new role, session, Proceed, approval, R1 row, work unit, or PR.\n\n## PR-30 phase boundary\n\nGiven a coherent locally tested candidate that is committed and deliberately published, PR-30 must not continue as a monolithic review/CI phase and must not route directly to PR-40. It returns `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED` and one fenced `text` `NEXT_PROMPT_HANDOFF` that invokes the exact selected PR-35 in the same dedicated PR-development session with complete lineage.\n\nThe shared phase identity preserves the exact ordered ten-field GCF-17 continuity list: `WORK_UNIT_ID`; original Product Owner Proceed; dedicated PR-development session; workspace/worktree; branch; pull request; PR instruction; detailed PR plan; primary skill authority; continuous recovery/artifact lineage. PR-30 and PR-35 share exactly one value for every field.\n\n## PR-35 review phase\n\nGiven the complete same-session PR-35 handoff, retrieve every applicable review, inline thread, summary comment, and check. Resolve known substantive findings before treating CI as a gate, retest locally, publish one coherent corrective checkpoint, and verify reviews, required threads, CI or an exact valid waiver, remote-head identity, and mergeability on the same current head before `MERGE_PENDING`.\n\n## Exact phase results and remote evidence\n\nPR-30 returns only `PR_CANDIDATE_PUBLISHED`, `RESCOPE_PENDING`, `RECOVERY_PENDING`, or `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`. PR-35 returns only `MERGE_PENDING`, `RESCOPE_PENDING`, `RECOVERY_PENDING`, `REMOTE_EVIDENCE_PENDING`, or `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`. `REMOTE_EVIDENCE_PENDING` requires an actually unavailable external review/check result, no useful local action, a saved/read-back checkpoint, and one same-session PR-35 re-entry; a normal short wait never qualifies. A recoverable inconsistency stays in the same phase as `RECOVERY_PENDING`; a missing owner/source/authority that Nathan must resolve is terminal `PRODUCT_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED` with no continuation block.\n\n## Remote-action ledger and checkpoint cadence\n\nMaintain `PR_REMOTE_ACTION_LEDGER` with local tests, commits, pushes, PR reuse/creation, reviews/findings, CI and stale/cancelled state, remote head, mergeability, remaining local action, and next evidence action. Save/read back a Drive checkpoint at PR-30 publication, at PR-35 entry when advancing that checkpoint, after each coherent correction push, before an extended remote-only wait, and at every nonterminal interruption or rescope boundary.\n\n## Interrupted session with existing work\n\nGiven a fresh session and evidence of an earlier worktree, inspect accessible worktrees, branches, commits, PR heads, and Drive artifacts. Reuse the verified matching workspace and completed valid work. Do not start over, overwrite it, or assert that an unavailable session-inspection service prevents recovery.\n\n## Ambiguous workspaces\n\nGiven two plausible worktrees with conflicting heads, preserve both, report the evidence, and request the smallest owner decision. Do not guess which is authoritative and do not delete either.\n\n## Connector available, `gh` unavailable\n\nGiven working local Git and an authenticated GitHub connector that supports the required PR operations, continue through publication, reviews, and checks using those surfaces. Do not install or authenticate `gh` as a prerequisite solely because it is absent.\n\n## Open review findings and active CI\n\nGiven substantive open review issues on a pushed revision, address the issues locally immediately. Do not wait for that revision's CI to pass. Cancel its stale CI run only when authorized and supported; otherwise label it stale. Run local tests, combine related fixes, and make the next push only when the corrected candidate is coherent. Never use `[skip ci]` or an equivalent without Nathan's direct, specific authorization.\n\n## CI failure without open review issues\n\nDiagnose the failure against the exact candidate, reproduce or narrow it locally where possible, fix in scope, run affected local checks, and push one coherent correction. Preserve the failed result; do not repeatedly push speculative fixes.\n\n## Material rescope\n\nGiven evidence that implementation requires an approved-boundary change, preserve valid work and PR state, save and read back one complete formal bounded `RESCOPE_REQUEST` in Drive, record exactly one `PR_RETURN_PHASE` from `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION`, `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION`, or `PR-35`, resolve the selected same-whole-change-IA RS-20 page, and return one fully populated RS-20 prompt another session can paste without reconstructing the conversation. RS-10 remains optional proposal support and is not a mandatory intermediate in this normal in-flight route. The PR session never approves the rescope, rewrites the approved base, restarts, or requests another Proceed. Do not return `NEXT_PROMPT_HANDOFF` metadata with blank fields.\n\n## Rejected or revision-required rescope\n\nGiven the same IA's RS-20 `REJECT` decision, preserve the immutable base, decision, PR session, workspace/worktree, branch, open PR, original Proceed, completed work and evidence, then return the bounded finding directly to the same PR-30 context with no rewrite and no PF10 addendum. Only a distinct RS-20 `REVISION_REQUIRED` decision routes the exact request/proposal redlines to the same author through RS-30; the complete revised request/proposal, preserving its input artifact type, returns to that same IA in RS-20. Neither outcome rewrites a Plan/Guide/Specification or emits an empty PF10 addendum.\n\n## Approved rescope continuation\n\nGiven the same IA's approved RS-20 decision, require exactly one standalone PF10 addendum with `READY_FOR_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `NON_CANONICAL_PENDING_MANUAL_DRAIN`, `drain_owner: Nathan / Product Owner`, the complete affected-surface fields, and stable `drain_verification_anchor`. Do not resume before Nathan manually drains it and the receiving phase independently resolves and completely reads current PF10 Markdown. For `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION` or `PR-35`, use selected RS-40 and resume the recorded phase in the same PR session, workspace/worktree, branch, open PR and original Proceed. For `PR-30_PREPUBLICATION`, bypass RS-40 and resume PR-30 directly with no manufactured open PR. Do not reauthor the base or create another Proceed.\n\nFor `PR-30_POSTPUBLICATION`, require the PR-30 phase result/checkpoint but do not require or invent a PR-35 handoff. Require that handoff only when the recorded return phase is `PR-35`.\n\n## Exhaustive post-drain result\n\nGiven an approved addendum and a return attempt, emit exactly one of `SOURCE_RESOLUTION_ERROR`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_REQUIRED`, `MANUAL_DRAIN_MISMATCH`, or `DRAIN_VERIFIED`. Source failure makes no assertion about Nathan's drain. A pre-drain PF10 link is only `PRE_DRAIN_BASELINE_EVIDENCE`. Only `DRAIN_VERIFIED` permits reliance on the delta and exact-phase resumption.\n\n## Native remediation return\n\nGiven a current ESC-40 `REMEDIATION_REVIEW`, an explicitly bounded delta against the original approved base, verified manual-drain evidence, the matching open PR and original Proceed, continue under PR-30. Preserve the actual source-native approval artifact name; use a legacy alias only when its equivalent semantics and lineage are evidenced. Do not relabel this as an RS-20 approval, route through RS-40, seek another review/addendum, or replace the Plan. Preserve the originating verification owner's return after delivery.\n\n## Other bounded work-unit discoveries\n\nGiven a planning, non-PR or merged-but-not-accepted bounded discovery, the selected RS-10/RS-20 contract uses existing evidence and the same IA. The approved overlay returns after manual drain to the original native owner/stage under unchanged authority. Do not manufacture an open PR, workspace, Proceed or RS-40 eligibility. An already accepted-final PR cannot be rerun or reopened by rescope.\n\n## Missing drain or source at continuation\n\nGiven missing or contradictory required manual-drain evidence, a missing decisive source, or unresolved owner identity at PR-30/RS-40 intake, preserve available evidence and return terminally to Nathan for this invocation. Emit no continuation handoff and make no abort or change-closure decision. Supply the exact missing fact and preserve original authority for later recovery.\n\n## Repeated failure and manual abort\n\nGiven repeated failure that the PR session cannot recover, save complete evidence and return Product Owner control terminally for this invocation with no continuation handoff. This is neither an abort nor a change-closure decision. Only Nathan / Product Owner may manually invoke the selected PR-50 terminal prompt. No agent, PR, IA, RS, QA, skill, automation, hub or handoff may route to it. PR-50 preserves the workspace, branch, open PR, commits and evidence; it does not delete, reset, overwrite, close, merge, force-push or rebase.\n\n## Approved change requiring Canon drainage\n\nGiven an approved rescope, escalation/remediation, or material Specification, Implementation Plan, or QA Plan change, carry the responsible prompt's exactly one standalone PF10 build notes addendum by verified Drive link and preserve Nathan's manual drain boundary. No affected implementation may rely on the qualifying delta before exact verified drain evidence; preservation, evidence return, and work independent of the delta may proceed. Do not edit PF10 or claim canonical status from approval or addendum creation alone. For a PR rescope, drainage is the explicit prerequisite to RS-40; for a non-qualifying outcome create no empty addendum.\n\n## Merge readiness\n\nGiven complete implementation, passing local checks, verified current pushed head, resolved current-head reviews and required threads, passing required current-head CI or an actual scoped waiver, and verified mergeability, PR-35 returns `MERGE_PENDING`, `Ready to merge`, the PR reference, and the conditional post-manual-merge PR-40 prompt. The result is historical pre-merge evidence. The conditional prompt separately requires Nathan's later manual-merge assertion and PR-40's independent verification of actual merged state and landed lineage. Nathan performs the merge manually; the skill never authorizes an agent to merge, enable auto-merge, schedule a merge, or poll indefinitely.\n\n## Not ready\n\nGiven an open substantive review, failing or stale CI, or unpushed intended commit, continue recoverable local work and report the precise state; never claim `MERGE_PENDING`. A substantiated bounded scope change has its actual same-IA rescope handoff. An unrecoverable conflict or missing decisive source/owner/drain evidence returns terminally for this invocation with no continuation handoff and no abort or change-closure decision.\n",
