\"`MANUAL_DRAIN_MISMATCH`\",\n        \"drain verified state\": \"`DRAIN_VERIFIED`\",\n        \"pre-drain evidence\": \"`PRE_DRAIN_BASELINE_EVIDENCE`\",\n        \"no source/drain inference\": \"never evidence that a manual drain did or did not occur\",\n        \"skip-ci boundary\": \"Never use `[skip ci]` or an equivalent suppression mechanism without Nathan's direct, specific authorization\",\n        \"stale automatic CI\": \"stop treating that run as a gate\",\n        \"current-head reviews\": \"required threads are resolved on the current remote head\",\n        \"remote-head proof\": \"verified remote-head identity\",\n        \"historical merge pending\": \"historical pre-merge evidence\",\n        \"three-event postmerge\": \"PR-40's duty to independently verify actual merged state and landed lineage\",\n        \"rejected rescope return\": \"`REJECT` or `IN_SCOPE_REPAIR`\",\n        \"specification change terminal\": \"`SPECIFICATION_CHANGE_REQUIRED` creates no RS-20 addendum and returns terminally to Nathan\",\n    }\n    for label, text in required.items():\n        if text not in combined:\n            fail(f\"missing {label} contract\")\n\n    forbidden = [\n        \"GCFPE-ASSESS-10\",\n        \"MODEL_HANDOFF\",\n        \"EPHEMERAL_LIBRARY\",\n        \"recommend a model\",\n        \"reasoning-level recommendation\",\n        \"normal Plan/instruction path\",\n        \"receives its own PO Proceed\",\n        \"actual Product Owner manual PF10 disposition\",\n        \"PR-35 receives a new Proceed\",\n        \"unless the Product Owner directly and specifically instructs\",\n        \"[TODO\",\n    ]\n    for text in forbidden:\n        if text.lower() in combined.lower():\n            fail(f\"forbidden or unfinished content present: {text}\")\n\n    case_headings = [\n        \"## Fresh work unit\",\n        \"## PR-30 phase boundary\",\n        \"## PR-35 review phase\",\n        \"## Exact phase results and remote evidence\",\n        \"## Remote-action ledger and checkpoint cadence\",\n        \"## Interrupted session with existing work\",\n        \"## Connector available, `gh` unavailable\",\n        \"## Open review findings and active CI\",\n        \"## Material rescope\",\n        \"## Rejected or revision-required rescope\",\n        \"## Approved rescope continuation\",\n        \"## Exhaustive post-drain result\",\n        \"## Native remediation return\",\n        \"## Other bounded work-unit discoveries\",\n        \"## Missing drain or source at continuation\",\n        \"## Repeated failure and manual abort\",\n        \"## Approved change requiring Canon drainage\",\n        \"## Merge readiness\",\n        \"## Not ready\",\n    ]\n    for heading in case_headings:\n        if heading not in cases:\n            fail(f\"missing behavior case: {heading}\")\n\n    print(\"PASS: Glow HDE PR development skill structural contract\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",
    "499b8c23a28f488efa50cf4aad61981ece33314633d520a631259153742bfb4b": "---\nname: glow-hde-devops\ndescription: Bootstrap, audit, and operate a bounded DevOps environment for the Glow HD Engine, including local Python QA, GitHub operations, Railway production access, authorized OpenRails vendor testing, and controlled direct-PostgreSQL operations. Use for glow-hdengine-v2 terminal setup and operations. Do not use as the primary skill for a GCFPE PR-30 development assignment, the full Glow application, generic cloud administration, Change Flow planning, or multi-session orchestration.\n---\n\n# Glow HDE DevOps\n\n`GLOW_HDE_DEVOPS_SKILL_REVISION: 1.5.0`\n\nOperate the Glow HD Engine as a small, reproducible DevOps workspace while preserving the repository's closed-rail, evidence, secret-handling, and authorization contracts.\n\n## Establish the operating contract\n\n1. Classify the request into exactly one primary mode:\n   - `ARCHITECTURE`\n   - `AUDIT`\n   - `BOOTSTRAP`\n   - `DEVELOPMENT`\n   - `QA`\n   - `GITHUB`\n   - `RAILWAY_CHECK`\n   - `RAILWAY_OPS`\n   - `OPENRAILS_VENDOR`\n   - `DATABASE_READ`\n   - `DATABASE_WRITE`\n   - `CLEANUP`\n   - `RESUME`\n2. Treat `ARCHITECTURE` and `AUDIT` as read-only. Do not install, authenticate, mutate, publish, or create temporary access in those modes.\n3. Locate the current repository rather than assuming a scratch path. Accept an explicit path, use the current Git worktree, or find `glow-hdengine-v2` beneath the authorized workspace.\n4. Read the repository's complete `AGENTS.md` before any repository action. Read only the current task-relevant PF Canon, QA, and operations sources identified by that file. Repository truth outranks this skill.\n5. State the repository identity, target identity, rail state, effect class, and required authorization before an effectful action.\n6. Default every engine and QA process to:\n\n```text\nLC_ALL=C\nLANG=C\nTZ=UTC\nSAFE_MODE=1\nALLOW_NETWORK=0\n```\n\n7. Use only the governed QA statuses: `PASS`, `FAIL_BEHAVIOR`, `FAIL_TOOLING`, `TOOLING_BLOCKED`, and `PARKED`.\n\n## Route to the relevant procedure\n\n| Mode | Load | Default effect |\n|---|---|---|\n| `ARCHITECTURE`, `AUDIT` | [repository-contract.md](references/repository-contract.md) | Read-only |\n| `BOOTSTRAP`, `QA` | [github-and-local-qa.md](references/github-and-local-qa.md) | Local workspace |\n| `DEVELOPMENT` | [github-and-local-qa.md](references/github-and-local-qa.md) | Assigned source/build work under current task gates |\n| `GITHUB` | [github-and-local-qa.md](references/github-and-local-qa.md) | Remote only when requested |\n| `RAILWAY_CHECK` | [railway-and-secrets.md](references/railway-and-secrets.md) | Read-only target probe |\n| `RAILWAY_OPS` | [railway-and-secrets.md](references/railway-and-secrets.md) | Exact authorized container, deployment or recovery operation |\n| `OPENRAILS_VENDOR` | [openrails-vendor.md](references/openrails-vendor.md) | Live, bounded, separately authorized |\n| `DATABASE_READ`, `DATABASE_WRITE` | [database-ops.md](references/database-ops.md) | Production data boundary |\n| `CLEANUP`, `RESUME`, any uncertain run | [evidence-and-recovery.md](references/evidence-and-recovery.md) | Reconcile before continuing |\n\nLoad no unrelated reference merely because it exists.\n\n## Run the common preflight\n\nFor HDE workstation setup, load [workstation-capabilities.md](references/workstation-capabilities.md). Prepare practical Codespaces equivalence across development, Git/PR publication, QA, Railway/runtime access, database operations, backups/restores, deployment and recovery. Map the complete requested capability set to actual execution evidence and material limits. Finish supported setup repairs and request the exact human sign-in help needed. Do not call the workstation ready from a doctor result, login, SELECT 1 or a subset of working routes.\n\nFor an authorized environment preparation request, use `BOOTSTRAP` and complete routine repairs before the readiness verdict. An absent checkout, missing dependencies, broken CLI wrapper or expired authentication is preparation work. Follow the repair loop in [github-and-local-qa.md](references/github-and-local-qa.md); retest the affected capability and distinguish an explicit runtime denial from a fixable setup defect. Preserve completed live-test request counts when resuming.\n\nPreserve the user's requested baseline. When it includes native GitHub and Railway CLIs, native authentication, Git publication transport or local production-variable injection, retain each as a requirement. Connector and Console checks are useful partial capabilities, not replacements for that baseline. When credentials are missing, prepare the provider's supported secure login and ask the user to complete it. Distinguish missing authentication from missing binaries or denied transport; never fabricate a login code, request secrets in chat, bypass restrictions or lower the readiness predicate.\n\n1. Run the deterministic local doctor:\n\n```bash\npython <skill-dir>/scripts/hde_devops.py doctor --repo <repo>\n```\n\n2. Require the expected origin `amthorn78/glow-hdengine-v2`, unless the user explicitly identifies a fork. Never silently switch repositories.\n3. Inspect the current branch, HEAD, worktree status, configured Python, pytest readiness, and required CLIs.\n4. Stop before modifying a dirty worktree when requested changes overlap user work. Preserve unrelated changes.\n5. Resolve Railway by names, not stored provider IDs:\n   - project: `ample-illumination`\n   - environment: `production`\n   - service: `glow-hdengine-v2`\n6. Verify the live target immediately before any Railway-backed action. Do not infer target identity from a previous session.\n7. Keep secret probes to `SET`, `UNSET`, or `REDACTED`. Never run or relay `env`, `printenv`, `railway variable list --json`, or `railway variable list --kv` in a secret-bearing context.\n\n## Separate authorization from execution\n\n- Treat the user's request as authority only for the actions it clearly names.\n- Apply existing exact task/session authorization to its unchanged target, effects and remaining limits. Ask only for an uncovered, changed, revoked or exhausted scope, including an additional live vendor run, database write, deployment, restart, variable mutation, temporary SSH key, push or pull request.\n- Successful login, tool access and script acknowledgment do not create authority. Continuation alone does not expire existing authority; a completed or exhausted live-test envelope cannot be spent again.\n- Use an acknowledgment accepted by a bundled script only after the user has authorized the matching scope. The acknowledgment is a local guard, not evidence of consent.\n- Keep `OPENRAILS_VENDOR` authority separate from all database, deployment, and configuration authority.\n- Require a concrete rollback or restore procedure covered by the applicable task approval before `DATABASE_WRITE`; an existing exact approved Ops/task plan can supply it without another approval.\n\n## Use the bundled controls\n\n### Bootstrap a workspace\n\nRun the idempotent bootstrapper from an authorized workspace:\n\n```bash\nbash <skill-dir>/scripts/bootstrap_hde.sh --workspace <workspace>\n```\n\nAdd `--install-tools` only when installation is within scope. The script never uses `sudo`. Review [github-and-local-qa.md](references/github-and-local-qa.md) first.\n\n### Check Railway without exposing values\n\n```bash\npython <skill-dir>/scripts/hde_devops.py railway-target --repo <repo>\npython <skill-dir>/scripts/hde_devops.py railway-env-check --repo <repo>\n```\n\nRun these only after CLI authentication. Review [railway-and-secrets.md](references/railway-and-secrets.md) first.\n\n### Run a synthetic OpenRails comparison\n\nUse the controller so Railway injects secrets only into the child process:\n\n```bash\npython <skill-dir>/scripts/hde_devops.py openrails-vendor \\\n  --repo <repo> \\\n  --output-dir <external-empty-directory> \\\n  --ack OPENRAILS_VENDOR_SYNTHETIC_PRODUCTION\n```\n\nDo this only in an `OPENRAILS_VENDOR` run with applicable unspent user authorization. Require an external output directory, two vendor request attempts maximum, zero database writes, and no retained raw payload. Review [openrails-vendor.md](references/openrails-vendor.md) first.\n\n### Validate the skill controls\n\nRun closed-rail self-tests without vendor, database, GitHub, or Railway traffic:\n\n```bash\npython <skill-dir>/scripts/validate_hde_devops.py\n```\n\n## Preserve repository and evidence ownership\n\n- Never edit `docs/pfcanon/**` without the exact Product Owner exception described by the current repository instructions.\n- Never hand-edit governed evidence, indexes, manifests, close reports, acceptance maps, path proofs, or generated companions.\n- Use the repository's current canonical writers and read-only validators.\n- Place ordinary QA output only where the active repository plan permits. Keep ad hoc operational output outside the repository.\n- Do not treat a successful command, vendor response, database connection, deployment, or CI run as broader acceptance or epic completion.\n\n## GCFPE and PR-development boundary\n\nFor a Product Owner-proceeded GCFPE PR-30 work unit, use `glow-hde-pr-development` as the primary execution skill. That skill owns workspace recovery, implementation, local testing, proportionate commits and pushes, PR publication/update, review remediation, CI verification, rescope handoff, Drive artifacts, and the merge-ready result.\n\nUse this skill only as supporting capability when the approved work specifically needs HDE environment preparation, Railway, OpenRails vendor access, database operations, deployment/recovery, or another bounded operational function it owns. Its generic `DEVELOPMENT`, `QA`, and `GITHUB` modes remain available outside a GCFPE PR-30 assignment.\n\nDo not reproduce or override GCFPE routing, artifact-storage, direct-handoff, rescope, review-order, Canon-drainage, session, or approval policy here. Do not introduce model, strength, configuration, or reasoning-level assessment or routing. Report a prompt/skill incompatibility to the current GCFPE management surface; do not repair prompts from this skill.\n\n## Handle GitHub operations\n\nMerging any PR is reserved to the Product Owner unless they directly and specifically instruct this agent to merge that identified PR. Ordinary GitHub publication, implementation, Ops or QA authority is insufficient; do not offer to merge or configure automatic merging as routine completion.\n\n- Fetch and inspect before changing remote state.\n- Confirm the base branch and exact outgoing commits before push.\n- Run applicable local checks before opening a pull request.\n- Push only the intended branch. Never force-push unless the user explicitly requests it and the repository policy permits it.\n- Create a pull request only when requested or when the user clearly authorizes publication.\n- Record the exact remote head and check state; distinguish pending, failed, and unavailable checks.\n\n## Handle database operations\n\n- Default to `DATABASE_READ` and least-privilege, bounded queries.\n- Use `DATABASE_URL` as the only active database transport input.\n- Reject the presence, including empty-value presence, of `DB_ALLOW_BRIDGE_IN_PROD`, `DB_BRIDGE_URL`, or `DB_FORCE_BRIDGE`.\n- Use repository-owned database tools and schema contracts. Do not invent generic production SQL.\n- Require `psql`, `pg_dump`, or `pg_restore` when the approved procedure needs them. Report `TOOLING_BLOCKED` if absent.\n- Refuse `DATABASE_WRITE` without an exact target, change set, transaction/lock posture, backup or rollback path, verification query, and applicable unspent authorization.\n\n## Freeze on uncertainty\n\nStop retries and reconcile observed state when any external action times out, returns an ambiguous result, loses authentication, changes target identity, or may have partially completed. Do not repeat a push, deployment, variable mutation, vendor call, database statement, or SSH-key operation until its actual state is known.\n\nFor temporary Railway SSH access, inventory the exact key before creation, record only its non-secret label/fingerprint, and remove that exact key at the end. Verify removal. Never expose private key material.\n\n## Report a terminal result\n\nReport:\n\n- primary mode and effect class;\n- repository branch and exact HEAD observed;\n- target names and rail state;\n- commands/checks actually run;\n- governed status for each material check;\n- external effects actually observed;\n- vendor request count, database construction/write count, and raw-payload retention posture when applicable;\n- artifacts created, using paths or hashes that reveal no secrets or personal inputs;\n- cleanup state and any remaining blocker;\n- explicit nonclaims for actions not run or not proven.\n\nNever report intent as execution or an unobserved result as `PASS`.\n\n## Hand off without coupling\n\n- Hand a GCFPE PR-30 development assignment to `glow-hde-pr-development`; use this skill only for any specifically needed supporting operational capability.\n- Hand other canonical workflow planning/orchestration requests to `change-flow`; keep environment preparation, task capability checks and other authorized source/build work in this skill. Preserve the current task's actual Plan, Proceed and reviewer gates.\n- Hand multi-session communication to `session-relay-flowmaster`; do not embed or reproduce Flowmaster core behavior.\n- Accept supplied handoff fields such as source skill, run identity, approved scope, and authorization boundary, but verify every live target and action at execution time.\n- Keep this skill standalone. Do not include it in Flowmaster propagation or embedded-core validation.\n",
    "0e3cb90ce59beb9abd08729369523e4c6fb5d97cefb49a52484c5b1459dd2245": "interface:\n  display_name: Glow HDE DevOps\n  short_description: Operate the Glow HD Engine safely\n  default_prompt: Use $glow-hde-devops to prepare and operate this Glow HDE DevOps\n    task.\n  icon_small: assets/icon.svg\n  icon_large: assets/icon.svg\npolicy:\n  products:\n  - chatgpt\n  - codex\n  - api\n  - atlas\n  allow_implicit_invocation: true\n",
    "bc733cce4edad4c16fdc2af7ec94388be68f465ca98ba7197c08c8a12df61eff": "# Database operations\n\n## Transport contract\n\nUse `DATABASE_URL` as the sole active database transport input. Reject the presence of:\n\n- `DB_ALLOW_BRIDGE_IN_PROD`\n- `DB_BRIDGE_URL`\n- `DB_FORCE_BRIDGE`\n\nDo not revive a historical bridge or infer current behavior from frozen bridge evidence.\n\n## Read-only default\n\nClassify a database request as `DATABASE_READ` unless it can change data, schema, locks, privileges, sequences, settings, extensions, or deployment state. Treat `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, functions with side effects, temporary schema changes, and maintenance commands as writes or elevated operations.\n\nBefore a production read:\n\n1. Verify the exact Railway target.\n2. Confirm the query purpose, tables, columns, row bound, timeout, and output sensitivity.\n3. Prefer repository-owned diagnostic tools.\n4. Require least-privilege credentials and a read-only transaction when direct SQL is approved.\n5. Avoid selecting payload, credential, personal, or raw vendor columns.\n6. Aggregate or redact results before reporting.\n\nDo not package a generic SQL executor in this skill.\n\n## Write boundary\n\nRequire applicable exact authorization for `DATABASE_WRITE`, distinct from unrelated read/vendor/setup authority. Preserve unchanged authorization already present in the assigned task. Before execution, establish:\n\n- target project, environment, service, database, and schema;\n- exact migration or statement set from the repository;\n- expected rows/objects affected;\n- transaction and lock-timeout posture;\n- backup, snapshot, or logically equivalent rollback source;\n- rollback command and owner;\n- preflight and postflight verification queries;\n- maintenance window or user-impact posture;\n- stop conditions.\n\nDo not use vendor-test authorization, repository push authorization, or a successful read as database-write authority.\n\n## Tooling\n\nUse the repository's canonical migration, adapter, and validation paths. If an approved procedure requires `psql`, `pg_dump`, or `pg_restore`, verify the executable and version first. During authorized setup, install/repair missing tools through permitted routes and retest before reporting the remaining `TOOLING_BLOCKED` result. Preserve explicit platform restrictions; do not replace required tools with ad hoc Python or an HTTP bridge.\n\n## Backup, restore and migration capability\n\nPrepare these as first-class workstation capabilities using the capability map linked from SKILL.md. Resolve the repository-owned procedure and a usable execution host; verify client/server compatibility, permitted target/role, required access, timeouts, capacity, and the private artifact destination and transfer route. A backup needs actual completed capture plus artifact integrity/readback; a restore needs its exact destination, recovery/rollback posture and post-restore verification. Successful SELECT 1 or client version output proves neither. Label an unexecuted operation as prepared or pending, never runtime-validated.\n\nDo not create a production dump, restore, migration or write simply to get a ready label. Prepare all necessary commands and checks, then obtain only any missing task-specific authority. Keep backup contents and production data out of chat and ordinary QA logs. Use existing task/evidence conventions without adding an approval token or universal readiness certificate.\n\n## Execution discipline\n\n1. Capture a redacted preflight and current schema/version identity.\n2. Create or verify the approved rollback source.\n3. Execute once with bounded timeouts.\n4. Stop on the first unexpected row count, lock, warning, or target change.\n5. Run the approved postflight checks.\n6. Record only redacted facts, counts, hashes, and schema identities.\n7. Reconcile uncertain outcomes before any retry.\n\nNever print `DATABASE_URL` or include it in a saved command transcript.\n",
    "77312b5eb86af9f112994a1d018739a4e0f23540b8f850594b79dc3dbdb0292b": "# Evidence, recovery, and cleanup\n\n## Evidence model\n\nSeparate four layers in every report:\n\n1. `OBSERVED`: command output or current external state actually read.\n2. `DERIVED`: a labeled inference from observed facts.\n3. `NOT_RUN`: a requested or relevant check not executed.\n4. `NONCLAIM`: a broader outcome the evidence does not establish.\n\nUse repository-governed statuses only for defined checks. Keep plain operational facts separate from QA status.\n\n## Redaction\n\nNever retain or report:\n\n- API keys, tokens, credentials, private keys, or connection strings;\n- endpoint/base URL values;\n- Railway variable values;\n- birth inputs or personal data;\n- raw vendor request/response bodies;\n- database payload rows unless separately approved and safely transformed.\n\nPrefer variable name plus `SET`, `UNSET`, or `REDACTED`. Redact subprocess output before displaying or saving it.\n\n## Uncertain external state\n\nWhen an external command times out, disconnects, or returns an ambiguous error:\n\n1. Stop automatic retries.\n2. Record the exact command class, target names, start time if known, and redacted failure code.\n3. Query the authoritative read-only state for that action.\n4. Determine whether it completed, partially completed, or did not occur.\n5. Continue only after state is known and remaining authority still covers the next action.\n\nApply this to pushes, pull requests, deployments, restarts, variable changes, vendor calls, database operations, and SSH-key changes.\n\n## Resume\n\nTreat a resumed session as a new observation boundary:\n\n- rediscover the repository and exact HEAD;\n- reread current instructions that govern the task;\n- recheck authentication and target names;\n- inspect previous artifacts for hashes and redacted status only;\n- verify that existing authorization still covers the unchanged task, target, effects and remaining limits; continuation does not expire it, and completed or exhausted live-test scope cannot be reused;\n- reconcile any pending cleanup before new work.\n\n## Cleanup inventory\n\nTrack temporary resources by exact path or non-secret identifier:\n\n- temporary SSH key label/fingerprint and local paths;\n- external output directory;\n- background processes or shells;\n- temporary branches or worktrees created within scope;\n- database transaction/lock state;\n- open-rail child process state.\n\nRemove only resources created by the run. Verify removal. Do not delete an uncertain or user-owned resource merely because its name resembles a temporary item.\n\n## Terminal report template\n\n- Mode / effect class\n- Repository / branch / exact HEAD\n- Target project / environment / service\n- Rails (`closed` or authorized child-only `open`)\n- Checks and governed statuses\n- External effects observed\n- Vendor attempts / database objects / rows written / raw payload retained\n- Artifacts and hashes\n- Cleanup complete or remaining item\n- Blockers\n- Explicit nonclaims\n\nKeep the report self-contained and factual. Never expose implementation secrets while proving that redaction occurred.\n\n## Recovery examples from the CRD alpha\n\nUse these distinctions when the corresponding condition occurs; they add no universal preflight or retry allowance.\n\n- **Polling error after a successful native process:** retrieve the original process's captured exit status and redacted output. An interface cancellation or transport error does not overturn native exit 0. Preserve both observations; do not reinstall or rerun merely to remove the polling error. Leave a deeper unproved cause unknown.\n- **Local helper fails after completed checks:** retain already-captured valid checks, correct the local helper under unchanged scope, and resume its missing operation. Record the helper failure and correction. A pre-execution packaging fault or harmless syntax normalization consumes no formal QA attempt; an actual failed QA execution retains its governed attempt and review route.\n- **Authorized evidence publication fails on one surface:** record the native failure and reconcile remote state first. An alternate supported channel may complete the already authorized write only if it preserves exact target, intended tree/content and publication scope. Verify bytes and resulting identity. Preserve the originally tested state separately from later storage commits. This does not prove that a required native CLI/transport capability has been repaired, and does not authorize a new PR or merge.\n- **Finding-label mismatch:** resolve the original finding from its substantive evidence before correcting a mapping. Preserve prior artifacts, record the explicit ID-to-finding correction and carry it through subsequent reviews. Never reassign a finding merely to match a helper's stale label.\n- **Parameterized test selection:** record selected pytest node identities and reconcile collected/executed members with the approved task coverage. Do not multiply assertion counts into test-case counts or substitute a passing sample for the complete selected set.\n\nKeep Product Owner QA selection, dependency eligibility, native command outcome, evidence persistence, QA review and change closure separate. A successful recovery at one layer does not certify the others.\n",
    "ee22dba7b61b12d26b0ebeb87acfba34c0d2b1b8f69cfc06655ec7829bac1171": "# GitHub and local QA\n\n## Bootstrap sequence\n\n1. Choose an authorized workspace with enough space and no conflicting checkout.\n2. Run `scripts/bootstrap_hde.sh --workspace <path>`.\n3. Let the script verify or clone `amthorn78/glow-hdengine-v2`, create `.venv`, install build prerequisites, runtime and development requirements plus the editable project, then run `pip check` and prove `pytest` readiness. Compare these dependencies with current CI before execution.\n4. Add `--install-tools` only when local CLI installation is requested. The pinned versions in the script are a reproducible baseline, not a claim that they are forever current.\n5. Re-run the doctor after bootstrap.\n\nThe bootstrapper refuses a mismatched origin and a dirty existing checkout. Resolve either condition explicitly; do not overwrite or hide it.\n\n## Complete preparation and repair\n\n- When current main is requested, fetch and fast-forward a clean main checkout, then verify HEAD against the freshly fetched remote. Preserve unrelated dirty work in place and use a separate clean checkout if necessary. The bootstrap script itself does not pull.\n- Diagnose, repair within the user's scope, and functionally retest each missing prerequisite. A successful `--version` must execute the actual CLI; an npm wrapper without its native binary is not installed tooling. CLI authentication and secret-safe child-process variable injection require their own real checks.\n- Use official verified releases and workspace-local installation. Reuse complete verified cached artifacts when available. A canceled or timed-out operation has an uncertain result: inspect its state before a bounded retry. Use the runtime's approved escalation path only if available. Respect explicit access denials; do not bypass them with browser transfers or another transport.\n- Reuse valid authentication or initiate the provider's supported secure sign-in when needed. Never ask for secrets in chat. Complete independent preparation before reporting the exact remaining interaction or runtime access requirement.\n- If the user authorizes repair of this skill's setup controls, use Skill Creator to make and save the narrow repair, retain behavioral/refusal checks, add a regression check for the observed defect, and rerun validation. Do not weaken a safety assertion to obtain PASS. Other skill and application changes require their own scope.\n- Retain completed vendor and database smoke results, request counts and cleanup evidence when resuming setup. Retest only capabilities affected by the repair; do not spend the same live-test authorization again.\n- Report native CLI, connector and remote-console capability separately. Working connector or console access does not prove terminal authentication or variable injection. Finish preparation only when every required capability is verified or an exact remaining blocker is identified; do not label incomplete required tooling ready.\n\n## GitHub connector and Git route\n\nUse this route when native `gh` is unavailable and the task does not require that executable or a CLI-only feature:\n\nIf the requested environment baseline requires native `gh` authentication or Git push, keep those requirements pending even while connector work proceeds. Do not amend the baseline to accept connector access without the user's agreement.\n\n1. Verify the connected GitHub user and the exact repository through authenticated connector reads. Read repository permission metadata separately from transport evidence.\n2. Fetch the named repository through Git's existing permitted transport and compare the resulting branch SHA with the connector's current branch observation. Do not copy connector credentials into Git configuration.\n3. Discover the current connector tools for the actual PR, diff, review and workflow operations. Prove read access on existing records; record write capabilities as available/permission-observed, not mutation-tested. Never create a dummy branch or PR to demonstrate readiness.\n4. Use ordinary local Git for source work and an authorized existing Git transport for publication. If a task specifically needs a local commit pushed and that transport cannot do it, report that exact blocker; do not substitute a connector-created commit with different attribution.\n5. Keep `gh` unavailable in tool results. The controller's native-tool doctor remains truthful; a separately verified connector route can satisfy supported API tasks without changing that doctor's result. Tasks requiring a native executable, an unavailable connector method or unattended CLI automation remain blocked.\n\n## Local QA sequence\n\n1. Export the closed deterministic rails.\n2. Use `<repo>/.venv/bin/python`, not an unrelated interpreter.\n3. Run `<python> -m pytest --version` before pytest-dependent checks.\n4. Inspect current acceptance bindings and applicable CI lanes.\n5. Run the narrowest relevant test or read-only canonical check first.\n6. Expand only when the task requires it.\n7. Preserve exact exit codes and distinguish collection/tooling failure from behavior failure.\n\nPytest availability check only (not a QA or workstation readiness verdict):\n\n```bash\nenv LC_ALL=C LANG=C TZ=UTC SAFE_MODE=1 ALLOW_NETWORK=0 \\\n  <repo>/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --version\n```\n\nNever invent a universal `make test` or full-suite requirement. Use current repository entry points.\n\nFor full workstation preparation, use the capability map linked from SKILL.md. Run actual current closed-rail refusal, isolated mocked open-rail, CLI installation and applicable redaction checks; a pytest version string is only prerequisite evidence. Inspect build, lint, test, container and evidence tools required by the assigned tasks, prepare them and preserve the complete selected QA collection.\n\n## Assigned source development\n\nUnder an actual implementation request and its current Plan/Proceed gates, prepare the task branch or isolated worktree, edit the exact source scope, build and run appropriate checks, then publish only when authorized. Preserve exact candidate commits, review findings and required reviewer ownership. Environment preparation alone does not create an application change, PR or merge task.\n\nThe Linux x86_64 bootstrap uses the official Railway standalone release with a verified digest, avoiding dependency on an npm wrapper. A different version or platform needs release review before changing that pin. An explicit network denial remains a restriction; do not repeat a denied download through another transport. Complete independent Python/workspace repairs outside a blocked bootstrap step. The bootstrap and doctor report only their stated check scopes.\n\n## GitHub authentication and remote safety\n\n- Detect `gh` from `PATH` or `<workspace>/.hde-tools/bin/gh`.\n- Check authentication without printing tokens.\n- If native authentication is absent or expired, prepare `gh`'s supported browser/device login and explicitly ask the user to complete it. A connected GitHub plugin does not authenticate the terminal. Configure supported Git credential-helper integration after successful login and verify it with a non-mutating push dry run; do not create a test commit.\n- Keep the device-login process alive through browser approval and token exchange, using a resumable terminal session. Browser approval alone is incomplete. An earlier successful HDE setup recovered a failed token exchange by restarting the supported login within one continuous permitted terminal operation; inspect authentication state before retrying and never reuse historical activation codes. This history does not establish that a currently denied network operation is permitted.\n- If the native executable or required login transport is unavailable, identify that separate prerequisite before requesting login help. Request the exact permitted installation input or user action needed; never invent a device code or ask for tokens in chat.\n- Use Git's configured credential helper through `gh`; never place a token in a remote URL.\n- Fetch before evaluating divergence.\n- Do not pull into a dirty worktree when incoming paths overlap local changes.\n- Never discard user changes to make a branch current.\n\n## Push procedure\n\n1. Require an explicit push request or equivalent publication authorization.\n2. Confirm current branch, upstream, base, exact outgoing commits, and clean/intentional worktree state.\n3. Run applicable checks against the exact candidate commit.\n4. Push the named branch non-interactively.\n5. Read back the remote branch head and compare it to the local candidate.\n6. Freeze and reconcile if the result is ambiguous.\n\nDo not force-push by default. Do not use broad staging commands in a dirty worktree; stage exact paths.\n\n## Pull request procedure\n\n1. Confirm the head repository, branch, base branch, title, and body.\n2. Summarize observed tests and explicit nonclaims.\n3. Check for an existing pull request from the same branch before creating another.\n4. Create the pull request only when authorized.\n5. Return its URL and observed check state.\n\nTreat pending and unavailable checks as pending and unavailable. Do not infer mergeability from local success alone.\n",
    "f07d139935e3fede8f1ea506ec20656d5aad8d487385aef2ba43a1e80eb91554": "# OpenRails vendor test\n\n## Authorized test envelope\n\nUse this mode only for a live, synthetic compatibility comparison. Require applicable unspent task authorization that identifies:\n\n- Railway project `ample-illumination`;\n- environment `production`;\n- service `glow-hdengine-v2`;\n- exactly one synthetic pair;\n- no more than one HTTP attempt per person and two total attempts;\n- no database construction or writes;\n- no deployment or configuration mutation;\n- no raw vendor payload retention;\n- an external empty output directory.\n\nDo not treat a login, completed prior test or script acknowledgment as new authority. Reuse valid authorization for the same unfinished operation; do not reset its attempts or repeat an exhausted envelope.\n\n## Native-path-first preflight\n\n1. Inspect the exact repository HEAD.\n2. Inspect `python -m engine.cli showcompat --help` and the current vendor route implementation.\n3. Prefer a current native path only if it supports the configured route, forces dry-run/zero database I/O, bounds retries to one attempt per person, and emits only the public compatibility payload.\n4. Use the bundled v2 adapter runner when the configured v2 chart route is not supported by native `showcompat` under those bounds.\n5. Stop with `TOOLING_BLOCKED` if neither path satisfies the envelope. Do not improvise an ungoverned HTTP call.\n\nThe current skill revision implements the governed `recommended_v2_chart` adapter path and the governed legacy BodyGraph payload path with a pinned retry profile of one attempt.\n\n## Execution\n\nAfter target and environment checks succeed, run:\n\n```bash\npython <skill-dir>/scripts/hde_devops.py openrails-vendor \\\n  --repo <repo> \\\n  --output-dir <external-empty-directory> \\\n  --ack OPENRAILS_VENDOR_SYNTHETIC_PRODUCTION\n```\n\nThe controller injects Railway variables into the child process and opens rails only there. The runner embeds deterministic synthetic inputs; do not print or log them.\n\n## Required output posture\n\nAccept only:\n\n- `compat.json`: canonical public compatibility bytes;\n- `run_summary.json`: redacted execution summary.\n\nRequire file mode `0600`, canonical JSON with one trailing LF, and no output inside the repository. The summary must include:\n\n- route family and adapter/path;\n- vendor requests attempted and completed;\n- compatibility SHA-256;\n- `database_constructed: false`;\n- `database_rows_written: 0`;\n- `raw_vendor_payload_retained: false`;\n- governed terminal status.\n\nDo not retain request bodies, response bodies, credentials, base URLs, birth inputs, or raw chart payloads.\n\n## Failure and retry\n\n- Do not retry automatically after any request was attempted.\n- Treat a timeout or lost response as an attempted call.\n- Preserve only a redacted failure code; do not include exception messages that may contain URLs or payload fragments.\n- Require fresh authorization before another live run.\n- Report a partial completion as failure or blocker, never as `PASS`.\n",
    "09e39a875ba415a27664db161491bd097d8a09377b8182cce93c2e98480992fa": "# Railway and secrets\n\n## Canonical target\n\nResolve and verify these names on every Railway-backed action:\n\n| Field | Expected name |\n|---|---|\n| Project | `ample-illumination` |\n| Environment | `production` |\n| Service | `glow-hdengine-v2` |\n\nDo not store or depend on provider IDs in the skill. If the user selects another target, require an explicit target change and restate its risk.\n\n## Authentication\n\n1. Prefer the Railway CLI's normal browser login when human interaction is available.\n2. Use browserless/device flow only when the environment truly cannot open a browser.\n3. Use the authenticated browser skill only as a fallback after the normal CLI flow actually fails and the task requires interaction.\n4. Treat authentication as identity proof, not authorization for a production action.\n\nWhen native credentials are absent or expired, prepare the supported CLI login and explicitly ask the user to complete its secure browser/device flow. Do not keep substituting an existing Console login for missing native credentials. If the binary or login transport is unavailable, first identify the exact installation input or permitted access action needed to start that flow. Never fabricate an activation code. Recheck native identity and scoped child-process injection after login.\n\nNever ask the user to paste a long-lived Railway token into chat or a repository file.\n\nKeep the supported login process alive until its token exchange finishes; the browser's approval screen alone is insufficient. Use a resumable terminal session, check authentication after interruptions, and generate a new code only through a new supported login when necessary. Recovered historical activation codes are expired evidence, never usable credentials.\n\nDiscover available official/provider integrations before claiming Railway access is unavailable. If a Railway integration is available but unconnected, request its supported account connection and inspect its advertised operations after connection. Verify actual target access and execution behavior; integration installation or login does not prove CLI authentication, local injection, arbitrary SQL, backup/restore or deployment readiness. Do not use a new integration to repeat an explicitly denied operation through another transport.\n\n## Secret injection\n\nUse `railway run` to inject variables into one child command. Do not create `.env` files, shell profile exports, checked-in secret files, or command lines containing secret values.\n\nExpected active variable names:\n\n- `DATABASE_URL`\n- `HD_API_BASE_URL`\n- `HD_API_KEY`\n- `GEO_API_KEY`\n- `APP_ENV`\n- `SAFE_MODE`\n- `ALLOW_NETWORK`\n\nExclude legacy `HD_API_SECRET`. Reject these retired database keys by presence, even when empty:\n\n- `DB_ALLOW_BRIDGE_IN_PROD`\n- `DB_BRIDGE_URL`\n- `DB_FORCE_BRIDGE`\n\nUse `scripts/hde_devops.py railway-env-check` to report only names and `SET`/`UNSET`. Do not use Railway variable-list JSON or key/value output because it includes raw values.\n\n## Target verification\n\nRun `scripts/hde_devops.py railway-target` before each live operation. Resolve one matching project, one accessible environment and one service, and verify that the service instance belongs to that environment. Matching words elsewhere in JSON are insufficient. Retain current IDs for the single action, pass those IDs explicitly, and compare injected child identities. Stop on missing, ambiguous or different objects.\n\nAvoid relying on a linked project in the repository. Resolve names then pass the verified project, environment and service IDs to each command.\n\n## Assigned Railway operations and recovery\n\nFor a container, deployment, restart or recovery task, inspect the actual supported command and exact target, required permissions, candidate/deployed source and runtime, expected effects, logs, finite completion checks and rollback target. Execute within the existing task authorization; finish preparation and a reviewable operation before requesting any uncovered authority. Read back actual completion, health and relevant release identity. Do not deploy, restart or alter provider configuration merely to prove preflight readiness.\n\nUse the workstation capability map for the complete access/tooling requirements. A successful health check, Console command or local injection is evidence for that operation only. Record unavailable native or unattended behavior explicitly. Reuse completed smoke evidence when its facts remain applicable.\n\n## Authenticated Railway Console route\n\nWhen the native Railway CLI is unavailable, an existing permitted Railway Console can execute supported remote tasks. Use Browser only under its own skill and plugin/network boundaries. This route runs commands inside the selected deployment; it does not install a local CLI or provide local `railway run` injection.\n\nKeep this as a partial capability when the user requested a fully configured native workstation. Native authentication and local injection stay pending until actually restored; do not change the acceptance criterion to declare the environment ready.\n\n1. Resolve the live project, production environment, service and deployment through the visible authenticated UI. Require the console to show Connected. Do not create SSH keys or change account access as a default recovery step.\n2. Inspect the container's interpreter and deployment/source identity before sending a task. Verify non-secret Railway identity variables against the UI and the task's expected target; keep deployed code separate from local main and Python versions.\n3. Start each ordinary diagnostic with explicit C/C/UTC and closed rails in the child. Report required provider variables only as SET/UNSET, reject retired DB flags, and capture a structured result plus exit code. The container already receives service variables; do not export them to this workspace.\n4. Use the inspected repository command or sanctioned runner for the exact task. Keep vendor request limits, no-DB vendor behavior, deadlines, serialization and cleanup unchanged. Preserve completed live smoke results when only connectivity or tooling is being repaired.\n5. Read completion and output from the actual terminal. Reconcile timeouts before retrying. An input echo or Connected label alone does not prove command success. Clean exact temporary files when required and verify return to closed defaults.\n6. Claim only the proven remote capability. A task requiring local production variables, a native Railway CLI feature, unattended terminal automation or a different candidate runtime remains blocked unless its own permitted route is verified. Do not download denied binaries through the console or browser, tunnel local traffic, or change platform restrictions.\n\n## Rail handling\n\n- Force `SAFE_MODE=1` and `ALLOW_NETWORK=0` for production-variable probes and local commands that do not require network.\n- Set `SAFE_MODE=0` and `ALLOW_NETWORK=1` only inside the authorized vendor child process.\n- Do not open rails for database reads, writes, deployments, SSH, or variable operations merely because a vendor test was authorized.\n- Return to closed rails in the parent process.\n\n## Temporary SSH access\n\n1. Require explicit authorization for one target and purpose.\n2. Generate a dedicated temporary key outside the repository with a clear label.\n3. Register only the public key.\n4. Use the exact private key path only for the authorized session.\n5. Remove the remote key and local private/public files when finished.\n6. Verify remote removal and report cleanup.\n\nNever display private key material. Freeze if creation or deletion has an ambiguous result.\n",
    "2ff70f201774a765d5ae0d58b30d963048590fb52e3cb122b09a852d3593ace6": "# Repository contract\n\n## Source precedence\n\n1. Read the repository-root `AGENTS.md` completely.\n2. Follow current PF Canon where `AGENTS.md` routes the task; apply the documented PF10 precedence where it speaks.\n3. Treat checked-in source, schemas, CLI help, CI, and canonical tools as current implementation evidence.\n4. Treat historical QA packets and frozen artifacts as capture-time evidence, not present capability.\n5. Treat this reference as a navigation aid only. If it conflicts with the repository, follow the repository.\n\n## Scope boundary\n\nOperate only `glow-hdengine-v2`. Do not bootstrap or configure the full Glow application. Do not assume frontend, identity, billing, messaging, or unrelated services are in scope.\n\nUse the expected origin `amthorn78/glow-hdengine-v2`. Accept a fork only when the user identifies it explicitly; record both the fork and its upstream relationship.\n\n## Deterministic default\n\nRun local QA and canonical read-only checks with:\n\n```text\nLC_ALL=C LANG=C TZ=UTC SAFE_MODE=1 ALLOW_NETWORK=0\n```\n\nOpen rails only for an individually authorized governed action. Return to closed rails immediately afterward.\n\n## Protected surfaces\n\n- Do not modify `docs/pfcanon/**` except under the exact repository-defined Product Owner exception.\n- Do not hand-edit generated or governed evidence.\n- Do not put ad hoc QA output in the repository root.\n- Do not regenerate current evidence unless the task explicitly authorizes the canonical writer.\n- Do not update dependencies, lockfiles, release identity, deployment configuration, or schemas as an incidental setup step.\n\n## Read-first checklist\n\n- Resolve repository root, origin, branch, HEAD, and worktree state.\n- Inspect `AGENTS.md` and any more-specific agent instructions.\n- Identify the current command surface from `python -m engine.cli --help` and subcommand help.\n- Inspect the relevant current tests and canonical tool before running or changing it.\n- Inspect applicable CI lanes before claiming local parity with CI.\n- Classify unavailable inputs as blockers rather than silently skipping them.\n\n## Claims discipline\n\nUse only the repository's governed statuses:\n\n- `PASS`: the defined check ran and its observed behavior satisfied the criterion.\n- `FAIL_BEHAVIOR`: the check ran and behavior contradicted the criterion.\n- `FAIL_TOOLING`: the runner or tooling failed after prerequisites were present.\n- `TOOLING_BLOCKED`: a required dependency, authorization, target, or locus was unavailable.\n- `PARKED`: the task was intentionally deferred with scope and reason recorded.\n\nNever convert `NOT RUN`, absent evidence, a dry run, a historical result, or a successful prerequisite into `PASS`.\n",
    "b6f9f9d869978a37fc16b3f5d5f42d652cf3b985fff351cd611f29d35bdcb281": "# HDE workstation capabilities\n\n## Required outcome\n\nPrepare practical GitHub Codespaces equivalence for the Product Owner's HDE development, DevOps and QA workflow. Cover performing the actual tasks and retaining their required evidence. A website, login, executable or successful connectivity query cannot establish the whole workstation's readiness.\n\nFor the full workstation baseline, preserve native Git, gh and Railway installation/authentication, Git publication transport, repository-compatible Python and complete CI dependencies, local Railway variable injection, and usable database tooling. Keep an explicitly required command, candidate commit, local context or evidence writer as a requirement. A supported alternate surface counts only for the specific operations it demonstrably supports. Do not silently replace the requested baseline with a smaller one.\n\n## Prepare, repair and prove\n\n1. Resolve current instructions and remote main; use a clean checkout, protect other sessions' work and record the tested commit. Preparation does not change approved task lineage.\n2. Install/repair missing supported tools, dependencies, PATH, virtual environment and credential integration. Verify actual executable behavior, package compatibility and current repository-supported QA smoke. Inspect commands before use.\n3. Reuse valid authentication. Otherwise start supported secure browser/device login and ask the Product Owner to complete its displayed approval. Distinguish missing binaries, expired credentials, target permissions and transport restrictions. Never request secrets in chat or invent an activation code.\n4. Execute applicable non-mutating checks below. Live vendor/database diagnostics require existing exact authorization. Preserve spent request counts on continuation; do not repeat completed live checks to repair unrelated tooling.\n5. Repair setup defects and retest affected capabilities; continue independent preparation when one operation is blocked. Respect an explicit runtime denial, record its reason and identify the permitted prerequisite needed. A canceled approval alone does not prove permanent provider denial.\n6. Keep setup incomplete while a required operation lacks a usable route. Separately identify tooling/access prepared for a later authorized task whose actual mutation and result remain untested. A bounded task may proceed on its own sufficient capabilities; a full-workstation claim may not omit gaps.\n\n## Capability and evidence map\n\n| Capability | Required preparation and evidence | Claim limit |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Source/development | Fresh remote-main comparison, clean correct-origin checkout, source/build tools, task branch when assigned, exact candidate diff/commit | Later source changes require relevant rechecks |\n| GitHub/Git/PR | Usable native gh, authenticated repo/PR/check reads, credential helper, Git fetch, non-mutating push dry run, permission evidence | Dry run is not publication; assigned push/PR requires remote readback and exact identity |\n| QA/evidence | Complete runtime/build/dev/editable dependencies, pip check, installed CLI, actual closed/mock-open tests, assigned collection and canonical writer/validator availability | Smoke is not full QA, hosted CI, acceptance or closeout |\n| Railway/runtime | Native identity, related target objects, local child injection and rails, actual remote completion/exit, runtime/source/release identity, relevant health/log access | Connected is not executed; deployed code and local main remain separate |\n| Live OpenRails | Exact synthetic scope, bounded attempts/deadlines, supported route, real completion, public serialization/hash, database/retention facts, return to closed defaults | Adapter success does not prove another CLI; no automatic repetition |\n| Database reads | Direct PostgreSQL, allowed target/schema/role identity, compatible clients/driver, bounded read-only diagnostic and task-specific access evidence | SELECT 1 proves connectivity, not schema access or write grants |\n| Changes/migrations | Repository-owned command, executables, target/objects, available grant evidence, transaction/lock/deadline posture, recovery source, postflight and task authority | Prepare the operation before remaining approval; no speculative production writes |\n| Backups/restores | Compatible pg_dump/pg_restore or governed provider mechanism, execution host, scoped source, private durable destination, capacity/transfer route, integrity/readback and exact restore target/verification | Tool versions are not a usable backup or successful restore. No dumps in chat, public links or ordinary QA logs |\n| Deployment/recovery | Exact candidate/target, supported deploy/restart/log/status commands, access, health checks and rollback target/procedure | Preflight does not deploy; assigned actions require actual completion/postflight |\n| Durable handoff | Authorized readable sources, task/Plan identity, results/limits, evidence writer/destination, cleanup and recovery owner | Saved guidance or relay delivery is not runtime proof |\n\nUse existing governed statuses for defined checks and plain language for overall setup. Record each required capability's command/procedure, observed result, local/remote surface, relevant identity, evidence and remaining prerequisite in the existing report/handoff. No new universal approval token, required plan artifact or workflow stage is created.\n\n## Scope and continuation\n\nExisting authorization persists for its unchanged task, target, effects and remaining limits. Recheck applicability on resume; ask again only for uncovered, changed, revoked or exhausted scope. Full workstation preparation does not authorize an unassigned production migration, backup/export, restore, deployment, PR, merge, SSH key or governed publication. Prepare capabilities and reviewable commands without exercising destructive effects to obtain a green status.\n\nKeep ordinary processes under C/C/UTC and closed rails; isolate authorized open children. Track and clean exact temporary resources while preserving tools and normal authenticated sessions. Reconcile uncertain effects before retrying. Keep environment preparation separate from another role's approval or orchestration.\n\nResolve shared guidance by name: NON-CANONICAL-HDE-Workstation-Readiness-and-Operations in Drive Glow / Ops / Access & Infrastructure, and Preflight in Notion AI Prompts / DevOps. This skill remains self-contained; these references introduce no hidden runtime dependency.\n\n",
    "b1dca102c3582e9f15bc049a2926eae3edfc618b859f84a8ad1c2eec1080cfeb": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\nset -euo pipefail\n\nexport LC_ALL=C\nexport LANG=C\nexport TZ=UTC\nexport SAFE_MODE=1\nexport ALLOW_NETWORK=0\nexport PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1\n\nEXPECTED_REPO=\"amthorn78/glow-hdengine-v2\"\nGH_VERSION_DEFAULT=\"2.98.0\"\nRAILWAY_VERSION_DEFAULT=\"5.45.7\"\n\nworkspace=\"\"\nrepo_dir=\"\"\npython_cmd=\"${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}\"\ninstall_tools=0\nskip_deps=0\nno_clone=0\ngh_version=\"${GH_VERSION:-${GH_VERSION_DEFAULT}}\"\nrailway_version=\"${RAILWAY_VERSION:-${RAILWAY_VERSION_DEFAULT}}\"\n\nusage() {\n  cat <<'EOF'\nUsage: bootstrap_hde.sh --workspace DIR [options]\n\nOptions:\n  --repo-dir DIR              Checkout path (default: WORKSPACE/glow-hdengine-v2)\n  --python COMMAND            Python used to create .venv (default: python3)\n  --install-tools             Install missing gh and Railway CLIs without sudo\n  --gh-version VERSION        Pinned gh version for installation\n  --railway-version VERSION   Pinned Railway CLI version for installation\n  --skip-deps                 Do not install Python dependencies\n  --no-clone                  Require an existing checkout\n  -h, --help                  Show this help\n\nThe script refuses mismatched origins and dirty existing checkouts. It never\nauthenticates, opens engine rails, writes secrets, pulls, deploys, or mutates a\nRailway target.\nEOF\n}\n\nfail() {\n  printf '%s\\n' \"$1\" >&2\n  exit \"${2:-2}\"\n}\n\nneed_arg() {\n  [[ \"$#\" -ge 2 && -n \"$2\" ]] || fail \"MISSING_ARGUMENT:$1\"\n}\n\nwhile [[ \"$#\" -gt 0 ]]; do\n  case \"$1\" in\n    --workspace)\n      need_arg \"$@\"\n      workspace=\"$2\"\n      shift 2\n      ;;\n    --repo-dir)\n      need_arg \"$@\"\n      repo_dir=\"$2\"\n      shift 2\n      ;;\n    --python)\n      need_arg \"$@\"\n      python_cmd=\"$2\"\n      shift 2\n      ;;\n    --install-tools)\n      install_tools=1\n      shift\n      ;;\n    --gh-version)\n      need_arg \"$@\"\n      gh_version=\"$2\"\n      shift 2\n      ;;\n    --railway-version)\n      need_arg \"$@\"\n      railway_version=\"$2\"\n      shift 2\n      ;;\n    --skip-deps)\n      skip_deps=1\n      shift\n      ;;\n    --no-clone)\n      no_clone=1\n      shift\n      ;;\n    -h|--help)\n      usage\n      exit 0\n      ;;\n    *)\n      fail \"UNKNOWN_ARGUMENT:$1\"\n      ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\n[[ -n \"${workspace}\" ]] || fail \"WORKSPACE_REQUIRED\"\nmkdir -p \"${workspace}\"\nworkspace=\"$(cd \"${workspace}\" && pwd -P)\"\n[[ \"${workspace}\" != \"/\" ]] || fail \"WORKSPACE_TOO_BROAD\"\n\nif [[ -z \"${repo_dir}\" ]]; then\n  repo_dir=\"${workspace}/glow-hdengine-v2\"\nelif [[ \"${repo_dir}\" != /* ]]; then\n  repo_dir=\"${workspace}/${repo_dir}\"\nfi\n\ntools_root=\"${workspace}/.hde-tools\"\ntools_bin=\"${tools_root}/bin\"\nmkdir -p \"${tools_bin}\"\nexport PATH=\"${tools_bin}:${PATH}\"\n\ncommand -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail \"TOOLING_BLOCKED:GIT_MISSING\" 3\ncommand -v \"${python_cmd}\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail \"TOOLING_BLOCKED:PYTHON_MISSING\" 3\n\n\"${python_cmd}\" - <<'PY'\nimport sys\nif sys.version_info < (3, 10):\n    raise SystemExit(\"TOOLING_BLOCKED:PYTHON_3_10_REQUIRED\")\nPY\n\ninstall_gh() (\n  [[ \"$(uname -s)\" == \"Linux\" ]] || fail --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -fsSLo \"${tmp_dir}/${archive}\" \\\n    \"https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v${gh_version}/${archive}\"\n  curl --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120     "4da572c959c814417138b439f71402db46dd2aa7f33858e8c8b548b29d529470": "---\nname: glow-merged-change-attribution-lock\ndescription: Resolve and validate the landed repository attribution of one merged PR or an ordered merged-PR lineage as temporary, read-only evidence for an active PR review. Separate attributable changes from later divergence without mutating the repository or making QA, PF, Ops, acceptance, repair, drainage, or closure decisions. Use when a Glow PR reviewer needs an in-flight attribution bundle. Do not use for implementation, planning, PR merge, repository repair, QA execution, Ops, or Change Flow orchestration.\n---\n\n# Glow Merged Change Attribution Lock\n\n`MERGED_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTION_SKILL_REVISION: 1.2.0`\n\n`MERGED_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTION_INTERFACE_ID: GLOW-MERGED-CHANGE-ATTRIBUTION-082826.3`\n\n`MERGED_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTION_ARTIFACT_VERSION: GLOW-MERGED-CHANGE-ATTRIBUTION-082826.3`\n\n`ADOPTION_POSTURE: SHADOW_VALIDATION`\n\nProduce a read-only attribution bundle for one merged change or one explicitly ordered merged-change lineage. The bundle is temporary evidence for the active PR-review task. It is not a durable project record, new infrastructure, or downstream authority.\n\nThis skill is standalone. It is not a Flowmaster specialization, does not invoke Change Flow, and does not alter existing prompts. A reviewer uses the validated bundle as one additional evidence layer while retaining every native review guard.\n\n## Inputs\n\nRequire:\n\n- `MERGED_CHANGE_IDS`: one merged PR identity or an exact oldest-to-newest ordered list.\n- `REPO_ACCESS`: a local Git repository path or an authorized read-only repository connector.\n\nAccept when supplied or derive only from unambiguous repository evidence:\n\n- `COMPARISON_REF`: the exact branch, tag, or commit whose resolved SHA defines the evidence cutoff.\n\nAccept optionally:\n\n- `EXPECTED_REPOSITORY_ID`\n- `EXPECTED_REPOSITORY_SOURCE_BINDING_SHA256` when a local repository identity must be matched independently of its display name\n- `ATTRIBUTION_RUN_KEY`\n- direct PR base/head references, merge commit or landed range, merge method, and authoritative merged-status pointers\n\nNever request or require an artifact store. Never infer lineage order from PR number, title, timestamp alone, or similarity. Never treat an open, closed-unmerged, or merely referenced change as merged. A change proven historically merged remains historically merged if a later commit reverts it; classify that revert as interstage or later non-lineage committed divergence rather than erasing the landed attribution.\n\n## Access modes and read-only invariant\n\nUse exactly one mode:\n\n- `LOCAL_GIT`: inspect a supplied local repository with observational Git commands and filesystem reads.\n- `CONNECTOR`: inspect repository and PR metadata through an authorized read-only connector. State that local worktree evidence is unavailable.\n\nIn `LOCAL_GIT`, capture outer and inner before/after snapshots containing sanitized repository identity and source kind, a domain-separated SHA-256 binding of the exact raw source, `HEAD`, the resolved comparison SHA when available, index/worktree status, and untracked-path inventory. Cross-bind the outer-before, initially resolved, inner-before, inner-after, and outer-after identities; an ABA identity change is still a mutation. Fingerprint independently observable repository state even if comparison-ref resolution fails. Require `HEAD` to equal the comparison SHA before classifying worktree divergence; do not checkout another ref to make it match. If the current worktree is not based on the comparison state, stop with `BLOCKED: CURRENT_COMPARISON_STATE_UNAVAILABLE`. Controller-owned dimensions must otherwise match byte-for-byte. A changed or internally inconsistent snapshot stops with `BLOCKED: READ_ONLY_INVARIANT_VIOLATED` and cannot produce a validated artifact.\n\nAllowed local Git operations include `rev-parse`, `rev-list`, `show`, `log`, `diff`, `diff-tree`, `merge-base`, `status`, `ls-files`, `config --get`, `hash-object --no-filters` without `-w`, and `patch-id --stable`. Every Git invocation must remove inherited `GIT_*` variables, disable optional locks, lazy fetch, replace objects, terminal prompts, `core.fsmonitor`, `core.untrackedCache`, pagers, external diff, and text conversion as applicable, and isolate global/system configuration. Sanitize credentials, query values, and fragments from emitted repository sources. Do not run checkout, switch, reset, clean, apply, am, commit, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, stash, tag, branch mutation, push, fetch, worktree mutation, configuration writes, or `hash-object -w`. If required refs or objects are absent, use an authorized read-only connector or stop; any repository update occurs outside this skill and requires a new pinned run.\n\nUse [scripts/collect_git_attribution.py](scripts/collect_git_attribution.py) when its local evidence manifest can be completed. It prints evidence to stdout and must not write the repository. Its JSON supports the temporary Markdown artifact and is subject to the same in-flight lifecycle.\n\n## Evidence procedure\n\nRead [references/merge-method-semantics.md](references/merge-method-semantics.md) before reconciling merge, squash, or rebase behavior. Then:\n\n1. Resolve exact repository identity and compare `EXPECTED_REPOSITORY_ID` when supplied.\n2. Resolve `COMPARISON_REF` once and pin its exact commit SHA.\n3. Require authoritative merged status and a source pointer for every change.\n4. Determine `MERGE`, `SQUASH`, `REBASE`, or `UNKNOWN`, and resolve every SHA-named input to a full pinned object ID. A merge binds the direct head to an actual non-first parent; a squash binds exactly one one-parent landing commit whose parent is the pre-stage commit; a rebase binds a linear, no-merge `pre..post` range.\n5. Resolve the pre-lineage baseline.\n6. Resolve each exact pre/post stage and landed delta in declared order.\n7. Reconcile the direct PR and landed deltas as `EXACT`, `EQUIVALENT`, or `CONFLICT`.\n8. Compute the final attributable stage bundle only from canonical JSON binding the ordered change IDs, pre/post object IDs, and landed delta hashes. Do not label the raw first-pre-to-last-post historical span as attributable when it contains interstage non-lineage commits.\n9. Record interstage and later non-lineage committed divergence separately through the comparison SHA.\n10. Capture staged, unstaged, and untracked worktree-only divergence, or mark it unavailable in connector mode.\n11. Mark unsupported propositions `UNPROVEN`; never convert an unproven required proposition into validation.\n12. Write the artifact and evidence manifest only inside one automatically created, task-owned temporary directory outside the target repository. Validate them there before review use.\n13. Deliver the complete validated artifact to the active PR reviewer, then discard the task-owned temporary directory after the review finishes.\n\nEach stage must prove chronological reachability: pre-stage is an ancestor of post-stage, post-stage is reachable from the comparison SHA, and an earlier post-stage is an ancestor of the next pre-stage. When intervening commits exist, the next stage manifest must declare `interstage_classification = NON_LINEAGE_COMMITTED_DIVERGENCE` and a nonempty `interstage_evidence_pointer`; otherwise stop on lineage conflict. Keep those commits outside the attributable stage-delta bundle and label any inclusive historical-span delta as non-attributable context.\n\n`EXACT` requires matching verified binary-diff SHA-256 values and records patch-ID fields as `NOT_USED`. `EQUIVALENT` requires different byte hashes but matching nonempty stable patch IDs produced by the same declared Git object algorithm. `CONFLICT` means both deltas exist and disagree. Missing direct or landed evidence is `UNPROVEN`, not `EQUIVALENT`.\n\nThe scope is `HISTORICAL_LANDED_DELTA`. A later revert does not erase historical merge proof. Record it only as interstage or later committed divergence, and use `CURRENT_EFFECT_STATUS = NOT_ASSESSED` unless separate authoritative evidence proves the effect at the comparison cutoff. Never infer a revert from commit-message text.\n\n## Stop precedence\n\n`BLOCKED: READ_ONLY_INVARIANT_VIOLATED` preempts every other outcome when repository state changes during collection.\n\nOtherwise return only the first applicable stop:\n\n1. `MISSING INPUT: MERGED_CHANGE_IDS`\n2. `AMBIGUOUS INPUT: MERGED_CHANGE_IDS`\n3. `MISSING INPUT: REPO_ACCESS`\n4. `AMBIGUOUS INPUT: REPOSITORY_IDENTITY`\n5. `CONFLICTING INPUT: EXPECTED_REPOSITORY_ID`\n6. `MISSING INPUT: COMPARISON_REF`\n7. `AMBIGUOUS INPUT: COMPARISON_REF`\n8. `AMBIGUOUS INPUT: ATTRIBUTION_RUN_KEY`\n9. `MISSING INPUT: COMPLETE_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE`\n10. `BLOCKED: CHANGE_NOT_MERGED`\n11. `BLOCKED: ATTRIBUTABLE_LANDED_RANGE_UNRESOLVED`\n12. `CONFLICTING INPUT: LINEAGE_ORDER`\n13. `CONFLICTING INPUT: PR_VS_LANDED_DELTA`\n14. `BLOCKED: CURRENT_COMPARISON_STATE_UNAVAILABLE`\n\nDo not emit a validated artifact after a stop. A temporary diagnostic must use `ATTRIBUTION_STATUS = BLOCKED` and cannot be supplied as validated evidence.\n\n## In-flight artifact and validation\n\nRead [references/attribution-interface.md](references/attribution-interface.md) before authoring or validating the artifact.\n\nUse this exact filename inside the task-owned temporary directory:\n\n`MCA-{ATTRIBUTION_RUN_KEY}-Attribution.md`\n\nAn operator-supplied run key must match `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, be at most 64 ASCII characters, and contain no whitespace, dot, repeated/trailing hyphen, separator, traversal, Unicode lookalike, or percent-encoded separator. When omitted, compute `RUN_BINDING_SHA256` over compact sorted UTF-8 JSON containing the interface ID, canonical repository ID, and exact ordered change-ID list, deliberately excluding the comparison SHA, then use `auto-` plus its first 24 lowercase hexadecimal characters as the run key. The collector returns the full binding hash, key source, and exact filename. Never interpolate an unvalidated value into a path. The key scopes one in-flight review bundle; it is not a durable identity.\n\nCreate the temporary directory with the environment's secure temporary-directory facility. It must be outside the target repository and owned by this run. Never follow a symlink, accept a different basename, or read/write outside that exact directory.\n\nDo not save, upload, copy, register, or promote the artifact or its manifest to ChatGPT Library, Google Drive, Notion, the target repository, a PR comment, a durable artifact store, or any other long-lived location unless the operator separately authorizes that exact publication. This skill requires no persistence receipt, fetchback, version history, registry entry, or stable artifact ID.\n\nRun:\n\n`python3 scripts/validate_attribution_artifact.py <artifact-path> --transient-root <task-owned-temporary-directory> --evidence-manifest <collector-evidence.json>`\n\nA successful artifact ends exactly `END MERGED CHANGE ATTRIBUTION: VALIDATED`. A blocked diagnostic ends exactly `END MERGED CHANGE ATTRIBUTION: BLOCKED`.\n\nAfter validation, provide the reviewer the complete artifact bytes within the active task. If the reviewer runs in the same environment, use the task-local file. If an already-active relay can transfer a task-scoped attachment, it may do so without becoming a dependency of this skill. Do not place a filesystem path into an ID-only prompt field. If complete transient delivery is unavailable, omit the bundle and let the reviewer run natively.\n\nThe reviewer should include a concise `Merged-change attribution` section in its own review output containing the comparison SHA, attributed change IDs, reconciliation result, later/worktree divergence, and any unproven item or stop. That review output is the retained record if the surrounding workflow retains one; the underlying artifact does not need to survive.\n\nWhen the reviewer finishes, remove only the exact run-owned temporary directory after confirming it is outside the repository and contains no followed symlinks. If safe explicit cleanup is unavailable, leave it only to the environment's normal transient expiry. Never promote it for retention.\n\n## Existing reviewer compatibility\n\nThis skill supplements, but never replaces, native PR-review evidence and guards. It does not create a prompt field, runtime requirement, or prompt-local skill dependency. It does not edit migrated prompts.\n\nDuring `SHADOW_VALIDATION`, compare the skill result with the reviewer's native result in the same review task. Record any material discrepancy and its disposition in the review output, not in a separate permanent attribution registry. Adoption requires a separate operator decision after representative live comparisons.\n\n## Maintenance\n\nRead [references/validation-matrix.md](references/validation-matrix.md) for deterministic fixture coverage and shadow criteria. After any skill or helper change, run:\n\n`python3 scripts/run_fixture_tests.py`\n\nAlso run the bundled collector and artifact adversarial suites when present. All deterministic, structural, adversarial, and suite-wide checks must pass before publication.\n\nIncrement the skill revision for material behavior changes. Increment the interface/artifact version only for a breaking receiver-facing schema change. Keep repository mutation, durable evidence infrastructure, and downstream governance decisions out of this skill.\n",
    "ccf8afd5c7bdc8f6369155f81e373f96f61383d681a05d43ea8c3ad163d0e444": "interface:\n  display_name: Glow Merged Change Attribution Lock\n  short_description: Produce temporary PR-review attribution evidence\n  default_prompt: Use $glow-merged-change-attribution-lock to produce a temporary,\n    read-only merged-change attribution bundle for the active PR review.\n  icon_small: assets/icon.svg\n  icon_large: assets/icon.svg\npolicy:\n  products:\n  - chatgpt\n  - codex\n  - api\n  - atlas\n  allow_implicit_invocation: true\n",
