    "8f987b006e8c17858f1bbe30d6d07800b507405ca34e2b020b37a141be693355": "# Merged Change Attribution interface\n\n## Identity\n\n- Interface ID: `GLOW-MERGED-CHANGE-ATTRIBUTION-082826.3`\n- Artifact version: `GLOW-MERGED-CHANGE-ATTRIBUTION-082826.3`\n- Producer revision: `1.2.0`\n- Adoption posture: `SHADOW_VALIDATION`\n\nVersion `.3` replaces the durable-artifact contract with a temporary PR-review evidence contract. Earlier artifacts remain historical but are not eligible as current validated evidence. No receiver prompt changes: the reviewer receives the complete artifact only within the active task and retains its native guards and fallback.\n\n## Required title and header\n\nThe first line is exactly:\n\n```text\n# MERGED CHANGE ATTRIBUTION EVIDENCE\n```\n\nUse these header fields exactly once and in this order:\n\n```text\nInterface Version: GLOW-MERGED-CHANGE-ATTRIBUTION-082826.3\nARTIFACT_KIND = MERGED_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTION\nARTIFACT_PROFILE = SINGLE_PR | ORDERED_PR_LINEAGE | UNRESOLVED\nATTRIBUTION_STATUS = VALIDATED | BLOCKED\nFIRST_STOP = NONE | <one exact allowed stop>\nADOPTION_POSTURE = SHADOW_VALIDATION\nPRODUCER_SKILL_REVISION = 1.2.0\nATTRIBUTION_RUN_KEY = <safe run key> | UNRESOLVED\nRUN_BINDING_SHA256 = <64 lowercase hexadecimal characters> | UNRESOLVED\nARTIFACT_FILENAME = MCA-<run-key>-Attribution.md | UNRESOLVED\nARTIFACT_LIFECYCLE = IN_FLIGHT_ONLY\nCONSUMER_SCOPE = PR_REVIEW_TASK\nRETENTION_POLICY = DISCARD_AFTER_REVIEW\nACCESS_MODE = LOCAL_GIT | CONNECTOR | UNRESOLVED\nREPOSITORY_ID = <canonical repository identity> | UNRESOLVED\nREPOSITORY_SOURCE_KIND = REMOTE_ORIGIN | LOCAL_TOPLEVEL | CONNECTOR | UNRESOLVED\nREPOSITORY_SOURCE_REDACTED = <credential-free source> | UNRESOLVED\nREPOSITORY_SOURCE_BINDING_SHA256 = <64 lowercase hexadecimal characters> | UNRESOLVED\nEVIDENCE_MANIFEST_SHA256 = <64 lowercase hexadecimal characters> | UNRESOLVED\nGIT_OBJECT_FORMAT = SHA1 | SHA256 | UNRESOLVED\nCOMPARISON_REF = <exact comparison ref> | UNRESOLVED\nCOMPARISON_SHA = <full commit object ID> | UNRESOLVED\nORDERED_CHANGE_IDS = <JSON string array in exact oldest-to-newest order>\nPROVEN_CHANGE_IDS = <JSON string array containing an exact ordered prefix>\nEVIDENCE_CUTOFF_UTC = YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ | UNRESOLVED\nEVIDENCE_CUTOFF_SHA = <the exact COMPARISON_SHA> | UNRESOLVED\n```\n\nA `VALIDATED` artifact resolves every variable evidence field, uses `FIRST_STOP = NONE`, and has identical nonempty ordered and proven arrays. The three lifecycle fields are fixed literals even in a blocked diagnostic. A blocked diagnostic may use `UNRESOLVED` only where the first stop prevented evidence resolution.\n\n## Run binding and transient containment\n\nAn operator-supplied run key must match `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` and be 1–64 ASCII characters. It cannot contain whitespace, dots, repeated or trailing hyphens, separators, traversal, Unicode lookalikes, or percent-encoded separators. When omitted, compute SHA-256 over compact sorted UTF-8 JSON containing `interface_id`, `ordered_change_ids`, and `repository_id`, with separators `,` and `:`. Deliberately exclude the comparison SHA so the key identifies the same review subject across cutoffs. The derived key is `auto-` plus the first 24 lowercase hexadecimal characters of that hash.\n\n`RUN_BINDING_SHA256` is the full hash of those same bytes. The filename is derived, never supplied independently. The artifact basename must equal `MCA-{ATTRIBUTION_RUN_KEY}-Attribution.md`; reject symlinks and paths outside the explicitly supplied task-owned transient root. The run key and filename have no durable identity semantics.\n\nThe transient root must be created automatically for the current review task, outside the target repository. The artifact and evidence manifest remain there only until the reviewer finishes. There is no persistence receipt, stable artifact ID, fetchback, version history, or durable-store requirement. Do not publish the files to Library, Drive, Notion, a repository, a PR comment, or another long-lived location without a separate explicit operator instruction.\n\n## Repository source and evidence-manifest binding\n\nNever place a raw credential-bearing remote URL in the artifact. Record a sanitized source with userinfo, query, and fragment removed while preserving transport, host, nondefault port, and repository path. For a local top-level path, display only `local:<basename>` and bind the exact resolved path by SHA-256 in supporting evidence. Connector evidence binds its provider and canonical repository locator without tokens.\n\nThe source kind, sanitized display, and source-binding SHA-256 must match the evidence manifest and the read-only before/after snapshots. A source-binding change invalidates the read-only invariant even if the normalized repository ID is unchanged.\n\nCanonical evidence-manifest bytes are UTF-8 JSON with keys sorted, separators `,` and `:`, and exactly one trailing LF. `EVIDENCE_MANIFEST_SHA256` is the SHA-256 of those bytes. A validated artifact requires the manifest and cross-checks repository identity, source binding, comparison, ordered changes, object format, stage fields, evidence pointers, and the read-only invariant.\n\nCollected evidence must declare `collector_schema_version = 3`, this exact interface ID, `attribution_scope = HISTORICAL_LANDED_DELTA`, and `current_effect_status = NOT_ASSESSED`. Its run binding, artifact filename, source identity aliases, ordered stage sequence, baseline, object width, and three material state objects must match the artifact and their derived evidence exactly. Every inner and outer read-only snapshot must independently report a consistent identity observation whose before/after repository, source kind, sanitized source, and source binding agree with the artifact; equality among already-inconsistent snapshots is not sufficient.\n\n## Required sections\n\nUse these exact level-two headings, once and in order:\n\n1. `## Input binding`\n2. `## Repository identity and comparison state`\n3. `## Merged-change verification`\n4. `## Per-stage attribution`\n5. `## Direct PR versus landed reconciliation`\n6. `## Final attributable merged state`\n7. `## Later non-lineage committed divergence`\n8. `## Worktree-only divergence`\n9. `## Unproven items and conflicts`\n10. `## Evidence commands and source pointers`\n11. `## Validation`\n\nNo section may be empty, comment-only, separator-only, or contain only `N/A`, `TBD`, `TODO`, `UNRESOLVED`, or “see above.” A blocked section that was not reached may contain exactly `- Section state: NOT_REACHED_DUE_TO_FIRST_STOP`.\n\nThe repository section must restate the repository ID, sanitized source, source-binding hash, and comparison SHA. The merged-change section must bind every proven change to `MERGED`. The reconciliation section must bind every proven change to its exact row result. The evidence section must include the evidence-manifest hash.\n\nFor collected evidence, sections 6–8 each contain exactly one machine-checkable line and no narrative additions:\n\n- `- FINAL_ATTRIBUTABLE_STATE_JSON = <canonical compact sorted JSON of final_attributable_state>`\n- `- LATER_COMMITTED_DIVERGENCE_JSON = <canonical compact sorted JSON of later_committed_divergence>`\n- `- WORKTREE_ONLY_DIVERGENCE_JSON = <canonical compact sorted JSON of worktree_only_divergence>`\n\nThe validator requires byte-semantic equality with those evidence-manifest objects, derives the final state from the ordered stages, binds later divergence from the final attributable SHA through `COMPARISON_SHA`, and binds all worktree hashes to the read-only snapshot. Contradictory or additional prose fails validation.\n\n## Per-stage table\n\nUse these exact columns:\n\n| Change ID | Claim state | Merge status | Merge method | Merge ID or range | Pre SHA | Post SHA | Direct base SHA | Direct head SHA | Direct delta SHA-256 | Landed delta SHA-256 | Patch ID algorithm | Direct stable patch ID | Landed stable patch ID | Reconciliation | Evidence pointers |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n\nRules:\n\n- Validated rows use `PROVEN`; blocked retained rows use `PROVEN_BEFORE_STOP`.\n- Rows correspond exactly to `PROVEN_CHANGE_IDS`, which is an ordered prefix of `ORDERED_CHANGE_IDS`.\n- Merge status is `MERGED`; merge method is `MERGE`, `SQUASH`, or `REBASE`.\n- `MERGE` and `SQUASH` use one full merge ID equal to the post SHA. `REBASE` uses the exact full `pre..post` range.\n- Pre, post, direct-base, direct-head, merge, range, comparison, and cutoff Git IDs all use the one declared `GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT`. SHA-1 IDs are 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters; SHA-256 IDs are 64.\n- Direct and landed delta values are always SHA-256, independent of Git object format.\n- `EXACT` requires identical direct and landed hashes and `NOT_USED` in all three patch-ID fields.\n- `EQUIVALENT` requires different nonempty-delta hashes, a declared `SHA1` or `SHA256` patch-ID algorithm, and identical nonempty patch IDs of that algorithm's exact length.\n- Evidence pointers are a nonempty JSON string array and include the stage's manifest pointer.\n\n## Cutoff\n\n`EVIDENCE_CUTOFF_UTC` uses fixed-millisecond RFC 3339 UTC syntax and must parse as a real calendar time. Offsets, lowercase `z`, missing milliseconds, invalid dates, and leap seconds are invalid. `EVIDENCE_CUTOFF_SHA` equals `COMPARISON_SHA` exactly.\n\n## Stop and blocked-diagnostic contract\n\nThe sole exact stop is the raw value of the `FIRST_STOP` header. Do not repeat it elsewhere. The validator renders Markdown link text, removes code/emphasis syntax, normalizes Unicode, and rejects any additional recognized or invented stop-like expression with a `BLOCKED:`, `MISSING INPUT:`, `AMBIGUOUS INPUT:`, or `CONFLICTING INPUT:` prefix.\n\nA blocked artifact retains only fully proven earlier rows. A conflict stage, an incomplete stage, or a stage at which the stop occurred cannot be labeled proven. Missing or ambiguous change identities require empty ordered and proven arrays and an empty table. A read-only invariant violation retains no proven rows.\n\nThe blocked conflicts section includes `- First stop is recorded in the FIRST_STOP header.` and must not claim `None.`. It cannot claim overall validation, completion, success, all changes verified, or any validated PASS predicate.\n\n## Exact Validation syntax\n\nA validated artifact uses these exact lines, once and in order:\n\n```text\n- Artifact schema and cross-field consistency: PASS\n- Run identity and transient lifecycle binding: PASS\n- Repository identity and source binding: PASS\n- Comparison ref, SHA, object format, and UTC cutoff: PASS\n- Merged-change verification: PASS\n- Landed ranges and chronology: PASS\n- Direct-versus-landed reconciliation: PASS\n- Later committed divergence separation: PASS\n- Worktree divergence separation: PASS\n- Required evidence completeness: PASS\n- Read-only invariant: PASS\n- PR-review consumer scope and non-persistence: PASS\n```\n\nEnd with exactly `END MERGED CHANGE ATTRIBUTION: VALIDATED`.\n\nA blocked diagnostic uses exactly:\n\n```text\n- Overall attribution outcome: BLOCKED\n- First stop binding: RECORDED\n- Retained proven row count: <decimal matching PROVEN_CHANGE_IDS>\n- Validated attribution claimed: NO\n```\n\nEnd with exactly `END MERGED CHANGE ATTRIBUTION: BLOCKED`.\n\n## Validator invocation and result\n\nRun inside the active review task:\n\n```text\npython3 scripts/validate_attribution_artifact.py \\\n  MCA-<run-key>-Attribution.md \\\n  --evidence-manifest <canonical-evidence.json> \\\n  --transient-root <task-owned-temporary-directory>\n```\n\nExit `0` means eligible validated evidence for this PR-review task; exit `2` means a structurally valid blocked diagnostic that is not eligible; exit `1` means invalid content or bindings.\n\n## Reviewer delivery and cleanup\n\nDeliver the complete validated bytes to the reviewer within the active task. A same-environment reviewer may read the task-local file. An already-active relay may transfer it as a verified task-scoped attachment, but this interface does not depend on relay behavior. Do not place a filesystem path into an ID-only prompt field and do not edit a receiver prompt.\n\nThe reviewer incorporates the useful result into a concise `Merged-change attribution` section in its own review output and remains authoritative for the review. When the review ends, delete only the exact task-owned transient directory if safe; otherwise allow normal transient expiry. The artifact and manifest are not retained as separate records.\n",
    "c6fa4b08de47e059ff3b7d221d4a95d533809500f04d826d16085dbb8096ce77": "# Merge-method semantics\n\n## Common rules\n\nUse repository objects and authoritative merged-status metadata together. A PR record establishes PR identity and merged status; Git objects establish landed trees and deltas. Neither silently substitutes for the other.\n\nFor each stage compute:\n\n- direct PR delta from the authoritative PR base tree to final reviewed head tree;\n- landed delta from the exact pre-stage tree to exact post-stage tree;\n- binary-diff SHA-256 for both; and\n- stable patch ID when Git can produce one.\n\nEvery SHA-named manifest value uses one full lowercase object ID of the repository's declared object format. `MERGE` and `SQUASH` emit the full post-stage ID. `REBASE` emits the full `pre..post` range. Symbolic, abbreviated, mixed-width, or raw movable bindings are not evidence.\n\nClassify `EXACT` only when binary-diff hashes match and record patch IDs as `NOT_USED`. Classify `EQUIVALENT` only when hashes differ and nonempty stable patch IDs produced under the same repository object algorithm match. Classify `CONFLICT` when both deltas exist and neither condition holds. Missing direct evidence stops with `MISSING INPUT: COMPLETE_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE`; missing or contradictory landed topology stops with `BLOCKED: ATTRIBUTABLE_LANDED_RANGE_UNRESOLVED`.\n\n## Merge commit\n\nRequire a merged PR pointer and one exact two-parent merge commit. Its first parent must equal the pre-stage SHA and its second parent must equal the authoritative direct PR head SHA; an arbitrary ancestor is insufficient. The exact merge ID equals the post-stage SHA, the merge is reachable from the comparison SHA, and the landed delta is pre-stage to merge. Reconcile conflict-resolution edits instead of silently attributing them to the direct PR. Octopus, merge-queue synthetic, or otherwise different topology blocks until governed as a distinct method.\n\n## Squash merge\n\nDo not require original PR commits to be ancestors of the landed commit. Require hosting evidence that binds the PR to one exact single-parent squash commit whose sole parent is the pre-stage SHA. The exact merge ID equals that post-stage commit. A range containing an intervening commit is not one squash landing. Compare the direct PR tree delta with the pre-stage-to-squash delta.\n\n## Rebase merge\n\nDo not identify rebase from commit-message similarity alone. Require hosting evidence and one exact nonempty full `pre..post` range. Walking from post back to pre, every landed commit must have exactly one parent; merge commits and side-parent topology are forbidden. Compare the original direct PR delta with the combined landed range. Different commit identities do not themselves prove equivalence.\n\n## Unknown method\n\n`UNKNOWN` is suitable only while collecting a blocked diagnostic. A validated artifact still requires complete direct-delta and landed-range evidence. If the range cannot be proven, stop with `BLOCKED: ATTRIBUTABLE_LANDED_RANGE_UNRESOLVED`.\n\n## Ordered lineage\n\nFor adjacent stages, require the earlier post-stage SHA to be an ancestor of the later pre-stage SHA. If commits intervene, require `interstage_classification = NON_LINEAGE_COMMITTED_DIVERGENCE` and an exact `interstage_evidence_pointer` on the later stage. Record each gap independently with its from/to IDs, ordered commits, delta hash, and name-status evidence. Keep the gap outside the canonical attributable stage-delta bundle. If order or intervening attribution cannot be reconciled, stop with `CONFLICTING INPUT: LINEAGE_ORDER`.\n\nThe final attributable representation is the ordered canonical stage bundle, not an inclusive first-pre-to-last-post diff when gaps exist. An inclusive lineage envelope is context and must be labeled non-attributable whenever it contains interstage divergence. Record later committed divergence from last post SHA through comparison SHA and worktree-only divergence separately.\n\nAttribution proves `HISTORICAL_LANDED_DELTA`, not surviving current effect. A later revert does not erase the original `MERGED` stage; keep the revert in interstage or later non-lineage divergence and use `CURRENT_EFFECT_STATUS = NOT_ASSESSED` unless separate authoritative evidence proves its effect. Never infer a revert from a commit message or tree equality alone.\n",
    "9e4bf01273e65a1fa4a7c854db38ab908adf4ccf6428114d7a862cf1d40b2a25": "# Validation matrix\n\n## Deterministic collector gate\n\n`scripts/run_fixture_tests.py` continues to cover repository collection:\n\n| Fixture | Required result |\n|---|---|\n| merge commit | exact merge topology and landed range resolve |\n| squash merge | one-parent landing and deltas reconcile |\n| rebased landing | a linear no-merge landed range reconciles |\n| later committed divergence | later commits remain outside attributable state |\n| dirty local worktree | staged, unstaged, and untracked divergence stays separate |\n| repository identity/source race | inner or outer fingerprint change blocks |\n| PR-versus-landed conflict | collection cannot validate |\n| invalid lineage order | `CONFLICTING INPUT: LINEAGE_ORDER` |\n| missing exact landed range | unresolved-range stop |\n| unclassified interstage commits | lineage-order stop |\n| global stop precedence | the first applicable higher-priority stop wins |\n| SHA-1 repository | all Git object IDs remain uniformly 40 characters |\n| SHA-256 repository | all Git object IDs remain uniformly 64 characters |\n\n## Artifact adversarial gate\n\nRun `scripts/run_artifact_adversarial_tests.py`. It must cover each interface invariant with a passing positive and failing negative case where applicable.\n\n| Area | Required cases |\n|---|---|\n| base v3 artifact | exact artifact, evidence manifest, lifecycle fields, and transient filename pass |\n| interface identity | `.1`/`.2`, wrong producer revision, altered title, duplicate title, or heading variant fails |\n| exact validation syntax | missing bullet, altered case, extra suffix, duplicate, reordering, or text after terminal fails |\n| transient lifecycle | exact `IN_FLIGHT_ONLY`, `PR_REVIEW_TASK`, and `DISCARD_AFTER_REVIEW` literals pass; any durable, stable-ID, or retention claim fails |\n| `EXACT` | equal hashes pass; unequal hashes fail |\n| `EQUIVALENT` | differing hashes plus matching nonempty patch IDs pass; equal hashes, missing base/head, wrong algorithm/length, empty delta, or unequal patch IDs fails |\n| Git object format | uniform SHA-1 and uniform SHA-256 pass; any mixed 40/64 object-ID family fails |\n| UTC cutoff | fixed-millisecond valid UTC passes; missing milliseconds, offset, lowercase `z`, invalid date, leap second, or cutoff-SHA mismatch fails |\n| source redaction | sanitized source and bound hash pass; credential, userinfo, query, fragment, changed port, source-hash mismatch, or before/after mismatch fails |\n| evidence manifest | canonical hash and field parity pass; whitespace-normalized but incorrectly hashed, stale field, missing stage, or altered evidence pointer fails |\n| manifest controls | exact collector schema/interface, historical scope, `NOT_ASSESSED` current effect, run binding, filename, ordered stages, baseline, and object width pass; any independently changed control fails |\n| material state sections | exact canonical JSON bindings for final attributable state, later committed divergence, and worktree-only divergence pass; narrative additions, body/manifest mismatch, non-stage-derived final state, wrong later boundary, or worktree/snapshot mismatch fails |\n| read-only snapshots | four equal, internally consistent, artifact-bound snapshots pass; false consistency flag, any before/after identity change, ABA source change, or inner/outer mismatch fails |\n| second stop | exact duplicate, emphasis, backticks, link, blockquote, mixed case, spacing variant, HTML comment, or invented stop prefix fails |\n| blocked retained claims | exact earlier proven prefix and full supporting-stage bytes pass; failing conflict row, non-prefix row, missing-ID claim, changed delta/method/pointer, or read-only-violation row fails |\n| blocked contradictions | `None.`, validated PASS lines, validated terminal, completion claim, or all-changes-verified claim fails |\n| hollow sections | empty, comment-only, separator-only, placeholder-only, or “see above” fails; the exact blocked not-reached marker passes |\n| run key | valid ASCII key passes; slash, backslash, traversal, leading punctuation, whitespace, control, encoded separator, or overlength key fails |\n| filename and transient root | exact derived basename inside the supplied task-owned root passes; missing root, renamed file, symlink, or escape fails |\n| output semantics | eligible validated artifact exits `0`; valid blocked diagnostic exits `2`; invalid artifact exits `1` |\n\nNo expected-failure or weak-regression case may be counted as a passing fixture merely because the validator reports an error. Each test declares the exact expected schema status, artifact status, eligibility, and exit behavior.\n\n## Blocked evidence matrix\n\n| First-stop class | Ordered IDs | Proven IDs and rows |\n|---|---|---|\n| missing/ambiguous change IDs | empty | empty |\n| missing repository or unresolved identity | may retain supplied ordered IDs | empty |\n| missing/ambiguous comparison | may retain supplied ordered IDs | empty |\n| incomplete evidence, not merged, unresolved landed range | supplied order | only complete earlier prefix |\n| lineage-order or PR-versus-landed conflict | supplied order | only complete earlier prefix; failing stage excluded |\n| read-only invariant violation | may retain supplied order | empty |\n| current comparison state unavailable | supplied order | fully reconciled rows may be retained without a validated outcome |\n\n## Shadow-validation gate\n\nBefore changing `ADOPTION_POSTURE`, compare the skill artifact with native results for:\n\n- one single-PR merge;\n- one squash or rebase case;\n- one ordered multi-PR lineage;\n- one later-committed-divergence case;\n- one local-worktree-divergence case when local Git is used; and\n- one conflict or incomplete-evidence stop.\n\nIn each PR-review output, record the repository/comparison SHA, artifact interface version and hash, native result, skill result, discrepancies, and disposition. The temporary artifact itself does not need to survive the review.\n\n## Adoption decision\n\nAdoption requires a separate operator decision after representative comparisons show that in-task delivery works without prompt edits, native guards remain intact, blocked or unavailable output falls back cleanly, repository state is unchanged, downstream governance does not leak into the artifact, and discrepancies are resolved or explicitly accepted.\n\nUntil then, keep `ADOPTION_POSTURE = SHADOW_VALIDATION`.\n",
    "17fa2d0c1daf219f8735f5d662596a6791b8fce8cdc9f87608f89ab366dcbaa0": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Collect deterministic, read-only local Git attribution evidence.\n\nInput is a JSON manifest. Output is JSON on stdout. The script never writes the\ntarget repository. Its JSON is supporting evidence for the task-scoped,\nin-flight attribution artifact.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport os\nimport re\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\nfrom urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit\n\n\nALLOWED_METHODS = {\"MERGE\", \"SQUASH\", \"REBASE\", \"UNKNOWN\"}\nFULL_OID_RE = re.compile(r\"^(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$\")\nRUN_KEY_RE = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$\")\nINTERFACE_ID = \"GLOW-MERGED-CHANGE-ATTRIBUTION-082826.3\"\nLOCAL_ID_RE = re.compile(r\"^local:[0-9a-f]{64}$\")\nCANONICAL_DIFF_OPTIONS = (\n    \"--binary\",\n    \"--full-index\",\n    \"--no-color\",\n    \"--no-ext-diff\",\n    \"--no-textconv\",\n    \"--no-renames\",\n    \"--no-indent-heuristic\",\n    \"--diff-algorithm=myers\",\n    \"--unified=3\",\n    \"--src-prefix=a/\",\n    \"--dst-prefix=b/\",\n)\n\n\nclass CollectionError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A stop condition with optional supporting evidence.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, stop: str, detail: str, evidence: dict[str, Any] | None = None):\n        super().__init__(detail)\n        self.stop = stop\n        self.detail = detail\n        self.evidence = evidence or {}\n\n\ndef git_observation_env() -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return a deterministic environment that cannot redirect repository reads.\"\"\"\n\n    env = {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if not name.startswith(\"GIT_\")}\n    env.update(\n        {\n            \"GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS\": \"0\",\n            \"GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH\": \"1\",\n            \"GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS\": \"1\",\n            \"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT\": \"0\",\n            \"GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM\": \"1\",\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM\": \"1\",\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL\": os.devnull,\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM\": os.devnull,\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"2\",\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"core.fsmonitor\",\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1\": \"core.untrackedCache\",\n            \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1\": \"false\",\n            \"GIT_PAGER\": \"cat\",\n            \"PAGER\": \"cat\",\n            \"LC_ALL\": \"C\",\n        }\n    )\n    return env\n\n\ndef git_observation_command(repo: Path, *args: str) -> list[str]:\n    return [\"git\", \"-C\", str(repo), *args]\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass GitRunner:\n    repo: Path\n    commands: list[list[str]]\n\n    def run(\n        self,\n        *args: str,\n        input_bytes: bytes | None = None,\n        check: bool = True,\n    ) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n        command = git_observation_command(self.repo, *args)\n        self.commands.append(command)\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            command,\n            input=input_bytes,\n            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n            check=False,\n            env=git_observation_env(),\n        )\n        if check and result.returncode != 0:\n            message = result.stderr.decode(\"utf-8\", \"replace\").strip()\n            raise CollectionError(\n                \"MISSING INPUT: COMPLETE_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE\",\n                f\"Git command failed ({' '.join(args)}): {message}\",\n            )\n        return result\n\n\ndef sha256_bytes(value: bytes) -> str:\n    return hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef repository_source_binding(value: bytes) -> str:\n    return sha256_bytes(b\"GLOW-REPOSITORY-SOURCE-V1\\x00\" + value)\n\n\ndef repository_source_kind(repository_id: str) -> str:\n    return \"LOCAL_TOPLEVEL\" if repository_id.startswith(\"local:\") else \"REMOTE_ORIGIN\"\n\n\ndef safe_ref(value: Any, label: str) -> str:\n    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():\n        raise CollectionError(\n            \"MISSING INPUT: COMPLETE_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE\", f\"Missing {label}.\"\n        )\n    value = value.strip()\n    if value.startswith(\"-\") or \"\\x00\" in value or \"\\n\" in value or \"\\r\" in value:\n        raise CollectionError(\n            \"AMBIGUOUS INPUT: COMPARISON_REF\" if label == \"comparison_ref\" else \"MISSING INPUT: COMPLETE_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE\",\n            f\"Unsafe or ambiguous {label}.\",\n        )\n    return value\n\n\ndef safe_artifact_cell(value: str, label: str, stop: str) -> str:\n    clean = value.strip()\n    if not clean or \"|\" in clean or any(ord(char) < 32 for char in clean):\n        raise CollectionError(stop, f\"{label} is empty or unsafe for artifact binding.\")\n    return clean\n\n\ndef is_local_repository_source(value: str) -> bool:\n    value = value.strip()\n    if not value:\n        return False\n    if value.lower().startswith(\"file://\"):\n        return True\n    if value.startswith((\"/\", \"./\", \"../\", \"~/\", \"\\\\\\\\\")):\n        return True\n    return bool(re.match(r\"^[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]\", value))\n\n\ndef canonical_local_path(value: str, repo: Path | None) -> Path:\n    raw = value.strip()\n    if raw.lower().startswith(\"file://\"):\n        parsed = urlsplit(raw)\n        if parsed.query or parsed.fragment or parsed.username or parsed.password:\n            raise ValueError(\"unsafe file repository source\")\n        path_text = unquote(parsed.path)\n        if parsed.hostname and parsed.hostname.lower() != \"localhost\":\n changes\")\n        if first_stop == \"BLOCKED: READ_ONLY_INVARIANT_VIOLATED\" and (proven or parsed_rows):\n            errors.append(\"read-only invariant violation cannot retain proven changes\")\n     "ad238a8fc07af27bcecf5afce71368766d96d0d40104649b2a005a0f721dd2f9": "# **0\\. Front Matter**\n\n**Title:** PF06-Canon-Change-Process-Guide\n\n**Version:** v2.5.4\n\n**Status:** Canon\n\n**Effective date**: 2026-09-08\n\n**Last Update Gate:** PF10 13.0.9\n\n9**Invocation tag:** INV-f2ac55d77ce9aacc\n\n## **0.1 Purpose and scope**\n\nThis guide defines the common change-delivery process for Epic and CRD work. The Epic lane forms planned development from the authoritative phased HDE Build Checklist source. The CRD lane forms observed change from a Product Owner-controlled CRD identity, exact primary source, bounded context, and current findings. PF09 is not the CRD source inventory.\n\nThe active substantive authorities for each change are:\n\n1. the approved class-specific Specification, either an Epic Specification or a CRD Specification; and  \n2. the approved class-bound change-wide Implementation Plan, either an Epic Implementation Plan or a CRD Implementation Plan.\n\nThe Specification establishes scope, intent, constraints, and outcome boundaries. The change-wide Implementation Plan establishes the detailed implementation method and planned PR work units and Ops tasks for that exact Specification. The approved Specification authorizes preparation of the required Implementation Audit and change-wide Implementation Plan; it does not authorize implementation.\n\nNo active Epic Plan, CRD Plan, Implementation Guide, PF20 record, or PF30 record sits between kickoff and these authorities. PF20 and PF30 are historical references only. Neither is an active planning source, work register, approval gate, implementation authority, required runtime input, or required closeout or drainage prerequisite.\n\nThe normal code-bearing route remains PR-based. An explicit current Product Owner instruction may separately authorize a bounded direct-to-main route for the exact change. Repository adoption, implementation evidence, QA, acceptance, closure, board state, and permanent documentation drainage remain separate states.\n\nThis is process guidance. It routes specialized schema, evidence, QA, environment, architecture, implementation, and template details to their current owning documents rather than reproducing those contracts here.\n\n## **0.1A Governing lanes, common lifecycle, and authority routing**\n\n### **Lane formation**\n\n* **Epic lane.** The Product Owner selects Epic. Master Scrum forms the Epic from the exact eligible work in the authoritative phased HDE Build Checklist source without crossing its applicable phase boundary. The kickoff produces a class-bound handoff and any contract-required audit-only proof. It does not produce a Specification, Implementation Plan, PR structure, PF20 entry, or implementation authorization.  \n* **CRD lane.** The Product Owner selects CRD. Master Scrum forms the CRD from its controlled identity, exact primary source, bounded Product Owner context, and current-state findings. It does not manufacture PF09 work or create or update PF30 as an active record. A genuine intersection with existing PF09 work does not convert the CRD into an Epic.  \n* **Convergence.** The lanes remain separate through class-specific Specification approval. They converge only after an approved class-bound Specification exists.\n\n### **Common lifecycle**\n\n1. The Product Owner selects Epic or CRD.  \n2. Master Scrum runs the matching class-specific kickoff.  \n3. Isis authors the initial class-specific Specification.  \n4. The same continuing Thoth session approves the Specification or returns an exact denial and redline.  \n5. When denied, Isis applies the redline, publishes a complete revised Specification with preserved lineage, and returns it to the same continuing Thoth session.  \n6. After Specification approval, the Implementation Agent creates the Implementation Audit first.  \n7. The Implementation Agent creates the class-bound change-wide Implementation Plan from the exact approved Specification and Implementation Audit.  \n8. Isis reviews the change-wide Implementation Plan and either approves it or returns an exact redline.  \n9. When redlined, the Implementation Agent revises the complete Plan and returns it to the same Isis decision owner.  \n10. The Implementation Agent creates PR Instructions and any required Ops Tasks from the approved change-wide Implementation Plan.  \n11. A dedicated PR session creates a per-PR Implementation Plan for each selected PR work unit.  \n12. The Product Owner reviews that per-PR plan and runs \"PR Implementation Proceed\" to approve and authorize its execution.  \n13. The same dedicated PR session implements the approved PR work unit and opens the actual PR or ordered PR lineage.  \n14. Authorized environment or DevOps operators execute separately authorized Ops work. Ops evidence returns to the responsible Implementation Agent review chain.  \n15. The final repository-documentation PR is completed before QA begins.  \n16. Continuing Isis runs QA-10, combining the fresh implementation audit, historical PF23 comparison, change-audit triage, and whole-change readiness assessment. QA-10 remains the return point for readiness remediation; READY\\_FOR\\_QA routes to QA-20 for the Live QA Guide.  \n17. Kronos creates the independent QA Audit and QA Plan. Isis reviews the QA Plan.  \n18. Authorized environment or DevOps operators execute the reviewed QA tasks. Evidence returns to Kronos.  \n19. Kronos reviews the evidence. Every completed QA run ends with both a final QA Report and an RCA, regardless of pass or fail.  \n20. Isis performs the terminal retrospective and makes the change-closure decision.  \n21. Post-closure PF10 drainage, closure-memo delivery, permanent PF maintenance, and board updates proceed through their manual owning routes. They are required maintenance but do not reopen or block an already completed runtime change unless another governing rule expressly says otherwise.\n\n### **Approval and lineage rules**\n\nThe only Product Owner runtime approval point in the ordinary PR route is the per-PR Implementation Plan. Running \"PR Implementation Proceed\" is the approval. No separate approval binding, token, signature, object, receipt, hash, ID, or second Product Owner confirmation exists or is required.\n\nDurable run, source, artifact, PR, commit, and evidence identities remain required where their owners require traceability. They prove lineage or observed state; they are not approval objects.\n\nA create, revise, or approve action may publish one substantive artifact and one separate proof artifact. A proof artifact does not replace the substantive Specification, Implementation Audit, or Implementation Plan. A revision is a complete successor artifact rather than an in-place mutation or redline-only authority.\n\n### **Authority routing**\n\nPF06 owns the end-to-end process and routes specialized authority by title:\n\n* **HDE Governance** controls permissions, authority, canon-change requirements, and governance semantics.  \n* **Plan Templates** controls reusable Specification, audit, implementation, PR, QA, review, Ops, remediation, and closeout templates.  \n* **Glow QA Guide** controls detailed QA planning, execution, evidence, remediation, and verdict rules.  \n* **HDE Schemas & Artifacts** controls governed evidence, manifests, artifact identity, canonical bytes, and path contracts.  \n* **7 Phases of Alchemical Engineering** controls phase meaning and non-mixing.  \n* **HDE Build Checklist** controls phased Epic work.  \n* **HDE Phased Epics** and **HDE CRD Records** preserve historical records only; they are not current runtime authorities for new work.  \n* **HDE Build Notes** records material decisions, results, history, and temporary pre-drain authority.\n\n\"Implementation Plan\" without another qualifier means the class-bound change-wide Implementation Plan. A per-PR Implementation Plan is always identified expressly.\n\nThe unresolved PF23 timing, class, accountability, and Kronos-handoff policy must be exposed and governed by an explicit reconciled Product Owner decision. PF06 does not silently select a policy from conflicting sources.\n\nHistorical records retain the identities and terminology that applied when they were created. They are not rewritten merely to adopt the current lifecycle.\n\n## **0.2 Policy and principles**\n\nMutation route is explicit.\n\nThe normal code-bearing route assigns each approved planned PR work unit to its own dedicated PR session. That session creates the per-PR Implementation Plan, waits for the Product Owner to run **PR Implementation Proceed**, and only then implements and opens the PR or ordered PR lineage. The PR includes the approved code changes, Doc Delta, and every evidence-index, mirror, hash, or path-proof companion required by the changed governed artifacts and current canon.\n\nThe Product Owner may instead authorize direct mutation of `main` through an explicit current instruction covering the exact change. An agent must not infer direct-`main` authority from PF06, repository access, an earlier authorization, or a per-PR proceed action. For an authorized direct-`main` route, the exact instruction and post-write exact-source evidence govern.\n\nImplementation Agent analyzes PR bundles and produces PF-canon Doc Deltas.\n\nCoding agents and Implementation Agents MAY NOT directly modify PF-Canon documents as part of implementation PR work.\n\nIf implementation work reveals canon drift, missing canon coverage, or a needed canon change, the agent MUST record that explicitly as a drift note or Doc Delta candidate with evidence pointers rather than editing the PF-Canon file directly.\n\nA PR review or remediation report MAY support a future PF-Canon status update, but the canon edit itself remains separate documentation work. This applies to HDE-Build Checklist rows and any other PF-Canon status tables.\n\nDocumentation drainage is never an execution or closeout gate.\n\nPF10 drain and any later drainage into PF-Canon, checklist, guide, or summary homes are never prerequisites, required deliverables, required checks, acceptance conditions, or blockers by themselves for plans, reviews, QA artifacts, OPS tasks, acceptance maps, token-to-evidence matrices, PR summaries, or closeout artifacts.\n\nAllowed blockers remain limited to real truth-and-proof failures, such as incomplete required QA steps, missing required deliverables, untrusted or non-governed evidence, unresolved FAIL\\_BEHAVIOR or FAIL\\_TOOLING or TOOLING\\_BLOCKED conditions that affect acceptance, or missing required close-gate QA artifacts.\n\nWhen a canon or checklist delta is known but not yet drained, PF10 remains the temporary live-truth home until the later drain occurs. Artifacts MUST record the drift or later drain target, use supportable-from-repo-evidence wording when the destination PF home is not yet updated, and MUST NOT require that drainage in order to approve execution, recommend merge, or support epic readiness or closeout.\n\nProduct Owner-approved bounded revision. An expressly approved, bounded Product Owner scope, architecture, or ADR revision MAY supersede conflicting PF-Canon only for the exact decision it adjudicates. The approval record MUST include a causal map, name the superseded language, preserve later-slice boundaries, state explicit nonclaims, and identify controlled later drainage. It MUST NOT be treated as a general waiver, unrestricted informal scope expansion, or authority outside the recorded decision. Permanent PF-Canon drainage remains required, but it is separate documentation work and MUST NOT be made a prerequisite for applying the approved bounded revision.\n\nExact-source acceptance model.\n\nRepository-native exact-source evidence and scoped authorized decisions are the primary acceptance and completion traceability model. Acceptance tokens are legacy-compatible, historical, and optional indexing metadata. New QA acceptance tokens MUST NOT be created by default. A complete token roster, per-step intended-token or claimed-token declaration, or token/evidence matrix MUST NOT be required when no active scoped roster exists, and their absence MUST NOT block otherwise sufficient exact-source evidence.\n\nExisting token IDs and historical evidence MUST remain unchanged and attributable to the exact candidate and scope they originally proved. Existing token-aware fields and tooling MAY remain; empty token arrays remain valid where the governing schema requires those fields. A future plan MAY opt into one bounded token or equivalent cross-reference only when existing PF, ADR, epic, task, test, or acceptance-criterion identifiers cannot supply necessary traceability. That exception does not reactivate a universal token system.\n\nEvery current acceptance or completion claim MUST be traceable, as applicable, through the repository identity; exact commit identity; PR base, head, merge, and post-merge identities when a PR is used; applicable workflow identity, exact tested SHA, conclusion, and check set; stable governing and work identifiers; exact governed artifact paths and SHA-256 digests when integrity is material; required manifests, indexes, mirrors, path proofs, tool or configuration references; the authorized decision, decision-maker, scope, and time; and any exception or waiver identity, owner, scope, reason, and expiry. Do not duplicate information that GitHub or an existing governed artifact already records reliably, and do not create a replacement token database or universal evidence form.\n\nRepository presence, applicable CI result, QA decision, operator or role acceptance, and lifecycle completion or closure are separate states. Landing a commit or canonical file on `main` establishes repository reality and, for a current canonical artifact, authority in its declared content lane. It does not by itself establish CI PASS, QA PASS, acceptance, PF09 completion, OPS completion, deployment, release readiness, epic closure, or production readiness.\n\nThe Product Owner retains direct-to-`main` authority. An agent MUST NOT infer that permission; a current operator instruction MUST cover the exact mutation. A direct-main route changes the mutation path, not the applicable correctness, evidence, QA, security, privacy, canon, or closure standard. Record the exact post-write SHA and diff and the applicable push-triggered CI result. Pending or failing validation MUST be stated as such. A failure on `main` MUST be corrected or explicitly accepted as a bounded known exception.\n\nWhen the current workflow's applicability classifier validly selects a reduced lane set, a passing final applicability audit is sufficient machine evidence for that CI scope. Irrelevant lanes need not be rerun merely to imitate a traditional full-PR process.\n\nBefore substantive work, resolve and record the current relevant ref and inspect the current authoritative files and repository state. Before mutation, verify that the working base has not been materially superseded; reconcile any movement or prove it immaterial. Before acceptance or completion language, recheck the candidate SHA, relevant files, applicable workflow result, evidence integrity, and decision scope. Historical PASS does not transfer automatically to a later candidate. Changed canon or acceptance criteria require renewed conformance analysis, and changed implementation or evidence-producing surfaces require appropriate review and validation.\n\nEvidence controls remain layered. Commit identity, PR history, workflow results, SHA-256 and path proofs, manifests and evidence indexes, attestations, and authorized decisions prove different facts. No one identifier replaces the others. Existing release-attestation, evidence-index, mirror, path-proof, source-provenance, deterministic-validation, and strict-claim controls remain in force.\n\nIf exact-source repository metadata or required governed evidence is unavailable, the affected acceptance or closure claim fails closed as unavailable or blocked. Confidence MUST NOT be reconstructed through invented tokens or unsupported claims.\n\nClosure axes remain separate. QA evidence, PF09 status drainage, PO closeout, board state, merge provenance, and PF-canon drainage are separate closure axes and MUST NOT be collapsed.\n\n* QA evidence proves QA-plan coverage and QA proof posture. It does not by itself perform PO closeout, board update, merge action, PF09 drain, or PF-canon drain.  \n* PF09 status drainage updates phased-checklist task or subtask status. It may be supported by PF10 and repo evidence, but it remains a documentation/status-drain action, not implementation work.  \n* PO closeout is a PO-owned process action. A Lead report or QA evidence package may support PO closeout, but does not perform it.  \n* Board state is a Scrum or board-state action. Board updates must be handled in the board source of truth and MUST NOT be inferred solely from QA evidence, PF10 text, or review approval.  \n* Merge provenance is a repo/history axis. It must be evidenced by repo, PR, or commit state where relevant and MUST NOT be inferred from planning approval or QA approval alone.  \n* PF-canon drainage applies stable documentation updates to the permanent PF homes. PF10 can stage live truth before drainage, but the drain itself is a separate documentation action.\n\nPF09 accountability for task-like work. PF09 remains the phased completion backbone for HDE implementation, QA, OPS, runtime, evidence, vendor, architecture, and product-behavior work. A task-like item may be outside the current epic, deferred, optional, future-scoped, backlog-scoped, non-gating, or follow-up work, but it may not escape PF09 accountability.\n\nEvery task-like item in an Epic Specification, CRD Specification, change-wide Implementation Plan, per-PR Implementation Plan, QA Plan, remediation plan, QA-readiness review, retrospective, closure review, Scrum handoff, PO planning handoff, or board-prep artifact MUST resolve to exactly one of:\n\n* in current epic with exact phased PF09 task or subtask mapping;  \n* out of current epic with exact phased PF09 task or subtask mapping;  \n* PF09 gap, when the work is legitimate HDE phased-build work but no current phased PF09 task or subtask accounts for it;  \n* documentation/status drainage only, when the item is only a document, board, archive, or status reconciliation action and not implementation, QA, OPS, runtime, evidence, vendor, architecture, or product-behavior work;  \n* out of HDE phased build scope, when the item truly does not belong to the HDE phased build checklist.\n\nBacklog is a scheduling state, not scope authority. If work is moved to backlog, the handoff MUST preserve the phased PF09 document, task ID, subtask ID where one exists, disposition, reason it is not included now, and whether a PF09 gap exists. If PF09 mapping cannot be proven, the item MUST be marked PF09 gap rather than placed into backlog without mapping.\n\nFuture work must be PF09-accounted. Future runtime claims, future QA claims, future OPS work, future adapter work, future vendor work, future evidence work, future app-integration work, future build improvements, and future remediation work MUST state the PF09 task or subtask they will satisfy or advance, or be marked PF09 gap or out of HDE phased build scope.\n\nSubtask-level mapping is required when a relevant subtask exists. Parent-task-only mapping is invalid unless no relevant subtask exists. A parent PF09 row may not be treated as closed or supportable for Done merely because one child row or one evidence dimension is mapped.\n\nReviewers MUST reject plans, retrospectives, closeout reviews, remediation guides, QA-readiness reports, and Scrum/PO handoffs that create unaccounted task-like backlog. This is a scope-accountability requirement, not a documentation-drainage requirement.\n\nPF09 closure-first assessment.\n\nFor every PF09 row that an approved Epic Specification or change-wide Epic Implementation Plan assigns to completed PR, OPS, or combined Epic work for closure, the reviewer MUST identify the exact phased PF09 document, row ID, title, physical status, approved scope, mapped PR and OPS lineage, and current evidence before creating remedial work. The approved Specification and change-wide Implementation Plan together with applicable active PF10 define the bounded row scope. A broader PF09 description, later-phase work, historical cleanup, future expansion, unrelated stale artifacts, physical PF09 drainage, permanent-canon drainage, QA PASS, acceptance, deployment, closeout, or an explicitly excluded requirement MUST NOT retroactively enlarge that scope.\n\nThe reviewer MUST inspect current repository reality at one exact endpoint for every current implementation or evidence claim, distinguish implementation gaps, OPS gaps, evidence-inspection gaps, closure-recording gaps, and later-drain documentation, and decide row closure posture before considering remediation. The reviewer MUST NOT design remediation and then search for evidence to justify it. When the operator asks whether a row can be closed, the reviewer MUST answer `Yes` or `No` before explaining the evidence.\n\nEach mapped row MUST receive exactly one disposition:\n\n* **CLOSURE SUPPORTED — Recommend `Done`.**  \n* **CLOSURE NOT SUPPORTED — PR work remains.**  \n* **CLOSURE NOT SUPPORTED — OPS work remains.**  \n* **CLOSURE NOT SUPPORTED — PR and OPS work remain.**  \n* **CLOSURE NOT YET PROVABLE — Additional inspection or evidence capture is required.**\n\nAn unchanged physical PF09 status, a missing PF10 closure addendum, an earlier assessment that identified no exact remaining work, incomplete reviewer inspection, surface command syntax, parser-compatible forms, test fixtures, historical transcripts, undrained documentation, or a row description broader than the approved assignment is not evidence that implementation or OPS work remains. The assessment MUST distinguish missing repository implementation, missing OPS execution, missing evidence capture, insufficient inspection, PF10 closure recording, and later PF09 drainage.\n\nA remedial PR may be proposed only when the assessment identifies the exact PF09 row and approved scope, the required repository behavior or deliverable, the exact inspected endpoint and implementation surface, direct evidence that current implementation fails the requirement, a complete execution trace when the finding concerns a command, parser, wrapper, harness, workflow, generator, or evidence producer, reconciliation with any accepted original or remedial lineage, confirmation that the alleged defect is not merely syntax-origin, rendering-origin, historical, test-fixture-only, documentation-only, or outside approved scope, the smallest bounded correction, and a testable done condition. If any element is absent, the reviewer MUST NOT create a remedial PR.\n\nA remedial OPS task may be proposed only when closure requires a specific external or privileged outcome that repository implementation cannot provide. The assessment MUST identify the exact mapped row and approved OPS obligation, the required external or privileged outcome, current evidence that the outcome has not occurred, why repository implementation cannot satisfy it, and the exact evidence that will prove completion. A missing PF10 record, unchanged PF09 status, missing reviewer evidence, repository defect, or documentation delta MUST NOT be converted into OPS work.\n\nWhen evidence is insufficient, the reviewer MUST identify and retrieve or inspect the missing proof when permitted, use `CLOSURE NOT YET PROVABLE` if the gap remains, and avoid assigning PR or OPS work unless the completed inspection independently proves that work remains. Incomplete assessment is not evidence of incomplete implementation.\n\nWhen PF10 records that an original or remedial lineage is accepted, preserve-required, supported by applicable passing CI, has no remaining review finding, and has no further remediation assignment, a later defect finding MUST state what evidence was previously unavailable, whether the repository changed, whether the earlier assessment overlooked an in-scope defect, why the new finding is behavioral rather than syntactic or documentary, how it prevents row closure, and why existing evidence cannot support closure. Without that reconciliation, the accepted lineage MUST NOT be converted into new implementation work.\n\nFor every mapped row, the assessment MUST state the exact phased PF09 document; row ID, title, and physical status; approved plan mapping; mapped PR tasks and complete original and remedial lineage; mapped OPS tasks or `None`; exact reviewed repository endpoint; implemented behavior or completed OPS outcome; material implementation and evidence surfaces; applicable tests and CI; governed evidence; exact remaining PR work, OPS work, and evidence inspection or `None`; live PF10 disposition; physical PF09 drainage posture; and the mandatory closure-first disposition.\n\nWhen closure is supported, the assessment MUST recommend `Done`, state directly that no PR or OPS work remains, and provide paste-ready evidence for a PF10 closure-authorization addendum in the same assessment cycle. PF10 records accepted implementation, OPS outcomes, supersession, evidence, and live closure authority during the active epic. Physical PF09 status remains unchanged until epic closeout drainage, and that temporary difference is not unfinished work.\n\nIf later inspection disproves an earlier finding, the reviewer MUST state the error and its analytical or evidentiary cause, withdraw every downstream PR, OPS, documentation, or plan task based solely on it, redo the affected row assessment from the controlling sources, and issue the corrected closure disposition. A superseded analytical mistake MUST NOT become project scope through repetition.\n\nRuntime-conformance sequencing for multi-slice epics. When an epic is trying to move a runtime or vendor surface from unsupported, insufficient, or nonclaim posture into bounded support, the plan SHOULD sequence proof from narrowest truth to broadest binding: first prove schema, field, or adapter insufficiency; then implement the pure mapping or adapter layer; then wire the runtime path; then prove internal compatibility; then run any required PO-only open-rails smoke; then bind parent or aggregate evidence. A parent-level evidence binding PR should be last when it depends on earlier PR slices and OPS evidence.\n\nParent binding does not rerun OPS. A parent-binding or aggregate-evidence PR may consume PO-produced OPS evidence, but it MUST NOT claim to have executed OPS, completed OPS, made live vendor calls, moved PF09 status, produced QA PASS, or performed closeout unless those actions happened as separate authorized actions with their own evidence. The parent-binding artifact MUST state whether it binds existing OPS evidence, reruns nothing, and preserves the relevant nonclaims.\n\nBoundary repetition is protective. For runtime-conformance chains, each decisive evidence artifact SHOULD repeat the nonclaims that prevent evidence-to-product overclaim, including no public Reader change, no new public route, no new HTTP home, no app-side vendor ownership, no raw secret or uncontrolled payload persistence, no AI scope, no QA PASS, no OPS completion by PR work, no PF09 status movement by PR work, and no closeout unless those claims are explicitly in scope and proven.\n\nAn epic MAY be delivered in a series of PRs (up to 10 PRs per epic), each PR carrying a coherent slice of work with its own code \\+ evidence parity.\n\nFor a PR route, the contract-defined review and evidence chain gates adoption; the Product Owner is the sole merger and uses squash on a supported PASS.\n\nImplementation Agents and other non-PR-session process roles do not run git and do not create PRs.\n\nPF06 does not require blanket protection of `main` or a PR for every change. Direct-main authority remains with the Product Owner. An agent may mutate `main` only under an explicit current operator instruction covering the exact change. When a PR is used, governed required checks and the exact reviewed candidate remain controlling; when direct-main is authorized, the exact post-write SHA, diff, applicable push CI, and all other applicable standards remain controlling.\n\nAutomated CI budget control.\n\nRequired CI MUST protect a current, continuing product or delivery risk independently of an epic’s closeout, evidence package, token record, reviewer convenience, or historical administrative state. Release or security automation, QA or audit automation, and epic-closeout automation MUST remain in their justified lanes. Epic-closeout preparation or validation MUST NOT become ordinary required PR CI unless a specific control independently protects the merge boundary. A permanent CI control MUST NOT test historical epic administration or require hosted results to be written back into tracked source.\n\nCI-budget governance MUST use an actionable automated repository or authorized-setting control. Valid enforcement surfaces include tracked workflow configuration, repository-owned validation tooling, automated trigger or job selection, concurrency or superseded-run cancellation, change-aware execution, reusable workflow or setup consolidation, deterministic caching or artifact reuse, automated lane separation, truthful required-check aggregation, or an authorized repository setting.\n\nManual push counts, agent promises, pause thresholds, operator continuation approval, push-count reports, exception narratives, transient reports, and documentation-only remediation are not CI-budget controls, acceptance conditions, remediation tasks, or approval blockers. There is no five-update circuit breaker. A CI-budget finding MUST identify the avoidable hosted execution, the automated control surface, the required behavior, the protection that must remain, and a method for verifying the resulting execution shape. If no durable automated implementation exists within authorized scope, the observation MUST NOT be converted into remediation or an acceptance blocker.\n\nAutomated budget control MUST structurally prevent duplicate equivalent full suites for one ordinary pull-request head, safely cancel, short-circuit, or avoid superseded expensive work, select heavy validation by event and change relevance, reduce repeated setup and validation, preserve truthful required-check continuity, and validate the exact final candidate head. It MUST NOT skip applicable protection, leave a required status pending or absent, hide failure behind a green summary, use stale or unverifiable caches, bypass branch protection, or misclassify an affected change as irrelevant.\n\nWhen a material structural CI-cost defect is within an epic’s approved remediation scope, the epic MUST implement and verify the automated correction. It MUST NOT defer that correction as an optional optimization or report-only follow-up. Reviewers MUST inspect repository and GitHub evidence directly when available and MUST NOT manufacture a transient report whose facts are already observable.\n\nRe-run proofs only on qualifying drift (green-freeze).\n\nEvidence parity in the same authorized mutation set.\n\nWhenever proofs or artifacts change, update in the same authorized mutation set:\n\n* The human Evidence Index (docs/evidence/INDEX.json)  \n* The hash sentinel  \n* The machine JSONL mirror (artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl)\n\nThe machine mirror is:\n\n* Records-only  \n* Canonical JSONL (UTF-8, sorted keys, compact, exactly one trailing LF)  \n* Strict: rejects unknown keys\n\nEach mirror record includes:\n\n* artifact\\_key  \n* role  \n* sha256  \n* size\\_bytes  \n* produced\\_at\\_utc  \n* discovered\\_physical\\_path  \n* proof\\_anchor (to a co-located path-proof)\n\nRepo-doc and docs-only changes must be evidence-backed.\n\nAny claim about CLI behavior, output bytes, tokens, governed artifacts, or system mechanics MUST be supported by at least one of:\n\n* a canon pointer (title-only) to the relevant rule.  \n* a targeted test run output referenced in the PR summary.  \n* an existing governed evidence artifact path already committed under governed roots.\n\nAdditional docs-only constraints:\n\n* Treat \"contract changes\" (even docs-only ones) as requiring a tight evidence posture. Tests, proofs, and artifacts should be captured in the same PR bundle whenever possible.  \n* If a docs-only PR is approved without captured CI/test output, the PR summary or review pack MUST (1) state that verification was diff-only, (2) cite the best available canon pointer or governed evidence path for each non-obvious claim, and (3) record any search method used to look for missing proof.\n\nCopy/paste command safety (docs-only and discovery PRs).\n\nInteractive-terminal safety (no shell-closing blocks).\n\nWhen a plan, runbook, or repo doc includes a command block intended for an operator to paste into an interactive terminal:\n\n* The block MUST NOT terminate the operator shell session (for example by using exit as part of enforcement).  \n* If strict enforcement requires exit semantics, the enforcement MUST run in an isolated subshell and report PASS/FAIL (and exit code) without closing the parent shell.  \n* If a shell-terminating block is genuinely required (rare), it MUST be explicitly labeled as non-interactive and an interactive-safe alternative MUST be provided.\n\nWhen repo docs include commands intended for copy/paste use:\n\nCommands MUST be truthy and CI-traceable:\n\n* If a command is intended to run a CI check or governed script, document the CI-style invocation as the default.  \n* Do not present multiple conflicting invocations as co-equal. Any compatibility alternative MUST be explicitly labeled optional and must state when/why it is needed.  \n* Example (mirror schema validation): default to ci/checks/check\\_mirror\\_schema.sh artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl (CI-style direct invocation). python ci/checks/check\\_mirror\\_schema.sh artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl is an optional compatibility fallback (the script has a Python shebang).\n\nThe default command shown MUST be safe and non-epic-specific.\n\n* Do not include unrelated epic IDs, unrelated flags, or “example” values in the default command.  \n* Any epic-specific selector (for example an \\--epic-id flag) MUST be explicitly labeled optional and MUST NOT be presented as the default.  \n* If a command is conditional on local repo state, environment, or path existence, the doc MUST state the condition and the safe fallback.\n\nDecision-bounded placement (no invented “fits at” paths).\n\nWhen a doc references a future artifact placement or a not-yet-decided path:\n\n* It MUST be labeled TBD and constrained to the smallest set of plausible options.  \n* It MUST NOT be presented as a single fixed “would fit at \\\\” path unless the placement is already governed by an existing canonical rule or governed artifact family.\n\nReview source-retrieval guard (no excerpt-based claims).\n\nReviewers MUST NOT assert canon violations or contradictions about:\n\n* token rosters (missing/wrong tokens, token semantics mismatch), or  \n* Live QA rails posture / evidence posture, or  \n* transport bytes / CLI contract expectations,\n\nunless they have fully retrieved the governing canonical passages being referenced (the relevant roster section(s) and the relevant registry / rails / contract entries).\n\nAI review retrieval and proof order.\n\n* Reviewers and AI agents evaluating plans, remediation guides, QA plans, repo audits, closeout artifacts, or related review documents MUST use retrieval-first, proof-first review.  \n* Where PF10 explicitly speaks, use the latest applicable PF10 addendum before older PF canon on that topic. Then read the current artifact under review end-to-end, retrieve the owning PF canon home for each specific issue, and prove any repo-reality claim with concrete repo-local evidence.  \n* For known literals, exact-string lookup comes before regex or broad search. This applies to task IDs, subtask IDs, token names, headings, route strings, command strings, filenames, artifact keys, environment variable names, and other exact literals.  \n* Do not rely on memory, truncated viewer snippets, ellipsized passages, partial excerpts, or broad semantic search as proof when exact retrieval is available.  \n* If a locus, path, route, command, flag, token spelling, heading, ID, artifact key, or environment variable cannot be proven, classify it as UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and do not invent or near-match it.  \n* Review findings MUST distinguish canon requirement, observed repo reality, and inference.\n\nBuild Notes reference posture (living addenda).\n\nWhen referencing Build Notes in reviews, plans, or Doc Delta notes:\n\n* Do not reference Build Notes by version strings.  \n* Prefer referencing by addendum number \\+ addendum title.  \n* Do not treat Build Notes section numbers as durable anchors for external enforcement.\n\nWhen PF10 or a closeout artifact records more than one QA pass, QA review, final review, or pass-like addendum for the same epic, each entry MUST be distinguishable by addendum number and addendum title or by another stable source-order label. Reviews and closeout summaries MUST NOT rely on repeated labels such as “QA Pass 2” alone when that label appears more than once for the same epic. If duplicate labels exist, cite source order and state the chronology explicitly.\n\nCanon mismatch posture (docs-only PRs).\n\nIf a docs-only PR documents current repo behavior that appears to diverge from a canonical PF home (for example CLI exit codes vs HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref), the PR MUST:\n\n* state plainly that the text reflects repo-tested behavior (citing the test/evidence used), and  \n* state that the PF doc remains the single home for the normative contract (titles only), and  \n* include a Doc-Delta note routing the reconciliation into the canonical home (update canon or update code) rather than implying “canon is satisfied.”\n\nDocs-only PRs MUST NOT claim “conforms to PF-Canon” when the PR’s own evidence indicates an implementation-vs-canon mismatch.\n\nDocs-only PRs MUST NOT introduce unverified assumptions (for example inventing unsupported CLI flags or asserting output formats not proven by canon/tests/evidence). If the evidence is missing, treat it as a spec gap and fix the spec or add the proof, rather than “fixing docs by habit.”\n\nA7 proof surface (when applicable).\n\n* Run HTTP success-path proofs only on a cataloged JSON success route from the Endpoint Catalog.  \n* The /internal/version endpoint is ops-only and not A7-eligible.\n\nSingle homes.\n\n* Public transport & CLI/Reader bytes → HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref.  \n* Governance & token semantics → HDE-Governance.  \n* Deterministic serializer/idempotence → HDE-Math-Spec.  \n* Architecture & single-emitter rules → HDE Architecture.  \n* Evidence index & mirror schema → HDE-Schemas & Artifacts.  \n* Infra and environment names → Glow Infrastructure.\n\nPF14 scope guard (doc roles).\n\nHDE-Mechanics Guide (PF14) is a components and operational-surface reference. It MUST NOT define, rename, alias, or curate acceptance tokens, and it MUST NOT be used as a planning authority for acceptance language. Token registry, naming, semantics, and enforcement remain governed by their single homes (titles only).\n\nFor HD Engine epics:\n\n* “Prod” is the production HD Engine service and its production database as defined in Glow Infrastructure.  \n* PF06 does not redefine environment semantics and treats those names as the single home.\n\nWhen epic docs or QA plans talk about “prod via Codespaces”:\n\n* They must treat Codespaces as a QA console that talks to that production service and DB, not as a prod environment in its own right.\n\nIn this guide, “prod via Codespaces” means:\n\n* “Run commands from Codespaces that talk to the production HD Engine service/DB and store QA artifacts in the repo,” consistent with PF07-Canon-Glow-Infrastructure.\n\nBaseline PR acceptance token names and semantics are defined by PF04-Canon-HDE-Governance. This guide does not reproduce that roster.\n\nOps tasks (PO-authorized execution; executed by the authorized DevOps/environment operator; IA-prepared or reviewed; not dedicated PR-session work).\n\nDefinition. An Ops task is any work item that requires privileged access to systems outside the repository. This includes (non-exhaustive): service configuration, secrets and env var changes, deploy/runtime settings, infrastructure console actions, and privileged database operations (creation, grants, production migrations, and other privileged state changes). A DevOps task is treated as an Ops task whenever it requires any of the above privileged external access.\n\nExecution authority. Ops work follows its separately authorized workflow. The Implementation Agent prepares or reviews the required Ops work; the authorized DevOps/environment operator executes it and returns evidence through the responsible review chain. Kronos has no Ops execution or approval role. Authorization, execution, evidence review, QA, and closure remain separate events.\n\nDelegation contract. A direct PO command to execute an identified Ops task constitutes project-level authorization to act as the PO's delegated executor only when:\n\n* The task identity, operational objective, and target are concrete in the PO instruction or an applicable approved Ops instruction.  \n* The requested action remains inside the task's approved scope.  \n* Every action-specific or phase-specific authorization required by the Ops contract exists in its required form and is valid at the dispatch boundary.  \n* The agent has the required tool capability, access, and credential presence without exposing credential values.  \n* Required preconditions, stop checks, rollback controls where applicable, and evidence-capture paths are concrete.  \n* The operation is permitted by system, platform, host, service-provider, organizational, legal, and safety controls external to PF-Canon.\n\nWhen these predicates are satisfied, the delegated agent MUST proceed with the authorized operation and MUST NOT demand a second generic human-only approval solely because the action is operational, privileged, live, mutating, deploy-related, configuration-related, secret-backed, or externally visible. Any additional task-specific or platform-required confirmation remains required. A broad directive is sufficient only when the approved Ops instruction supplies the concrete commands, targets, stop checks, and evidence contract; it is not authority to invent missing commands, widen scope, bypass required approval, or perform unrelated work.\n\nPermitted stops and required blocker response. A delegated agent MUST stop only when an objective blocker prevents valid execution, including a prohibiting higher-priority rule; unavailable tools, network, access, credentials, or capability; an absent or invalid mandatory target, command, authorization artifact, byte identity, hash, stop check, rollback control, or evidence path; material ambiguity that could affect unintended state; changed state that invalidates authorization or safety boundaries; or an operation outside delegated scope. When stopped, the agent MUST identify the concrete blocker, preserve completed safe work and evidence, state exactly what PO value or external action resolves it, and resume once resolved. It MUST NOT substitute a generic actor-type refusal for a specific blocker.\n\nProduct Owner authorization is final within the Glow project-governance lane, but it cannot override higher-priority system or platform policy, manufacture unavailable capability or credentials, validate nonexistent run-specific artifacts, or make an unsafe or ambiguous command concrete.\n\nMutating, privileged, deployment, configuration, database, and secret-backed operations are eligible for explicit PO delegation when otherwise permitted. Before dispatch, the exact target and authorized effect MUST be concrete; any task-required rollback or recovery action MUST be concrete when feasible; and any required STOP CHECK MUST occur immediately before the irreversible or externally mutating boundary. Secret values MUST remain out of commands, logs, chat output, and repo evidence unless an external system securely injects them without disclosure. Completion MUST be supported by the required secret-free Ops evidence.\n\nIA facilitation posture. Ops tasks MAY be part of an epic. When included, they are facilitated by the Implementation Agent (IA). The IA’s job remains to specify intent, constraints, verification, and evidence requirements in a what-not-how manner, then work directly with the PO and any delegated executor. IA facilitation does not create approval authority or widen the delegated scope.\n\nCanon-grounded OPS instructions are required when available. If the relevant PF canon already provides concrete operator steps, commands, required fields, safety rails, validation checks, evidence captures, canonical paths, or decision rules for an Ops task, the task plan MUST include those instructions explicitly.\n\nThe what-not-how posture still applies where canon is silent or incomplete, but it MUST NOT be used to suppress canon-grounded instructions that already exist.\n\nIf canon is silent, incomplete, or ambiguous for a required Ops step, the task MUST state that the missing instruction is unknown and MUST NOT fabricate procedure.\n\nAny PF references used for these instructions MUST remain titles-only.\n\nNot a PR. Ops tasks are not dedicated PR-session work. They MUST NOT be represented as implementable PR work. Every implementation or remediation artifact MUST separate Ops tasks from PR work and label the authorized DevOps/environment operator, Implementation Agent preparation or review, dependencies, safety checks, evidence, and completion boundary.\n\nOps tasks are not QA tasks. They are implementation work that changes runtime state outside the repository and are executed by the authorized DevOps/environment operator under the separately authorized Ops workflow. Ops execution does not convert the work into PR work or QA work.\n\nOps evidence is not a substitute for QA evidence. Ops completion evidence may be a prerequisite for QA, but QA verification still requires functional proof and the required QA evidence outputs defined in QA planning.\n\nSeparation rule (no category mixing). Planning artifacts MUST keep these categories distinct and explicitly labeled:\n\n* Implementation work and deliverables (code and implementation changes)  \n* Ops tasks (environment changes)  \n* QA planning (verification plan and evidence posture)  \n* QA execution (functional runs and governed QA evidence)\n\nOps task record format (required fields). Every Ops task record MUST include:\n\n* Task ID (stable; referenced consistently)  \n* Owner: PO  \n* Facilitator: IA  \n* Target system/service (name only; no secrets)  \n* Intent / desired end state (what changes; what “done” looks like)  \n* Constraints / safety rails (what must remain true while executing)  \n* Success criteria (observable outcomes; not assumptions)  \n* Evidence to capture (what artifact(s) prove the change; where stored)  \n* Rollback intent (what “revert” means at a high level)  \n* Secret handling note (explicitly: no plaintext secrets in docs or evidence)\n\nEvidence posture (required). Completion of an Ops task MUST produce a repo-stored evidence artifact (text-first) under a lowercase audit path such as:\n\n* audit/ops/\\\\/ for Ops execution evidence, or  \n* audit/qa/\\\\/ when the evidence is part of QA execution.\n\nEvidence MUST NOT include secrets. If a setting/value is sensitive, evidence must be presence-only, redacted, or hashed, while still being sufficient to verify that the intended state was reached.\n\nOps evidence provenance minima (required).\n\nEvery Ops task evidence bundle MUST include, at minimum:\n\n* Command transcript: the exact command(s) run, recorded verbatim (including any env var names set). Secret values MUST be redacted or presence-only noted.  \n  Outputs and exit status: stdout, stderr, and the exit code (or equivalent) captured as files.  \n* Verification outputs are captured, not asserted: if a task claims “checksum OK”, “schema validated”, or similar, the evidence MUST include the tool output that shows the check result (not just a narrative statement).  \n* Sanitized embedded excerpts: if file contents are embedded in a report, the excerpt MUST be sanitized to remove terminal control sequences. If sanitization would risk altering meaning, embed only a minimal safe excerpt and rely on the on-disk file path as the authoritative content.  \n* Retained-path manifest when evidence paths diverge: if a PO-authorized OPS task or later OPS review retains evidence under paths, names, formats, or nested run roots that differ from approved deliverable names, the OPS evidence bundle MUST include a manifest mapping each approved deliverable name to the retained evidence path and the equivalence status. The manifest MUST preserve the approved deliverable identity, the retained repo-relative path, any known format mismatch, any nested evidence-root convention used, and the remaining non-claim posture. It MUST NOT move, rename, or rewrite already-produced OPS evidence merely to make the paths match the plan unless the approved task explicitly requires that remediation.\n\nBuild Checklist tracking requirement. Any Ops task included in an epic MUST be represented as a subtask in the module specific build checklist so it can be tracked and reused. The checklist entry MUST use the same Task ID and carry the same required fields listed above.\n\nNo governance drift. Ops tasks MUST NOT create new acceptance tokens or redefine acceptance semantics. If an Ops task affects acceptance, it MUST map to existing governance-defined acceptance posture and be proven via evidence artifacts.\n\nClarification. If a change is fully achievable as code, including tests and deterministic artifacts, it is PR work. If any step requires privileged access to systems outside the repository, that step is an Ops task even if adjacent code changes exist.
