Documentation Outcomes**  \n* Canon references used: list only the canon homes that materially informed the closeout analysis.  \n* Source posture and inputs used: name the primary source of truth for what happened, state which plans or other artifacts were used only for intended scope or framing, and state explicitly whether PF20, PF23, or any non-PF artifacts were used.  \n* When PF10 provides the primary change-specific account of what happened but does not restate the original business case or consolidated PR or Ops sequence, the report MAY use the historically applicable Epic Plan, the approved class-specific Specification, or the change-wide Implementation Plan for those specific gaps only.  \n* The report MUST say explicitly which facts are taken from PF10 and which facts are taken from plan artifacts as gap-filling inputs.  \n* Plans used in this way are framing inputs only and MUST NOT override a live PF10 addendum on the same point.  \n* When PF10 is silent on a docs-only repo-docs sweep, a retrospective or closeout artifact MAY use the docs PR artifact only for documentation-step history, docs file list, validation posture, repo-proof notes, and scope-boundary facts.  \n* The artifact MUST label PF10 silence and MUST NOT use the docs PR artifact to prove implementation behavior, QA completion, close-pack completion, PF-canon drainage, acceptance-token satisfaction, or epic closure unless those stronger proofs are separately present.  \n* Important limits: state any material limits in the current session or evidence set, especially when merged-PR proof, close-pack proof, or other closure-defining artifacts are missing.  \n* Repo-proven versus formally closed posture: if the retrospective can support completion or status moves from repo evidence but cannot prove formal merge or close, say that distinction plainly rather than blurring it.  \n* Later-drain PF-canon updates: when the artifact is intended to support a later PF-canon drain, name the exact affected PF canon home or homes, the exact affected locator or locators, the supported later-drain action, the drain readiness classification, the evidence basis, and whether the drain is expected at epic close, after an additional PR or OPS slice, or after a separate canon-only drain step.  \n* Proposed addenda or live deltas: record any still-live canon deltas, their intended drain homes, and whether they are implementation work, documentation work, or unresolved analysis.  \n* Uncertain drain targets: state None when there are none. Otherwise record the uncertainty explicitly.  \n* Token and evidence semantics, if applicable: distinguish registry or semantics drift from binding or completeness drift, and state whether the issue is resolved, unresolved, or observational only.\n\n### **Final QA Closeout Review \\+ QA RCA (recommended)**\n\nUse this review when closeout depends on synthesizing step-level QA outcomes, remediation history, and canon-alignment posture. It may live inside the close report or as a governed artifact referenced by it.\n\nMinimum structure\n\n* Artifact Map. Name the epic reviewed, the primary epic-specific source of truth, the canon homes used for closeout interpretation, and any framing inputs such as the Implementation Audit or change-wide Implementation Plan or QA Plan.  \n* Source-of-Truth Posture. State which artifact is primary for epic-specific events, which sources are framing only, and any internal mismatch that affects trust or traceability.  \n* Exact Candidate. Record the exact repository and candidate SHA, applicable workflow or check identities and results, and whether the reviewed evidence is current for that candidate.  \n* Verdict Posture. Record the QA scope and governing acceptance criteria; relied-upon tests, checks, commands, fixtures, configurations, and governed evidence; results and failures; decision-maker and decision time; and limitations, exclusions, waivers, or unresolved conditions.  \n* If a prompt label, artifact-map label, or non-PF input name conflicts with PF10, PF23, the Implementation Audit or change-wide Implementation Plan, the QA Plan, or another governing source used for closeout interpretation, the review MUST record the mismatch explicitly. The review MUST evaluate the epic under the governing source-of-truth identity and may preserve the supplied label only as provenance in the Artifact Map.  \n* Closure Registers. When the review is used as a closure-oriented decision aid, include compact registers that separate:  \n  * Deliverables register. Record each closure-critical deliverable, its source, the anchor quote or governing claim, and any exact evidence, path, or token strings that matter.  \n  * QA verification register. Record each QA step or verification item, its source, and the required evidence outputs or pass/fail posture.  \n  * Execution results register. Record the governing execution or remediation claims the review relies on and the outcome labels those claims carry.  \n  * Current-reality register. Record any repo-reality or surface-existence confirmations used to support closure, the relevant path or surface strings when they matter, and whether each confirmation supports, contradicts, or does not address closure.  \n* Closure Trace Ledger. For each closure-critical deliverable or slice, map the deliverable to the QA verification item or items that validate it, the governing execution result or results that claim completion, whether current-reality confirmation was used, a status line (Satisfied | Not satisfied | Caveat), and a short why statement grounded in those inputs.  \n* Path and Surface Reality Ledger. When closure depends on named routes, entrypoints, governed ledgers, or close-pack files, list each required path or surface string verbatim, its source or sources, whether it is proven in current reality or only by execution record, whether it is required for closure, and a short note explaining its closure role.  \n* Proof-Class Separation. When a closure claim relies on more than one proof class, the review MUST name each proof class and state which artifacts prove each class. Do not let public output proof, internal/admin compute proof, vendor-backed behavior proof, QA proof, OPS proof, PF09 drain proof, or close-pack proof imply another proof class unless the review names and proves the bridge.  \n* QA Closeout Summary. State the step-level QA outcome, the overall readiness recommendation, the main blocker or non-blocker themes, and the highest-impact closure risks or gaps that remain.  \n* Closure-decision wording discipline. When a final QA closeout review, retrospective, closure evidence snapshot, ADR, or Lead decision aid uses SATISFIED, Satisfied, READY WITH CAVEATS, supportable to Done, or equivalent closure-oriented wording, it MUST state the exact decision axis covered by that wording.  \n* Unless directly proven in the reviewed evidence, the artifact MUST mark the following as not performed, no claim, or not proven: PO closeout action, board update, merge provenance, formal OPS action, formal close-pack completion, PF-canon drainage, and final PF09 status update.  \n* A closure-trace SATISFIED statement, readiness recommendation, or supportable-status statement is not by itself a PO closeout action, board update, merge provenance assertion, formal OPS completion, formal close-pack completion, or canon-drain completion.  \n* Canonical RCA Requirement Basis. List the canon sections that justify the review method.  \n* For each canonical basis item, include the PF document title and either a short proof excerpt or a precise evidence pointer showing why that source governs the review method.  \n* Required elements checklist. Confirm the presence or absence of the D0 Discovery artifact, runtime functional proof when required, governed current-state QA evidence under the epic QA root, the QA RCA summary, Coverage vs QA Plan accounting, a readiness recommendation, indexed evidence, and the applicable venue posture.  \n  * When the approved proof includes a venue-specific claim, confirm the required governed venue binding and treat absent, ambiguous, or contradictory venue proof according to the plan’s stated effect.  \n  * When venue is not material, record `NOT CLAIMED`, `NOT APPLICABLE`, or `UNKNOWN - NON-MATERIAL`, as appropriate, and do not treat absent Codespaces provenance as an uncovered QA step or missing closeout element.  \n  * Do not infer the execution venue from a provider name, repository path, current console session, devcontainer configuration, or artifact location.  \n* The required elements checklist MUST end with a compliance statement that states Complete, Complete with caveats, Incomplete, or Not assessed. It MUST NOT say Complete when any required element is absent, ambiguous, or unsupported by governed evidence.  \n* Step-cluster approval proof. When a final QA closeout review asks the reviewer to approve an executed Live QA step cluster, governed current-state QA evidence MUST be surfaced at cluster level, not only as a result summary. For every executed step cluster under review, the review MUST identify the manifest entry or entries, the manifest path-proof posture, the primary log or logs, primary-log path-proof binding, captured\\_env posture, evidence\\_artifacts posture, intended\\_tokens posture, claimed\\_tokens posture, and the result sidecar or other plan-defined decisive receipt.  \n* A result JSON, PASS label, or summary sentence is not sufficient by itself for final closeout review when the step cluster is being used as current-state Live QA evidence. The closeout review must show the manifest, header, tokenless or token-claim posture, and path-proof surfaces that make the PASS auditable.  \n* QA Timeline. Summarize the major remediation loops, ADR or audit events, and QA step outcomes in a stable chronology. If the governing source is append-only, the review MAY use source order as the canonical chronology and MUST say so explicitly.  \n* Coverage vs QA Plan. List every planned QA step in plan order, record whether it is Fully evidenced, Partially evidenced, or Not evidenced, note any material mismatch, and state the closeout impact for each step.  \n* Coverage vs QA Plan MUST separately call out any accepted plan-execution deviation, even when the step is Fully evidenced and PASS. Examples include bounded Moon Loop reruns, rails changes, and step-local dependency-preflight corrections. Coverage status alone is not sufficient when accepted execution materially diverged from the approved plan.  \n* For each remediated step, Coverage vs QA Plan accounting MUST distinguish original planned receipts from accepted remediation receipts and identify the final accepted receipt or evidence basis. Failed or superseded receipts remain part of the record and MUST NOT be hidden, but they MUST NOT be treated as the governing PASS basis once an accepted remediation receipt is proven.  \n* Findings. Record each substantive finding with what happened, why it matters, classification, PF touchpoints when needed, and evidence-pointer posture.  \n* Root Cause Analysis. State the primary root cause, contributing factors, what made the issue hard to detect or hard to close, and the role of any remediation loops in reducing or preserving uncertainty.  \n* Remediation Loop Assessment. For each major remediation loop, rerun sequence, or ADR-backed correction path used in closeout, state whether it reduced uncertainty, corrected evidence or closure-posture drift, or only preserved a caveat, and explain why. Distinguish productive bounded remediation from churn  \n* Evidence Hygiene Assessment. State which evidence families were strong, which remained risky, and whether each decisive proof depended on step logs, path-proof surfaces, validators, checksums, close-pack binding, or other governed evidence discipline. When a risk could recur in future epics, state the canon, planning, QA, or evidence-posture change that would prevent recurrence.  \n* Implementation Gaps and Proposed Fixes. For each remaining gap, state the symptom, the expected behavior, the likely locus, a high-level fix, and a verification hook.  \n* Doc Deltas. State whether PF06 has any delta from the review. If the correct home is another PF document, route the delta there and say why PF06 is not the correct home.\n\nGuidance on evidence-light decision records\n\n* If a guidance record, ADR set, or other closeout decision note is used but does not carry explicit evidence-pointer lines, the review MUST label it as evidence-light guidance.  \n* Evidence-light guidance MAY inform decision framing, but it MUST NOT be treated as stronger than the evidence-backed implementation, QA-pass, or close-pack records around it.  \n* When possible, the review SHOULD pair each evidence-light guidance item with the governing evidence-backed lines that make the decision auditable.\n\n### **Closure Evidence Snapshot (for Lead decision)**\n\nEvidence produced:\n\n* \\\\\n\nEvidence missing or ambiguous:\n\n* \\\\\n\nOpen closure items or Lead questions:\n\n* \\\\\n\n# **Appendix A — Large Schemas & Assets (dedicated PR-session constraints)**\n\n## **Purpose**\n\nDefine how to include large schemas or assets when content is too large to paste inline or when the dedicated PR session cannot reliably receive external attachments. This appendix preserves ownership, auditability, and single-home discipline while keeping execution mechanical and repeatable.\n\n## **Constraints (facts)**\n\n* The dedicated PR session can read available PF and repository sources, but may not have reliable access to large external assets through attachment workflows. The Implementation Agent includes execution-critical formats and small schemas or snippets in the PR Instruction when needed for an unambiguous handoff.  \n* Only the Product Owner may load a large file into the repository or PR branch when the active tooling requires a human upload. That upload does not substitute for **PR Implementation Proceed**, review, or merge.  \n* The dedicated PR session may adapt implementation detail within approved scope and records every material change or deviation in the Detailed Change Report.  \n* Assets live only in governed locations under `artifacts/**`, `docs/**`, or, for governed evidence, `audit/**`. Transient or generator paths are not durable homes.  \n* When assets are introduced or moved, update the `PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts`\\-required human Evidence Index, hash sentinel, Machine Evidence Mirror, and path proofs in the same PR when their current applicability rules require those changes.  \n* Apply the complete current Machine Evidence Mirror and path-proof contract in `PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts`; this appendix does not reproduce its schema or byte rules.\n\n## **Roles and responsibilities**\n\n### **Implementation Agent**\n\n* Decide whether approved execution detail can be supplied inline or requires an Asset Draft Pack.  \n* Prepare execution-critical formats, small schemas, snippets, and the Asset Draft Pack when needed.  \n* Include the asset handoff, exact target paths, constraints, and evidence expectations in the PR Instruction.  \n* Review the Detailed Change Report and route any proposed scope change through the governing Specification route.\n\n### **Product Owner**\n\n* Run **PR Implementation Proceed** only after reviewing the complete per-PR Implementation Plan.  \n* Load Asset Draft Pack files into the PR branch at the specified targets only when the active tooling requires the human upload.  \n* Squash-merge only after the contract-defined review chain supports adoption.\n\n### **Dedicated PR session**\n\n* Validate the actual repository baseline and asset availability while preparing the per-PR Implementation Plan.  \n* Use the approved inline materials, loaded assets, and repository contents during implementation.  \n* Open the PR, run applicable validation, and list every added, modified, or removed file and every deviation in the Detailed Change Report.  \n* Stop and return an exact blocker when a missing asset or repository fact would require a change to approved scope.\n\n## **When to use an Asset Draft Pack**\n\nUse a pack when a required artifact cannot reasonably be supplied inline to the dedicated PR session, such as a large JSON or YAML schema, binary, or long fixture.\n\n## **Asset Draft Pack — minimal fields**\n\nSupply the completed pack to the Product Owner and identify it in the PR Instruction. The Product Owner loads the listed files to the PR branch only when required by the active tooling.\n\n```\nasset_pack:\nepic_id: \"EPIC-?.?\"\nowner: \"Implementation Agent\"\nassets:\n  - asset_id: \"schema_user_profile_v3\"\n    title: \"User Profile Schema v3\"\n    repo_target_location: \"<REPO_RELATIVE_PATH>\"\n    size_bytes: 123456\n    sha256: \"<64-hex>\"\n    license_note: \"<LICENSE_AND_SOURCE>\"\n    single_home_category: \"Architecture\"\n    notes: \"Consumed by component X; the dedicated PR session validates this location.\"\n```\n\n## **Guardrails**\n\n* No secrets or PII. Include license and source.  \n* Maintain exactly one durable home per concept and route by category title rather than version number.  \n* Keep paths repository-relative and stable; list titles and paths in the human Evidence Index when applicable.  \n* For governed assets, apply the indexing, Machine Evidence Mirror, and co-located path-proof requirements in `PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts`.  \n* A recorded SHA proves the bytes hashed at that event. Revalidate after candidate movement; the SHA alone is not a progression gate.\n\n## **Flow (high level)**\n\n1. The Implementation Agent decides inline versus Asset Draft Pack and creates the self-contained PR Instruction.  \n2. The dedicated PR session validates repository and asset reality and creates the per-PR Implementation Plan.  \n3. The Product Owner reviews that Plan and, if approved, runs **PR Implementation Proceed**.  \n4. The same dedicated PR session implements, tests, opens the PR, and reports any missing asset, stub, or deviation.  \n5. The contract-defined review chain evaluates the exact PR head and applicable evidence; bounded failures return to the same PR.  \n6. The Product Owner supplies any required human-loaded asset and is the sole squash merger.  \n7. The Implementation Agent ensures that the Doc Delta and applicable human index, hash sentinel, machine mirror, and path proofs reflect the final assets in the same PR.\n\n## **Planning mode**\n\nPlanning may propose file trees, stub schemas, and integration points and must surface gaps early. It is advisory until the Product Owner runs **PR Implementation Proceed** on the complete per-PR Implementation Plan.\n\n## **Acceptance and drift guards (exact-source; legacy tokens optional)**\n\n* Evidence parity: use the stable governing requirement, acceptance-criterion, test, artifact, commit, workflow, and decision identities applicable to the changed surface. Preserve all required index, mirror, hash, manifest, path-proof, provenance, and deterministic-validation controls.  \n* Mutation posture: for a PR, bind review and relied-upon CI to the exact PR head and distinguish base, head, merge, and post-merge identities. For authorized direct-`main` mutation, record the current instruction, exact post-write SHA, diff, and applicable push-triggered CI result. Revalidate after candidate movement. A complete acceptance-token roster is not required. Existing token IDs may remain as optional historical indexing metadata.  \n* Report completeness: the Detailed Change Report lists every file added, modified, or removed and every deviation from the approved per-PR Plan.  \n* No surprises: if an asset was not present at implementation time, the dedicated PR session records the blocker or bounded stub; the Implementation Agent reconciles it before acceptance.\n\n# **Appendix B — Remediation Implementation Guides (DEV/OPS only)**\n\n## **Purpose**\n\nIdentify the canonical home and PF06 scope for Remediation Implementation Guides used for escalations and remediation execution.\n\n## **Scope**\n\nThis appendix applies to Remediation Implementation Guides only. It does not change Live QA plan formats.\n\n## **Canonical owner and PF06 boundary**\n\n`PF27-Canon-Plan-Templates` is the single canonical home for the reusable Remediation Implementation Guide template. Use its complete current `Remediation Implementation Guide (Template)` section for the permitted step types, embedded verification, OPS posture, strict lane separation, exact cross-lane dependency-line contract, and paste-ready template fields. This appendix retains only the PF06 purpose and scope stated above; it does not reproduce the governed template contract.\n\n# **Appendix C — Remediation Task Plans (DEV PRs \\+ OPS tasks)**\n\n## **Purpose**\n\nDefine the canonical structure and approval gates for Remediation Task Plans that combine DEV PR work and OPS procedures.\n\n## **Scope**\n\nThis appendix applies to remediation task plans submitted for approval. It does not change Live QA plan formats.\n\n## **Task model (locked)**\n\nA remediation task plan MUST contain only two task types:\n\n* DEV tasks are PRs only and MUST be enumerated as PR-01, PR-02, PR-03 (continue as needed) (no mixed-task steps).  \n* OPS tasks are separately authorized procedures prepared or reviewed by the Implementation Agent and executed by the authorized DevOps/environment operator. OPS tasks MUST be enumerated as OPS-01, OPS-02, OPS-03 (continue as needed) with no mixed-task steps.\n\nEach task MUST also declare its closure posture as exactly one of:\n\n* CLOSURE-CLAIMING  \n* NON-CLOSURE\n\nA CLOSURE-CLAIMING task is one whose approved job is to bring one or more mapped PF09.x rows to Done, support a Done recommendation now, or perform final closure, final binding, final acceptance promotion, or equivalent closure work.\n\nA NON-CLOSURE task is one whose approved job is bounded validation, blocker classification, sequencing correction, evidence-only work, repo-side wiring, contributory work, or another approved intermediate step that does not itself claim PF09 closure.\n\nApproval and review of a NON-CLOSURE task MUST judge only the truthful completion of that approved task purpose. PF09 row closure is not a task-level approval gate for a NON-CLOSURE task.\n\nEach task MUST declare its intent as exactly one of:\n\n* DISCOVERY  \n* CHANGE\n\nCross-lane dependencies (locked line). If a task depends on outputs produced by a prior task in the other lane, the dependent task MUST include exactly one dependency line in this exact form:\n\nInputs needed from Task \\\\ during implementation: \\\\\n\nPlaceholders (for example TBD, to be determined, Sx) in this line are a mechanical blocker.\n\n## **Execution-ready gate (normative)**\n\nA remediation task plan submitted for approval MUST be execution-ready:\n\n* every task has a syntax-normalized semantic contract that is executable by its assigned authorized actor; literal paste-and-run syntax is not a plan-approval test  \n* there are no missing inputs, no missing outputs, and no ambiguous success criteria\n\n## **Approval gate scope (tight)**\n\nFor remediation task plans, approval MUST focus on:\n\n* correct task model (OPS vs DEV; DISCOVERY vs CHANGE; no mixed tasks)  \n* correct sequencing and explicit cross-lane dependencies  \n* concrete deliverables (lowercase paths \\+ filenames)  \n* concrete verification success criteria (what done means)\n\nNot approval blockers: Detailed command lines and step-by-step failure handling are not required as plan-approval conditions.\n\n## **Evidence posture remains non-negotiable (in-flight detail allowed)**\n\nIn-flight operational detail is allowed during execution (OPS command selection, exact CLI flags, procedural failure handling), as long as evidence posture remains intact.\n\nEven when commands and failure handling are developed in flight, OPS execution MUST still capture (as repo-stored artifacts under lowercase audit paths):\n\n* the exact commands actually run (verbatim)  \n* stdout/stderr \\+ exit code (or equivalent output)  \n* the produced artifacts at the declared output paths  \n* deviation notes explaining why a different command/flag was used\n\nOPS execution preflight and classification. Before any OPS task executes external, vendor-backed, privileged, or open-rails behavior, the producing plan or in-flight OPS evidence MUST prove the execution preflight that applies to that task: executable command, target facts, input shape, secret posture, rails posture, deterministic pins, prerequisite proof, PO authorization, and required env or credential presence where applicable. Missing command proof, unresolved placeholders, missing target facts, missing prerequisite proof, absent PO authorization, or uncaptured required env posture is TOOLING\\_BLOCKED unless the approved task defines a narrower non-execution outcome.\n\nOPS outcome labels. Use PASS only when the task preflight passes, the approved command or action runs, the captured outputs satisfy the task success criteria, no secret or identity contamination occurs, and the result summary preserves any non-claims that apply. Use FAIL\\_BEHAVIOR only when prerequisites are proven and the observed behavior fails. Use FAIL\\_TOOLING when the run or evidence is contaminated, unsafe, secret-bearing, identity-bearing when forbidden, guessed, missing required outputs after an attempted run, or otherwise invalid as a tool run. Use TOOLING\\_BLOCKED when the task cannot safely run.\n\nPost-failure command discipline. OPS commands, flags, targets, credentials, hostnames, ports, birth or user inputs, or evidence locations MUST NOT be changed after a failed run merely to force PASS. Any retry-changing fact MUST be canon-backed or approved in the task context, recorded in the result summary, and reflected in the produced evidence.\n\nIn-flight flexibility MUST NOT permit:\n\n* changing governed artifact locations or filenames  \n* introducing new governed files without explicitly stating indexing/mirror intent  \n* indexing remediation-only diagnostics into governed indices/mirror\n\n## **Mechanical blockers (auto-reject if present anywhere in the plan)**\n\n* Any PR-xx task missing an embedded PR-session prompt. A present prompt’s syntax-origin or paste-readiness defect is non-blocking and may be normalized during execution when the semantic contract is preserved.  \n* Any task that mixes DEV \\+ OPS work in a single task.  \n* Any task output specified only as a directory. Deliverables MUST be concrete file paths including filenames (for example audit/qa/\\\\/\\\\/\\\\), and directory names MUST be lowercase ASCII.  \n* Any cross-lane dependency missing the exact dependency line, or using non-concrete exact items.  \n* Any task missing explicit verification success criteria (what done means and how it is recognized from produced artifacts).\n\n## **Governed evidence filenames and path-proofs**\n\nAny remediation task plan that includes tasks touching governed evidence indices, mirrors, or path-proofs MUST name the exact current files as task outputs and as embedded verification checks inside the owning DEV or OPS task, not as standalone verification-only tasks.\n\nThe complete current filenames, locations, canonical-byte rules, sibling path-proof relationships, and indexing and mirror requirements are owned by `PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts`. Use that source directly; this appendix does not reproduce the roster.\n\nIf a plan proposes a new file under governed surfaces, it MUST state whether it is intended to appear in the Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror. Absence of that statement is a blocker.\n\n## **Portability vs provenance (non-PF evidence)**\n\nRemediation task plans may include a short Evidence inventory reviewed (non-PF) list for provenance, but MUST NOT require the reader/executor to open external files to execute the plan.\n\nIf a remediation plan depends on any non-PF fact (command outputs, headers, error strings, observed file paths, status lines), the plan MUST embed that fact directly in the document as a short quote or precise paraphrase inside an Observed Evidence Snapshot section.\n\nIf an Artifact Map is included, it MUST explicitly label non-PF inputs as provenance only; not required to execute. Otherwise the non-PF input is treated as an execution dependency and becomes a portability blocker.\n\nWhen a non-PF observation drives a branching decision, the plan MUST include:\n\n* the observation to look for (exact string/status/shape)  \n* the decision rule  \n* the output artifact path where the observation is captured (file path including filename; lowercase directory names)\n\n## **Canonical Remediation Task Plan Template (paste-ready)**\n\n### **Artifact Map**\n\n* Inputs (non-PF): provenance only; not required to execute  \n* Output: Remediation Task Plan (for approval)\n\n### **Observed Evidence Snapshot (self-contained; non-PF)**\n\n* Evidence excerpts required for execution (quotes or precise paraphrases only)\n\n### **Task Overview**\n\n* Task ID  \n* Task name  \n* Task type (DEV/OPS)  \n* Task intent (DISCOVERY/CHANGE)  \n* Task closure posture (CLOSURE-CLAIMING or NON-CLOSURE)  \n* Owner/role  \n* Depends on  \n* Cross-lane dependency  \n* Outputs\n\n### **Task Details (repeat per task)**\n\nTask ID:\n\n* Task name:  \n* Task type (DEV or OPS):  \n* Task intent (DISCOVERY or CHANGE):  \n* Task closure posture (CLOSURE-CLAIMING or NON-CLOSURE):  \n* Owner/role:  \n* Preconditions:  \n* Inputs:  \n* Actions (what-not-how; execution detail may be developed in flight for OPS):  \n* Outputs (required; concrete paths \\+ filenames; lowercase directory names):  \n* Verification (required; success criteria and what artifacts prove done):  \n* PR-session prompt (required for DEV; omit for OPS):  \n* Evidence capture (required for OPS): where commands/output/deviations are recorded (paths \\+ filenames; lowercase directory names):\n\nInclude the dependency-line rule exactly once when cross-lane dependency exists.\n\n",
    "2a4a254422da92933e7f4dce9e074bcd7e1a1a6609ed54a7897d3f5f8cc059d0": "# **0\\. Front Matter**\n\n## **0.1 Header**\n\n**Title:** PF19-Canon-Glow-QA-Guide  \n**Status:** Canon  \n**Version:** v3.0.5  \n**Effective date:** 2026-09-08  \n**Last Update Gate:** PF10 13.0.9  \n**Invocation tag:** INV-f2ac55d77ce9aacc\n\n## **0.2 Purpose & scope**\n\nPurpose. Standardize pre-commit and post-commit QA across HDE, Catalog/A7, Aux, App FE/BE, DB/Vendor ingest, and CLI/API. This guide defines what to check and where to route policy; concrete bytes, schemas, and tokens remain in their existing single homes.\n\nScope rule. Any document with “HDE” in its title is HD Engine–specific. PF19 points to those documents by title only and does not duplicate their contents. PF19 itself covers all projects (Engine \\+ App \\+ shared tooling).\n\nChange-lane QA applicability (normative).\n\nPF19 applies the same applicable QA rigor to Epic and CRD work. A CRD identity does not abbreviate QA or substitute implementation validation for independent QA. The approved Epic or CRD Specification is the intent and scope baseline; the separately approved whole-change Implementation Plan governs delivery. QA planning and execution remain separate work products under §3.1.\n\nFor PF19, `<change-id>` means the actual governed Epic or CRD identity. Epic work retains its applicable phased PF09 mapping. CRD work retains its assigned CRD ID, approved Specification, Implementation Plan and decision lineage; PF30 registration or an invented PF09 mapping is not a prerequisite. PF20 and PF30 are historical records, not active planning or approval authorities. Generally applicable Epic QA references also apply to CRDs through the corresponding change identity. Event-bounded Epic history and expressly Epic-only contracts retain their original scope.\n\nThe CRD-compatible evidence references remain:\n\n* QA evidence root: `audit/qa/<crd-id>/`.  \n* Current-state manifest: `audit/qa/<crd-id>/qa_step_logs_manifest.json`.  \n* Per-check evidence: `audit/qa/<crd-id>/checks/<check_id>/`.  \n* Remediation staging: `audit/qa/<crd-id>/remediation/<lowercase_slug>/`.  \n* Distinct Ops evidence consumed by QA: `audit/ops/<crd-id>/<task_id>/`.\n\nAuthored off-repository QA work products use ChatGPT Library under §0.4.3. Existing repository plans such as `docs/qa/<crd-id>-live-qa-plan.md` retain their recorded role; their existence is not a universal QA prerequisite. This does not re-home repository-controlled execution evidence or authorize migration of historical files.\n\nLowercase directories, governed evidence, manifests, path proofs, indexes, mirrors, failure classification and claim separation remain required where applicable. Verdicts bind the actual tested scope, governing criteria, checks, fixtures, configuration, evidence, actor, time and limitations. Apply §10.8 for available execution PF copies, truthful source attribution and substantive currentness. A changed or unavailable SHA alone creates no progression, reapproval or rerun gate. CI success is distinct from QA acceptance; no token roster, token claim or token matrix is required.\n\nHD Engine specifics are delegated, titles-only, to:\n\n* PF01 — HDE-Math-Spec  \n* PF02 — HDE Architecture  \n* PF04 — HDE-Governance  \n* PF05 — HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref  \n* PF09 — HDE-Build Checklist  \n* PF12 — HDE-Schemas & Artifacts  \n* PF14 — HDE-Mechanics Guide  \n* PF16 — HDE Epics Map (historical context only)  \n* PF17 — HDE Narratives Guide  \n* PF09 phased reference rule (normative).  \n  * The former single-document PF09 is retired for active reference use.  \n  * New QA plans, review artifacts, remediation guides, and future PF19 updates MUST reference the relevant phased PF09 document or documents, identified as PF09.1 through PF09.7, rather than the retired single-document PF09.  \n  * Existing PF19 mentions of “PF09 — HDE-Build Checklist” should be read as family references to the phased PF09.x documents until those mentions are drained to the narrower phase-specific home.  \n  * Where a QA question crosses phase boundaries, the artifact MUST name the exact phased PF09.x document or documents consulted rather than treating the retired single-document PF09 as the active source.\n\nEpics and phased planning (titles-only).\n\nPF19 treats epic planning and phase mapping as outside its scope.\n\nFor HD Engine epic history:\n\n* HDE Phased Epics is historical-only: it MUST contain only completed epic records (formally closed per Change Process Guide, titles-only) and is maintained through authorized post-closure recording (no in-flight placeholders or active planning gate).  \n* HDE Epics Map is maintained as historical context only and must not be used as the source of truth for new work.\n\nIn particular:\n\n* HDE-EPIC011 — Vendor Ingest & Data Durability is recorded as a failed epic; its acceptance roster (DB posture, ingest idempotence, evidence discipline, partition plan, SAFE rails, BodyGraph invariance) did not reach a fully green, production-ready state.  \n* HDE-EPIC012–HDE-EPIC014 are preserved as “won’t do” (historical design), and any residual work they described must be captured as recorded debt or re-scoped into a future epic, not treated as open acceptance here.\n\nRole boundary (normative; no governance / no tokens / no planning).\n\nPF14 is a mechanics/components reference only. It:\n\n* MUST NOT define, rename, alias, or curate acceptance token spellings.  \n* MUST NOT act as a planning authority (it may inform planning, but does not govern epic plan structure, acceptance rosters, or close gates).  \n* When PF14 needs to mention governance or acceptance, it MUST route to the governing document by title (and section if needed) and remain descriptive about component fields and mechanical responsibilities only.\n\nPF19 may reference these epics by title when describing QA history or preservation surfaces. New change-level QA decisions belong in the approved Specification and Implementation Plan where they affect scope or delivery, and in the responsible QA artifact where they concern QA. Historical Epic or CRD recording follows the actual closure decision and authorized post-closure administration; it does not become an in-flight tracker or an acceptance prerequisite. HDE Epics Map and HDE Phased Epics remain historical context.\n\nPF19 owns QA principles, checklists, and cross-component playbooks; it routes all transport, math, schema, and token details to those single homes.\n\nReality Audits, readiness and QA acceptance (titles-only).\n\nFor current HDE Epic and CRD work, continuing Isis performs the integrated QA-10 implementation audit, historical PF23 comparison, complete change-audit triage and whole-change readiness assessment defined in §3.1. Its fresh Reality Audit Markdown, separate Change Audit Triage Markdown and QA\\_READINESS are distinct outputs. Historical PF23 observations supply comparison context; current implementation facts require current implementation evidence.\n\nReadiness does not establish QA PASS or closure. Historical discrepancies do not independently impose current requirements or block the approved change. A demonstrated failure of an applicable approved objective prevents readiness; missing decisive evidence leaves an incomplete assessment. PF23 and PF10 publication remain Product Owner actions and are not additional readiness or QA-progression gates. General audit methods remain owned by Reality Audits; technical requirements remain with their current owning PF documents.\n\n## **0.3 Legacy acceptance-token compatibility (names-only)**\n\n`QA_PRECOMMIT_CHECKLIST_OK` and `QA_POSTCOMMIT_CHECKLIST_OK` are preserved names for historical or explicitly bounded legacy use. They are optional indexing metadata, not acceptance authority, and PF19 does not require a token roster, token claim, or token-evidence matrix for current work. Their historical definitions and semantics remain in HDE-Governance and HDE-Build Checklist.\n\n## **0.4 Principles & Single Homes (routing only)**\n\n### **0.4.1 Intent**\n\nPin what PF19 owns (process, checklists, playbooks) versus where bytes and policy live. PF19 stays names-only and routing-only.\n\nPF19:\n\n* stays titles-only for all external references, and  \n* never redefines transport bytes, schemas, or token semantics; §9 may mirror registered names only for QA operational mapping and must identify the owning source.\n\n### **0.4.2 Single homes (titles-only)**\n\nPF19 routes to these existing single homes:\n\n* Transport bytes & public routes: PF05 — HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref  \n* Schemas & artifacts (catalogs, mirror, proof JSON): PF12 — HDE-Schemas & Artifacts  \n* Governance (A7 policy, refusal/writers, tokens): PF04 — HDE-Governance  \n* Architecture (single emitter, boundaries): PF02 — HDE Architecture  \n* Build checklists & CI gates: PF09 — HDE-Build Checklist  \n* Narrative rules & surfaces: PF17 — HDE Narratives Guide  \n* Process (PR-first): PF06 — Change Process Guide\n\n### **0.4.3 Core principles (names-only).**\n\nPF19 assumes and reinforces these core QA principles.\n\nPF19 is titles-only for cross-references. It does not duplicate bytes or schemas and always routes to the owning PF by title. PF19 never redefines wire contracts or token semantics. Those definitions remain in the owning PF homes (for example the CLI/API reference, schemas and artifacts, governance, and the build checklist).\n\nDeterminism and env pins apply in all environments whenever governed bytes are produced. All canonicalization, hashing, header snapshotting, and governed evidence capture must run with LC\\_ALL=C, LANG=C, and TZ=UTC in dev, stage, prod, and CI. Interpreter/runtime knobs such as PYTHONHASHSEED must not be treated as required rails pins unless a specific step explicitly depends on hash-iteration determinism. If such a knob is present, plans may record it as observed context. If absent, plans must not fail or block on that basis.\n\nEvidence is governed by same-PR parity and completeness, not just formatting. The Human Evidence Index (docs/evidence/INDEX.json \\+ docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256) and the Machine Mirror (artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl) must be updated together in the same PR whenever evidence changes, and QA must treat “code change without evidence parity” as a failure, not a warning.\n\nFor every governed artifact under a governed evidence root declared in the Evidence Catalog (titles-only, with schemas and semantics defined only in HDE Schemas and Artifacts), QA must ensure the triple is complete:\n\n* one Human Evidence Index entry,  \n* one Machine Mirror record, and  \n* one co-located path\\_proof.txt whose path is referenced by the Mirror record’s proof\\_anchor.\n\nThis also applies to lifecycle and OPS-managed artifacts (for example backup/restore/retention runs). If any leg is missing, QA must treat the evidence as incomplete and block tokens that depend on it.\n\nPath-proof freshness is normative for the Human Evidence Index and its hash sentinel. docs/evidence/INDEX.json and docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256 are governed artifacts, and their co-located path-proof transcripts (docs/evidence/INDEX.json.path\\_proof.txt and docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256.path\\_proof.txt) must be refreshed whenever the index or sentinel bytes change, in the same PR. Stale INDEX path-proofs are merge-blocking evidence integrity failures and must be remediated by rerunning canonical evidence tooling, not by hand-editing proofs.\n\nBaseline HD Engine evidence must remain agent-readable at the PR level. The primary evidence ledger must be expressed through plain-text artifacts under governed paths (docs/**, artifacts/**, audit/\\*\\*), such as the Human Evidence Index, the Machine Mirror, bundle manifests, and key QA logs and step transcripts.\n\nBinary or compressed bundles may exist as supplementary artifacts, but they must not be the only governed evidence for any acceptance token that requires payload inspection by an agent. Hash-only or status-only proof families are acceptable only when the evidence consumer does not need to inspect payload content. Otherwise, they must be paired with at least one governed text artifact (for example a bundle manifest, QA log, or summary) that exposes the relevant payloads at the evidence ledger level. Titles and schemas for these artifacts remain in HDE Schemas and Artifacts, the build checklist, and related PF docs.\n\nLive QA and bootstrap evidence is produced mechanically under the responsible governed check or existing owning evidence family: logs, JSON, exit codes, tree/env snapshots and scripted captures. Narrative synthesis does not replace those receipts.\n\nOff-repository change-process artifacts, including QA readiness, audit, triage, Guide, Plan, task, review, final Report, separate RCA and remediation work products, are saved in ChatGPT Library. Scratch is transient preparation space. File size, a large attachment or an export does not create a Drive fallback; Notion may carry concise status and usable links, not a second artifact body. Repository-controlled code, tests and governed mechanical evidence remain at their approved repository paths. Existing historical artifacts are not migrated automatically. Product Owner publication of PF10, PF23 or historical change records remains separately authorized administration.\n\nActual prompt-use attribution belongs in the responsible actor's existing permitted artifact or handoff: actual role/stage, change and approved-source lineage, ecosystem and prompt identity/version, resolved source revision, capture or execution point, outputs and observed PR/commit references. Preserve multiple uses and corrections. Record unavailable history and its reason; recommended model settings are not observed settings. Read-only actors pass this metadata to the next authorized writer without acquiring repository write authority. The deferred provenance helper, schema and ledger implementation are not prerequisites for QA or closure, and this rule installs none of them.\n\nCI runs with rails closed by default. CI pipelines run with SAFE\\_MODE=1 and ALLOW\\_NETWORK=0 unless explicitly opened. Any job that opens rails must pin SAFE policy (timeouts/retries/backoff from closed domains, no jitter) as defined in governance, attach governed evidence, and update the Human Index and Machine Mirror in the same PR.\n\nA7 is Catalog-only and is gated by the Endpoint Catalog. A7 proofs run only on a cataloged JSON success route and do not treat /internal/\\* routes (including /internal/version) as an A7 surface. Aux HEAD/304 are out of scope under EPIC-010. A7 QA runs only when docs/ENDPOINTS\\_CATALOG.json exists and is valid per HDE Schemas and Artifacts, and the Catalog row for the Reader JSON success surface exists and is marked as a JSON success route. If those conditions are not met, QA treats the A7 suite as gated off: no A7 tokens are claimed for that PR, and the missing or invalid Catalog entry is reported as a QA failure, not a cosmetic skip.\n\nIndustry anchors are reference-only. PF19 aligns its QA rules and proofs with IETF RFC 9110/9111 for HTTP semantics and caching, RFC 8785 (JCS) as an external anchor for JSON canonicalization, OWASP ASVS for FE/BE security verification, and NIST SSDF and SLSA for supply-chain QA and provenance expectations. PF19 remains titles-only: bytes, schemas, and token definitions stay in their owning PF homes (for example PF05, PF12, PF04, PF09).\n\n---\n\n# **1\\. Environments & surfaces map (names-only)**\n\n## **1.1 Intent**\n\nName the QA-relevant surfaces and where their ownership lives, with a clear split between:\n\n* App layer (FE/BE)  \n* HD Engine layer (HDE service and its callers)  \n* Shared tools and evidence system\n\nHDE-titled PF docs apply only to HD Engine surfaces. They do not define contracts for pure App FE or non-HDE App BE endpoints. PF19 stays names-only here: no header matrices, no byte listings, no schemas.\n\n## **1.2 App layer (FE and non-HDE backend)**\n\nThese components use their own product and API docs. HDE PF docs are only relevant where the App talks to the Engine.\n\n* App FE (public web/app).  \n  * Public-facing web and app experience. QA focuses on routing, feature flags, user flows, and integration with backend APIs.  \n  * Implementation and deploy: frontend repo and deploy target (names-only).  \n  * Contracts and behavior: app-level product and API docs (titles-only, non-HDE).  \n  * HDE docs: not authoritative for FE; only relevant at the points where FE calls backend endpoints that themselves proxy HDE.  \n* App BE (service APIs beyond HDE).  \n  * Application backend services that are not the HD Engine. QA focuses on API contracts, auth, data validation, and error posture.  \n  * Implementation and deploy: backend repo and service surface (names-only).  \n  * Contracts and behavior: backend API specs and app-specific docs (titles-only, non-HDE).  \n  * HDE docs: apply only to those BE endpoints that directly call or proxy HD Engine routes; all other BE endpoints are governed by app-specific docs, not HDE PF docs.\n\n## **1.3 HD Engine layer (HDE-only)**\n\nHDE PF docs apply only to the Engine’s surfaces and their direct callers: Catalog/Reader JSON success (A7 surface), Aux narrative text (non-A7), CLI admin preview using the same emitter, and the Required-Now admin bundle CLI and HTTP surfaces that package the full product payload for a single match. Admin bundle surfaces are admin-only, explicitly non-A7 requirements and are routed by PF19 to Governance, CLI/API, Mechanics, and Schemas & Artifacts by title only. App FE/BE are out of scope for HDE policy except where App endpoints proxy HDE; in those cases they must preserve HDE contracts.\n\n* HD Engine service (Reader and Aux; Required-Now admin bundle HTTP route not found in the inspected repository).  \n  * Current Engine HTTP surfaces exposed to the App BE as internal services include Reader JSON and Aux narrative text. The Required-Now admin bundle HTTP route remains an implementation gap in the inspected repository.  \n  * Implementation and deploy: engine service on Railway prod (names-only, see Glow Infrastructure).  \n  * Transport bytes and public routes (including the admin bundle HTTP route): HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref.  \n  * Architecture and boundaries (including separation of Catalog/Reader, Aux, admin-only routes, and ops endpoints): HDE Architecture.  \n  * Governance, A7 policy, and admin-surface auth/logging posture: HDE-Governance.  \n  * Admin bundle builder mechanics and use of the canonical serializer/emitter: HDE-Mechanics Guide and HDE-Schemas & Artifacts.  \n  * All other Engine details: HDE-titled PF docs by title only.  \n  * Epics map (historical-only). For HD Engine epics, HDE Epics Map is historical-only; it records past epic allocations, including HDE-EPIC011 as a failed epic and HDE-EPIC012–HDE-EPIC014 as “won’t do”. HDE Phased Epics is also historical-only: it contains only completed epic records and is maintained through authorized post-closure recording (no in-flight records or active approval gate). QA must treat these documents as historical context and MUST NOT use them for in-flight tracking or as a planning gate.  \n* Admin bundle CLI surface (admin-only; Required-Now).  \n  * Required behavior: call the admin bundle builder and return the full product payload for a single match as a single canonical JSON object.  \n  * Implementation posture: `hdctl admin-bundle` was not found in `engine/cli/main.py` at the pinned commit. Its exact invocable and remote-request bytes remain `OPEN` in HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref.  \n  * Target environment: Railway HD Engine prod service and DB, configured via infra canon (titles-only).  \n  * Governance and auth: HDE-Governance (admin token or equivalent credential required; numeric-bearing content remains admin-only and outside the Reader public covenant).  \n  * QA playbooks and tokens: this guide (PF19) and HDE-Build Checklist (titles-only).  \n* HD Engine integration in App BE.  \n  * Backend endpoints that call HDE are responsible for preserving HDE contracts at the integration boundary.  \n  * HDE contracts: defined only in HDE-titled PF docs (titles-only, no duplication).  \n  * App BE wrapping behavior: defined in backend API docs; PF19 treats it as part of App BE QA with additional checks that HDE contracts, including admin-only boundaries, are honored.\n\n## **1.4 Shared tools and evidence system**\n\nThese pieces are cross-cutting. Some are HDE-specific in terms of contract, but they affect how QA is done across projects.\n\n* CLI/API and SDKs (dev tools).  \n  * Developer-facing tools that exercise the Engine and App. QA focuses on parity with emitters and deterministic behavior.  \n  * Implementation: CLI and SDK repos (names-only).  \n  * Transport and CLI contracts for HDE flows: PF05 — HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref.  \n  * For App-only tools, contracts live in app-specific docs; HDE PF docs only apply when the tool calls HDE.  \n  * For CLI/API and SDKs, PF19 treats two equivalent QA surfaces:  \n    * a Codespace attached to the engine repo acting as a QA console, and  \n    * any other terminal or shell that is configured (by infra canon) to reach the HD Engine prod service and DB on Railway.  \n  * Both surfaces are governed by the same CLI/API contracts (titles-only) and QA tokens; plans must not assume that CLI QA is restricted to Codespaces only when other terminals can reach the canonical Railway endpoints defined in infra canon.  \n* Internal/dev HTTP harnesses (e.g. /internal/dev/sampler).  \n  * Dev-only HTTP routes exposed by the Reader/adapter for internal QA or evidence flows (for example POST /internal/dev/sampler for sampler behavior).  \n  * Implementation and wiring (start commands, ports, host binding) live in infra-facing docs such as Glow Infrastructure and HDE-Mechanics Guide (internal/dev surfaces sections, titles-only).  \n  * Transport behavior and internal/dev HTTP semantics (JSON shape, writer-style error envelopes, headers such as Cache-Control: no-store and “no ETag” posture) live in HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref and HDE-Mechanics Guide (titles-only). PF19 does not restate these bytes; it only routes QA to them.  \n  * Infra/ops ownership. For any internal/dev HTTP harness intended for QA or evidence:  \n    * Infra/ops MUST provide and own:  \n      * a canonical dev start command or service definition that runs the Reader process in dev/Codespaces with APP\\_ENV=dev (and any determinism rails required by Mechanics), and  \n      * a corresponding base URL and port per environment (for example Codespaces vs local dev), from which concrete URLs such as DEV\\_SAMPLER\\_URL=[http://127.0.0.1](http://127.0.0.1/):\\\\/internal/dev/sampler can be derived.  \n    * These URLs MUST NOT be guessed by PO, QA, or doc agents. They MUST be derived from the actual Reader process wiring (ports and host binding) as configured by infra and captured in infra canon.  \n    * Before handing any dev harness URL to QA (for curl, scripts, or external tools), Infra/ops MUST validate it locally with a simple HTTP/1.1 JSON POST under appropriate rails (at minimum APP\\_ENV=dev and, where feasible, determinism env pins) and confirm that the response shape and headers match the internal/dev HTTP behavior specified by the owning PF docs (titles-only).  \n  * QA consumption rule. QA and PO agents:  \n    * MAY consume infra-provided dev harness URLs in QA plans, scripts, and Live QA steps, but  \n    * MUST NOT define or change those URLs themselves. If a dev harness URL or start command is missing or unclear, QA must treat that as a spec/infra gap (see §11.3 canon-first rule), mark affected steps as blocked by infra wiring, and request an infra update rather than guessing ports or paths.  \n* DB/Vendor ingest (authoring plane, sealed packs).  \n  * Pipelines that turn vendor/bodygraph inputs and authored narratives into sealed, versioned packs used by the Engine.  \n  * Implementation: ingest and authoring jobs plus DB layer (names-only).  \n  * Schemas and artifacts (packs, manifests, proof JSON): PF12 — HDE-Schemas & Artifacts.  \n  * Vendor HTTP posture and ingest calls: PF05 — HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref.  \n* Evidence system (indices, mirror, proofs).  \n  * Cross-project system that records what was proven, where, and when. Used by both Engine and App QA, but contracts are defined in HDE PF docs.  \n  * Human Evidence Index and hash sentinel: PF09 — HDE-Build Checklist (process) and PF12 — HDE-Schemas & Artifacts (schema).  \n  * Machine mirror, path-proofs, composite proof JSON: PF12 — HDE-Schemas & Artifacts.\n\n(Names-only section. No header tables, no byte or schema listings.)\n\n# **2\\. Pre-commit QA (local/CI)**\n\n## **2.1 Intent**\n\nCatch issues before PRs merge by enforcing a consistent local/CI QA baseline across all projects.\n\nPre-commit QA focuses on:\n\n* code quality and formatting  \n* deterministic behavior (no hidden I/O or randomness)  \n* snapshot and evidence hygiene  \n* early detection of schema/contract drift\n\nConcrete CI wiring and gates are instantiated in PF09 — HDE-Build Checklist (titles-only); PF19 defines the shared “what,” not the CI job syntax.\n\n## **2.2 Checklist (to be instantiated in PF09 CI)**\n\n### **2.2.1 Lint and format**\n\nPre-commit pipelines SHOULD run language-appropriate linters/formatters and fail on style or syntax issues.\n\n### **2.2.2 JSON/JSONL canonicalization and final-LF checks**\n\n* Enforce canonical form for governed JSON/JSONL files.  \n* Require exactly one trailing linefeed on governed text artifacts.  \n* Reject non-canonical or mixed-style JSON in governed paths.\n\n### **2.2.3 Deterministic, no-I/O unit tests**\n\n* Pure paths MUST NOT depend on RNG, wall-clock time, external network, or filesystem state.  \n* Tests SHOULD prove two-run identity where applicable (same inputs → same outputs/bytes).\n\n### **2.2.4 Env pins for snapshot generation**\n\nFor any job that produces snapshots or evidence, export:\n\n* `LC_ALL=C`  \n* `LANG=C`  \n* `TZ=UTC`\n\nThis applies to Engine, App, and shared tools whenever they emit governed artifacts.\n\n### **2.2.5 Tooling vs behavior failures (pytest and harnesses)**\n\nQA plans and CI logs MUST distinguish tooling failures (for example, missing or non-executable test entrypoints such as `.venv/bin/pytest`) from application/behavior failures (for example, ingest tests failing assertions). A failure where the test harness cannot even start (for example, “cannot execute: required file not found” when invoking `.venv/bin/pytest`) MUST be classified and recorded as an environment/tooling defect, not as a red behavior verdict for the suite under test.\n\nIn Codespaces and similar venv-based environments, the preferred invocation pattern for QA and CI is:\n\n* Activate the venv (for example `source .venv/bin/activate`).  \n* Run tests via `python -m pytest <args>` rather than relying on a wrapper script in `.venv/bin/pytest`.\n\nQA plans SHOULD use `python -m pytest` in copy/paste-ready commands for test-driven steps (including ingest tests), and PF09 CI harnesses SHOULD mirror this pattern where practical.\n\nWhen a tooling failure is encountered (for example `.venv/bin/pytest` is broken but `python -m pytest` succeeds):\n\n* The failure MUST be captured mechanically in a QA log under `audit/qa/<epic-id>/<EPIC_QA_SUBPATH>` with a clear label (for example a `D0-<id>` or `D2-<id>` log entry noting “tooling failure: pytest shim unusable; rerun with python \\-m pytest”).  \n* The suite MUST be re-run once a working invocation (`python -m pytest <args>`) is available under the same intended rails (`SAFE_MODE`, `ALLOW_NETWORK`, env pins).  \n* Only the rerun outcome (pass/fail under correct tooling and rails) is used to judge the behavior of the tests and to satisfy behavior tokens such as `TESTS_PASS_OK`. Tooling failures that are successfully bypassed via the canonical `python -m pytest` pattern must not be treated as ingest/behavior failures.\n\nIf neither `.venv/bin/pytest` nor `python -m pytest` can run the required tests (for example pytest is not importable or the venv is missing), the affected checklist items and tokens (for example ingest-related DISS tasks) are considered blocked by tooling under PF19/PF09/PF07 until the environment is fixed. QA must record this as a tooling blocker (not as a red behavior verdict) and resolve the infra/venv issue before treating the underlying tests as truly failing.\n\nImport-time dependency failures are tooling, not behavior.\n\nIf a pytest run fails during collection/import (for example `ModuleNotFoundError: jsonschema`) before any tests execute, QA MUST classify this as a tooling failure (`FAIL_TOOLING` / `TOOLING_BLOCKED`). Acceptable remediation patterns are:\n\n* Required dependency mode: treat the dependency as required for the relevant CI job and ensure CI installs the required dependency set (for example dev requirements) so the tests actually run.  \n* Optional dependency mode: guard optional dependencies so pytest collection succeeds and the relevant tests either run or skip with an explicit, actionable install hint (for example `pytest.importorskip(\"jsonschema\", reason=\"install requirements-dev.txt to run schema validation\")`).\n\nQA MUST NOT treat “collection died due to missing optional dependency” as a product behavior failure.\n\nProof-string checks against governed prose are harness checks, not behavior proof by themselves. A casing-only, punctuation-only, whitespace-only, or phrase-shape mismatch against governed prose MUST NOT be classified as final `FAIL_BEHAVIOR` until the raw artifact, intended semantic proof target, and governed source posture have been reviewed. When the intended proof target is preserved and the mismatch is a QA evidence-harness defect, the final verdict must come from the accepted rerun or remediation receipt, and the original failed proof must remain preserved as failure context rather than being erased or treated as product behavior failure.\n\nThis is also a plan-review requirement for executable QA steps.\n\n* Any pytest-backed or tool-backed QA step MUST declare the exact dependency set it requires, the explicit preflight check or checks that prove each dependency is present and runnable, and the exact activation or installation action to use when the dependency is missing and remediation is allowed in the execution venue.  \n* If the plan cannot truthfully specify the activation or installation action, it MUST say so explicitly and MUST classify a failed preflight as `FAIL_TOOLING` or `TOOLING_BLOCKED`. It MUST NOT invent installation commands and it MUST NOT let dependency failure collapse into `FAIL_BEHAVIOR`.  \n* Per-step enforcement is required. A shared bootstrap step does not remove step-local responsibility. Each later QA step MUST either include its own dependency preflight and remediation logic inline or explicitly depend on the bootstrap step and rerun a short step-local readiness check before the main command.  \n* The dependency preflight result, any install or activation action taken, and the final ready or not-ready outcome MUST be captured in the step’s governed QA evidence stream.  \n* Any QA plan or QA step that omits dependency preflight and install or remediation posture for a required dependency is non-conforming and blocked for approval.\n\n### **2.2.6 Rails posture in CI (default CLOSED)**\n\nRun pre-commit/CI with `SAFE_MODE=1`, `ALLOW_NETWORK=0` by default.\n\nIf any pre-commit job opens rails (network I/O), it MUST produce governed evidence and index it in the same PR (titles-only routing to PF12/PF09).\n\n### **2.2.7 Machine mirror quick-check (includes path-proofs)**\n\n* Verify `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl` exists and is the only mirror file; records are canonical JSONL (sorted keys, compact, one LF, unknown-key reject, pinned field order).  \n* Verify each record’s `proof_anchor` points to an adjacent stored path-proof; fail CI if any proof is missing.  \n* Enforce “governed roots only”: all indexed artifacts MUST live under a governed evidence root declared in the Evidence Catalog (HDE Schemas & Artifacts, titles-only). Indexed artifacts MUST NOT use transient/generator paths or ad-hoc roots that are not cataloged.\n\n### **2.2.8 Snapshot hygiene (tolerant vs strict)**\n\n* Classify snapshots as strict (must match exactly) or tolerant (pattern-based).  \n* Pin patterns where applicable (for example text posture harnesses; see §6.2 harness).  \n* Fail if strict snapshots drift unexpectedly.\n\n### **2.2.9 Keys-only logs in tests**\n\nWhen tests exercise logging, ensure logs are keys-only and contain no payload bodies or secrets.\n\nLogging policy and redaction rules live in HDE-Governance; PF19 only requires that tests respect them.\n\n### **2.2.10 Drift / schema enforcement for governed artifacts**\n\nTreat each of the following as a CI failure for governed artifacts:\n\n* unknown keys in the machine Mirror  \n* non-canonical snapshots under governed paths  \n* missing trailing LF on governed text\n\nSchema and gate definitions live in HDE-Schemas & Artifacts and HDE-Build Checklist; PF19 requires CI to enforce them.\n\n### **2.2.11 Evidence-governed CI sequence (names-only)**\n\nFor PRs that change governed evidence artifacts, authorized local or pre-commit authoring and hosted CI verification are separate phases. Both phases MUST run under closed rails (`SAFE_MODE=1`, `ALLOW_NETWORK=0`) and determinism pins (`LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, `TZ=UTC`).\n\nAn authorized authoring phase MAY run canonical writers to prepare governed artifacts. Hosted CI MUST verify the exact committed source under review and MUST NOT repair, refresh, or rewrite tracked source to make a decisive committed-state check pass.\n\n* Generate ordering artifacts when in scope.  \n  * During authorized authoring, run the canonical ordering writer once and then run its actual check entrypoint to prove a stable fixed point.  \n  * Hosted CI MUST run the check entrypoint against the committed ordering artifacts. Missing, stale, or drifting artifacts MUST fail the check rather than being repaired in the source checkout.  \n* Treat every non-writing check as non-mutating.  \n  * A non-writing check MUST NOT mutate the repository or external state. Prohibited external-state actions include opening a database connection, executing SQL, committing a transaction, applying a migration, or mutating an external service.  \n  * When a verifier executes a route with a persistence seam, direct side-effect interception tests MUST prove that the persistence seam is not invoked.  \n* Update the Human Evidence Index and Machine Mirror during authorized authoring, then verify them without repair.  \n  * The authorized writer MUST refresh the Index, Mirror, and applicable path proofs from the final on-disk bytes, including at minimum:  \n    * `docs/evidence/INDEX.json.path_proof.txt`  \n    * `docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256.path_proof.txt`  \n  * The writer’s actual check entrypoint MUST then confirm a stable second pass with no drift, dangling artifacts, missing proofs, or schema violations.  \n  * Hosted CI MUST execute that check entrypoint against the committed bytes and MUST fail rather than regenerate a stale or inconsistent evidence graph.  \n* Run topology orientation during authorized authoring, then verify it without repair.  \n  * The authorized writer MUST refresh `audit/gates/topology/orientation_demo.txt` only after the final Index and Mirror state exists.  \n  * The writer’s actual check entrypoint MUST confirm that the orientation output matches the final Index and Mirror and remains stable.  \n  * Hosted CI MUST run the check entrypoint against the committed orientation output and MUST fail rather than refresh it.  \n* Enforce Mirror schema and path-proof discipline.  \n  * Run the Mirror-schema quick-check described in §10.5 to validate canonical JSONL, schema strictness, required fields, pinned field order, stable line endings, the single Mirror file, and `proof_anchor` alignment with `*.path_proof.txt`.  \n* Run ordering and evidence test suites.  \n  * Run the pytest suites that cover ordering properties and evidence correctness. Any failure is a CI failure for the affected governed artifacts.  \n* Keep scoped closure lanes additive.  \n  * A scoped CI or QA lane MAY provide additional proof for a governed evidence subset.  \n  * The main lane MUST continue to run the full repo-wide evidence and fail-closed coverage applicable to the touched governed surfaces.  \n  * QA MUST NOT narrow the main lane to the scoped subset or treat the scoped lane as a substitute for broader evidence correctness, Mirror discipline, or retained global safeguards.  \n  * A scoped closure result is trustworthy only when the scoped lane and the retained main-lane safeguards are green.  \n* Verify proof producers through their real entrypoints.  \n  * Each governed artifact family MUST have one deterministic writer.  \n  * Authorized authoring MUST exercise the writer’s actual write and check entrypoints. Hosted CI MUST exercise the actual check entrypoint against committed bytes.  \n  * A failed predicate MUST leave no partial writes.  \n  * Write-capable execution MUST require explicit write authorization where applicable.  \n  * Every decisive transport predicate MUST have a direct malformed-response test.  \n* Enforce manifest-derived release identity and exact-head external attestation when in scope.  \n  * `catalog/manifest.json` is the single tracked release-identity input. CI MUST derive and verify the release ID read-only from its canonical bytes.  \n  * Release verification MUST NOT require a generated release-ID source constant, regenerated checked-in release derivatives, source-tree execution of an identity-closure writer, or release identity embedded in registry or configuration evidence.  \n  * The external attestation MUST be bound to the exact clean source commit under review. Any required producer closure MUST run only in an isolated tracked-file copy outside the source checkout, and the source checkout MUST remain byte-stable.  \n  * When packaged-entrypoint verification is part of the release claim, the attestation process MUST build the real wheel, install it in an isolated environment without ambient package inheritance, and exercise the registered `hdctl` console entrypoint rather than a shim or source-tree substitute.  \n  * Repeated attestation builds for the same exact source MUST produce the same content tree.  \n  * The external artifact is bounded exact-head PR evidence. Its existence does not by implication establish QA PASS, acceptance-token satisfaction, OPS completion, PF09 status movement, or durable final release admission.  \n* Verify the complete HDE-EPIC038 release-sanity family when in scope.  \n  * The governed release-sanity log at `audit/gates/sanity_pipeline/sanity_pipeline.log` MUST contain exactly one ordered result for each of the nineteen configured stages, followed by `first_failed_stage:NONE` and `summary:PASS`. An omitted, duplicated, reordered, or non-OK stage MUST fail release-sanity validation.  \n  * The nineteen-stage log and the exact-head external attestation are distinct evidence surfaces. Neither surface, alone or together, establishes QA PASS, acceptance-token satisfaction, OPS completion, PF09 status movement, release admission, or closeout by implication.  \n* Enforce generated development and packaging cleanliness.  \n  * Local `.venv` trees and generated `*.egg-info` metadata MUST remain ignored and untracked.  \n  * A tracked virtual-environment root or tracked generated package metadata is repository contamination and MUST fail source-inventory or clean-tree validation.  \n* Keep iterative local validation, remote-only validation, and exact-final-head confirmation distinct. Remote-only validation belongs only to conditions that cannot be proven locally; it MUST NOT replace iterative local checks or exact-final-head protection.  \n* Classify automated controls by continuing product and delivery risk and by lane.  \n  * Required PR CI MUST protect continuing product and delivery risk independently of epic administration.  \n  * Release and security, QA and audit, and closeout validation are distinct lanes. Evidence generation, audit work, or closeout work MUST NOT substitute for ordinary required PR CI or become required PR CI solely because it was required during one epic.  \n* CI-budget control MUST be automated and durable. Manual push counts, agent promises, operator pause gates, exception narratives, transient reports, and documentation-only remediation MUST NOT serve as enforcement substitutes.  \n  * Automated control MUST prevent or short-circuit duplicate, superseded, irrelevant, and unnecessarily repeated work while preserving every applicable protection.  \n  * Applicability MUST be deterministic and truthful. A stable required-check conclusion may be green only when every applicable protection passed or the check deterministically established that it did not apply.  \n  * The exact candidate presented for merge MUST receive every applicable required protection. An earlier green commit does not validate a later head.  \n* Review CI-budget and exact-head claims by directly inspecting the pinned workflow and configuration plus the relevant GitHub run behavior. Do not require a separate report when those facts are directly observable, and do not allow a report to substitute for automated remediation.  \n* These requirements do not mandate a particular YAML structure, job name, cache implementation, concurrency syntax, or change-detection mechanism.\n\nPF19 defines the required sequence at the QA level. PF09 — HDE-Build Checklist, PF12 — HDE-Schemas & Artifacts, and HDE-Mechanics Guide provide the concrete tool names, schemas, artifact ownership, and CI job definitions.\n\n### **2.2.12 Engine serializer/composer determinism**\n\nProve two-run identity and AB↔BA parity (where defined) for Engine serializer/composer behavior. Ban RNG/time/FS/network in pure paths; governed outputs follow canonical JSON rules. Tokens live in PF04/PF09; bytes in PF14/PF12.\n\n### **2.2.13 Secrets & SCA/SAST/DAST**\n\nRun secrets scanning and composition analysis; add SAST/DAST appropriate to the repo. Keep test logs keys-only (no payloads/secrets). Governance lives in PF04; CI wiring in PF09.\n\n### **2.2.14 Reproducibility & flake control**\n\nFix seeds; avoid uncontrolled wall-clock dependence; pin locale and timezone. Treat flakiness as an unresolved condition. Quarantine MAY be used only as temporary containment under a traceable record that identifies the test, observed failure, responsible owner, tracking item, review or expiry condition, and dequarantine criterion. Preserve every attempt result and classify a fail-then-pass result as flaky, not passed. Quarantine does not satisfy `TESTS_PASS_OK`; if the quarantined test protects an in-scope acceptance predicate, that predicate remains unresolved until the test is deflaked and passes under the governed rails, or the acceptance scope is changed by separate authority.\n\n### **2.2.15 Test data & PII**\n\n* Use synthetic fixtures where possible.  \n* Redact payloads.  \n* Enforce keys-only logs in tests (policy PF04).\n\n## **2.3 Rails & environment posture — PO/epic mandated rails**\n\nEvery EPIC’s PO specifies what rails posture must be used to accept the epic (open rails vs closed rails). This posture is non-negotiable: it informs which tests must be run and how results are interpreted.\n\nIf an EPIC requires open-rails testing (`SAFE_MODE=0`; `ALLOW_NETWORK=1`), then QA MUST confirm those rails are actually in effect for any Live QA run used for acceptance.\n\nIf only closed-rails tests are run (`SAFE_MODE=1`; `ALLOW_NETWORK=0`) when open rails are required, then the run cannot be used as open-rails acceptance evidence. The step’s primary log (and any token claims) MUST record this explicitly via its status and a clear reason (in the header or at the top of the log body).\n\nRails posture must be operator-visible and tool-neutral.\n\n* QA helpers, evidence generators, and review harnesses MUST NOT silently flip rails from closed to open on the operator’s behalf.  \n* When an acceptance-relevant proof lane requires open rails, the command or step definition MUST require caller-provided `SAFE_MODE=0` and `ALLOW_NETWORK=1`, and MUST fail closed if those rails are absent.  \n* If the emitted bytes for the proof lane depend on additional environment fields beyond the base rails pins, the step MUST capture and pin those influencing fields or treat the result as nondeterministic and non-claimable.  \n* This applies to internal/dev writer or readback proof lanes as well as CLI or vendor behavior checks.  \n* Explicit open-rails writer proof does not widen A7 scope or change the owning surface classification.\n\nRails evidence (normative) is required: each Live QA step’s primary log MUST include a `captured_env` header field as described in §4.4, capturing at least:\n\n* `SAFE_MODE`  \n* `ALLOW_NETWORK`  \n* `APP_ENV`  \n* `LC_ALL`  \n* `LANG`  \n* `TZ`\n\nThis is canonical evidence of which rails were actually in effect for that step. It must be present even when Rails posture is “obvious” from context, because reviewers cannot accept implicit environment assumptions.\n\nWhen mandated rails cannot be met due to environment constraints (for example, `SAFE_MODE` is enforced on CI runners), the QA plan must either (a) route that step to a compatible environment, or (b) mark the affected steps as `TOOLING_BLOCKED` or `FAIL_TOOLING` in their headers with a clear reason (in the header or log body) (see §7.2), referencing the rail mismatch.\n\n# **3\\. Post-commit QA (staging/prod)**\n\n## **3.1 Intent**\n\nProve route posture, capture evidence, and update indices in the same PR once changes are deployed to a staging or production-like environment.\n\nPost-commit QA focuses on:\n\n* confirming each surface behaves as promised (status, headers, body)  \n* capturing stable evidence (snapshots and proof JSON)  \n* updating both the human index and the machine mirror in the same PR that carries the evidence\n\nConcrete schemas, tokens, and CI wiring live in PF04, PF09, and PF12 (titles-only); PF19 defines the shared checklist.\n\nWorkflow placement (HDE Epic and CRD work; normative).\n\nThe approved Specification supplies intent, scope, exclusions and objectives. The separately approved whole-change Implementation Plan supplies the coherent delivery basis. They may identify QA objectives and eventual proof obligations without embedding a Live QA runbook or requiring an active Epic Plan, CRD Plan or Implementation Guide as an additional planning layer. Applicable phased PF09 work remains mapped; PF20 and PF30 supply history only.\n\nComplete and accept the required implementation PRs, applicable Ops and final repository-documentation PR before whole-change QA entry. Repository documentation delivery is distinct from later permanent PF drainage. Implementation tests, a successful PR subset and Ops evidence do not establish independent QA acceptance. Functional changes require trustworthy runtime functional proof on the changed surface, or a CI-sourced proof that actually executes it; artifact-only validation cannot satisfy that obligation.\n\n### **3.1.1 Integrated implementation audit and readiness**\n\nContinuing Isis owns QA-10. Resolve the exact approved Specification, whole-change Implementation Plan and amendments, required delivery and documentation acceptance evidence, relevant implementation/environment references, current technical Canon and audit/triage methods, and historical PF23 observations. A prior readiness decision is optional history.\n\nPerform the complete fresh implementation audit, including traceable positive and negative findings, applicable coverage and explicit unknowns. Compare historical observations as new, persistent, resolved, changed/equivalent or unverifiable. Triage every finding without losing identity, evidence, relationship to approved objectives, disposition, proposed action or owner. Reconcile the entire approved change and its dependencies; a successful subset or lack of discovered defects is insufficient.\n\n| QA-10 output | Required purpose |\n| :---- | :---- |\n| Fresh Reality Audit Markdown | Complete current implementation audit, source and evidence coverage, limitations and dated historical PF23 comparison; suitable for manual PF23 publication. |\n| Separate Change Audit Triage Markdown | PF10-addendum-ready account of every finding, evidence, objective/scope relationship, disposition, proposed work/owner and known existing-entry references. Proposals remain distinct from approvals and actual recorded entries. |\n| QA\\_READINESS | Exact approved lineage, whole-change reconciliation, audit/triage references, readiness result, unresolved dependencies and the actual next action. Include the conditional remediation handoff here unless its receiving contract requires a separate substantive artifact. |\n\n| Assessment state | Decision and route |\n| :---- | :---- |\n| Fresh evidence demonstrates failure of an applicable approved objective | NOT\\_READY. State the objective and approved source, expected outcome, demonstrated shortfall and required resolution evidence; route to §10.6.
