Codespaces QA environments (environment details)**\n\n## **14.1 Intent**\n\nCodespaces is a supported Live QA execution environment, but it introduces pitfalls: ephemeral state, container drift, and unclear prerequisite documentation. This section defines the canonical requirements for Codespaces-based Live QA.\n\nHDE Live QA execution-environment contract (normative).\n\nGitHub Codespaces remains the canonical and preferred shared HDE QA console. `Canonical` and `preferred` do not mean `exclusive` or `mandatory for every epic`.\n\nHDE Live QA may execute in Codespaces or in another execution environment permitted by the owning Live QA Plan or applicable QA authority, provided that the environment satisfies the plan’s material environment contract and produces governed, reproducible evidence.\n\nExact Codespaces execution and venue provenance are mandatory only when Codespaces is material to the approved proof. Codespaces is material when at least one of the following is expressly part of the proof scope:\n\n1. The epic changes or validates the devcontainer, Codespaces bootstrap, Codespaces base image, Codespaces-specific tool availability, or another Codespaces-specific runtime dependency.  \n2. The claim concerns Codespaces secret injection, environment provisioning, network egress, forwarded ports, repository mounting, filesystem behavior, provider identity, or another provider-specific integration.  \n3. A supported operator workflow promises that the relevant harness, command, service, or application surface works in Codespaces.  \n4. The behavior or defect is reasonably capable of differing in Codespaces because of the container, operating system, architecture, shell, dependency, filesystem, networking, or provider configuration.  \n5. The Live QA Plan defines a venue-specific acceptance criterion and explains why venue can affect the result.  \n6. The closeout claim asserts a Codespaces-run capability or relies on Codespaces execution as proof of operational readiness.\n\nCodespaces is not made material merely because a plan names it as the intended venue, infrastructure canon calls it canonical or preferred, a command can run there, the repository contains a devcontainer, a secret name may be provisioned there, an optional dependency command uses a devcontainer script, a governed QA path exists, a current Codespace can inspect an earlier artifact, or a reviewer prefers uniform provider provenance.\n\nA Live QA Plan that makes venue normative MUST state all four of the following:\n\n* `Venue-specific claim`  \n* `Why venue can affect the result`  \n* `Required venue evidence`  \n* `Effect of missing venue evidence`\n\nWithout those four statements, an execution-venue field records an intended or preferred operator surface. It does not create an acceptance criterion or closeout blocker.\n\nEvery governed HDE Live QA execution MUST capture the material environment facts required to interpret and reproduce the result, including as applicable:\n\n1. the stable QA step or check identity;  \n2. the actual source and relevant implementation/environment identity, with observed commit identifiers where available and unknown identifiers explained under §10.8;  \n3. the governed entrypoint, command, command family, endpoint, or harness invocation used;  \n4. the required repository root or working locus;  \n5. interpreter, runtime, toolchain, and dependency readiness;  \n6. deterministic environment pins;  \n7. rails and network posture;  \n8. the external target identity when the check reaches an external service, database, or vendor;  \n9. secret-presence or binding posture without secret values;  \n10. the applicable PASS or FAIL predicate;  \n11. actual exit status and result output;  \n12. governed evidence paths and required manifest, index, hash, or path-proof bindings; and  \n13. any accepted execution deviation that materially changed how the planned check ran.\n\nWhen Codespaces is material, at least one governed, secret-safe artifact MUST bind the exact check or governed artifact, the Codespaces venue, the canonical repository association, the execution-source identity, the command or command family, the Codespaces-specific property being proven, and sufficient event or chronology information to connect execution to the evidence. A present-day Codespaces session does not retroactively prove an earlier venue.\n\nMoving execution to another permitted environment is a material plan deviation only when venue is a proof axis, the substitution changes a material dependency, target, rails, network, secret, or runtime condition, or the plan forbids substitution for a supported reason. Otherwise, substitution is acceptable when the complete environment contract and all check predicates remain satisfied and the actual posture is recorded truthfully.\n\nWhen venue is not material:\n\n* absence of Codespaces provenance is not a QA failure;  \n* absence of Codespaces provenance is not a closeout blocker;  \n* an otherwise supported result MUST NOT be downgraded solely because the hosted or physical venue is unknown;  \n* reviewers MUST NOT infer where execution occurred; and  \n* the venue MUST be recorded as `NOT CLAIMED`, `NOT APPLICABLE`, or `UNKNOWN - NON-MATERIAL`, as appropriate.\n\nMinimum required content (normative) is as follows:\n\n* A stable, documented Codespaces/devcontainer configuration and required secrets/env var names (names-only; no values).  \n* A reference to the authoritative environment profile in this PF (see §14.5) for the epic being tested.  \n* A Step-0 Doc Delta Capture posture for missing/ambiguous prerequisites discovered during planning (see §14.6).  \n* A maintenance rule: actual prerequisite changes and their evidence must be recorded in the approved work and routed for permanent PF maintenance under §14.6; a pending permanent drain alone is not an execution or closure gate.\n\nConformance note (normative): Codespaces conformance is evaluated using the Codespaces-specific requirements in §14.6; reviewers MUST NOT treat any optional snapshot artifacts as an approval gate.\n\n## **14.2 Definitions (codespaces vs prod vs QA console)**\n\nDefinitions in this section are as follows:\n\n* Codespaces / QA console. A Codespace is a QA console and artifact sink: it runs commands and stores ordinary Live QA evidence under the canonical `audit/qa/<epic-id>/` root and its PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts-authorized children.  \n* Prod. For Live QA, prod is the deployed service surface defined in infra canon, not the Codespaces container.  \n* Closed rails vs open rails. Closed rails (`SAFE_MODE=1`, `ALLOW_NETWORK=0` plus env pins) are the default for CI and determinism work; open rails from a QA console are allowed only for explicitly defined Live QA steps and mandated rails postures.\n\n## **14.3 QA environment set (Codespaces)**\n\nPF19 recognizes four product QA environment classes. A class is supported for Codespaces-based QA only when its profile is explicitly marked `Defined/supported` and every required field is populated from owner-authorized facts. At this revision, only the HD Engine Codespaces profile is defined/supported. The three App profiles are recognized but unsupported/undefined for Codespaces use.\n\n* HD Engine — `Defined/supported`  \n* App Back End — `Unsupported/undefined`  \n* App Front End — Web — `Unsupported/undefined`  \n* App Front End — Mobile — `Unsupported/undefined`\n\n`Unsupported/undefined` is a configuration-status boundary. It does not claim that the product component is unsupported, absent, or untestable. Planning may identify the missing profile facts, but a check that materially depends on an undefined profile is `TOOLING_BLOCKED` until owner-authorized facts and a complete profile are canonized. Another execution environment may be used only when its owning plan or authority defines the complete material environment contract; it must not be represented as Codespaces conformance.\n\n## **14.4 Shared invariants (apply to every Defined/supported Codespaces QA profile)**\n\n### **14.4.1 Determinism env pins for governed bytes**\n\nAny job that produces governed snapshots or evidence MUST export:\n\n* `LC_ALL=C`  \n* `LANG=C`  \n* `TZ=UTC`\n\nCanonical set only (normative): the pins above are the only determinism env pins required by PF19 for Live QA conformance. Live QA plans MUST NOT introduce additional required pins (for example PYTHONHASHSEED or any `MODO_*` variable) as rails, prerequisites, or approval gates.\n\nDeterminism posture (normative): if any governed bytes are nondeterministic, determinism MUST be achieved in the producing tool via explicit ordering (stable sorts, deterministic serialization), not via interpreter/environment knobs. Treat nondeterminism as a repo/tooling defect to drain via canon.\n\n### **14.4.2 QA root and write-scope rails**\n\nCodespaces is a QA console and artifact sink. It MUST NOT be treated as prod.\n\nThe canonical Live QA evidence root is `audit/qa/<epic-id>/`, with a lowercase `<epic-id>`. Check evidence belongs under `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/`; stable epic metadata belongs under `audit/qa/<epic-id>/00_meta/`; the current-state manifest remains `audit/qa/<epic-id>/qa_step_logs_manifest.json`.\n\nOrdinary Live QA evidence MUST remain under the canonical epic QA root and its PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts-authorized children. The standard external-path exception is the draft/staging Doc Delta at `audit/docdeltas/<epic-id>_doc_deltas.md`; its stable QA counterpart is `audit/qa/<epic-id>/00_meta/doc_deltas.md`.\n\nA separately authorized `QA_PLAN_UPDATE`, `DOC_UPDATE`, PR, or Ops route may create or refresh governed evidence outside the QA root only under its owning canon and approved work item. That routed output is not a generic QA-subpath exception, and the final QA receipt MUST identify the route before relying on it.\n\n### **14.4.3 Step-0 “Codespaces snapshot” (optional; non-gating evidence)**\n\nA Codespaces snapshot artifact may be useful for debugging and reviewer context, but it is not a required Live QA deliverable.\n\nNon-gating rule (normative) is as follows:\n\n* Plans MUST NOT require, validate, or gate approval on a Codespaces snapshot artifact.  \n* Reviewers MUST NOT use the presence, absence, or contents of a snapshot to decide PASS vs REMEDIATION.\n\nIf produced, the snapshot MUST use the current-state path `audit/qa/<epic-id>/00_meta/codespaces_snapshot.json` and conform to the complete canonical JSON, schema, capture, and indexing contract in PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts under `8.17.5 Codespaces snapshot (Step-0; current-state) [Optional]`. It records effective rails and deterministic pins, tool versions, and presence-only required environment or secret names without values. Static configuration does not prove that the Codespace launched, a service ran, a secret exists, or a QA predicate passed.\n\nThe optional snapshot is separate from, and MUST NOT replace, the per-check `primary.log`, required path proofs, current-state manifest, Human Evidence Index, Machine Mirror, exact check proof, or Step-0 Doc Delta Capture outputs.\n\n## **14.5 Environment profiles (Codespaces config \\+ minimum checks)**\n\nA profile is usable for Codespaces-based QA only when it is marked `Defined/supported` and every required fact is owner-authorized and populated. Optional facts may be omitted when not applicable.\n\n### **14.5.1 HD Engine — Codespaces QA environment**\n\nProfile status: `Defined/supported`.\n\n#### **Purpose and boundaries**\n\n* The profile supports a QA console into the PF07-Canon-Glow-Infrastructure-defined Railway production targets for expressly approved Live QA steps.  \n* The profile supports a local dev-harness runner for closed-rails deterministic checks.  \n* Codespaces is a client/console and artifact workspace. It is not production.  \n* Codespaces is canonical and preferred for shared HDE QA, but it is not automatically material to every proof and is not mandatory when the owning plan authorizes an equivalent complete environment contract.\n\n#### **Primary repository and workspace**\n\n* Repo name: `amthorn78/glow-hdengine-v2`  \n* Default branch: `main`  \n* Current devcontainer name: `Glow HD Engine Codespace`  \n* Codespace naming convention: not defined; this optional field is omitted.\n\n#### **Toolchain and entrypoints**\n\n* CLI entrypoints: `hdctl`; `python -m engine.cli`  \n* Test runner: `pytest`  \n* Devcontainer image: `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.11`  \n* Runtime posture: Python 3.11 in the current devcontainer; project floor Python `>=3.10`.  \n* Node is not a required HDE profile runtime merely because a generic snapshot schema can report a Node version when applicable.\n\n#### **Runtime targets**\n\n* Railway project: `ample-illumination`  \n* HD Engine service: `glow-hdengine-v2`  \n* Production base URL: `https://glow-hdengine-v2-production.up.railway.app`  \n* Production database instance: `ample-illumination/production/postgres`  \n* HD Engine database schema: `hde`  \n* Local configured dev-sampler endpoint: `DEV_SAMPLER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/internal/dev/sampler`  \n* Local port when that dev sampler is used: `8000`\n\nListing a target does not authorize access, prove reachability, prove secret presence, or establish runtime success. The plan selects only the target needed by the check.\n\n#### **Rails, environment, and secrets**\n\n* Default rails posture: closed rails.  \n* Closed rails: `SAFE_MODE=1`, `ALLOW_NETWORK=0`, `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, and `TZ=UTC`.  \n* Allowed rails-toggle names: `SAFE_MODE` and `ALLOW_NETWORK`.  \n* Open rails: `SAFE_MODE=0` and `ALLOW_NETWORK=1`, only for an expressly approved step whose owner, target, authorization, secret-safety, evidence, and rollback boundaries are defined. Privileged or external-system mutation remains PO-authorized Ops work; execution follows PF06-Canon-Change-Process-Guide, including its explicit-delegation controls.  \n* `APP_ENV` is propagated exactly when a check requires it. Infra helpers MUST NOT silently default an empty or unset value. Local/dev HDE checks that require the dev-gated surface use the owner-defined `APP_ENV=dev` posture.  \n* Required secret names for the base closed-rails profile: none.  \n* Check-specific secret names: the applicable plan lists the exact owner-defined names. Current known names such as `DATABASE_URL`, `HD_API_KEY`, and `GEO_API_KEY` are required only when the selected check uses their target; they are not universal profile prerequisites.  \n* Secret values MUST NOT appear in PF19, snapshots, primary logs, manifests, Doc Deltas, or other governed evidence. Use presence-only, redacted, or approved hashed posture.\n\n#### **Minimum bootstrap and readiness checks**\n\nBefore a newly created or materially changed HDE Codespace is treated as ready for a selected QA check:\n\n1. `.devcontainer/scripts/post-create.sh` completes successfully.  \n2. The virtual environment and repository dependencies install successfully from `requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt`, and editable project installation.  \n3. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest --version` exits successfully.  \n4. `.venv/bin/python -m engine.cli --help` exits successfully.  \n5. The effective deterministic pins are captured and equal `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, and `TZ=UTC` for governed-byte production.  \n6. If the check uses the local dev sampler, capture the exact `DEV_SAMPLER_URL` binding and perform the plan-defined service/up check. The static devcontainer value does not prove that a service is running.  \n7. If the check reaches Railway, a database, or a vendor, execute the plan-defined Step-0 handshake or prerequisite proof under the approved rails. Static PF07-Canon-Glow-Infrastructure inventory does not prove reachability or authorization.\n\nFailure of a mandatory prerequisite is `TOOLING_BLOCKED` unless attempted tooling itself is defective, in which case the applicable PF27-Canon-Plan-Templates failure classification controls.\n\n#### **Evidence sinks and environment records**\n\n* QA root: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/`  \n* Per-check directory: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/`  \n* Per-check receipt and environment/rails record: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/primary.log`  \n* Required receipt proof: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/primary.log.path_proof.txt`  \n* Current-state manifest: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/qa_step_logs_manifest.json`  \n* Required manifest proof: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/qa_step_logs_manifest.json.path_proof.txt`  \n* Optional non-gating Codespaces snapshot: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/00_meta/codespaces_snapshot.json`  \n* Draft/staging Doc Delta: `audit/docdeltas/<epic-id>_doc_deltas.md`  \n* Stable epic Doc Delta record: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/00_meta/doc_deltas.md`\n\nThe two Doc Delta files are byte-identical where PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts requires the QA-root copy. The optional Codespaces snapshot does not replace the receipt, manifest, path proofs, Human Evidence Index, Machine Mirror, or exact selected-check proof.\n\n#### **Ownership**\n\n* Responsible for environment wiring and profile currency: `Infra / Ops owner`  \n* Responsible for HDE CLI, test, and playbook content consumed by the profile: `HDE Lead / Engine owner`  \n* Accountable reviewer: `Lead Developer`  \n* The Product Owner retains authorization, accountability, and acceptance for privileged Ops actions. Any delegated execution follows PF06-Canon-Change-Process-Guide.\n\n### **14.5.2 App Back End — Codespaces QA environment**\n\nProfile status: `Unsupported/undefined`.\n\nPF19 recognizes the App Back End QA environment class but does not define a conforming Codespaces profile. The missing required fact classes are:\n\n* App Back End Codespaces purpose and supported QA uses  \n* owner-authorized repository name and default branch  \n* default rails posture  \n* required secret names, names-only  \n* closed-rails bootstrap checks  \n* responsible owner and accountable reviewer\n\nIf local runtime or HDE integration is required, its start command, base URL, ports, integration boundary, and up-check evidence must also be owner-authorized before use. HDE contracts remain owned by the HDE-titled PF documents. A materially dependent check is `TOOLING_BLOCKED` until the complete profile is canonized. Evidence uses the canonical root and check grammar in §14.4.2 only after that gate is met.\n\n### **14.5.3 App Front End — Web — Codespaces QA environment**\n\nProfile status: `Unsupported/undefined`.\n\nPF19 recognizes the App Front End — Web QA environment class but does not define a conforming Codespaces profile. The missing required fact classes are:\n\n* FE-Web Codespaces purpose and supported QA uses  \n* owner-authorized repository name and default branch  \n* package manager and test runners  \n* default rails posture  \n* required secret names, names-only  \n* build and test bootstrap checks  \n* responsible owner and accountable reviewer\n\nNo start command, local base URL, port, package-manager choice, test-runner choice, rails value, secret, or bootstrap command may be inferred. A materially dependent check is `TOOLING_BLOCKED` until the complete profile is canonized. Evidence uses the canonical root and check grammar in §14.4.2 only after that gate is met.\n\n### **14.5.4 App Front End — Mobile — Codespaces QA environment**\n\nProfile status: `Unsupported/undefined`.\n\nPF19 recognizes the App Front End — Mobile QA environment class but does not define a conforming Codespaces profile or an alternate mobile QA console. The missing required fact classes are:\n\n* Mobile Codespaces purpose and supported QA uses  \n* whether Codespaces supports the required mobile runtime surfaces  \n* owner-authorized repository name and default branch  \n* required alternate QA console by title when Codespaces cannot support the needed runtime  \n* build system or tooling and test runners  \n* default rails posture  \n* required secret names, names-only  \n* bootstrap checks  \n* responsible owner and accountable reviewer\n\nNo mobile runtime-support claim, alternate environment, repository, branch, build tool, test runner, rails value, secret, or bootstrap command may be inferred from HDE repository state. A materially dependent check is `TOOLING_BLOCKED` until the Codespaces profile or a complete owner-authorized alternate environment contract is canonized. An alternate environment must not be represented as Codespaces conformance.\n\n## **14.6 Ownership and maintenance**\n\nProfile ownership and future-definition gates are as follows:\n\n| Profile | Responsible owner | Accountable reviewer | Definition gate |\n| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |\n| HD Engine | `Infra / Ops owner` for environment wiring and `HDE Lead / Engine owner` for HDE CLI, tests, and playbooks | `Lead Developer` | Keep required facts current through approved work and evidence; route permanent profile maintenance under §14.6 without a drainage-only execution gate. |\n| App Back End | `BE Lead / App Backend owner`, with Infra/Ops for environment wiring | `Lead Developer` | Complete every required §14.5.2 fact from the owning App repository and infrastructure canon in one coordinated change. |\n| App Front End — Web | `FE Lead / App Frontend owner`, with Infra/Ops for environment wiring | `Lead Developer` | Complete every required §14.5.3 fact from the owning App repository and infrastructure canon in one coordinated change. |\n| App Front End — Mobile | `Mobile/App Frontend owner`, with Infra/Ops for environment wiring | `Lead Developer` | Establish whether Codespaces supports the required mobile surfaces and, if not, canonize the alternate QA console before completing §14.5.4. |\n| Update trigger(s) include: |  |  |  |\n\n* repo/toolchain change that affects QA steps  \n* Codespaces base image change  \n* secrets or env-var interface changes (names-only)  \n* devcontainer changes that affect shells, entrypoints, or tooling availability\n\nPrerequisite maintenance (normative). Record changes to Codespaces/devcontainer requirements, required environment/secret names and other Live QA prerequisites in the actual approved change and its documentation evidence. Identify the affected §14.5 profile or owning PF destination for permanent drainage. Plan-only invention and tribal knowledge are non-conforming, but a pending permanent PF edit alone is not a QA or closure gate when applicable current authority and sufficient concrete evidence already establish the prerequisite. A genuinely missing or contradictory material prerequisite remains blocked until resolved by its actual owner; §10.8 governs source access and substantive currentness.\n\nDoc delta capture step (normative, planning allowed) is as follows: Live QA planning is allowed even when Codespaces prerequisites are incomplete or unclear, but plans MUST NOT assume or invent missing details.\n\nRouting (normative) is as follows: mandatory Step-0 artifacts (including Doc Delta Capture posture) are governed by PF27 — Plan Templates. This section adds Codespaces-specific requirements for how doc deltas are recorded.\n\nEvery Live QA plan executed in Codespaces MUST include a Step-0 Doc Delta Capture step that:\n\n* lists each missing or ambiguous prerequisite discovered during planning, separated into:  \n  * BLOCKERS (execution cannot proceed without resolution)  \n  * CAVEATS (execution can proceed with constrained scope or reduced confidence)  \n* names the intended fix location for each item (either §14.5 profile fields, or an owning PF doc by title only)  \n* records a resolution status for each item (for example unresolved, resolved by doc update, resolved by existing canonical reference)\n\nThe Doc Delta Capture step MUST produce two artifacts: `audit/docdeltas/<epic-id>_doc_deltas.md` (canonical doc-delta ledger record) and `audit/qa/<epic-id>/00_meta/doc_deltas.md` (in-epic QA copy). The two files MUST be byte-identical. Both artifacts MUST be names-only (no secret values). If no deltas are found, the step MUST still produce an explicit no deltas output.\n\nStep-0 Doc Delta Capture must preserve existing proof-bearing doc-delta surfaces.\n\nIf generator-owned, PR-owned, OPS-owned, QA-owned, or previously produced doc-delta surfaces already exist for the same epic, Step-0B MUST NOT overwrite them with a generic no-deltas template. Step-0B may verify them, copy them when explicitly required, append a clearly labeled capture section when the owning plan permits it, or produce its own additional record. It must not silently erase proof-bearing content.\n\nA no-deltas output is valid only when the run has inspected the relevant approved surfaces and no proof-bearing doc-delta surface exists or no delta is actually present. If a Step-0B command overwrites a proof-bearing doc-delta surface, classify the result as an evidence-assembly or tooling failure until remediated. Remediation must preserve the original failed evidence, identify the overwritten path or paths, restore or reconstruct only from authoritative current sources, and rerun the affected check or accepted validation path.\n\nConformance rule (normative) is as follows: a Live QA run executed in Codespaces is non-conforming for approval if either of the following is true:\n\n* the relevant environment profile is `Unsupported/undefined`, retains missing or contradictory required facts, and the check materially depends on that profile; or  \n* the plan did not include, and the run did not produce, the required Step-0 Doc Delta Capture output defined above.\n\nA check that materially depends on an unresolved profile prerequisite is `TOOLING_BLOCKED` until its actual owner establishes the material prerequisite through applicable authority and sufficient evidence. A later permanent PF edit alone is not the missing prerequisite. Missing or contradictory prerequisites MUST be captured as Doc Deltas during planning. Environment details for a Defined/supported profile MUST be kept current so QA plans do not rely on guessing.\n\n",
    "e8234398902ab47e3492d54a83d79ef5e2d17399dee8ad03d0688aec98a23696": "# **0 Document Control \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n## **0.1 Header**\n\n**Title:** PF04-Canon-HDE-Governance  \n**Version:** v2.8.6  \n**Status:** Canon  \n**Effective date:** 2026-09-08  \n**Last Update Gate:** PF10 13.0.9  \n**Invocation tag:** `INV-f2ac55d77ce9aacc`\n\n## **0.2 Scope & boundaries \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n**Role.**  \nThis document defines **governance, validation, and operational policy** for the Glow HD Engine. It owns:\n\n* Acceptance gates (A3 / A4 / A7 and Epic-level and CRD-level gates).  \n* Evidence and release discipline (freeze-pack identity, rollback posture).  \n* SAFE-rails posture and vendor HTTP policy.  \n* Logging & privacy requirements (keys-only logs; no secrets/PII).  \n* The public resonance posture (Reader v1 is bands-only, numeric-free; SR-only α=1.0; hysteresis=1 armed for future XR and not exposed).\n\n**Supersession (PF10-HDE-Build-Notes addenda).**\n\n**PF10-HDE-Build-Notes** is living. Consult its complete latest active logical base version: one unlettered document or the complete verified contiguous lettered set, including the actual body through EOF when an index is incomplete. Authority operates at the level of independently scoped addenda. A higher-numbered applicable addendum governs only overlapping scope or guidance it explicitly supersedes; unrelated addenda and distinct unsuperseded portions remain authoritative. A later document letter extends the same base set and supersedes nothing by itself. Do not mix base versions, combine an unlettered file with its parts, or discard distinct older addenda because another part has a later letter. Where the complete active PF10 is silent on a point, the owning PF canon governs. This document integrates applicable PF10 positions and routes by titles only to single-home PF documents, without version numbers.\n\n**PF10-HDE-Build-Notes reference posture (stable unit: addendum entry).**\n\n* Do not reference **PF10-HDE-Build-Notes** by version strings.  \n* Prefer referencing **PF10-HDE-Build-Notes** by addendum number \\+ addendum title (for example: “PF10-HDE-Build-Notes Addendum 2.10 — Token Load Reduction \\[OMITTED: remaining title\\]”).  \n* Do not treat **PF10-HDE-Build-Notes** section numbers as durable anchors for external enforcement; the stable unit is the addendum entry itself.  \n* When an addendum supersedes earlier **PF10-HDE-Build-Notes** guidance, it must explicitly name what it supersedes (by addendum number/title).  \n* Legacy note: this document may contain legacy PF10-style labels (for example “PF10-A” / “PF10-AA”) inside headings or notes. Treat them as legacy identifiers only. Do not introduce new PF10-style labels. Replace them with addendum-number references when the correct mapping is known.\n\n**Ownership boundaries (titles-only routing).**\n\n* **Transport & ops policy (this document).**  \n  A7 invariants, cache & writers policy, conditional delivery rules, parity requirements, refusal posture, the Aux-suppression carve-out, and the `/internal/version` ops surface are governed here.  \n  Exact wire bytes / presenter / CLI flows live in **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref**.  \n* **Math & algorithms.**  \n  Composite logic, scoring, bands, constants, and preimage definitions live in **PF01-Canon-HDE-Math-Spec**.  \n* **Schemas, pack/manifest, canonical JSON, mirror schema.**  \n  Catalog/manifest, canonical JSON rules (UTF-8, no BOM; ASCII-sorted keys; compact; one trailing LF; arrays-as-sets deduped & ASCII-sorted), and the machine-mirror schema & ordering live in **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts**.  \n  All byte checks run under `LC_ALL=C`, `TZ=UTC` (and `LANG=C` where applicable).  \n* **Architecture.**  \n  Engine/adapter/presenter boundaries and flows live in **PF02-Canon-HDE-Architecture**; this document references those boundaries by title only.  \n* **Endpoint Catalog (A7 proof surface).**  \n  The Endpoint Catalog (JSON success) is the **single proof surface** for A7. The Catalog is internal-only and env-gated per entry; entries not gated for prod are unreachable in production.  \n  A7 transport proofs **must** run on a Catalog JSON success route (titles-only; path-agnostic).  \n  The `/internal/version` ops surface is explicitly excluded and governed in §10.5.  \n  A headers-only env-gate proof is required to demonstrate non-prod entries are unreachable in prod.  \n  For EPIC-010, Aux HEAD and 304 are explicitly out of scope; A7 proofs remain Catalog JSON success only.\n\n**Single homes.**\n\n* **Legacy token catalog.**  \n* §2.0 is the single historical compatibility catalog for existing governance-token names and semantics. Tokens are optional indexing metadata and are not an acceptance authority or a prerequisite for planning, implementation, review, QA, acceptance, or closure.  \n* **Evidence Index & Machine Mirror (PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts single home).**  \n  **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts** is the single home for:  \n  * Evidence titles/paths.  \n  * The human Evidence Index (`docs/evidence/INDEX.json`) and its hash sentinel.  \n  * The machine JSONL mirror (`artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`).  \n* **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts** governs records-only JSONL, one trailing LF, unknown-key rejection, ASCII field order, sort-before-write, single mirror file, and required `proof_anchor` path-proofs.  \n  **PF04-Canon-HDE-Governance** may reference required titles only; **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts** remains the single home for index/mirror schema and catalogs.\n\n## **0.3 Tagging convention**\n\nEach section is tagged to show implementation status:\n\n* \\[Implemented\\] — verified in repo and enforced by tests.  \n* \\[Required-Now\\] — required for the current build or acceptance gates.  \n* \\[Speculative\\] — design accepted for a future release; not yet wired.  \n* \\[OPEN\\] — unresolved or gated pending Doc-Delta review.\n\n## **0.4 Change policy**\n\n**Single homes; no duplication.**  \nMath and Architecture bytes are not restated here. Transport bytes remain in **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref**. Artifacts and mirror schemas are owned by **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts**.\n\n**Governed paths only.**\n\nRepository-native evidence artifacts whose owning contract requires governed publication MUST live under governed repo paths and retain the applicable Evidence Index/Mirror and proof bindings. “Single-home” refers to the authoritative binding between artifact keys and repo paths, not one directory. Off-repository change-process artifacts, reports and exports use §9.1.3 Library storage; that rule does not relocate repository-controlled evidence or replace its canonical writers.\n\nDefault governed roots include `artifacts/**`, `docs/**`, and `audit/**`. Additional evidence roots (for example, `reports/**`, `validation/**`, `proofs/**`, `parity/**`, `scan_reports/**`, `catalog/**`, `narratives/**`, `internal/**`) are permitted only when they are explicitly treated as governed evidence families and are bound into the Evidence Index and machine mirror with co-located path-proofs.\n\n`scripts/**` and `tools/**` are code and tooling roots by default. If any outputs under these roots are claimed as governed evidence, they MUST be re-homed under governed evidence roots or explicitly bound as governed evidence families with Evidence Index, mirror, and path-proof linkage.\n\nTransient generator paths (for example, `codex/out/**`) are not authoritative and MUST NOT be indexed. Mirror entries pointing to non-governed paths fail CI.\n\n**Lowercase directories (ASCII only).**\n\nAll directories in the repository and application codebase **MUST** use **lowercase ASCII** names. Introducing any mixed-case or upper-case directory name is **non-conforming**. Under governed roots (`docs/**`, `artifacts/**`, `audit/**`), mixed-case directories are a **QA failure**, not cosmetic drift.\n\nThis rail applies to **directory names** only (not filenames). Uppercase filenames are allowed unless separately forbidden by canon.\n\nAutomated enforcement MUST scan directory names (for example: `find <root> -type d`) rather than file paths (`-type f`).\n\n**Remediation posture.**  \nIf mixed-case directories exist, treat them as legacy drift and **normalize to lowercase**. Do not copy mixed-case names forward into new work.\n\n**Evidence coupling (same-PR).**  \nAny directory rename that affects governed artifact paths **MUST** be accompanied by the required Evidence Index and machine mirror updates (and any affected path-proofs) in the **same PR/commit** as the rename.\n\n**Determinism first.**  \nAny change that affects byte identity (serializer path, schema keys, A7 headers, `/internal/version` headers) must include updated parity and idempotence evidence.\n\n**Doc-Delta discipline.**  \nAll **normative** edits (math/public/acceptance/rails) require a Doc-Delta entry: scope, affected sections, acceptance impact, evidence updates, and freeze-pack effect.\n\n**Evidence synchronization (PR-first).**  \nWhen any golden or artifact path changes, the Evidence Index and mirror **must** be updated in the same PR/commit that changes those items, with a matching entry under the change-management rules in **PF06-Canon-Change-Process-Guide**.\n\n**Mirror hygiene (merge-blocking).**  \nThe machine mirror must be canonical JSONL (one trailing LF; unknown keys rejected). Each record must include a `proof_anchor` pointing to a path-proof stored alongside the artifact.  \nField order and sort/join rules live in **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts**; this document references policy only.\n\n**Editorial vs normative.**  \nStylistic or non-functional rewordings need not be logged. Any change that modifies bytes, tests, or acceptance criteria must be logged via Doc-Delta and reflected in Evidence Index updates.\n\n---\n\n# **1\\. Purpose & Single-Home Governance \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n## **1.1 Purpose \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nThis governance document defines **how the HD Engine is built, validated, and released** under explicit Epic and CRD gates.\n\n* Each Epic functions as a **governance gate**: a bounded set of features and acceptance tests that must be fully implemented, validated, and evidenced before the next Epic begins.  \n* Each CRD functions as a **governed change gate**: a bounded change container that may include one or more PRs, Ops tasks, or both and that remains accountable through its controlled CRD identity, approved CRD Specification and approved class-bound Implementation Plan.  \n* Governance, validation, and operations are inseparable: an Epic or CRD **closes** only when its applicable governance and evidence gates pass.  \n* Supersession rule: a higher-numbered applicable addendum governs only overlapping scope or guidance it explicitly supersedes; unrelated addenda and distinct unsuperseded portions remain authoritative. This document integrates the applicable positions from **PF10-HDE-Build-Notes** and preserves relevant historical context from **PF20-Reference-HDE-Phased Epics**.\n\nThis document owns:\n\n* **Acceptance gates (A-gates and Epic/CRD gates).**  \n  * A3 / A4 / A7 enforce determinism, Reader↔CLI parity, and transport correctness.  \n  * Every Epic and CRD uses the same applicable internal criteria: AB↔BA parity, two-run identity, canonical JSON discipline, and A7 transport compliance.  \n  * Governance and testing during an Epic or CRD use the same applicable binary proofs required for release acceptance.  \n* **Reader transport and A7 policy.**  \n  * Governs public transport behavior (headers, conditional delivery, caching).  \n  * Single proof surface: A7 proofs run on a Catalog JSON success route (see Endpoint Catalog in **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref**).  \n  * The Catalog is internal-only and env-gated per entry; entries not gated for prod are unreachable in production.  \n  * `/internal/version` is ops-only and excluded from A7; its posture is governed separately (§10.5).  \n  * Required A7 posture includes, at minimum:  \n    * Strong quoted ETag on 200\\.  \n    * `Vary: Authorization, Accept-Encoding`.  \n    * HEAD 200 with validator parity and `Content-Length == len(identity 200 body)`.  \n    * 304 only after 200, with no body, omitting both `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`.  \n    * Writers/errors `Cache-Control: no-store` and **no ETag**.  \n    * Success route non-conditional; encoding invariance (identity stable across accepted `Accept-Encoding` values).  \n* **Rails and environments (vendor posture).**  \n  * SAFE-rails model for vendor HTTP: default closed, explicit open conditions, deterministic refusal semantics, and non-PII observability.  \n* **Public resonance posture (Reader v1).**  \n  * Public surface is bands-only, numeric-free.  \n  * Resonance is SR-only (α=1.0).  \n  * Hysteresis=1 is armed for future XR and is not exposed.  \n  * Any XR diagnostics, if supported, are CLI-only behind an admin guard (never present on Reader 200).  \n* **Operations and evidence.**  \n  * Required evidence classes (parity, idempotence, transport, rails, band-edge, constants).  \n  * CI hygiene (grep-guards, LF/encoding checks).  \n  * Evidence Index single-home rule (**PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts**) and requirement that Index updates land in the same PR as artifacts.  \n* **Release discipline.**  \n  * Manages freeze-pack identity (`release_id`), immutable packaged-release promotion, exact-artifact rollback, and drift checks.  \n  * Any frozen-math or manifest canonical-bytes change yields a new `release_id` (pack manifest is canonical JSON with `root:\"catalog/\"`, `version`, `built_at_utc`, and `files:[{path,sha256,size}]`).  \n* **Security and privacy.**  \n  * Enforces the numeric-free public covenant.  \n  * Keys-only logging; no secrets/PII in logs.  \n  * Labels and correlation IDs remain bounded and deterministic.  \n* **Change management.**  \n  * Defines the Doc-Delta workflow (scope, targets, acceptance, evidence, freeze-pack impact).  \n  * Mandates that every normative change updates the Evidence Index in the same commit.\n\n## **1.2 Single homes & routing \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n**Ownership (this document).**  \nGovernance owns **operational and transport policy** for the HD Engine:\n\n* A-gates (acceptance policy and token semantics).  \n* Reader transport (headers, conditional delivery, caching).  \n* Rails posture (enable/disable vendor HTTP).  \n* Logging/privacy.  \n* Bench/SLO posture.  \n* Immutable packaged-release promotion and exact-artifact rollback policy.  \n* Evidence/CI hygiene policy.\n\n**Titles-only routing (no duplication).**\n\n* **Math and architecture.**  \n  Mathematical rules (scoring, thresholds, fixed-point/rounding, preimage definition) and architectural boundaries (engine/adapter/presenter responsibilities) are referenced by title only from **PF01-Canon-HDE-Math-Spec** and **PF02-Canon-HDE-Architecture**; they are not restated here.  \n* **Aux Narrative.**  \n  Aux Narrative payload and route bytes (examples, endpoint bytes, CLI admin flags) are documented in **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref** and **PF17-Canon-HDE-Narratives-Guide**. This document owns the acceptance matrices and policy carve-outs only (e.g., suppression posture).  \n* **Admin bundle & admin surfaces.**  \n  The internal **admin bundle builder** (composition of per-person BodyGraphs, compat JSON, narratives, and meta) and the concrete **CLI/HTTP admin bundle surfaces** are defined mechanically and byte-wise in **PF14-Canon-HDE-Mechanics-Guide** and **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref** (titles-only). Governance owns only the **policy** for these admin surfaces: authentication/authorization, logging/audit posture, and the applicable acceptance-token semantics in §2.0.17. Admin bundle bytes are not part of the Reader v1 public contract and are not A7 proof surfaces; they are admin-only internal surfaces.  \n* **Serializer/emitter and schemas.**  \n  Canonical serializer/emitter rules and public payload schemas are owned by **PF01-Canon-HDE-Math-Spec**, **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts**, and **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref** and are referenced by title here.  \n* **Change process and authority.**  \n  The **Change Process Guide** owns the common lifecycle and routing for both governed change lanes. Epic-originated work uses Epic identity and **HDE Build Checklist** accountability. CRD-originated work uses controlled CRD identity and its approved Specification/Implementation Plan lineage. **HDE CRD Records** is historical/reference-only and creates no active registration gate. This document owns authority, approval boundaries, exact-source acceptance and claim separation, and the approved-ADR requirement for canon-changing CRDs.\n\n**Change discipline.**\n\n* If a change touches **Math or Architecture**, it must be made in that home and routed here via Doc-Delta.  \n* If a change alters **transport/ops** (including admin bundle auth/logging policy), it lands here with updated evidence and pointers, never by duplicating content across documents.\n\n**Auditability.**\n\n* All references to external homes are titles/anchors only.  \n* Proofs (goldens, scripts, snapshots) are indexed in the Evidence Index governed by **PF12-Canon-HDE-Schemas-and-Artifacts** and kept in sync with repo changes.\n\n## **1.3 EPIC-011 preservation surfaces \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nEPIC-011 introduced a **preservation guard** over key public and admin surfaces. Under this Epic, certain contracts are treated as **frozen**:\n\n* Governance and QA may **strengthen proofs and evidence**,  \n* but **may not change wire contracts** for these surfaces within EPIC-011’s scope.\n\n**Preserved surfaces (names-only).**\n\n* **CLI admin preview (Aux preview).**  \n  Wire bytes, stdout/sidecar contracts, and exit-code behavior for CLI admin preview are owned by **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref**. EPIC-011 allows QA and evidence changes only (additional proofs, harnesses), not contract changes.  \n* **Vendor ingest wire bytes.**  \n  Vendor HTTP request/response shapes, paths, and typed error envelopes are owned by **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref**. Governance ensures SAFE rails posture and observability; EPIC-011 does not change vendor wire contracts.  \n* **Compat JSON surface.**  \n  The compat surface used by `showcompat` and other callers is governed by **PF01-Canon-HDE-Math-Spec** and **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref**. EPIC-011 treats this as frozen; only QA evidence around compat (AB↔BA parity, two-run identity) may change.  \n* **Aux narrative surface.**  \n  Narrative packs, text, suppression rules, and Aux routes are governed by **PF17-Canon-HDE-Narratives-Guide** and **PF05-Canon-HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref**. Under EPIC-011, narrative contracts are preserved; QA captures headers, packs, IDs, and transport proofs only.\n\n**Governance stance.**\n\n* Governance may tighten tests, define acceptance criteria, and require new evidence artifacts **without** changing preserved wire contracts. A new acceptance token is exceptional and may be introduced only through the bounded opt-in rule in §2.0.0.  \n* Any change to a preserved surface’s contract must be treated as **out of scope** for EPIC-011 and routed through a future Epic. **PF20-Reference-HDE-Phased Epics** supplies historical context only and does not control current planning.\n\n---\n\n# **2\\. Acceptance Policy — A3–A4–A7 \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n---\n\n## **2.0 Acceptance Tokens (single-home roster) \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n**Current acceptance model.** Exact-source evidence and scoped decisions are the primary traceability model for current acceptance and completion claims. PF10 uses independently scoped numbered addenda; the highest-numbered applicable addendum governs only overlapping or explicitly superseded scope, while unrelated addenda and distinct unsuperseded portions remain authoritative.\n\nEvery current acceptance or completion claim MUST bind, as applicable, to:\n\n* repository identity and observed commit identifiers appropriate to the claim; QA/Ops actual-source attribution and unavailable identifiers follow §9.1.4;  \n* PR number, base SHA, candidate or head SHA, merge SHA, and immutable review record when a PR is used and those events/identifiers exist;  \n* workflow name, run identifier or URL, actual tested SHA when available, conclusion, and applicable check set;  \n* stable PF, ADR, epic, CRD, task, acceptance-criterion, test, schema, or artifact identifiers;  \n* exact governed artifact paths and SHA-256 digests where integrity is material;  \n* applicable manifests, indexes, mirrors, path proofs, tool versions, and configuration references;  \n* the QA or approval decision, decision-maker, scope, and time; and  \n* any exception or waiver identity, owner, scope, reason, and expiry.\n\nA PR, commit, workflow run, governed report, manifest, index, or closeout artifact MAY carry this evidence directly. Records MUST NOT duplicate information that GitHub or a governed repository artifact already records reliably. Governance creates no replacement token database and no universal new evidence form.\n\n**Claim separation.** Repository presence, CI result, QA verdict, operator or role acceptance, and completion or closure are distinct states and MUST NOT be collapsed. Landing a commit on `main`, including an operator-authored direct push, establishes repository reality only. It does not by itself establish CI PASS, QA PASS, acceptance, PF09 completion, PF30 status movement, OPS completion, deployment, release readiness, epic or CRD closure, or production readiness.\n\nA repository-controlled canonical artifact on `main` governs only its declared artifact-content lane. Repository PF copies remain publication mirrors of the Drive authority and are usable as bounded QA/Ops execution sources under §9.1.4; repository presence does not confer independent PF editing authority. Artifact authority remains separate from implementation conformance, repository validation, QA acceptance and closure.\n\n**Direct-to-`main` authority and evidence.** The Product Owner retains authority to push directly to `main`. An agent MUST NOT infer that authority from this section; agent direct-main mutation requires an explicit current operator instruction covering the exact change. The normal direct-main lane is bounded documentation, metadata, or administrative correction selected by the Product Owner, although the Product Owner may explicitly authorize a broader change.\n\nA direct-main route changes the mutation path, not the applicable correctness, evidence, QA, security, privacy, canon, or closure standard. The post-write commit MUST be identified by its exact SHA; its diff and applicable push-triggered CI result are the minimum repository evidence. A valid applicability classifier MAY select a reduced lane set, and irrelevant lanes need not be rerun solely to imitate a full-PR process.\n\nPending or failing push CI MUST be reported truthfully. The commit MUST NOT be described as CI-green. Any acceptance under an actual bounded exception must identify that decision and its scope separately from the failed or pending CI outcome. A failure on `main` MUST be surfaced and corrected or explicitly accepted as a bounded known exception; it MUST NOT be hidden by a legacy token, historical PASS, or operator authorship.\n\n**PR candidate fidelity.** When a PR is used, record the actual PR, reviewed source, base/head/landing relationships, relied-upon checks, substantive findings, corrections and corrected-source coverage. Relied-upon CI identifies the source it actually checked; a request, reaction, activity label or merge alone does not prove completed review. Preserve the historical evidence and distinguish later pushes and landing. Assess material changes to reviewed content and its acceptance basis through the existing review owner. For QA/Ops evidence and downstream use, apply §9.1.4; SHA progression alone requires no reset, rerun or routine equivalence certificate.\n\n**QA decision fidelity.** A verdict identifies the actual task and governing Plan, repository or environment tested, available source identifiers, scope and acceptance criteria, commands/configuration, checks/evidence, results/failures, decision-maker/time and every limitation, exclusion or unresolved condition. Existing workflow metadata, reports, manifests, indexes and closeout artifacts may carry that evidence; no token claim or universal matrix is required.\n\nThe tested state, a later evidence-storage commit and review-time HEAD are distinct. Preserve the original result; never relabel it as testing a later commit. Record unavailable identifiers with the reason. §9.1.4 governs bounded QA/Ops sources and substantive currentness: a changed, different or unavailable SHA alone does not block progress, revoke approval or force rerun/reapproval/equivalence certification.\n\n**Drift and staleness.** Before substantive work, resolve the relevant current authority and repository/environment facts needed for that work. Before mutation, establish that the approved substantive basis and exact authorized effect still apply. Assess relevant actual changes to requirements, implementation, inputs, dependencies, configuration, tests, acceptance and evidence; route an affected claim or missing decisive proof to its existing owner for focused review, revision or retest. Preserve unaffected valid progress. A documentation label or SHA alone establishes neither harmlessness nor failure. Changed governing criteria require conformance assessment even when runtime bytes are unchanged.\n\n**Layered integrity.** A commit identifies a repository tree; a PR identifies a proposed change and review relationship; a workflow run identifies checks executed against a stated commit; hashes and path proofs bind artifacts to bytes and paths; manifests and indexes declare artifact sets and relationships; attestations record defined provenance; and authorized decisions establish acceptance within a stated scope. No one identifier proves every fact. Existing release-attestation, Evidence Index, Machine Mirror, path-proof, exact-source, provenance, deterministic-validation, and strict-claim controls remain in force.\n\n---\n\n### **2.0.0 Token admission & lifecycle (value-only)**\n\n**Role.** This section defines the legacy-compatibility and bounded opt-in posture for Acceptance Tokens.\n\n**Legacy compatibility.** Existing token names and their historical semantics remain readable in this catalog. Existing token IDs MUST NOT be reinterpreted, reassigned, or deleted from historical records. Existing token evidence remains attributable to the candidate and proof that established it and does not become current acceptance for a later repository state.\n\n**No default issuance.** New QA acceptance tokens MUST NOT be created by default. A complete token roster, per-step intended-token or claimed-token declarations, and a token/evidence matrix MUST NOT be prerequisites for planning, implementation, review, QA execution, acceptance, or closure. Their absence MUST NOT block otherwise sufficient exact-source evidence.\n\n**Schema compatibility.** Token-aware tools and schemas MAY remain. Empty token arrays remain valid where a governing schema requires the fields. No bulk rewrite of historical plans, logs, reports, indexes, or audit artifacts is required, and no code migration is required merely to retire mandatory token issuance.\n\n**Bounded opt-in.** A plan MAY explicitly opt into a bounded token or equivalent cross-reference only when an existing PF, ADR, epic, CRD, task, test, or acceptance-criterion identifier cannot provide the necessary traceability. The plan must identify that insufficiency and the bounded scope of the cross-reference. This exception does not reactivate a universal token system.\n\n**Catalog semantics when used.** Existing names are case-sensitive. An optional token reference may be used only where the bound artifact, validator, QA step, or evidence family directly proves its cataloged semantics. A token name does not replace exact candidate identity, governed evidence, or an authorized scoped decision.\n\n**Guard proofs.** Guard proofs are evidence obligations, not token obligations by default. They remain mechanically generated and reviewable when required, but do not require token issuance unless the bounded opt-in rule above is satisfied.\n\n**Retired database-bridge token and proof-label posture.** `DEV_DB_BRIDGE_FALLBACK_OK` is retired from current claimability. `DB_PROVIDER_PARITY_OK`, `DB_BRIDGE_CAPS_OK`, and `DB_BRIDGE_FALLBACK_OK` are non-token historical proof labels only; they are not current bridge, transport, or acceptance predicates.\n\n* No new implementation plan, PR summary, OPS record, QA log, acceptance map, token/evidence matrix, close report, close manifest, or governed evidence row may claim `DEV_DB_BRIDGE_FALLBACK_OK`, bridge availability, bridge parity, bridge consistency, bridge capability, bridge fallback, or successful bridge selection.  \n* Historical evidence and historical token references MAY retain their accurate bridge-era names and results. They MUST remain historical, MUST NOT be rewritten merely to remove the retired names, and MUST NOT be relabeled as current evidence or current token satisfaction.  \n* Retirement of the bridge does not mint a replacement bridge or direct-transport token. Current direct-only database transport remains an implementation and evidence obligation governed through applicable existing database, environment, evidence-integrity, and test-token semantics.  \n* OPS-03 and any other bounded direct-only OPS evidence family do not mint, satisfy, replace, or expand an acceptance token by implication. OPS evidence remains subject to its explicit nonclaims and the general OPS-versus-QA and OPS-versus-acceptance separation rules.  \n* Any future acceptance token for a distinct supported database-transport predicate MUST be expressly admitted through this Token Registry or minted by a numbered PF10 addendum before an acceptance artifact may claim it.\n\n**Review-time requests vs close-out claims.** Acceptance and completion claims MUST bind exact-source evidence and the applicable scoped decision. A bounded token requested or used under §2.0.0 does not replace those bindings.\n\n**Operational discovery, open-rails, Codex Audit, and OPS evidence posture.** Operational discovery, bounded OPS evidence, PO-authorized open-rails evidence, and read-only repository observations MAY support planning, implementation, QA design, review, or drainage. They do not by themselves prove QA PASS, OPS completion, live-vendor truth, PF09 or PF30 status movement, epic or CRD closure, PF-canon drainage, or acceptance.\n\nIf such an observation supports a current repository claim, validate the claim against the current exact repository state before using it as fact. If it must support acceptance, bind it to the exact candidate, governing criterion, evidence, and authorized decision rather than converting it into a token.\n\n**Optional token semantic-fit rule.** When an existing token is used as a bounded cross-reference, it may be claimed only where the bound artifact, validator, QA step, or evidence family directly proves its cataloged semantics. Proximity within the same PR, epic, evidence bundle, or acceptance record is insufficient.\n\nGeneric privacy, logging, canonical-JSON, path-proof, Evidence Index, Machine Mirror, and rails labels must bind to the exact proof family that proves those predicates. Artifacts that record only scope, nonclaims, route selection, field sufficiency, adapter mapping, parent binding, or documentation deltas may record those facts without claiming unrelated tokens.\n\n**Command syntax and helper-code posture.** Command syntax, heredoc form, rendered escapes, indentation, copied-chat formatting, literalness, and paste-readiness are not acceptance conditions by themselves. They affect acceptance only when they change or obscure the proof target, evidence family, artifact identity, executed result, rails posture, secret-safety posture, PF09 scope, public/private boundary, or other governing acceptance criterion. Without that separate material harm, the issue is an in-flight normalization note, operator caution, caveat, suggestion, or nit.\n\n### **2.0.1 Determinism & identity**\n\n* **TWO\\_RUN\\_IDENTITY\\_OK** — Two serializations of the same inputs produce identical bytes. (Owned: HDE-Math-Spec; HDE-Mechanics Guide; Evidence & Artifacts)  \n* **COMPOSITE\\_ABBA\\_IDENTITY\\_OK** — AB↔BA fingerprint byte-equality (no vendor flags in composite). (Owned: HDE-Math-Spec; Evidence & Artifacts) **Canonical name.** This is the only canonical acceptance token name for AB/BA composite identity. Any alternate spellings or legacy variants are non-canonical and MUST NOT appear as acceptance tokens in Epic Plans, acceptance maps, or token/evidence matrices. If an epic inherits legacy wording from a doc, the plan may include a one-line clarification (“legacy name → canonical COMPOSITE\\_ABBA\\_IDENTITY\\_OK”), but the claimed token name remains canonical. Any proposal to introduce a new AB/BA identity token name is prohibited unless routed through ADR \\+ conflict check \\+ Governance Doc-Delta.  \n* **JSON\\_CANONICAL\\_CHECK\\_OK** — Canonical JSON everywhere: UTF-8 (no BOM), ASCII-sorted keys, compact separators, exactly one trailing LF; arrays-as-sets deduped and ASCII-sorted wherever required. **Canonical name.** Any alias or near-match (for example `CANON_JSON_OK`) is non-canonical and MUST NOT appear as an acceptance token in Epic Plans, acceptance maps, token/evidence matrices, or step-log claims. (Owned: HDE-Mechanics Guide; Evidence & Artifacts)  \n* **PREIMAGE\\_RECOMPUTE\\_OK** — Strip `idempotence_hash`, canonicalize the preimage (as defined in HDE-Math-Spec), recompute `sha256(preimage_bytes)`, and match the published hash; evidence includes recompute logs/scripts and mirror records under determinism pins. (Owned: HDE-Math-Spec; Evidence & Artifacts)\n\n**DETERMINISM\\_ENV\\_PINS\\_OK** — All **determinism-sensitive suites** (at minimum: serializer/idempotence proofs, AB↔BA identity, evidence ordering/orientation demos, and other invariance tests named in HDE-Mechanics Guide and Glow QA Guide) MUST run under the **closed determinism env pins**  \n`SAFE_MODE=1`, `ALLOW_NETWORK=0`, `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, `TZ=UTC`  \nas enforced by the canonical determinism env helper and CI rails harness.\n\n**Canonical evidence surface (single valid binding).**  \n`DETERMINISM_ENV_PINS_OK` MUST be satisfied only by the canonical governed log:\n\n* `audit/gates/determinism/env_pins.log`  \n* `audit/gates/determinism/env_pins.log.path_proof.txt`\n\n`DETERMINISM_ENV_PINS_OK` MUST NOT be bound to `artifacts/proofs/env_pins.txt` (or any other similarly named env-pins artifact).\n\n**Ledger \\+ indexing parity (mechanical).** When this token is claimed, all acceptance ledgers MUST reference `audit/gates/determinism/env_pins.log`, and parity MUST be correct:\n\n* token\\_evidence\\_matrix references `audit/gates/determinism/env_pins.log`  \n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.json` points the determinism env pins artifact\\_key to `audit/gates/determinism/env_pins.log`  \n* `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl` mirrors that exact discovered\\_physical\\_path and uses `audit/gates/determinism/env_pins.log.path_proof.txt` as proof\\_anchor\n\nAny deviation is a mechanical blocker. The binding must be corrected, not interpreted.\n\n**Epic roster tokens (determinism suites; composite).**  \nThese tokens may appear in epic acceptance rosters and QA artifacts as **composite** determinism claims. They do not replace the canonical A-gate token names already defined in this section.\n\n* **TK-ENGINE-SERIALIZER\\_COMPOSER\\_DETERMINISM\\_2RUN** — The deterministic serializer/composer proof suites used for acceptance demonstrate two-run byte identity under the canonical determinism env pins. Minimum proof: a two-run byte-compare artifact and its backing test/harness are linked in the token/evidence matrix.  \n* **TK-ENGINE-SERIALIZER\\_COMPOSER\\_DETERMINISM\\_ABBA** — The deterministic serializer/composer proof suites used for acceptance demonstrate AB↔BA byte identity under the canonical determinism env pins. This is not a synonym for `COMPOSITE_ABBA_IDENTITY_OK`; where AB↔BA composite identity is claimed as a governance token, the canonical name remains `COMPOSITE_ABBA_IDENTITY_OK`.  \n* **TK-ENGINE-SERIALIZER\\_COMPOSER\\_DETERMINISM\\_CLOSED\\_RAILS** — The determinism-sensitive suites used for acceptance run under the canonical closed determinism env pins (`SAFE_MODE=1`, `ALLOW_NETWORK=0`, `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, `TZ=UTC`) and bind to the canonical env-pins evidence surface defined in `DETERMINISM_ENV_PINS_OK`.\n\n---\n\n### **2.0.2 Internal-ops identity (/internal/version)**\n\n* **INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_200\\_CTYPE\\_JSON\\_UTF8\\_OK** — `GET /internal/version` 200 uses `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. (Owned: Governance; Mechanics Guide)  \n* **INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_HEAD\\_PARITY\\_OK** — `HEAD /internal/version` 200 mirrors GET validators (no body). (Owned: Governance; Mechanics Guide)  \n* **INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_CONDITIONALS\\_IGNORED\\_OK** — `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` are ignored; success uses 200 (never 304). This token name is canonical and non-aliasable: any other name intended to mean “conditionals return 200 and never 304” (including `INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_COND\\_200\\_NO\\_304\\_OK`) is non-canon and MUST NOT be emitted or required in acceptance artifacts. (Owned: Governance; Mechanics Guide)  \n* **INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_NO\\_ETAG\\_OK** — No `ETag` on `GET`/`HEAD`. (Owned: Governance; Build Notes — Prod QA)\n\n**Epic roster tokens (/internal/version; composite).**  \nThese tokens may appear in epic acceptance rosters as **composite** claims over the `/internal/version` invariants and evidence bundle governed in §10.5 and Appendix D.6.\n\n* **TK-SERV-PLATFORMS\\_INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_SURFACE** — A governed `/internal/version` capture \\+ validation exists and is auditable: the canonical `/internal/version` evidence bundle is produced under the governed repo paths and is indexable/mirrored per the evidence rules.  \n* **TK-SERV-PLATFORMS\\_INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_HEADERS\\_OK** — `/internal/version` headers and caching invariants pass, including: `Cache-Control: no-store` present; `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` present (GET↔HEAD parity where applicable); `ETag` absent; `Last-Modified` absent; HEAD parity expectations satisfied; conditionals ignored (200, never 304).  \n* **TK-SERV-PLATFORMS\\_INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_CANONICAL\\_BYTES\\_OK** — `/internal/version` body bytes are canonical and fixed-schema: exactly the six identity keys in the fixed order, UTF-8 (no BOM), compact, LF-terminated, and validated by the `/internal/version` proof surface invariants in §10.5.  \n* **TK-SERV-PLATFORMS\\_INTERNAL\\_VERSION\\_COUPLED\\_TO\\_RELEASE\\_ID** — `/internal/version` identity is coupled to release identity: the `release_id` field in `/internal/version` matches the canonical freeze-pack `release_id` evidence, and the coupling verification is recorded in the governed coupling proof log for this surface (see §10.5).\n\n*Naming cleanup.* The `INTVER_*` aliases are deprecated in favor of `INTERNAL_VERSION_*`. Use only the canonical names above going forward.\n\n---\n\n### **2.0.3 Reader A7 (Catalog JSON success; prove on the Endpoint Catalog)**\n\n* **ENDPOINTS\\_CATALOG\\_OK** — Catalog of JSON success routes is present (titles-only in CLI/API Vendor Ref) and includes A7 eligibility metadata for A7 proof binding. (Owned: Governance; CLI/API Vendor Ref)  \n* **A7\\_HEAD\\_PARITY\\_OK** — `HEAD` 200 mirrors 200 validators (no body).
