CRD-originated work MUST NOT be duplicated in PF09 unless the Product Owner explicitly maps or promotes it into the PF09 product-development backlog.\n\nWhere an owning schema, governed path, manifest, evidence root, validator, or artifact contract currently accepts only Epic identity, the CRD Plan MUST record that compatibility dependency and route it to the owning canon or change lane before the affected CRD relies on it. PF27 MUST NOT invent a CRD path, schema field, validator behavior, or artifact identity.\n\n### **Canon, QA, and closeout boundaries**\n\nA canon-changing CRD requires an accompanying approved ADR. The ADR MUST identify the affected canon and drainage consequences. Material CRD canon activity and decisions enter HDE Build Notes before permanent drainage. A CRD Plan alone does not supersede canon.\n\nEvery CRD requiring validation uses the full applicable Glow QA Guide process and, as applicable, a separate QA Plan. The QA record MUST bind its verdict to the exact candidate, scope, criteria, checks, evidence, decision-maker, decision time, limitations, and unresolved conditions. CI success alone is not QA acceptance, and QA MUST NOT be reduced to a development check.\n\nCRD closeout MUST distinguish:\n\n* implementation completed;  \n* Ops completed;  \n* QA accepted;  \n* evidence reviewed;  \n* ADR approved and canon drained or explicitly deferred;  \n* residual or deferred work;  \n* superseded or rejected scope; and  \n* the authorized closure decision.\n\n### **Compact PF30 record contract**\n\nPF30 is the concise CRD accountability register, not the implementation log, QA archive, evidence store, runbook, or retrospective. Update the existing CRD record when material scope, status, authority, or final outcome changes.\n\nThe initial PF30 record contains:\n\n* CRD ID and title;  \n* status and creation date;  \n* observed need or requested change;  \n* Lead Developer disposition and bounded scope;  \n* alchemical phase block or blocks;  \n* planned PR and Ops units with dependencies;  \n* canon impact and approved ADR reference, when applicable;  \n* QA requirement; and  \n* CRD Plan and material HDE Build Notes references.\n\nThe PF30 closure update contains:\n\n* final status and closure date;  \n* implemented PR, commit, merge, and Ops references;  \n* QA verdict and exact candidate identity;  \n* material deviations or deferred work;  \n* ADR and canon-drain status; and  \n* final authorized outcome.\n\nPF30 records reference detailed governed sources. They MUST NOT reproduce full plans, commands, logs, evidence payloads, QA runbooks, or retrospectives. No PF27-derived artifact creates a new PF30 volume; volume rollover remains controlled by the PF30 register.\n\n## **3\\) Ops Task Record (Template)**\n\n### **Definition**\n\nAn **Ops task** is any work item that requires privileged access to systems outside the repository and therefore requires Product Owner authorization. The PO may execute an authorized task personally or explicitly delegate execution to an automated session agent acting on the PO's behalf. This includes (non-exhaustive):\n\n* service configuration  \n* secrets / env var changes  \n* deploy / runtime settings  \n* infrastructure console actions  \n* live or shared Glow database access that crosses the repository boundary or uses privileged database credentials  \n* certain database operations (creation, grants, production migrations, other privileged state changes)\n\n### **Execution authority (normative)**\n\nRecord the exact approved class-bound IP, planned Ops task, change identity, IA instruction and authorized DevOps/environment operator. IA owns preparation and the responsible evidence-review chain. Kronos has no Ops execution or approval role. A per-PR planning approval does not authorize an external action; existing task-specific PO delegation, dispatch predicates and safety controls remain binding.\n\n* Ops tasks **MUST** be authorized by the **PO**.  \n* The PO **MAY** execute an authorized task personally or explicitly delegate execution to an automated session agent.  \n* Throughout PF27, **PO-only** identifies PO authority and accountability for the external action; IA remains responsible for the assigned Ops review chain and the specific acceptance owner follows the governing task. It does not require the PO to be the physical keystroke actor when the PO directly delegates execution.  \n* A delegated agent **MAY** perform the authorized operation on the PO's behalf and **MUST** follow the same scope, safety, evidence, redaction, and completion-claim controls that bind a human operator.  \n* When the approved scope and task-specific predicates are satisfied, the delegated agent **MUST** proceed and **MUST NOT** refuse solely because it is not human or demand a second generic human-only approval.  \n* Automated agents **MUST NOT** act without explicit PO delegation, independently approve an operation, invent missing commands, widen scope, bypass a required task-specific approval, simulate external state changes, or claim completion without the required evidence.  \n* System, platform, host, service-provider, organizational, legal, and safety controls remain binding and cannot be overridden by PO delegation.  \n* Delegation does not authorize an automated session agent to edit PF-Canon contrary to canon-maintenance controls.\n\n### **IA facilitation posture (normative)**\n\n* Ops tasks **MAY** be part of an epic. When included, they are facilitated by the **Implementation Agent (IA)**, who **MUST** guide the PO and any PO-delegated executor through preparation and execution.  \n* IA guidance **MUST** specify **intent, constraints, verification, and evidence requirements**.  \n* When canon already provides concrete operator instructions, commands, required fields, safety rails, validation checks, evidence captures, canonical paths, or decision rules for the task, the Ops task record **MUST** include those canon-grounded instructions explicitly.  \n* If canon is silent, incomplete, or ambiguous, the Ops task record **MUST** state that the missing instruction is unknown and **MUST NOT** fabricate steps.\n\n### **Not a PR (normative)**\n\n* Ops tasks are **not** Codex PRs and **MUST NOT** be represented as “implementable PR work.”  \n* Any plan/guide that includes both DEV work and OPS work **MUST** separate them and clearly label OPS work as: **PO-only execution, IA-guided**.\n\n### **Ops Task record fields (required; what-not-how)**\n\nEvery Ops task record **MUST** include:\n\n* **Task ID** (stable; referenced consistently)  \n* **Owner:** `PO`  \n* **Facilitator:** `IA`  \n* **Executor:** `PO` or `PO-delegated automated session agent`  \n* **PO delegation record, when delegated:** secret-free reference to the direct PO instruction, exact Task ID, operational objective, target, and approved scope.  \n* **Task-specific authorization identity and dispatch-boundary validity, if required:** exact secret-free authorization artifact or identity, applicable validity predicate or window, and the required STOP CHECK immediately before dispatch.  \n* **Objective blocker and resume posture:** concrete blocker, preserved safe work and evidence, exact PO value or external action required, and resume condition.  \n* **PF07 posture:** `PF07-derived` or `PF07-gap`  \n* **Infra/ops fact inventory** (as applicable):  \n  * target provider  \n  * target project  \n  * target service  \n  * target repository  \n  * target base URL or port  \n  * target database instance or schema  \n  * exact config key name  \n  * exact governed evidence root or QA root  \n  * exact expected value or exact value source in PF07  \n* **PF07 gap statement** (required when the exact value is missing from PF07; state the missing fact set and mark the affected task or claim blocked by missing PF07 infrastructure inventory)  \n* **External execution classification, if applicable:** CLI-local smoke | hosted-service operation | vendor-backed smoke | discovery only | not applicable  \n* **Exact command proof or unresolved-command posture, if applicable:**  \n* **Input identity boundary, if applicable:** state whether no app user IDs, no `person_uid`, no `user_id`, or other prohibited identity inputs are allowed.  \n* **Secret persistence posture:** presence-only | redacted | hashed | not applicable; plaintext secret persistence is forbidden.  \n* **Non-claims preserved:** state that delegation does not convert OPS into PR or QA work and that the task does not claim QA PASS, Live QA completion, acceptance-token satisfaction, PF09 status change, epic completion, deployment success beyond the evidenced target, or closeout.  \n* **Completion-claim boundary:** no executor may claim OPS completion without the required secret-free evidence meeting the task success criteria. Retain task/report/export files in Library; repository-governed primaries remain at their authorized cataloged paths.  \n* **Intent / desired end state** (what changes; what “done” looks like)  \n* **Constraints / safety rails** (what must remain true while executing)  \n* **Success criteria** (observable outcomes; not assumptions)  \n* **Closure dimension, if the task claims or supports closure** (exact environment, surface, or status dimension affected)  \n* **Closure mode, if applicable:** direct runtime validation | binding-equivalence | substitution | documentation/evidence normalization only | not applicable  \n* **Unchanged runtime facts already evidenced, if a non-runtime closure mode is used:**  \n* **Governed evidence family to normalize, if applicable:**  \n* **Superseded contradictory artifacts or reports, if any:**  \n* **Evidence to capture** (what will prove the change; where it will be stored)  \n* **Rollback intent** (what “revert” means at a high level)  \n* **Secret handling note** (explicitly: no plaintext secrets in docs or evidence)  \n* **Canon-grounded instructions, when available** (titles-only PF references; carry forward concrete operator steps, commands, required fields, safety rails, validation checks, evidence captures, canonical paths, or decision rules that already exist in canon)\n\n**Controlled execution contract (required for exact-command, vendor-backed, external-smoke, or controlled-smoke ops tasks)**\n\nUse this block when the Ops task depends on an exact command, external system, vendor-backed smoke, controlled network rails, or a proof classification that must be preserved before PO execution.\n\n* **Command template or command source:** exact canon-backed command template, discovered command file, or unresolved-command posture.  \n* **Command substitution source:** exact source for operator-substituted values, if applicable.  \n* **Executable command artifact:** path where the final executable command must be stored before execution.  \n* **Placeholder rule:** state how unresolved placeholders are detected and which classification applies if any remain.  \n* **Target classification:** CLI-local smoke | hosted-service operation | vendor-backed smoke | discovery only | not applicable | other approved classification.  \n* **CLI-local smoke classification rule:** for a CLI-local smoke, do not require hosted-service PF07 facts unless the approved target classification changes to a hosted-service operation. The plan or Ops task must still prove CLI-local facts, including command target, data source, execution context, runtime or prerequisite binding when applicable, required config-key presence, determinism pins, rails posture, application environment, and secret-safe evidence posture.  \n* **Required target facts:** command target, data source, execution context, required config keys, credential-presence keys, deterministic pins, rails posture, and application environment.  \n* **Target facts not required for this classification:** state any infra fact that is not required and why.  \n* **Target-change rule:** if the target classification changes, state which owning canon or approved live addendum must provide the replacement target fact set before execution.  \n* **Prerequisite proof:** list any prior PR, OPS, QA, or canon proof that must exist before execution and state the classification if it is absent or contradicted.  \n* **Preflight matrix:** for each preflight row, record requirement, required proof, and status rule.  \n* **Execution wrapper or operator command:** exact wrapper or command posture the PO must use after preflight passes.  \n* **Run rules:** state forbidden retries, guessed substitutions, command edits after failure, unauthorized or out-of-scope automated-agent execution, secret persistence, forced-PASS edits, execution before any required task-specific authorization is valid at the dispatch boundary, and any retry or changed authorization identity that requires fresh PO approval.  \n* **Required evidence outputs:** concrete governed files to produce under the approved ops evidence root.  \n* **Required content for evidence outputs:** exact content expectations for each required file, including command, input summary, environment posture, stdout, stderr, exit code, result summary, prerequisite matrix, and checksum ledger when applicable.  \n* **Outcome classification map:** define exact PASS, FAIL\\_BEHAVIOR, FAIL\\_TOOLING, and TOOLING\\_BLOCKED conditions for the task.  \n* **Non-claims:** state whether the task does not claim QA PASS, Live QA completion, final acceptance, public-surface change, CLI flag change, PF09 status change, epic closure, or PF-canon drain completion.\n\n### **Evidence posture (required)**\n\nOps tasks are required to capture evidence in governed paths and include path-proof transcripts where applicable.\n\nWhen retained OPS evidence paths, filenames, formats, or run-root nesting diverge from approved plan deliverables, the plan, remediation guide, review artifact, or binding artifact may accept the retained evidence only when a manifest maps each approved deliverable name to the retained evidence path and status.\n\nThe manifest MUST state, for each mapped item, whether the retained evidence is equivalent by mapping, equivalent by content despite a name mismatch, partial and supplemented by another retained file, or not acceptable. It MUST identify supplemental files that complete a partial original capture.\n\nText or markdown summaries MAY be accepted as retained OPS evidence only when the approved task does not require machine-readable JSON semantics, or when the manifest explicitly states that the text or markdown file is not being treated as schema-governed JSON.\n\nA nested run-label evidence root is acceptable only when the governed parent OPS root remains clear, the retained-path manifest is present, required sibling path proofs and index or mirror bindings are produced when promoted into governed evidence, and all nonclaims remain explicit.\n\n**Evidence posture:**\n\n**Artifacts:**\n\n* `audit/ops/<epic-id>/<task_id>/` — Task work products for this ops task.  \n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/<task_id>/` — QA evidence for this ops task (only if the task produces QA evidence).\n\n**Path proofs:**\n\n* For any governed artifact path included in acceptance or close-pack, include the sibling path-proof transcript using the suffix `<artifact>.path_proof.txt`.\n\n### **Build Checklist tracking requirement (normative)**\n\nEvery Ops task included in an epic **MUST** use the same stable Task ID in the task record and the applicable phased mapping. Complete these fields:\n\n* **Work item ID:**  \n* **PF09 disposition:** in the current epic with exact phased PF09 task or subtask mapping | out of the current epic with exact phased PF09 task or subtask mapping | PF09 gap | documentation/status drainage only | out of HDE phased-build scope  \n* **Phased PF09 document:** exact current in-document title, or `N/A` only for a non-mapping posture  \n* **Task ID:** exact ID, or `N/A` with the selected non-mapping posture  \n* **Subtask ID:** exact relevant ID; `None exists` only after verifying no relevant subtask exists  \n* **Exact source heading:**  \n* **Contribution:** advances | satisfies | leaves open | documents  \n* **Status nonclaim:** this artifact does not itself move PF09 status\n\n### **No governance drift (normative)**\n\nOps tasks **MUST NOT** create new acceptance tokens or redefine acceptance semantics. If an Ops task affects acceptance, it **MUST** map to existing acceptance posture and be proven via evidence artifacts.\n\n### **Current class, source and output boundary**\n\nUse Epic PF09 mapping only for actual Epic-originated work. A CRD task binds its controlled ID, approved CRD Specification/IP and exact selected Ops unit, not a fabricated PF09 map or active PF30 entry. Resolve actual governed evidence paths and admitted identity through HDE Schemas and Artifacts; do not mechanically invent an Ops family from an Epic example.\n\nFor bounded authorized actual execution, a repository-capable DevOps/operator may use available repository PF copies when they are its only access. Drive remains the planning/review authority; do not add a Drive comparison, synchronization certificate or SHA-only restart gate. Before a repository-dependent claim, inspect the relevant current sources and assess actual changes to governing requirements, behavior, dependencies, configuration, scope and evidence. Capture the source actually inspected or tested, the later evidence-storage commit and the current review HEAD separately when available. Normal implementation, evidence retention and documentation synchronization can advance HEAD. SHA movement alone MUST NOT revoke an approval, make valid QA unready, require a rerun or reapproval, impose a freeze, or demand a formal scope-equivalence certificate. Revisit only the affected claim when substantive change or missing decisive evidence requires it. Preserve earlier outcomes, failures and source chronology. An unavailable SHA is recorded as unavailable, not invented and not an automatic gate; genuinely missing evidence required to decide the claim remains a blocker. Exact identity and byte bindings remain required where their distinct governed proof function actually depends on them.\n\n## **3A) Change Remediation Record**\n\n### **Scope and authority**\n\nUse for a bounded Epic or CRD remediation case arising from integrated implementation audit/readiness, QA or other supported current findings. It preserves the exact approved Specification, substantive Audit and change-wide IP; it is not a replacement scope baseline or a new generic approval object. The actual stage may precede a QA Plan or QA attempt. Do not invent a Kronos decision, QA Plan, attempted run or failed task to fit a later-stage example.\n\nAn unmet applicable approved-IP objective makes integrated readiness NOT\\_READY without an additional severity/materiality threshold. Continuing Thoth diagnoses and proposes the bounded remedy; Isis approves the concrete remedy and any incorporated exact successor IP once; IA coordinates delivery through the ordinary PR/Ops lanes. When needed for a complete remedy, IA prepares the complete successor IP before Isis's substantive approval. Author corrections return to that same Isis reviewer. Do not obtain an abstract remedy approval and then a second approval for its already-incorporated plan.\n\n### **Required compact versioned record**\n\n* **Identity and actual stage:** change class/ID, remediation ID, visible version, predecessor, current author and continuing role/session references.  \n* **Trigger:** exact finding, observed condition, source evidence, applicable approved-IP objective and unmet proof burden.  \n* **Baseline:** exact approved Specification, substantive Implementation Audit, IP and relevant prior decisions/results; current repository or operational source and limitations where relevant.  \n* **Diagnosis and proposed change:** supported cause, causal uncertainty, bounded remedy, exclusions, dependencies, risks and preserved acceptance objectives.  \n* **Work items and owners:** PR, Ops, QA-plan/task or documentation work only as supported; exact mapped Epic inventory or CRD source/work-unit lineage. Distinguish proposed from approved and completed.  \n* **Verification:** objective-by-objective resolution evidence, unchanged facts reused, new proof needed, actual failure handling and recovery limits.  \n* **Plan consequence:** no IP change, or exact complete successor IP incorporating the remedy before review; keep source class and scope intact.  \n* **Decision:** exact Thoth proposal and Isis decision/version/time, approved boundaries and outstanding corrections. Approval text is a scoped substantive decision, not a token.  \n* **Delivery:** selected PR Instructions/per-PR plans and separate Ops Tasks, actual results, accepted lineage, deviations, remaining members and evidence references.  \n* **Return:** exact originating readiness/QA/review step, required updated source set, re-entry condition and responsible continuing actor.  \n* **Claims and maintenance:** no unproved QA PASS, acceptance, closure, PF09/PF30 status, deployment or canon drainage; record proposed documentation follow-ups separately.\n\n### **Iteration and escalation**\n\nRemediation may iterate without an arbitrary numerical cap. Preserve ordinary QA retry limits, attempt counts and prior failure evidence; a remediation revision does not reset them. In-scope delivery corrections may continue under existing authority. Changed remedy, scope or risk returns to Thoth for revised advice and Isis approval. Changed approved objectives or exclusions require PO scope adjudication and the applicable Specification revision/approval cycle. Recurrence without meaningful new evidence requires diagnosis, not blind retries. Return to the actual originating gate; do not automatically repeat the entire audit suite.\n\nThe detailed repository work is planned only in the selected per-PR Implementation Plan, held at ASK OK? — PR IMPLEMENTATION PLAN until PO invokes PR Implementation Proceed. Ops remains separately authorized. Section 4 carries subordinate delivery-detail fields and cannot bypass this chain. PF, historical-record, board and other administrative drainage remains separate non-gating maintenance.\n\n## **4\\) Remediation Implementation Guide (Template)**\n\n### **Scope**\n\nThis is subordinate remediation delivery detail, not an active standalone Implementation Guide or source of scope/approval. Use its applicable fields only inside the selected per-PR Implementation Plan or separately authorized Ops Task derived from the approved Change Remediation Record and exact class-bound IP. A combined DEV/OPS overview is an index of distinct authorized members, not permission for one executor to act in both lanes. Preserve the actual stage, source class and return path; do not require an additional Guide artifact or approval.\n\n### **Copy/paste command safety (normative)**\n\nIf the guide includes command lines intended for copy/paste, default commands **MUST** be safe for the current epic context.\n\nCommands included for operator use MUST be mechanically valid in-repo and MUST NOT be dead, ambiguous, or misleading.\n\nWhere a check/tool has a single canonical invocation form demonstrated by repo/CI usage, the guide MUST use that exact form as the default command. If multiple invocation variants exist, non-default variants MUST be labeled as non-default and the default choice MUST be justified as **Observed Evidence (non-PF)**.\n\nDo not present an epic-id flag for a different epic as a default. If an `--epic-id` (or similar) flag is mentioned, it **MUST** either:\n\n* match the current epic ID, or  \n* be explicitly labeled optional/non-default with a one-line rationale.\n\n### **Open Decisions**\n\nIf no open decision exists, state `None.` and do not include the marker below.\n\n#### **Decision-bounded \\[TBD\\] rule (placement and coupling)**\n\nThis subsection is the only permitted home for `[TBD]`. Each unresolved material placement or coupling decision MUST use a unique `OD-001`\\-style record:\n\n* **Decision ID:**  \n* **Decision:**  \n* **State:** `[TBD]`  \n* **Plausible options:**  \n* **Decision criteria:**  \n* **Fail-closed validator or test:**  \n* **Dependent step, path, or claim:**  \n* **Decision authority:**  \n* **Resolution source:**  \n* **Resolution effect:**\n\nUnbracketed placeholder spelling is prohibited. The marker is prohibited outside this subsection and in paths, commands, token names, schemas, environment keys, acceptance predicates, and safely discoverable facts. A dependent step MUST NOT execute or claim PASS until the decision is resolved and the selected option is bound to its enforcing validator or test. Resolution replaces the marker; it is not retained beside the answer.\n\n### **Closure-mode declaration (required when closure is claimed without a new runtime exercise)**\n\nIf the guide intends to close or recommend closure for an environment, surface, or other closure dimension by binding-equivalence, substitution, or documentation/evidence normalization rather than by a newly exercised runtime, it MUST state all of the following explicitly:\n\n* **Closure dimension:** exact environment, surface, or status dimension affected.  \n* **Closure mode:** direct runtime validation | binding-equivalence | substitution | documentation/evidence normalization only.  \n* **Unchanged runtime facts already evidenced:** exact previously proved runtime facts being relied on.  \n* **No-new-runtime-claim statement:** state that no new runtime command, route behavior, environment binding, or OPS action is being claimed beyond the evidenced basis.  \n* **Governed evidence family to normalize:** exact governed artifact family or path set that must be rewritten or refreshed to one authoritative posture.  \n* **Superseded contradictory artifacts or reports:** identify any prior contradictory bundle or report that will be treated as superseded evidence.  \n* **Same-change evidence refresh requirement:** when indexed governed bytes change, refresh the Human Evidence Index, Machine Mirror, checksum sidecars, and required sibling path-proofs coherently in the same change.\n\n### **Permitted step types (only)**\n\nA Remediation Implementation Guide **MUST** use only two step types: **DEV** and **OPS**.  \nNo other step types are permitted (no QA, DOC, REVIEW, or “verification-only” steps).\n\n### **Verification embedding requirement (normative)**\n\nAll verification **MUST** be embedded inside the owning DEV or OPS step.\n\nVerification **MUST** identify concrete required evidence outputs. Repository-governed evidence stays in authorized repository homes; off-repository plans, reports and exports use Library. Do not treat a narrative report as a governed repository primary or create a second evidence home.\n\n### **OPS posture linkage (normative)**\n\nOPS steps **MUST** follow the OPS posture defined in **Ops Task Record (Template)**: PO-authorized and personally executed or explicitly delegated, IA-guided, not PR work, evidence-bound, secret-safe, and within governed lowercase paths.\n\n### **Strict lane separation (normative)**\n\nA step labeled DEV **MUST** contain only DEV actions.\n\nA step labeled OPS **MUST** contain only OPS actions.\n\nIf a DEV action depends on an OPS output (or vice versa), the producing step **MUST** come first and the dependent step **MUST** declare its dependency explicitly using the cross-lane dependency line rule below.\n\n### **Cross-lane dependency line rule (locked; required when applicable)**\n\nIf a step depends on outputs produced by a prior step in the other lane, the dependent step **MUST** include exactly one cross-lane dependency line in this exact form:\n\n**Inputs needed from Step S\\\\ during implementation: \\\\**\n\nRules for this line:\n\n* `S<N>` **MUST** be the actual producing step ID (no placeholders such as `Sx`).  \n* The line **MUST** appear exactly once in the dependent step. It **MUST NOT** be duplicated, nested, or prefixed by a placeholder field label.  \n* If there is no cross-lane dependency, the line **MUST** be omitted (no placeholder line).  \n  **/internal/version auth posture non-invention (when relevant)**\n\n**Interim posture (normative; until the auth epic lands).**\n\n* `/internal/version` is treated as **operator-network-only** until token auth exists.  \n* Until token auth exists, guides MUST treat any auth header as **optional (never required)**. triage and QA readiness**\n\n### **Identity, actor and exact inputs**\n\nContinuing Isis performs one integrated task after implementation and required repository documentation completion. Record the change class/ID; exact approved Specification, mandatory Implementation Audit, change-wide IP and review; ordered accepted PR lineage; applicable Ops outcomes or evidenced non-applicability; documentation completion; current repository/evidence scope; and the dated historical Reality Audit used for comparison. An earlier READY decision is not an input prerequisite, and no separate mandatory QA-15 stage is inserted.\n\n### **Fresh Reality Audit artifact**\n\nProduce a complete standalone Markdown audit: identity/version, actual sources and inspection times, source roles, actual repository attribution and coverage limits, fresh whole-change findings, every applicable approved-IP objective and its evidence-backed achieved/unmet/unproven posture, historical-finding comparison and current observations, unknowns and nonclaims. Keep configured versus deployed truth, logical versus physical artifact identity and absence observations distinct. Historical source statements are not fresh runtime proof.\n\n### **Separate Change Audit Triage artifact**\n\nAccount for every fresh and historical finding exactly once, preserving its ID/source and comparison mapping. Record observed condition, evidence, approved-IP objective linkage, in-scope/out-of-scope/historical-debt/future-QA distinction, disposition, correct owner/home, remediation consequence or non-action reason, and unresolved evidence. Use the applicable HDE Build Notes addendum format for drain candidates: source/approval record, retained decisions and requirements, task/status effects, required canon drainage, deferred obligations, scope/nonclaims and evidence/traceability. Proposal, approval and physical publication are separate states. Triage is not a PF23 publication, a new work allocation or acceptance proof.\n\n### **QA Readiness artifact**\n\n* Exact audit and separate triage references, approved lineage and actual scope reviewed.  \n* Complete objective reconciliation, finding dispositions, dependencies, documentation completion and applicable Ops posture.  \n* Readiness decision and concrete basis. Any applicable approved-IP objective unmet in substance yields NOT\\_READY. Missing decisive audit evidence yields incomplete/blocked assessment, never READY. Unrelated historical debt and unperformed proof properly reserved for runtime QA do not constitute implementation failure or proof of PASS.  \n* Exact next action: READY\\_FOR\\_QA proceeds to Isis's Live QA Guide; otherwise use the bounded Thoth proposal → Isis approval → IA delivery → originating readiness re-entry route in section 3A.  \n* Conditional remediation handoff: finding/objective, complete evidence, current baseline, precise unmet burden and actual return step. No severity gate beyond objective failure, no invented QA attempt, and no automatic repeat of the whole audit.\n\n### **Live QA Guide and independent QA preparation**\n\nAfter readiness, Isis prepares a self-contained Live QA Guide with exact approved lineage, actual delivered scope, source/currentness limits, applicable Ops posture, required runtime proof, known caveats, exclusions and independent-QA handoff. It neither executes QA nor supplies a QA verdict.\n\nIndependent Kronos's QA Audit records current relevant implementation, governing predicates, complete required proof coverage, source-grounded existing loci, dependencies, rails, tools, evidence families, gaps and limits. Kronos then authors the QA Plan under section 1; Isis reviews it. The operator executes the exact approved task collection, and continuing Kronos reviews every member's evidence. Preserve stable QA IDs, dependencies, per-member outcomes, attempts and remaining IDs; do not silently narrow the collection or reset counters. A substantive Audit is not replaced by an audit-only provenance proof.\n\nAll off-repository artifacts in this section use Library. an additional PR or OPS slice | after a separate canon-only drain step**\n\n## **12\\) Implementation Audit and class-bound Implementation Plans**\n\n### **Mandatory substantive Implementation Audit**\n\nThe IA receives the exact approved Epic Specification or CRD Specification, validates class, identity, approval and complete scope, and creates the substantive Implementation Audit before the IP. Record:\n\n* Audit identity/version, author, actual source/repository state and inspection coverage/limits.  \n* Exact approved Specification and decision, change class/ID and source lineage.  \n* Every approved objective and acceptance boundary; existing capability and reuse, gaps, conflicts, dependencies, risks and unknowns.  \n* Source-grounded component/locus observations, relevant tests and evidence families, feasibility and safe implementation constraints.  \n* Required implementation consequences and any Specification insufficiency; do not silently change scope.\n\nAn incomplete, contradictory, stale or nondeterministic Specification returns to its class-specific revision cycle. Audit-only proof cannot substitute for this substantive Audit. No PO approval gate is added for Audit creation.\n\n### **Change-wide IP — shared fields with mandatory class binding**\n\nThe IA authors a separate IP derived from the exact approved Specification and its required Implementation Audit. Use EPIC\\_IMPLEMENTATION\\_PLAN or CRD\\_IMPLEMENTATION\\_PLAN visibly and structurally; a generic unclassified plan is not accepted.\n\n* **Identity/revision:** exact IP identity/version, class, change ID, actual IA author/time and predecessor.  \n* **Required lineage:** exact approved Specification/decision and substantive Implementation Audit; IP review and revision must resolve that same lineage directly or unambiguously through the IP.  \n* **Purpose/scope:** approved objectives, in/out boundaries, non-goals, intended outcomes, acceptance boundaries and nonclaims; no scope backfill.  \n* **Current-source map:** governing PF titles/locators, validated repository observations, known constraints, contradictions and discovery limits. Distinguish planned from observed and actual.  \n* **Complete planned work-unit map:** stable selected PR\\_ID or Ops task ID, lane, purpose, bounded scope, intended outcome, applicable phase, owner, order, producer/consumer dependencies, exact inputs, outputs, completion predicate and downstream handoff. Each PR or Ops unit belongs to one phase; preserve class-specific source accountability. This map does not create an actual PR or execute Ops.  \n* **Change-wide method:** sufficient implementation approach, validation, migration, compatibility, rollback/safe refusal, evidence, security/privacy, data and persistence, rollout/release boundaries and execution-critical inputs for each applicable unit. State source-grounded non-applicability when appropriate.  \n* **Documentation and QA handoff:** required repository-documentation completion, high-level independent QA scope and proof families, intended Ops dependency results and evidence. Do not claim unexecuted QA or make administrative drainage a completion predicate.  \n* **Open decisions:** explicit consequence/owner and source, with the existing decision-bounded Open Decisions contract where needed; do not invent a dependency or technical locus.  \n* **Isis review:** exact IP/version and incorporated lineage, scoped approve/redline decision, time/source and unresolved corrections. IA applies exact redlines and returns to Isis. Proposed hold: ASK OK? — EPIC IMPLEMENTATION PLAN or ASK OK? — CRD IMPLEMENTATION PLAN. Approved label: APPROVED — EPIC IMPLEMENTATION PLAN or APPROVED — CRD IMPLEMENTATION PLAN.\n\nOnly the exact approved class-bound IP enters downstream PR/Ops preparation. No change-wide PO approval gate, abstract Implementation Analysis artifact or standalone Implementation Guide is required. Complete replacement revisions preserve the same class/Specification/Audit lineage unless an authorized scope revision changes it. Each selected prompt's separate proof records provenance only.\n\n### **PR Instruction — IA-authored selected work unit**\n\nRecord the exact approved class-bound IP and selected PR\\_ID, purpose, bounded scope, intended outcome, dependencies/handoffs, verified relevant repository context, applicable canon, execution-critical inputs, required validation/evidence, exclusions, safety and mutation boundaries. Embed execution-critical facts necessary for a self-contained downstream instruction; source pointers or an audit-only proof do not force an executor to infer omitted instructions. The instruction does not create the PR, provide PO approval or bypass repository validation.\n\n### **Per-PR Implementation Plan — dedicated PR session**\n\nConsume the exact PR Instruction and approved IP work unit. Record the plan identity/version, actual dedicated session, approved lineage, selected PR\\_ID, current repository inspection and validated existing loci, detailed bounded coding/file/test/execution plan, required docs and evidence companions, dependencies, safety, validation, rollback, outputs, limits and exact approval-held version. Do not invent or expand scope into the Specification or IP.\n\nHold at ASK OK? — PR IMPLEMENTATION PLAN. The PO invokes PR Implementation Proceed after review; that invocation is the approval and authorization for the reviewed plan. There is no separate approval prompt, token, signature, binding, receipt, hash, ID or approval artifact. Record the actual invocation as ordinary provenance without creating another approval object. The same dedicated PR session executes only the reviewed scope and reports actual implementation/PR lineage, failures, corrections, evidence and remaining work. Existence of a plan alone authorizes no implementation. Merge is manual unless directly authorized for the specific agent and PR.\n\n### **Conditional planning and evidence safeguards**\n\nPreserve the existing General Implementation Plan field coverage below as shared subordinate planning guidance where applicable.     "4b2b0d198cecf6f4ece852c82951342e512124abfb93fa90678df8d97b4f4f86": "# 0\\) Front Matter\n\n**Name:** PF10-HDE-Build-Notes   \n**Version: v13.2.6**  \nEffective Date: Sep 14, 2026  \n**Status:** Living  \n**Invocation tag:** INV-f2ac55d77ce9aacc\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis file is a **working scratchpad for new, not-yet-merged documentation**. Treat it as the current source of truth **only for the specific items it explicitly covers**. For everything else, PF-Canon (PF01, PF02, PF04, PF05, PF09, PF12, PF14, PF19, PF20, etc.) remains the single home.\n\n---\n\n## **Precedence, versioning, and scope**\n\n### **1\\. PF10 authority**\n\nPF10 IS CANONICAL. For any topic explicitly addressed by an applicable, active PF10 addendum, that addendum is the current authoritative source of truth and supersedes conflicting permanent PF canon until the guidance is formally reviewed and drained into the relevant permanent PF document.\n\nNo competing canon may be used against an applicable PF10 addendum. Agents must not prefer, merge, reinterpret, or reconcile conflicting permanent-canon language while the PF10 guidance remains active.\n\nPF10 authority is limited to the scope actually addressed by its addenda. The presence of a topic elsewhere in a PF10 document does not make PF10 authoritative over related topics that no addendum addresses.\n\n### **2\\. Scope within an individual PF10 document**\n\nAn individual PF10 document is a container for multiple numbered addenda. It must not be treated as one undifferentiated rule or as blanket authority over every topic associated with the current epic.\n\nEach addendum is an independent unit of authority with its own scope. That scope is established by the addendum’s heading and substantive content, including the decisions, requirements, exceptions, artifacts, behaviors, processes, or canon topics it explicitly addresses.\n\nWithin one PF10 document:\n\n1. Every active, non-superseded addendum remains authoritative for its own stated scope.  \n2. A higher-numbered addendum does not automatically invalidate every lower-numbered addendum in the document.  \n3. Unrelated addenda remain independently authoritative and must be applied together when more than one is relevant to the current task.  \n4. An addendum must not be applied outside the scope established by its actual content.  \n5. The entire document must be searched for relevant addenda. Agents must not consult only the first, last, or highest-numbered addendum.  \n6. Document-level relevance does not establish addendum-level relevance. An agent must identify which specific addendum or addenda govern the current question.\n\nFor example, if addendum `2.12` governs evidence indexing and addendum `2.18` governs compatibility routing, both remain authoritative within their separate scopes. The existence of `2.18` does not supersede `2.12` merely because `2.18` has a higher number.\n\n### **3\\. Single-document and multi-document PF10 versions**\n\nAn active PF10 base version may consist of either:\n\n1. One unlettered document, such as `10.x.x`; or  \n2. One multi-document lettered set, such as `10.x.xa`, `10.x.xb`, `10.x.xc`, and so forth.\n\nA lettered set may be used when an epic’s build notes exceed the practical capacity of one document and drainage before the end of the epic is not practical.\n\nAll documents sharing the same base version and carrying sequential letter suffixes belong to the same PF10 version set. For example:\n\n* `10.x.xa`  \n* `10.x.xb`  \n* `10.x.xc`\n\nTogether, these documents constitute the complete active `10.x.x` PF10 set.\n\nThe letter suffix identifies a physical document within the set. It does not create a newer base version, determine topical scope, or give one document greater authority than another.\n\nAll documents in the active lettered set are equally authoritative containers of PF10 addenda. A later lettered document extends the set. It does not replace, obsolete, drain, or supersede an earlier lettered document merely because it has a later suffix.\n\nFor example, `10.x.xb` does not replace `10.x.xa`. Active, non-superseded addenda in both documents remain authoritative for their respective scopes.\n\n### **4\\. Continuous addendum sequence**\n\nA lettered PF10 set must preserve one continuous addendum-number sequence across all documents in the set.\n\nEach subsequent lettered document must begin with the addendum number immediately following the final addendum in the preceding document.\n\nExample:\n\n* `10.x.xa` contains addenda through `2.28`.  \n* `10.x.xb` begins with addendum `2.29`.  \n* If `10.x.xb` ends with addendum `2.41`, `10.x.xc` begins with addendum `2.42`.\n\nThe numbered addendum sequence establishes the order of PF10 guidance. The document-letter sequence identifies where that guidance is stored.\n\n### **5\\. Individual-addendum supersession**\n\nSupersession operates at the individual-addendum level, not automatically at the document level.\n\nThis rule applies:\n\n* Between addenda in the same individual PF10 document.  \n* Between addenda located in different documents within the same lettered PF10 set.\n\nEach addendum remains authoritative for its stated scope unless a higher-numbered addendum revises, replaces, narrows, expands, or otherwise supersedes that scope.\n\nWhen two or more addenda address the same or overlapping scope:\n\n1. The highest-numbered applicable addendum is the sole authority for the overlapping scope.  \n2. Conflicting or replaced language in every lower-numbered addendum is superseded and must not be applied in parallel.  \n3. A lower-numbered addendum remains authoritative for any distinct scope not superseded by the higher-numbered addendum.  \n4. If the higher-numbered addendum explicitly supersedes the earlier addendum in full, no portion of the earlier addendum remains authoritative.  \n5. Supersession applies regardless of whether the addenda appear in the same document or in different documents within the active lettered set.\n\nExample within one document:\n\n* Addendum `2.17` establishes a rule.  \n* Addendum `2.22` in the same document revises that rule.  \n* Addendum `2.22` controls the revised scope.  \n* Addendum `2.17` remains authoritative only for any distinct scope that `2.22` does not supersede.\n\nExample across a lettered set:\n\n* Addendum `2.17` appears in `10.x.xa`.  \n* Addendum `2.34` appears in `10.x.xb` and revises the same rule.  \n* Addendum `2.34` controls the overlapping scope.  \n* Addendum `2.17` must not be used as competing or parallel authority for that scope.  \n* Any distinct portion of addendum `2.17` not superseded by `2.34` remains authoritative.\n\nA later document letter alone supersedes nothing. Addendum number and addendum scope determine supersession.\n\n### **6\\. Current-version rule**\n\nOnly the latest active PF10 base version matters. That version may be represented by one unlettered document or by a complete lettered set.\n\nOlder base versions are fully drained, obsolete, or both. Once a newer base version exists, agents must not read, reuse, compare, reconcile, or carry forward content from an older base version.\n\nThis rule does not apply between documents belonging to the same active lettered set. If `10.x.xa`, `10.x.xb`, and `10.x.xc` form the active version, all three remain part of the authoritative PF10 source set.\n\nAn earlier lettered document remains authoritative for every applicable addendum it contains that has not been superseded by a higher-numbered addendum. It must not be discarded merely because a later lettered document exists.\n\n### **7\\. Live-content rule**\n\nThe active PF10 document or complete lettered set contains the current live guidance that has not yet been drained into its permanent PF home.\n\nDrained guidance is removed when PF10 is formally revised.\n\nIf a lower-numbered addendum remains physically present after a higher-numbered addendum supersedes some or all of its scope, the superseded language is no longer live authority. Physical presence does not defeat individual-addendum supersession.\n\nAll unaffected, non-superseded addenda within the same document or lettered set remain live and authoritative for their respective scopes.\n\n### **8\\. Silence rule**\n\nPF10 governs only through applicable, active, non-superseded addenda.\n\nPF10 is silent when no addendum in the complete active PF10 document or lettered set addresses the current topic.\n\nWhen PF10 is silent, authority returns to the relevant permanent PF-Canon document.\n\nPF10 silence must be determined only after checking:\n\n1. Every potentially relevant addendum within each applicable individual document.  \n2. Every document belonging to the complete active lettered set, when a lettered set exists.  \n3. Any higher-numbered addendum that may have superseded earlier guidance.\n\n### **9\\. Operational rule for agents**\n\nAgents must apply PF10 in this order:\n\n1. Identify the latest active PF10 base version.  \n2. Determine whether it consists of one unlettered document or a multi-document lettered set.  \n3. If it is a lettered set, identify all documents sharing that base version, such as `10.x.xa`, `10.x.xb`, and `10.x.xc`.  \n4. Treat each document as a container of separately scoped numbered addenda.  \n5. Search every applicable document for all addenda relevant to the current topic.  \n6. Determine the actual scope of each relevant addendum from its heading and substantive content.  \n7. Compare the scopes of all relevant addenda, including addenda within the same document.  \n8. Where addendum scopes overlap, apply only the highest-numbered applicable addendum to the overlapping scope.  \n9. Continue applying lower-numbered addenda to any distinct scope not superseded by a higher-numbered addendum.  \n10. Do not infer document-level supersession from a later letter suffix.  \n11. Ignore all older PF10 base versions.  \n12. Fall back to permanent PF canon only when the complete active PF10 document or lettered set contains no applicable, active, non-superseded guidance for the topic.\n\n## Cross-references\n\n Inside this file, all references to PF documents MUST be **titles-only** (for example “HDE-Phased Epics”, “Glow QA Guide”), never file names or version numbers in the body text.\n\nWhen editing or extending HDE Build Notes governs a PF12-owned point only when an active, non-superseded addendum explicitly addresses that point. When the complete active HDE Build Notes version is silent on the point, PF12 governs.\n\nPF12 integrates applicable HDE Build Notes guidance and routes cross-document references by title only. Cite HDE Build Notes by addendum number and addendum title, not by document version, document letter, or section number.\n\n### **Ownership**\n\nThis document is the single home for the catalog and repository-evidence contracts listed below and the native change-process artifact identity, minimum content, lineage, and storage boundaries in §8.18. Native change-process records are not automatically repository evidence families and do not acquire Human Index, Machine Mirror, checksum, or path-proof requirements merely by being retained or reviewed.\n\n* Engine catalogs under `catalog/`, including the current catalog homes defined in §2.  \n* The Freeze-Pack Manifest at `catalog/manifest.json`.  \n* Checksum sidecars only for families whose owning contract explicitly requires one. A Freeze-Pack Manifest entry, Human Index/Mirror hash-and-size binding, or path-proof does not create an unstated sibling-sidecar requirement.  \n* Closed domains and canonical artifact rules, including the Freeze-Pack Manifest to `release_id` contract.  \n* Canonical JSON schemas and Evidence Catalog families for stateless or no-database BodyGraph exports, compatibility exports, and optional run-bundle aggregates under §8.13.\n\n`CANON_CHECKSUMS.json` is deprecated. `catalog/manifest.json` is authoritative for frozen inputs and pack identity.\n\n### **Human Evidence Index**\n\nThe canonical Human Evidence Index is `docs/evidence/INDEX.json`. It is a records-only pointer and metadata ledger; it does not contain governed payload bytes. Its canonical JSON, record shape, legacy-row treatment, and parity join are governed by §8.3.\n\nEach current parity row binds at least `artifact_key` and `discovered_physical_path`. The exact allowed metadata remains governed by §8.3. The index MUST maintain 1:1 key/path parity with `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`.\n\n`docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256` is the hash sentinel over the canonical bytes of `docs/evidence/INDEX.json`. Acceptance-token semantics remain owned by HDE-Governance.\n\n### **Historical minimal Human Index rows**\n\nAn older governed evidence artifact MAY retain a Human Evidence Index row containing only key/path-style pointer data when that row predates the current richer evidence shape.\n\nSuch a row MAY support closed-task revalidation only when all of the following are true:\n\n* The governed artifact bytes and path are unchanged.  \n* The minimal row is not used by itself to support evidence regeneration, schema migration, a new acceptance claim, QA PASS, OPS completion, HDE Build Checklist status movement, closeout, or a runtime-behavior claim.  \n* The Human Evidence Index preserves the expected key/path binding.  \n* The Machine Evidence Mirror contains the matching artifact record with coherent `sha256`, `size_bytes`, and `proof_anchor` values.  \n* `proof_anchor` identifies the matching sibling path-proof transcript.  \n* The path-proof records the same governed path, hash, and size.  \n* The revalidation artifact discloses the minimal-row caveat.\n\nDo not downgrade a historical evidence family solely because an older Human Index row is minimal when the Machine Mirror record and sibling path-proof provide coherent path, hash, size, and proof-anchor linkage. Treat that condition as a historical evidence-shape caveat unless a later PO-governed migration requires richer historical rows.\n\nIf artifact bytes or paths change, the family is regenerated, a new acceptance claim is made, or a migration changes the Human Index shape, the current Human Index, Machine Mirror, hash-sentinel, and path-proof rules apply in full.\n\n### **Machine Evidence Mirror**\n\nThe canonical Machine Evidence Mirror is `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`. It is a governed, records-only JSONL artifact. §8.3 is the single home for its complete schema, optional metadata extension, ordering, self-record, timestamp, parity, and path-proof rules.\n\nEvery non-self record MUST bind the referenced artifact through `artifact_key`, `role`, `sha256`, `size_bytes`, `produced_at_utc`, `discovered_physical_path`, and `proof_anchor`. Unknown keys outside the §8.3 extension are rejected. Every present key is serialized in ASCII order, records are sorted by `(artifact_key, discovered_physical_path)`, and each record has exactly one terminating LF.\n\nEach governed artifact has a sibling `<artifact-path>.path_proof.txt` transcript unless its owning family expressly defines another PF12-governed companion relationship. `proof_anchor` MUST point to the governed companion. `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl` is the only Machine Mirror path.\n\n### **Dual-home layouts**\n\nThe Evidence Catalog defines governed payload paths, normally under `audit/` or `artifacts/`. Human-facing navigation under `docs/` MAY point to those paths but MUST NOT create a surrogate payload home.\n\n* Governed payload bytes remain at their Evidence Catalog paths.  \n* A `docs/` pointer or index MAY reference governed bytes by repository-relative path.  \n* A derived rendering or records-only catalog under `docs/` MUST state whether it is authoritative or points to another authoritative path and MUST be updated with the governed source when its owning contract requires synchronized change.  \n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.json` and `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl` are a paired pointer-ledger surface and MUST maintain strict parity.  \n* A truth-like root is non-authoritative unless PF12 or another owning canon explicitly catalogs its artifact family.\n\nEvidence may span multiple governed roots. Single-home means that the Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror provide the authoritative artifact-key/path bindings and that each governed artifact has the required companion proof. Root count alone does not establish drift. A root becomes drift when it is treated as an independent authority outside the Evidence Catalog, Human Index, Machine Mirror, and path-proof contract.\n\n`tools/` and `scripts/` are code and tooling roots by default. Their outputs are non-governed unless an owning Evidence Catalog entry expressly promotes them and binds them through the normal evidence discipline. Test fixtures and snapshots are governed evidence only when an owning PF section or Evidence Catalog family explicitly catalogs their path family.\n\n### **External evidence-package caveats**\n\nAn external closeout package, uploaded archive, rendered-deliverables package, zip manifest, or review-package listing is not a PF12 evidence home unless PF12 catalogs the package and binds it through the Human Index, Machine Mirror, hash, and path-proof rules.\n\nA zero-byte, missing, unreadable, or malformed package copy MAY be recorded as an evidence-package caveat instead of a PF12 evidence failure only when all of the following are true:\n\n* The owning QA, closeout, or HDE Build Notes record explicitly records the caveat.  \n* Current governed repository evidence supplies the same proof target.  \n* The governed artifact is non-empty unless its family permits a cataloged sentinel.  \n* The governed artifact has every required Human Index, Machine Mirror, hash, and sibling path-proof binding.  \n* The caveat does not conceal a missing QA step, required deliverable, unresolved behavior or tooling failure, tooling blocker, missing close-gate artifact, or untrusted evidence source.\n\nThe caveat MUST NOT make the package authoritative, bypass a governed non-empty requirement, create another evidence home, or replace the Human Index, Machine Mirror, hash sentinel, or path-proof. A package promoted as evidence becomes an explicit governed family and is subject to the same rules as any other governed artifact.\n\n### **Mirror self-record semantics**\n\nNormative Machine Evidence Mirror self-record construction, hash, size, path-proof, canonical-path, and validation semantics are defined once in §8.3. Implementations, validators, and regression tests MUST use that section. This Document Control section does not restate a parallel rule set.\n\n### **Evidence-schema validation dependencies**\n\nEvidence tooling that validates governed JSON against JSON Schema MUST use one of these postures:\n\n* Declare the validation dependency as required and ensure the applicable CI environment installs it.  \n* Treat the dependency as optional and skip cleanly with an explicit reason when it is unavailable.\n\nA schema-validation test MUST reflect the selected posture. It MUST NOT fail solely because an optional dependency is unavailable unless current canon declares that dependency required.\n\n### **Governed locations and operational summaries**\n\nGoverned evidence MUST use a cataloged repository-relative path. A transient generator path such as `codex/out/` is not authoritative and MUST NOT be indexed.\n\nBounded OPS discovery and open-rails evidence MAY be promoted only as a text-first artifact under a governed root. It MAY record key names, provider or environment labels, endpoint or route-family labels, credential-binding names, base-URL posture, account or tier posture, authorization and task identity, safe status or error classes, redacted excerpts when approved, decisions, and bounded non-secret outcomes. It MUST NOT record raw secrets, bearer tokens, API keys, database passwords, uncontrolled production data, or private payload bodies.\n\nOpen-rails evidence MUST NOT establish QA PASS, checklist status movement, epic closure, public Reader expansion, new public routes, new acceptance tokens, or broad runtime conformance unless the owning canon and separately governed evidence support that claim. Candidate evidence is non-authoritative until its exact path is indexed, mirrored, and path-proved.\n\n### **Directory naming**\n\nRepository and application directory names MUST use lower-case ASCII. This rule applies to directory segments under governed roots, including `artifacts/`, `docs/`, `audit/`, `catalog/`, and `schemas/`.\n\nThe rule does not independently constrain filenames. An uppercase character in a canon-defined close-pack filename is not directory-case drift when every directory segment is lower-case and the filename satisfies its owning pattern.\n\nEvaluate path identity from raw repository bytes, governed records, or canonical bindings. Rendering escapes in chat, Markdown, previews, or review prose are not source defects. A claimed escape-character blocker MUST identify the raw source, the read-only inspection method, the exact raw line, the identity or semantic change, and why the character is not display-layer escaping. Without that source-level proof, the blocker is invalid.\n\nA governed directory rename requires synchronized updates to every affected Human Index row, hash sentinel, Machine Mirror row, and path-proof under §§8.3 and 8.6.\n\n### **Evidence bundles and manifests**\n\nA governed evidence family MAY use a textual JSON or JSONL bundle instead of many separately governed member files. Each bundle has a textual manifest that records, for every logical member, at least a logical identity or `artifact_key`, lowercase 64-hex `sha256`, and `size_bytes`, plus any descriptors required by its owning schema.\n\nThe bundle and manifest are separate governed artifacts. Each receives its own Human Index row, Machine Mirror row, and path-proof. Internal members MAY remain manifest-addressed instead of receiving separate ledger rows when the family contract so specifies. A bundle or its manifest MUST NOT include itself as a logical member.\n\nEvidence used for agent-evaluated acceptance remains inspectable through text artifacts, including the Human Index, Machine Mirror, bundle manifests, and required QA logs. Binary or compressed files MAY be supplementary but MUST NOT be the sole governed proof for such acceptance.\n\n### **HDE-EPIC020 Candidate 1 transition**\n\nThe HDE-EPIC020 Candidate 1 bundle producer MUST accept both structured artifact entries and legacy path-string entries from `docs/acceptance_map_epic020.json` without requiring the acceptance map to be rewritten.\n\nFor a legacy string entry, the producer MAY infer transitional logical keys from the token and path. This exception is limited to HDE-EPIC020 Candidate 1\\. Canonical artifact and bundle identities remain governed by PF12 and may be pinned by a later Doc-Delta.\n\nBundle generation MUST exclude its own bundle and manifest outputs from membership even when those paths appear in an acceptance map. Membership is restricted to underlying evidence files. This prevents self-reference and does not authorize bundles to contain themselves or other governed bundle outputs.\n\n### **Evidence Catalog**\n\n§8.3 and §8.6 together form the Evidence Catalog and are the single home for governed evidence families, record shapes, and artifact paths. Other PF documents reference those families by name and MUST NOT maintain parallel path lists. HDE-Phased Epics is historical and planning context; it MUST NOT define current evidence paths, evidence shapes, or remediation predicate targets.\n\n### **Epic and CRD work accountability**\n\nTask-like future PF12 work involving evidence, schemas, implementation, QA, Ops, runtime, vendor, architecture, or product behavior MUST distinguish:\n\n* Epic-originated phased product work: the exact mapped HDE Build Checklist task or subtask, or an explicitly identified gap in that phase's inventory. When both parent and subtask exist, use the subtask.  \n* CRD-originated observed change: the Product Owner-controlled CRD identity, primary source, approved CRD Specification, and class-bound Implementation Plan or applicable pre-approval intake state. Do not manufacture an Epic identity, PF09 inventory, acceptance map, token roster, matrix, or viability prerequisite.  \n* Work outside those selected change scopes, or documentation/status drainage only, with its actual disposition and owner.\n\nHDE-Phased Epics and HDE CRD Records retain historical/reference roles; neither is an active Specification, Implementation Plan, registration gate, or prerequisite to implementation, QA, acceptance, or closure. A genuine intersection with PF09 may be referenced without converting a CRD to an Epic. Moving or expanding scope requires the actual authorized decision.\n\nPF12 defines artifact contracts. It does not allocate change identities, create work-register rows, decide status, or turn an evidence note into an implementation obligation. Preserve historical identities and planned states; later actual results remain separately attributable under §8.18.\n\n### **Planning observations**\n\nA read-only repository audit MAY identify existing governed artifacts, evidence helpers, ledger files, path-proofs, and candidate loci for planning. That observation is planning input only. It does not replace a governed artifact, ledger row, path-proof, QA artifact, OPS completion record, acceptance proof, checklist status, or closeout record. Later work relying on the observation MUST verify the locus at its pinned repository state and bind any promoted artifact through PF12.\n\n### **Routing and process ownership**\n\nScoring, thresholds, deterministic preimage arithmetic, Reader and CLI transport bytes, vendor shaping, architecture boundaries, and governance-token semantics are routed by title to HDE-Math-Spec, HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref, HDE Architecture, and HDE-Governance. PF12 does not restate their owned bytes.\n\nHDE-Governance owns historical Token Registry interpretation and any semantics for an explicitly scoped exceptional token cross-reference. For new work, exact-source evidence and scoped decisions are the primary acceptance model. Acceptance tokens are legacy-compatible, historical, optional indexing metadata. They are not acceptance authority or a required drift-control mechanism.\n\nPF12 names-only token bindings, token-aware evidence families, and token fields are compatibility surfaces. They MUST NOT require new token issuance, a complete roster, per-step intended-token or claimed-token declarations, or a token-evidence matrix as a prerequisite for a new plan, implementation, review, QA, acceptance, or closure record. Existing token IDs and historical bindings remain governed in their original scope and MUST NOT be reinterpreted, reassigned, deleted, or bulk-rewritten.\n\nExisting token fields MAY remain where required for backward compatibility. Where a governing schema already permits an empty token array, or requires a token field whose valid value may be empty, that empty array remains valid. No PF12 schema or artifact migration is required solely to retire mandatory token use.\n\nA future scoped record MAY use a bounded token or equivalent cross-reference only when existing PF, ADR, epic, task, acceptance-criterion, test, PR, commit, workflow, schema, or artifact identifiers cannot provide the needed traceability. This exception does not reactivate a universal token system.\n\nChange Process Guide owns the change lifecycle and PR/Ops workflow. PF12 defines artifact identity, minimum content, lineage, and which repository catalogs, manifests, ledgers, proofs, and companions remain synchronized; Plan Templates owns reusable document shapes, HDE-Governance owns authority, and Glow QA Guide owns QA procedure and verdict semantics. Apply explicit active HDE Build Notes overrides only in their stated scope.\n\nFor operative repository-evidence synchronization requirements, “same PR” means the same authorized change: a PR route retains its PR-bound companions; an expressly authorized bounded direct-main route retains the same integrity obligations and its actual authorization and post-write evidence. This interpretation supplies no mutation permission, changes no historical PR attribution, and does not rewrite named legacy-family contracts. New off-repository change-process outputs follow §8.18, not repository indexing by analogy.\n\n### **Magic-10 seed metadata**\n\n`catalog/magic10_seeds.json` is the governed Magic-10 seed-metadata catalog under §2.7. It is a frozen input. A byte change requires the release-identity and evidence treatment defined by §§5–6 and 8\\.\n\n## **0.3 Tagging**\n\nSection labels distinguish contract state:\n\n* `[Implemented]` means the named behavior is verified in repository bytes and enforced by the referenced current validation surface.  \n* `[Required-Now]` means the contract is required for the current build or release discipline; the label does not by itself claim repository conformance.  \n* `[Future-Promotion]` means design intent is retained but excluded from current implementation, manifest, validation, or acceptance scope until promoted by Doc-Delta.  \n* `[Speculative]` means a proposal is retained for later review and is not an accepted current contract.  \n* `[OPEN]` identifies an unresolved decision or toggle awaiting the named decision path.  \n* `[Tracking]` identifies a status ledger that may contain both resolved and open entries.\n\n## **0.4 Change policy \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n### **Single homes**\n\nPF12 owns:\n\n* The catalogs named under §2.  \n* The Freeze-Pack Manifest at `catalog/manifest.json`.  \n* Checksum sidecars only for families whose owning contract expressly requires one.  \n* The schema, artifact, Evidence Catalog, and release-identity contracts assigned to PF12.\n\nBytes owned elsewhere are routed by title and are not restated here:\n\n* HDE-Math-Spec owns scoring, thresholds, deterministic preimage, and idempotence arithmetic.  \n* HDE Architecture owns architecture boundaries and single-home routing.  \n* HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref owns transport and vendor shaping.  \n* HDE-Governance owns acceptance gates, token semantics, and Reader transport policy.\n\n### **Doc-Delta triggers**\n\nA Doc-Delta is required for a change to:\n\n* A current catalog closed domain, identity, enum, or normative order.  \n* A catalog schema or executable validation contract.  \n* Canonical JSON serialization rules.  \n* `catalog/manifest.json` structure, path semantics, or entries.  \n* A frozen input, including the order in `catalog/magic10.json`, caps in `catalog/magic10_caps.json`, topology bytes in `catalog/gates_v1.json` and `catalog/channels_v1.json`, seed metadata in `catalog/magic10_seeds.json`, threshold inputs in `math/thresholds.json`, and the narratives inputs governed by §2.8.  \n* The Machine Evidence Mirror path, required or optional record schema, parity rule, timestamp semantics, self-record semantics, or path-proof relationship.  \n* Promotion of an Authorities, Profiles, Presets, enriched UMS, full-ten seed, governed seed-body, or hash-only/index-only evidence surface from Future-Promotion into the current contract.\n\nEach Doc-Delta states its scope, targets, acceptance impact, evidence updates, and release-identity impact.\n\n### **Governed records-only artifacts**\n\nGoverned records-only families under §8 include:\n\n* `docs/ENDPOINTS_CATALOG.json` and its explicitly required checksum.  \n* `artifacts/proofs/reader_success_get_head_304.json`.  \n* Historical bridge-era runtime records, including `artifacts/runtime/env_connectivity.snapshot.json`, only under the historical nonclaims defined by §8.7.  \n* CLI parity, help, and installability families cataloged under §8.6.  \n* `/internal/version` proof families cataloged under §8.6.  \n* Registry report, database fingerprint, start-command capture, environment inventory, and validator-output families cataloged under §8.6.  \n* BodyGraph release bindings, refresh policy, metrics, and sanitized keys-only sample families cataloged under §8.6.\n\nThis list routes families to §8; §8.6 remains the authoritative artifact-key/path catalog.\n\n### **Synchronized evidence updates**\n\nWhen a governed artifact, snapshot, script, or path changes, update every affected surface in the same change:\n\n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.json`.  \n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256`.  \n* `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`.  \n* `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl.sha256` when required by the Machine Mirror family.  \n* Every affected sibling path-proof.\n\nAdd the applicable change record and Doc-Delta hook under §9. Change Process Guide owns the PR procedure.\n\n### **Release identity**\n\nA byte-level change to a manifest-listed frozen input or to the canonical bytes of `catalog/manifest.json` MUST produce a new `release_id` and record it in the Doc-Delta. The narratives pack manifest and its governed members are frozen inputs under §2.8. `catalog/magic10_seeds.json` is also a frozen input.\n\nAn editorial rearrangement that changes no governed catalog, schema, canonical-byte rule, artifact identity, or normative contract does not require a Doc-Delta. A normative change does.\n\n### **Required enforcement behavior**\n\nThe applicable validation workflow MUST fail when:\n\n* A catalog fails its schema or closed-domain contract.  \n* A governed JSON artifact fails its canonical-byte contract.  \n* A required Human Index, Machine Mirror, sentinel, checksum, or path-proof update is absent or incoherent.  \n* A Machine Mirror record violates its required/optional key set, canonical JSONL form, ASCII key order, record sort order, final-LF rule, path-proof relationship, or single-file rule.  \n* An explicitly required family checksum sidecar is missing or invalid.  \n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256` does not match the canonical Human Index bytes.  \n* `artifacts/runtime/env_matrix.snapshot.json` is missing or invalid where its schema-v3 singleton contract applies.\n\nThis subsection defines required behavior, not current workflow, test, deployment, or PASS state.\n\n## **0.5 Tracked decisions \\[Tracking\\]**\n\nThis section records tracked decisions and their current status. Purpose & Single-Home Rule \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n## **1.1 What lives here**\n\nThis document is the single home for the engine’s pack inputs and pack artifacts.\n\nClosed catalogs (IDs, enums). Canonical lists and enums used by the engine (e.g., centers, gates, channels, Magic-10 category IDs, viewer-preference keys). Catalogs MUST be schema-validated, closed-domain, and locale-neutral.\n\nArtifact serialization policy. Canonical JSON for all pack files: UTF-8, ASCII-sorted keys, compact separators (,/:), exactly one LF, no BOM/ANSI. Arrays treated as sets are deduped then ASCII-sorted; value conflicts fail-closed.\n\nFreeze-Pack Manifest (single home). The authoritative manifest lives at catalog/manifest.json.\n\nEntry shape (normative): each item contains exactly three fields: `path` (a repository-relative POSIX path string), `sha256` (a lowercase 64-hex digest of the file’s exact governed on-disk bytes after its format-specific validation passes), and `size` (the non-negative integer byte length of those same exact bytes).\n\nSidecars. Governed files carry sibling `.sha256` sidecars only where the owning artifact family explicitly requires them. Otherwise the manifest, Index/Mirror, and path-proof hash-and-size bindings remain authoritative without inventing a sidecar.\n\nRelease identity: release\\_id \\\\= sha256(canonical\\_manifest\\_bytes) (lowercase 64-hex). Any byte change to frozen inputs or to the manifest’s canonical bytes requires a new release\\_id.\n\nDeprecation note: CANON\\_CHECKSUMS.json is deprecated; use catalog/manifest.json.\n\nStateless QA export artifacts (no-DB mode).\n\nPF12 also governs the schemas and Evidence Catalog families for stateless QA exports produced directly by the engine and CLI from birth data or vendor JSON, without requiring database user records:\n\nBodyGraph export JSON — a canonical JSON object that records:\n\n* raw birth inputs used for the computation (date, time, location as normalized fields)  \n* the resolved BodyGraph topology (centers, gates, channels, profile, authority, definition, type) as IDs and structures only  \n* any internal registry IDs required for downstream compat or narratives\n\nIt MUST NOT embed app-level user identifiers or database primary keys. It is a pure engine result over frozen catalogs and math inputs (titles-only to HDE-Math-Spec and HDE-Schemas & Artifacts).\n\nCompat export JSON (stateless mode) — a canonical JSON object that records compat results computed either from two BodyGraph export files or two birth tuples:\n\n* the pair of inputs (referenced by birth data and/or BodyGraph export identity)  \n* the internal compat result (closed Magic-10 IDs and bands only; numbers remain admin/internal)  \n* the Reader v1 public envelope (six-key object per PF01/PF05) as a nested structure for parity checks\n\nThis artifact is a QA/admin surface only; it remains numeric-free at the public Reader layer.\n\nOptional “run bundle” JSON — a composite QA artifact that aggregates, for a single compat run:\n\n* the originating birth inputs or vendor JSON  \n* the resulting BodyGraph export JSON for each chart  \n* the compat export JSON for the pair\n\nIt exists to support reproducible QA runs and audits; concrete schema and usage live under §8.x Evidence Catalog.\n\nAll three stateless QA artifact types MUST follow the canonical JSON policy defined in this document (UTF-8, sorted keys, compact separators, exactly one trailing LF; arrays-as-sets deduped and ASCII-sorted) and MUST be admissible to the Evidence Index/Mirror under governed paths (artifacts/**, audit/**) when used as part of QA. They are not public app payloads; transport bytes and CLI flags live in HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref and HDE-Governance (titles-only).\n\nBy design, math arithmetic (scoring, thresholds, preimage recipe) and transport bytes (Reader/CLI/vendor) are not duplicated here and are referenced by title only in their owning documents.\n\n## **1.2 Titles-only routing \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nArtifact binding rules (paths-of-record; normative)\n\nPF12 is the single home for governed artifact families and their canonical paths-of-record. Plans and acceptance artifacts MUST bind to these canonical surfaces and MUST NOT invent alternates.\n\n**Authority order (explicit; titles-only).**\n\n1. HDE-Schemas and Artifacts is the source of truth for canonical artifact paths and sibling `.path_proof.txt` transcript naming for governed evidence families.  \n2. HDE-Build Checklist defines which checks are required for closure, but required checks MUST bind to PF12 canonical surfaces when a PF12-governed family exists.\n\n**Evidence path binding authority order (artifact sources; normative).**\n\nAuthority order: repo manifests → audit manifests → rendered reports → QA Plan.\n\nWhen multiple sources disagree on the bound path for a required artifact, the higher-authority source wins and the mismatch is treated as drift to remediate, not a license to invent alternate paths.\n\nGuard proofs are evidence-only by default (promotion discipline)\n\nGuard proof artifacts MAY be required deliverables, but they do not create new acceptance token obligations.\n\nIf a guard proof artifact is used for closure wiring (for example referenced by an acceptance map, token↔evidence matrix, or close-pack), it MUST be treated as governed evidence like other PF12 families:\n\n* stable path under governed roots  \n* updated in the Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror in the same PR when bytes change  \n* sibling \\*.path\\_proof.txt transcripts when required by the Evidence Catalog posture\n\nCanonical JSON gate artifacts (primary family plus legacy coexistence)\n\nCanonical JSON gate artifacts MUST use the canonical family under: audit/gates/json\\_gate/canonical/\n\nCanonical family (authoritative):\n\n* audit/gates/json\\_gate/canonical/json\\_gate\\_check\\_log.ndjson (required)  \n* audit/gates/json\\_gate/canonical/json\\_gate\\_compare\\_log.ndjson (required)  \n* audit/gates/json\\_gate/canonical/json\\_gate\\_structured\\_record.json (optional by default; Canonical-byte equality alone is insufficient for acceptance.  \n* When `audit/gates/json_gate/canonical/json_gate_structured_record.json` is emitted for this family, each probed locus MUST record both `expected_http_status` and `http_status`.  \n* After any fix to route-probe status logic, the authoritative canonical JSON gate family, the Human Evidence Index, the Machine Evidence Mirror, and the required sibling path-proofs for changed governed artifacts MUST be regenerated coherently in the same change.\n\nAcceptance bindings MUST cite audit/gates/json\\_gate/canonical/ as the authoritative family.
