Catalogs and Closed Domains \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nThis section defines the current catalog homes and closed domains consumed by the engine. Canonical bytes remain single-homed at their governed repository paths and are not duplicated here. A path not named in this section is not part of the current PF12 catalog surface. A new catalog home, standalone schema, enriched field, or closed-domain change requires a Doc-Delta under §9.\n\n## **2.1 Topology catalogs**\n\n### **Gates and centers**\n\n**Current repository surface.** The Gate Catalog is `catalog/gates_v1.json`; its declarative schema home is `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json`. The catalog contains one top-level `gates` array with 64 rows. Each row contains exactly an integer `gate` and one machine `center` ID.\n\n**Required contract.** Gate IDs are the unique integers `1..64`. The closed center-ID set is:\n\n`ajna`, `ego`, `g`, `head`, `root`, `sacral`, `solar_plexus`, `spleen`, `throat`.\n\nThe catalog contains these Gate counts by center: `head:3`, `ajna:6`, `throat:11`, `g:8`, `ego:4`, `spleen:7`, `solar_plexus:7`, `sacral:9`, and `root:9`.\n\nCenters are derived from the Gate Catalog. No separate Centers catalog or schema belongs to the current implemented catalog surface. For machine data, `g` is the canonical ID for the G Center and `ego` is the canonical ID for the Heart/Ego Center. Descriptive or legacy forms such as `g_center` and `ego_heart` are not canonical catalog IDs. An explicitly governed ingestion alias MAY map to a canonical ID; canonical outputs contain only canonical IDs.\n\n### **Channels**\n\n**Current repository surface.** The Channel Catalog is `catalog/channels_v1.json`; its declarative schema home is `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json`. The catalog contains one top-level `channels` array with 36 primary rows. Each row contains exactly `id`, `gates`, `centers`, `circuit_primary`, `substream`, `primary_domain`, `domains`, and `flags`.\n\n**Required contract.** A Channel `id` is the two distinct Gate IDs in numeric ascending order, zero-padded as `NN-NN`. The two values in `gates` MUST equal the values encoded by `id`, and both Gates MUST exist in the Gate Catalog. The two Channel centers MUST be distinct and, when treated as a set, MUST equal the centers derived from the two Gate rows. Positional equality between `gates` and `centers` is not required. Collections declared as sets, including Channel `centers`, `domains`, and `flags`, are normalized under §4.2 before comparison or derived emission.\n\nFor the Magic-10 v1 scoring-bound Channel contract:\n\n* the top-level object contains only `channels`;  \n* every row retains exactly `id`, `gates`, `centers`, `circuit_primary`, `substream`, `primary_domain`, `domains`, and `flags`;  \n* Channel rows are ASCII-sorted by `id` and contain exactly the closed 36-Channel roster;  \n* `circuit_primary` is exactly one of `individual`, `collective`, or `tribal`;  \n* `substream` is exactly one of `knowing`, `logic`, `sensing`, `ego`, `defense`, `centering`, or `integration` and MUST NOT be null; and  \n* `primary_domain`, `domains`, and `flags` remain non-scoring Product metadata. Magic-10 MUST NOT read them, and no default signal row may depend on them.\n\nHuman-facing copy MAY render `logic` as Understanding or Logic and `defense` as Defence or Defense. Canonical bytes retain the machine spellings `logic` and `defense`. Any later correction or removal of the non-scoring Product metadata requires a separate contract migration covering the affected bundle schemas and generated artifacts.\n\nThe closed Channel-ID set, in ASCII order, is:\n\n`01-08`, `02-14`, `03-60`, `04-63`, `05-15`, `06-59`, `07-31`, `09-52`, `10-20`, `10-34`, `10-57`, `11-56`, `12-22`, `13-33`, `16-48`, `17-62`, `18-58`, `19-49`, `20-34`, `20-57`, `21-45`, `23-43`, `24-61`, `25-51`, `26-44`, `27-50`, `28-38`, `29-46`, `30-41`, `32-54`, `34-57`, `35-36`, `37-40`, `39-55`, `42-53`, `47-64`.\n\n`engine/config/registry_loader.py` is the executable topology-validation home. It MUST fail closed on missing files, malformed shapes, duplicate IDs, unknown Gate or center references, malformed or noncanonical Channel IDs, Channel/Gate identity mismatches, endpoint-center set mismatches, and aliases outside the explicit input-only policy. `artifacts/registry/registry_report.json` is the generated projection governed by §8.5; it is not a second catalog.\n\n## **2.2 Authorities and Profiles \\[Future-Promotion\\]**\n\n**Current implementation boundary.** The current catalog loader, root manifest, topology schemas, and registry projection do not define or consume separate Authorities or Profiles catalogs. These domains are excluded from current catalog-validation and Freeze-Pack scope. This exclusion does not retire the Human Design concepts.\n\n**Future-Promotion requirement.** Introducing either catalog requires, in the same governed change, an exact catalog path, a schema or executable validation contract, consumer wiring, Freeze-Pack Manifest treatment, tests, evidence, and a Doc-Delta.\n\n## **2.3 Magic-10 closed ID set**\n\nThe Magic-10 closed ID set is:\n\n`alignment`, `balance`, `comfort`, `communication`, `consistency`, `creativity`, `drive`, `expansion`, `harmony`, `heat`.\n\nNo consumer, viewer-preferences object, configuration artifact, seed map, narrative key, or evidence artifact may introduce another Magic-10 ID.\n\n## **2.4 Viewer preferences**\n\n**Required contract.** A viewer-preferences object contains exactly `top_category` and `weights`.\n\n* `top_category` MUST be one ID from §2.3.  \n* `weights` MUST contain exactly all ten §2.3 IDs as keys.  \n* Every weight MUST be an integer in `0..100`; booleans and non-integer numbers are invalid.  \n* Unknown, missing, or duplicate category identities fail closed.  \n* A zero weight is preserved for the sampler or ranker exclusion decision; normalization MUST NOT replace it with a positive value.\n\nJSON object-key serialization remains governed by §4. The semantic key set does not create a second category order.\n\n## **2.5 Magic-10 caps and future Presets**\n\n**Current repository surface.** The caps catalog is `catalog/magic10_caps.json`. It contains exactly the ten §2.3 IDs. Each row contains a non-empty `inputs` array and `bounds` whose current integer values are `min:0` and `max:100`.\n\n**Required contract.** Unknown or missing category rows fail closed. Caps do not redefine the Magic-10 ID set, frozen order, or score thresholds.\n\n**Future-Promotion.** No governed Presets catalog belongs to the current implemented catalog surface. A future Presets catalog MUST reference the §2.3 IDs and §2.6 order instead of embedding a second Magic-10 domain, order, cap, or threshold table. Promotion requires an exact catalog path, schema or executable validator, consumer wiring, Freeze-Pack Manifest treatment, evidence, tests, and a Doc-Delta.\n\n## **2.6 Frozen Magic-10 order and bands**\n\nThe single home for the frozen Magic-10 emission order is `catalog/magic10.json`. The exact order is:\n\n1. `harmony`  \n2. `heat`  \n3. `communication`  \n4. `alignment`  \n5. `comfort`  \n6. `consistency`  \n7. `expansion`  \n8. `creativity`  \n9. `drive`  \n10. `balance`\n\nConsumers MUST use this order and MUST NOT define an alternate canonical order.\n\nThe band labels, in ascending order, are `Cool`, `Open`, `Warm`, and `Glow`. Numeric threshold arithmetic remains owned by HDE-Math-Spec. The current governed threshold input is `math/thresholds.json`, which carries clamp bounds, inclusive edges, rounding mode, and version. Caps live in `catalog/magic10_caps.json`; neither caps nor threshold edges live in `catalog/magic10.json`.\n\n## **2.7 Magic-10 seed metadata**\n\n**Current repository surface.** The seed-metadata catalog is `catalog/magic10_seeds.json`. It is a partial map with current rows for `harmony` and `heat`. Each current row contains exactly `template_id`, `seed_version`, `updated_at_utc`, and `checksum_sha256`. No `admin_only` field belongs to the implemented shape.\n\n**Required contract.** Catalog keys MUST be a subset of §2.3, and unknown category keys fail closed. `checksum_sha256` MUST be lowercase 64-hex and identifies the referenced seed content; it is not a digest of the metadata row itself.\n\nFull-ten coverage, a governed seed-body catalog, or a new checksum projection is a Future-Promotion change requiring a Doc-Delta. None may be inferred from this metadata map.\n\nAny byte change to `catalog/magic10_seeds.json` changes each manifest or generated configuration artifact that binds those bytes and requires the corresponding release-identity and evidence refresh under §§5–6 and §8.\n\n## **2.8 Narratives pack**\n\n**Current repository surface.** The narratives pack manifest is `catalog/narratives/manifest.json`. It identifies these four JSON members:\n\n* `catalog/narratives/keys.json`  \n* `catalog/narratives/palettes.json`  \n* `catalog/narratives/suppression_map.json`  \n* `catalog/narratives/templates.json`\n\nEach member and the pack manifest have sibling `.sha256` sidecars in the checked-in repository. Sidecar presence alone does not establish hash, size, canonical-byte, or release-coupling conformance.\n\n**Required integrity contract.** Manifest member paths MUST be unique and ASCII-sorted. Each member record MUST bind `path`, `sha256`, and `size_bytes` to the member's canonical bytes. The pack manifest and all pack members MUST be canonical JSON under §4. Their canonical form includes exactly one final LF.\n\n`pack_sha` is the SHA-256 digest of the canonical bytes of `catalog/narratives/manifest.json`. Composer and governed preview or evidence surfaces echo `pack_sha` as required by HDE-Narratives-Guide.\n\nThe root Freeze-Pack Manifest MUST list the narratives pack manifest and all four required members exactly once before a release may claim that the pack is coupled to its `release_id`. A pack present in the repository but omitted from `catalog/manifest.json` is not proven part of that manifest's release identity. Validation MUST report the gap rather than infer coupling.\n\n## **2.9 Magic-10 v1 mechanics configuration and result contracts**\n\n### **Authoritative configuration identity**\n\nThe authoritative active Magic-10 v1 mechanics configuration is `catalog/magic10_mechanics_v1.json`. Its owning schema is `schemas/magic10_mechanics_v1.schema.json`, and its configuration schema identity is `magic10_mechanics_config.v1`.\n\nThe configuration MUST be canonical JSON under §4, schema-valid, manifest-bound, and immutable within one release. Production code reads exactly one active configuration from this governed catalog path and MUST NOT use this Markdown document, a candidate tuning bundle, a generated evidence snapshot, or a caller-supplied config ID as an alternate configuration source.\n\nThe initial `config_id` is `m10-channel-state-v1.0.0`. The configuration’s top-level object has `additionalProperties: false` and exactly these properties:\n\n* `category_weights`  \n* `config_id`  \n* `profiles`  \n* `response_scale`  \n* `result_schema`  \n* `rounding`  \n* `schema`  \n* `signal_scale`  \n* `signals`  \n* `sources`\n\nThe fixed identity and scale values are:\n\n* `schema`: `magic10_mechanics_config.v1`;  \n* `result_schema`: `magic10_result.v1`;  \n* `response_scale`: `10000`;  \n* `signal_scale`: `2`;  \n* `rounding.signal`: `round_half_up_to_half_score_unit`; and  \n* `rounding.category`: `round_half_up_once`.\n\n`sources` has exactly `caps`, `categories`, `channels`, and `thresholds`. Each source row has exactly `path` and `sha256`, with no additional property. The exact paths are:\n\n* `caps` → `catalog/magic10_caps.json`;  \n* `categories` → `catalog/magic10.json`;  \n* `channels` → `catalog/channels_v1.json`; and  \n* `thresholds` → `math/thresholds.json`.\n\nEvery source hash MUST equal the SHA-256 digest of the exact referenced bytes. A change to any referenced caps, category-order, Channel, or threshold bytes requires a new immutable `config_id`, new canonical configuration bytes, refreshed manifest membership, and a new `release_id`.\n\n### **Closed configuration shape**\n\n`profiles` is ordered by ASCII `profile_id` and contains exactly `activation_bp_v1`, `coherence_bp_v1`, and `expression_bp_v1`. Each profile has exactly `profile_id` and `responses`; `responses` has exactly the five relationship-state properties and no additional property.\n\n`signals` contains exactly the twenty signal IDs obtained by flattening each `catalog/magic10_caps.json` input pair in `catalog/magic10.json` category order.\n\nAn ordinary signal row has exactly `channels`, `operation`, `profile_id`, and `signal_id`. A Balance signal row has exactly `channels`, `operation`, and `signal_id`; `profile_id` is prohibited. Every `channels` array is ASCII-sorted by `channel_id`; each member has exactly `channel_id` and `weight`.\n\n`category_weights` contains exactly ten rows in `catalog/magic10.json` order. Each row has exactly `category_id`, `reducer`, and `weights`. `reducer` is `weighted_mean_half_unit_v1`; `weights` is an ordered two-integer array whose values are each in `1..3`.\n\n`catalog/magic10_caps.json` is the sole authority for each category’s ordered two-signal input pair and score bounds. The mechanics configuration MUST NOT duplicate those signal identities. The loader joins each category-weight row to the caps row by `category_id` and input position.\n\nGenerated timestamps, seeds, notes, labels, and unrecognized metadata are prohibited from the authoritative configuration. Schema-declared array order is preserved; object keys use PF12 canonical JSON order.\n\n### **Tuning and loader closure**\n\nThe allowed v1 tuning ranges are:\n\n* ordinary Channel weight: integer `1..3`;  \n* state response: integer `0..10000`, while the required profile ordering remains valid;  \n* category-input weight: integer `1..3`;  \n* Channel membership: one through six unique canonical Channels per ordinary signal;  \n* signal profile assignment: one of the three ordinary profiles;  \n* Balance Channel membership: one through six unique canonical Channels; and  \n* band maxima: four strictly increasing integers ending in `100`, initially `[24,49,74,100]`.\n\nThe five relationship states, twenty signal IDs, ten category IDs, two-signals-per-category structure, ordinary weighted-sum operation, two Balance operations, fixed-point scales, half-up reducers, `0..200` signal domain, and `0..100` category-score domain are fixed v1 invariants, not tuning knobs.\n\nThe loader MUST reject the active configuration unless:\n\n* the Channel catalog has exactly the closed 36-Channel roster and valid endpoint projections;  \n* every configured Channel exists in that catalog;  \n* the signal key set exactly equals the flattened caps-owned twenty-signal roster;  \n* every category appears exactly once and has two weights aligned to its caps-owned ordered inputs;  \n* caps bounds are integers satisfying `0 <= min <= max <= 100`;  \n* ordinary and Balance signal Channel lists each contain one through six unique valid rows;  \n* Channel weights are integers in `1..3`;  \n* every profile has exactly five state keys, every response is an integer in `0..10000`, and `none` is exactly `0`;  \n* the three required profile orderings hold;  \n* Balance operations have their required maps and no profile;  \n* no Channel appears twice within one signal or in both signals of one category;  \n* every Channel is used by at least one signal;  \n* signal and category outputs remain within `0..200` and `0..100`;  \n* category order equals `catalog/magic10.json`;  \n* every source path and hash matches the exact referenced bytes;  \n* thresholds close the full `0..100` domain;  \n* the configuration hash matches the manifest; and  \n* the release selects exactly one active mechanics configuration.\n\nA caller cannot pass weights, profiles, bands, or a configuration ID. Production MUST NOT blend configurations.\n\n### **Governed result schemas**\n\nThe pure Engine Core result schema is `schemas/magic10_result_v1.schema.json`, with result identity `magic10_result.v1`. It exists only for an eligible distinct-person pair. Its top-level object has `additionalProperties: false` and exactly:\n\n* `schema`;  \n* `config_id`;  \n* `release_id`;  \n* `pair_key`;  \n* `signals`; and  \n* `categories`.\n\n`schema` is the constant `magic10_result.v1`. `release_id` and `pair_key` are lowercase 64-hex identities. `signals` contains exactly twenty rows in flattened caps-input order; each row has exactly `signal_id` and integer `q` in `0..200`. `categories` contains exactly ten rows in `catalog/magic10.json` order; each row has exactly `category_id`, integer `score` in `0..100`, and `band` equal to `Cool`, `Open`, `Warm`, or `Glow`.\n\nThe pure result contains no names, UIDs, timestamps, viewer preferences, copy, personal keys, shared keys, request metadata, or mutable configuration handles.\n\nThe complete internal/admin result schema is `schemas/magic10_compat_result_v1.schema.json`, with result identity `magic10_compat_result.v1`. It retains the same top-level identity fields and signal array. Each category row contains exactly `category_id`, `score`, `band`, required nonempty `shared_key`, required nonempty `personal_lo_to_hi_key`, and required nonempty `personal_hi_to_lo_key`.\n\nNarrative augmentation MUST NOT change signal values, category scores, bands, ordering, `config_id`, `release_id`, or `pair_key`. The complete result is confined to internal/admin CLI and authenticated internal HTTP surfaces.\n\n### **Release rollback coupling**\n\nA rollback MUST select one complete prior release containing mutually compatible code, catalog, configuration, schema, and manifest bytes. If that complete target is unavailable or its identity cannot be reproduced, the affected calculation or surface MUST fail closed. A rollback MUST NOT mix prior code with current configuration or current schemas, rewrite user identity into the intrinsic result, or silently serve a stale result under a different configuration or release identity.\n\n# **3\\. Catalog Validation & Integrity \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nThis section defines the required validation and integrity contract for the current catalog surfaces in §2. Declarative schemas, executable validators, and companion checks together form the gate. A required rule is not evidence that the current repository already enforces it; implementation status and remaining gaps are stated explicitly below and routed to §§8.1–8.2 for validation ownership and evidence.\n\n## **3.1 JSON Schema and catalog validation**\n\nEvery current catalog MUST pass its owning validation contract. A catalog with an owning JSON Schema MUST validate against that schema with no errors. Catalogs whose current contract is executable rather than schema-owned MUST pass the executable validator and every required companion check. The existence of a catalog does not imply an unlisted schema home.\n\n### **Scope**\n\nA catalog is a JSON artifact that enumerates a closed or structured domain consumed by the engine. An owning schema is the single declarative schema that defines the structure, types, and constraints for a catalog. The current declarative topology-schema homes are `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json` and `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json`; current executable validation is owned by the paths identified in §2.\n\n### **Normative rules**\n\n* Every property required by an owning schema or executable contract MUST be present.  \n* Additional properties are invalid at a closed object level. A validator MUST reject unknown keys unless the owning contract explicitly permits them at that level.  \n* Values MUST satisfy their owning types without coercion. In particular, booleans are invalid where an integer is required, and strings MUST NOT be converted to numeric values to make invalid input pass.  \n* Every enum is closed. A value outside its owning enum is invalid.  \n* An array declared as a set MUST contain no duplicate identity. If JSON Schema cannot express the identity or uniqueness rule, a companion check MUST enforce it.  \n* An object-array declared as a set MUST have an owning identity projection for deduplication and ordering. Absence of that projection is a contract defect and MUST be covered by a companion check until corrected.  \n* A simple string identifier such as `id` MUST be non-empty and MUST match `^[a-z0-9_]+$`, case-sensitively. A schema-defined composite identifier MUST match its own canonical projection. Any maximum length MUST be defined by the owning schema.  \n* Numeric bounds and cardinalities MUST be enforced exactly as owned; validators MUST NOT widen them.  \n* Seed metadata in `catalog/magic10_seeds.json` MUST use only keys from the Magic-10 domain. Every present row MUST contain exactly `template_id`, `seed_version`, `updated_at_utc`, and `checksum_sha256`. `checksum_sha256` MUST be lowercase 64-hex and identifies referenced seed content; it MUST NOT be recomputed over the metadata row itself unless a future governed seed-body projection defines that operation.\n\nSchema and executable validation govern data shape, values, identity, and cross-reference integrity. Canonical bytes, key ordering, set ordering, encoding, and the final LF remain governed by §4.\n\n### **Schema hygiene**\n\n* Every owning JSON Schema MUST include both `$schema` and `$id`.  \n* The required draft is JSON Schema 2020-12. `$schema` MUST be `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema`.  \n* `$id` MUST be a stable repository-path identity for its owning schema. Current schema examples are `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json` and `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json`. Reference-only UMS drafts are not owning schemas for the current catalogs.  \n* Closed object levels SHOULD set `additionalProperties` to `false`; an open level MUST be intentional and explicit.  \n* Cross-catalog membership, identity projection, derived-field equality, graph degree, and multiplicity rules that JSON Schema cannot express MUST be enforced by companion checks.  \n* A schema SHOULD encode a constrained composite identity directly. If it does not encode the full projection, a companion check MUST enforce the remainder.\n\nAt the pinned repository state, both current topology schemas declare JSON Schema 2020-12 and their exact stable repository-path `$id` values: `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json` and `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json`. The former `$id` omission is closed. This fact does not by itself prove CI wiring, complete companion validation, or conformance of a future schema introduced by a later governed contract.\n\n### **Enforcement**\n\n* Catalog validation MUST run locally and in CI. A failure is a hard stop.  \n* A change to a catalog, schema, executable validator, or referenced closed domain MUST rerun all dependent checks in the same governed change.  \n* Uniqueness, cross-reference, ordering, identity-projection, and arrays-as-sets rules outside JSON Schema capability MUST run as companion checks.  \n* Deterministic validation and ordering checks MUST run under `LC_ALL=C` as defined in §4.3.\n\nAcceptance hints: `CATALOG_SCHEMA_OK`, `CATALOG_NO_ADDITIONAL_PROPS_OK`, `CATALOG_ENUM_DOMAIN_CLOSED_OK`, `ARR_SET_NO_DUPLICATES_OK`, `ARR_SET_IDENTITY_DECLARED_OK`, `SCHEMA_HYGIENE_OK`, and `SCHEMA_ID_STABLE_OK`.\n\n## **3.2 Graph coherence checks**\n\nTopology integrity is evaluated across the Gate and Channel catalogs, using the closed center domain derived from Gate rows under §2.1. No separate Centers catalog belongs to the current implemented surface.\n\n### **Scope and derived projections**\n\nInputs are `catalog/gates_v1.json` and `catalog/channels_v1.json`.\n\n* `center_of_gate[g]` is the canonical center ID owned by Gate `g`.  \n* `gates_of_channel[ch]` is the two-Gate set declared by Channel `ch`.  \n* `centers_of_channel_derived[ch]` is the set obtained by projecting both members of `gates_of_channel[ch]` through `center_of_gate`.\n\nAll comparisons of declared and derived sets use the set rules in §4.2.\n\n### **3.2.1 Channel degree and identity**\n\n#### **Cardinality**\n\n* Each Channel MUST reference exactly two Gate IDs.  \n* The two Gate IDs MUST be distinct and MUST exist in the Gate Catalog.  \n* The Channel Catalog MUST contain exactly the 36 primary Channel identities owned by §2.1.\n\n#### **Identity and uniqueness**\n\nA Channel identity is the two referenced Gate IDs in numeric ascending order, zero-padded and encoded as `NN-NN`. Both components MUST be in `01..64`. The exact lexical pattern is `^(?:0[1-9]|[1-5][0-9]|6[0-4])-(?:0[1-9]|[1-5][0-9]|6[0-4])$`; matching the pattern does not replace the min-first or Gate-pair equality checks.\n\nThe `id` components MUST equal the two values in `gates` after canonical ordering. No two rows may share a canonical Channel identity. Repeated identity with identical or different row bytes is invalid and fails closed.\n\n#### **Arrays-as-sets coupling**\n\nAny array that lists Channels as a set MUST deduplicate by canonical `NN-NN` identity and MUST be ASCII-sorted by that identity. Duplicate, conflicting, or out-of-order identities are validation errors.\n\nAcceptance hints: `TOPOLOGY_CHANNEL_DEGREE_2_OK`, `ARR_SET_NO_CONFLICTS_OK`, `ARR_SET_ASCII_SORT_OK`, `CATALOG_ORIENTATION_CANON_OK`, and `TOPOLOGY_COHERENCE_OK`.\n\n### **3.2.2 Gate-center and Channel-center consistency**\n\n* Every Gate MUST map to exactly one member of the closed center domain in §2.1.  \n* For each Channel, the validator MUST derive `centers_of_channel_derived[ch]` from the two referenced Gate rows.  \n* The two derived centers MUST be distinct; a Channel connects Gates belonging to two different centers.  \n* The Channel row's `centers` set MUST equal `centers_of_channel_derived[ch]`. Positional equality between `gates` and `centers` is not required.  \n* A declared center value that is closed-domain-valid but does not match the Gate-derived set is invalid.\n\nAcceptance hints: `TOPOLOGY_CENTER_CONSISTENCY_OK`, `TOPOLOGY_DOMAIN_CLOSED_OK`, and `XREF_MEMBERSHIP_OK`.\n\n### **3.2.3 No orphans**\n\n* Every center ID referenced by a Gate MUST belong to the closed center domain in §2.1.  \n* Every Gate ID referenced by a Channel MUST exist in the Gate Catalog.  \n* Every explicit Channel center MUST be derivable from one of its two Gate rows.  \n* There MUST be no dangling topology reference. A missing target is a hard validation failure.\n\nAcceptance hint: `TOPOLOGY_NO_ORPHANS_OK`.\n\n### **3.2.4 Declared degree vectors**\n\nA degree vector is optional until an owning catalog or governed proof artifact declares it. When declared, the validator MUST compute `gate_degree[g]` as the number of distinct Channels that reference Gate `g` and compare the observed vector with the declared expectation.\n\n* Every declared Gate key MUST exist in the Gate Catalog.  \n* Every degree MUST be a non-negative integer.  \n* Every declared value MUST equal the observed value.  \n* A vector declared closed MUST have exactly the same Gate-key set as the observed projection. A vector declared partial governs only its listed Gate keys.  \n* An exception or temporary exclusion MUST be encoded in the governed declaration, not supplied as ad hoc validator behavior.\n\nThe check MUST rerun whenever either topology catalog or the declared vector changes.\n\nAcceptance hints: `DEGREE_VECTORS_DECLARED_OK`, `DEGREE_VECTORS_MATCH_OK`, and `DEGREE_VECTORS_NONNEG_INT_OK`.\n\n### **3.2.5 Distinguished sets**\n\nA distinguished set is an optional, named, governed subset of Gate or Channel identities. It is enforced only after an owning artifact declares it.\n\nEach declaration MUST contain:\n\n* `name`, as a non-empty string;  \n* `type`, with the value `gates` or `channels`;  \n* `members`, as an array governed as a set; and  \n* only metadata explicitly permitted by its owning contract.\n\nFor `gates`, member identity is the integer Gate ID. For `channels`, member identity is canonical `NN-NN`.\n\nWhen a distinguished set is declared:\n\n* every member MUST belong to its current closed domain;  \n* members MUST be unique by identity and ASCII-sorted by their canonical string projection;  \n* a Channel member MUST pass Gate membership, canonical identity, distinct-center, and derived-center checks;  \n* a set declared closed MUST contain its complete owned membership; and  \n* a set declared partial governs only its listed membership and set semantics.\n\nAcceptance hints: `DISTINGUISHED_DECLARED_OK`, `DISTINGUISHED_DOMAIN_CLOSED_OK`, `DISTINGUISHED_NO_CONFLICTS_OK`, `DISTINGUISHED_ASCII_SORT_OK`, and `DISTINGUISHED_TOPOLOGY_CONSISTENT_OK`.\n\n### **3.2.6 Integration and multiplicity invariants**\n\n* In the current Gate graph, only Gates `10`, `20`, `34`, and `57` have degree `3`; every other Gate has degree `1`. Any other degree vector fails closed.  \n* Reducing Channels to unordered center pairs MUST produce 36 total Channel edges. Any expected per-pair multiplicity vector MUST be encoded in a governed artifact or as an explicit closed declaration in `catalog/channels_v1.json`; validation MUST compare the observed vector with that owned declaration.  \n* At Channel identity level, the graph is simple: canonical `NN-NN` edges are unique. At center-pair level, the graph is a multigraph and parallel center-pair edges are permitted. Engine mechanics remain per Channel identity.\n\nThe executable topology-validation home already rejects missing files, duplicate primary identities, unknown Gate and center references, malformed Channel IDs, and Channel/Gate identity mismatch. It does not yet enforce exact topology cardinalities, exact allowed-key sets, distinct Gate or center pairs, declared-versus-derived center equality, the frozen degree vector, center-pair multiplicities, or canonical catalog bytes. Those companion checks are required before the complete topology contract may be claimed.\n\nAcceptance hints: `TOPOLOGY_INTEGRATION_DEGREE_OK`, `TOPOLOGY_CENTER_MULTIPLICITY_OK`, and `TOPOLOGY_SIMPLE_GRAPH_OK`.\n\n## **3.3 Domain closure and enums**\n\nAll identities and enum values in a current closed domain MUST come from that domain's owning catalog or schema. Unknowns are rejected.\n\n### **Scope**\n\nThis subsection applies to the current closed domains in §2: Gate IDs, derived center IDs, Channel IDs and enums, Magic-10 IDs, order and caps, viewer-preference keys, present seed-metadata keys, and narratives identities. Authorities, Profiles, Presets, full-ten seed coverage, and enriched UMS fields are Future-Promotion surfaces. They are not current closed-domain or CI inputs until promoted through a Doc-Delta.\n\n### **Normative rules**\n\n* For a given release, each current catalog defines the complete set of valid identities or enum values in its scope.  \n* Every referenced identity or enum value MUST belong to its owning current domain. An unknown value fails closed.  \n* Unknown values MUST NOT be silently coerced, normalized, or substituted. Only an explicitly governed input alias may map to a canonical ID, and canonical outputs contain only canonical IDs.  \n* Simple IDs are case-sensitive ASCII matching `^[a-z0-9_]+$`. A schema-defined composite identity is an explicit exception and MUST match its owning projection; Channel IDs use canonical `NN-NN` under §3.2.1.  \n* A closed-domain addition, removal, rename, or semantic reassignment requires explicit review, a Doc-Delta, dependent validation, and release-identity treatment when the affected bytes are frozen inputs.  \n* When order is semantically consumed, the consumer MUST use the owning catalog order. Otherwise the domain is a set and deterministic emissions MUST ASCII-sort by canonical identity.\n\n### **Specific applications**\n\n* Magic-10 categories. Only the ten IDs in §2.3 are valid. Canonical emission order is exactly the order in `catalog/magic10.json` and §2.6.  \n* Viewer preferences. The object MUST contain exactly `top_category` and `weights`. `top_category` MUST be one Magic-10 ID, and `weights` MUST contain exactly all ten Magic-10 IDs. Each weight MUST be an integer in `0..100`.  \n* Magic-10 caps. `catalog/magic10_caps.json` MUST contain exactly the ten Magic-10 keys. Artifact Serialization Policy**\n\nContract posture: required but not yet repo-conformant.\n\nThis section owns the exact serialization bytes for pack files, `catalog/manifest.json`, and governed JSON evidence registered in §8.6. Operational logs are outside canonical-JSON scope; they remain keys-only under HDE-Governance and need not be canonical JSON. Schema content, arithmetic, and transport behavior remain in their owning specifications.\n\n## **4.1 Canonical JSON rules**\n\nA governed JSON document MUST satisfy all of these rules:\n\n* Encode as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark.  \n* Emit object keys in strict ASCII ascending order at every object level.  \n* Preserve schema-declared array order. Reorder only arrays defined as sets, and only under §4.2.  \n* Use compact separators: `,` between members and `:` between a name and value, with no surrounding whitespace.  \n* End the file with exactly one LF byte. Do not emit carriage returns, trailing spaces, tabs, or blank lines outside string values.  \n* Delimit strings with `\"`. Escape only characters JSON requires: `\"`, `\\`, and controls U+0000 through U+001F, using the shortest legal escape such as `\\n`, `\\t`, or `\\u00XX`.  \n* Emit non-ASCII characters directly as well-formed UTF-8. Reject unpaired surrogates and do not alter string values through normalization, trimming, or case conversion.  \n* Follow the owning schema's types. Encode integers in base 10 without a leading plus sign, unnecessary leading zeros, decimal point, or exponent. Pack artifacts MUST NOT contain non-integer numbers, `NaN`, or infinity. A future non-integer quantity requires a Math-owned exact integer or string encoding.  \n* Emit `true`, `false`, and `null` exactly; `null` is allowed only where the owning schema permits it.  \n* Use the field names defined by the owning schema. New unspecified field names SHOULD use lower-snake ASCII.\n\nCanonicalization MUST NOT otherwise change values. Re-serializing the same in-memory value MUST produce identical bytes, and a validator MUST compare those bytes with the on-disk file.\n\nA records-only JSONL artifact contains one canonical JSON object per line, no array wrapper or blank line, and exactly one LF after the final record.\n\n### **Acceptance hints**\n\n`CANON_JSON_UTF8_OK`, `CANON_JSON_SORTED_KEYS_OK`, `CANON_JSON_COMPACT_OK`, `CANON_JSON_SINGLE_LF_OK`, `CANON_JSON_NO_BOM_OK`, `CANON_JSON_IDENTITY_OK`, `JSONL_RECORDS_CANON_OK`.\n\n## **4.2 Arrays-as-sets discipline**\n\nThis discipline applies only when the owning schema defines an array as a set. An ordered array retains its schema-declared order.\n\nThe schema MUST define an identity rule:\n\n* A scalar's identity is its value.  \n* An object's identity is the value of its schema-designated identity field.  \n* A composite identity uses the schema-defined canonical projection to one string.  \n* A set of objects without a defined identity rule is a schema error and fails closed.\n\nNormalize a set in this order:\n\n1. Project each element to its canonical identity without trimming, case conversion, locale transformation, or other value change.  \n2. If one identity repeats with byte-identical elements, retain one element.  \n3. If one identity repeats with different element values, fail closed and identify the first divergent field.  \n4. Sort the remaining elements in strict ASCII ascending identity order.\n\nProducers MUST write the normalized order; validators reject duplicates, conflicts, and out-of-order sets.\n\nFor Channels, the identity is `channel_id = \"<low>-<high>\"`: each Gate is zero-padded to `01..64`, and the lower Gate is first. Canonical examples are `07-31`, `10-57`, `20-57`, and `34-57`.\n\n### **Acceptance hints**\n\n`ARR_SET_IDENTITY_DECLARED_OK`, `ARR_SET_NO_DUPLICATES_OK`, `ARR_SET_NO_CONFLICTS_OK`, `ARR_SET_ASCII_SORT_OK`, `ARR_SET_PROJECTION_CANON_OK`.\n\n## **4.3 Locale & determinism pins**\n\nEvery pack-file or manifest generation and verification step MUST use `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, and `TZ=UTC`.\n\nGeneration MUST NOT depend on:\n\n* locale-sensitive collation, case folding, or string comparison;  \n* wall-clock reads or time-derived values;  \n* randomness, seed-dependent libraries, memory addresses, unordered iteration, or other process-specific state; or  \n* floating-point arithmetic or floating-point output.\n\nA required timestamp such as `built_at_utc` MUST be supplied by governed release or CI metadata and MUST NOT be sampled during serialization. It must not influence any artifact except the field that owns it.\n\nTwo runs over identical declared inputs and code MUST produce byte-identical pack files and manifest bytes. Checks MUST fail closed on a missing environment pin, nondeterministic output, wall-clock or randomness dependency, float emission, or any §4.1 or §4.2 violation.\n\n### **Acceptance hints**\n\n`ENV_LC_ALL_C_OK`, `NO_WALL_CLOCK_OK`, `NO_RANDOMNESS_OK`, `NO_FLOATS_IN_GEN_OK`, `TWO_RUN_IDENTITY_OK`, `DET_SERIALIZER_OK`, `JSON_CANONICAL_CHECK_OK`.\n\n# **5\\. It MUST NOT refresh or compare historical checked-in release evidence as a current-equality predicate. |\n| `ci/checks/check_release_identity.sh` | Current release-identity gate over the canonical manifest and its declared member bytes. |\n| `tools/evidence/build_release_attestation.py --output <external-empty-directory> --require-clean` | Creates current release derivatives outside the source repository after the exact candidate is committed and clean. |\n| `tools/evidence/build_release_attestation.py --verify <external-directory> --require-clean` | Verifies the external attestation against the unchanged clean candidate. |\n| `schemas/hde_release_attestation.v1.json` | Successful external attestation schema. |\n| `schemas/hde_release_attestation_failure.v1.json` | External attestation failure schema. |\n\nCurrent validation MUST operate on `catalog/manifest.json` and its declared member bytes. The tracked source MUST NOT be mutated to incorporate a hosted-CI fact or current external derivative.\n\nFor a Magic-10 current-release claim, the external `hde.release_attestation.v1` MUST validate with `source_commit_exact: true`, `validation_result: \"PASS\"`, `release_id == manifest_sha256`, `release_admission: \"PR06R_B_FINAL_PASS\"`, and `pipeline_stop: null`. It MUST NOT be copied into the repository, added to `catalog/manifest.json`, added to the Human Evidence Index or Machine Evidence Mirror, or used as a `release_id` input.\n\nFor purposes of a current Magic-10 release claim, these checked-in HDE-EPIC022 surfaces remain frozen historical captures:\n\n* `artifacts/math/freeze_pack_manifest.json`;  \n* `artifacts/math/release_id.txt`;  \n* `artifacts/math/release_id_recompute.log`;  \n* `artifacts/math/checksums_audit.log`;  \n* `artifacts/math/manifest_snapshot.json`;  \n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.json`;  \n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256`;  \n* `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`; and  \n* `artifacts/bodygraph/release_bindings.json`.\n\nThey MUST NOT be regenerated, rewritten, relabeled, or compared with the current manifest to manufacture current equality or current attestation. Static presence or a historical PASS line proves only historical capture.\n\n`RELEASE_ID_RECOMPUTE_OK` remains a historical EPIC022 label.
