Interfaces to Other Specs (titles-only) \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nThis section routes governed truth by exact document title. It does not restate another specification's contract and does not include version numbers.\n\n## **7.1 Math (by title)**\n\nReference: HDE-Math-Spec.\n\nHDE-Math-Spec owns scoring, thresholds, deterministic preimage and idempotence rules, arithmetic, weighting, tie-breaking, and precedence.\n\n## **7.2 Governance/CLI (by title)**\n\nReferences: HDE-Governance; HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref.\n\nThese documents own public success and error shapes, headers and conditional delivery, CLI and vendor request shaping, typed field mapping, and operational log policy.\n\n## **7.3 Architecture (by title)**\n\nReference: HDE Architecture.\n\nHDE Architecture owns system boundaries, single homes, component responsibilities, and the contract-free architecture overview.\n\n# **8\\. CI & Evidence \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nContract posture: required but not yet repo-conformant.\n\n## **8.1 Catalog schema and closed-domain validation \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n### **Ownership**\n\nSource bytes are owned by the catalog paths named in §2. Structural topology shapes are owned by `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json` and `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json`. Executable cross-catalog, Magic-10, manifest, and alias validation is owned by `engine/config/registry_loader.py`. Tests verify those owners; tests are not alternate catalog authorities.\n\n### **Current executable and declarative surfaces**\n\n* `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json` — exact object/row keys, 64 rows, gate range `1..64`, and the nine-center enum using machine IDs `g` and `ego`.  \n* `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json` — exact object/row keys, 36 rows, current field types/enums, and uniqueness for `domains` and `flags`.  \n* `engine/config/registry_loader.py` — JSON parsing, duplicate gate/channel refusal, channel-ID/gate-pair agreement, referenced gate/center membership, frozen Magic-10 order, caps key coverage and basic shape, subset-only seed keys and basic row shape, manifest parsing, and fail-closed alias policy.  \n* `tests/config/test_alias_policy_enforcement.py` and `tests/config/test_config_loader_unknown_ids_fail_closed.py` — current loader regression coverage within the default `pytest.ini` discovery scope.\n\n### **Required validation contract**\n\nA conforming topology change MUST first validate against both current schemas as applicable, then pass the hardened loader. The combined checks MUST reject malformed JSON, missing or additional properties, wrong types or enums, wrong cardinality, duplicate identities, gates outside `1..64`, noncanonical Channel identity, unknown gate/center references, Magic-10 order or caps drift, malformed caps/seed rows, seed keys outside the Magic-10 set, malformed or unsafe manifest paths/structure, and aliases outside the explicit allow-list policy.\n\n`catalog/magic10_caps.json` MUST have exact rows and current integer bounds `0..100`. Present `catalog/magic10_seeds.json` rows MUST have exact keys, valid timestamp shape, and lowercase-64-hex checksum shape. Viewer preferences MUST reject extra top-level keys and booleans/non-integers as weights. Authorities, Profiles, and Presets are excluded until a Doc-Delta adds verified paths, schemas or validators, and consumers.\n\nA failure MUST make the invoking workflow fail. This section defines ownership and behavior, not a GitHub Actions job name. No `catalog_*` workflow/job name is asserted.\n\n### **Current-to-required gaps**\n\nAt the pinned repository baseline:\n\n* `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json` and `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json` declare JSON Schema 2020-12 and their exact stable repository-path `$id` values;  \n* the loader enforces the exact 64-Gate and 36-Channel rosters;  \n* Channel endpoints are distinct and agree with the canonical min-first Channel ID;  \n* declared Channel centers are checked against the Centers projected from the Gate catalog;  \n* the frozen Magic-10 order, caps key coverage, input order, integer bounds, and allowed shapes are checked; and  \n* manifest parsing rejects malformed structure, unsafe paths, duplicates, out-of-order paths, and other fail-closed identity defects.\n\nThe former `$id`, distinct-endpoint, and Gate-derived-center omissions are not current gaps.\n\nThe Magic-10 v1 contract creates these remaining schema and loader obligations:\n\n* revise `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json` so `substream` is non-null and exactly one of `knowing`, `logic`, `sensing`, `ego`, `defense`, `centering`, or `integration`;  \n* add and enforce `schemas/magic10_mechanics_v1.schema.json` for `magic10_mechanics_config.v1`;  \n* add and enforce `schemas/magic10_result_v1.schema.json` for `magic10_result.v1`;  \n* add and enforce `schemas/magic10_compat_result_v1.schema.json` for `magic10_compat_result.v1`; and  \n* make the loader validate and hash-bind exactly one active `catalog/magic10_mechanics_v1.json` against Channels, categories, caps, thresholds, and the current manifest.\n\nThe required evidence-output names remain:\n\n* `artifacts/catalog/catalog_schema_validation.log`; and  \n* `artifacts/catalog/domain_closure_report.log`.\n\nTheir names are requirements, not proof that they exist or pass. Do not claim workflow wiring, schema conformance, or PASS until the applicable files and checks are generated, validated, indexed, mirrored, and path-proved.\n\n### **Acceptance hints (names-only)**\n\n`CATALOG_SCHEMA_OK`, `CATALOG_NO_ADDITIONAL_PROPS_OK`, `CATALOG_NO_UNKNOWN_KEYS_OK`, `CATALOG_DOMAIN_CLOSED_OK`, `SCHEMA_HYGIENE_OK`, `SCHEMA_ID_STABLE_OK`, `MANIFEST_PATH_SAFE_OK`, `EVIDENCE_INDEX_UPDATED_OK`, `EVIDENCE_INDEX_MIRROR_OK`.\n\n## **8.2 Topology, set, canonical-byte, and projection integrity \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n### **Ownership**\n\nThis section owns integrity beyond §8.1 shape and domain closure: topology coherence, arrays-as-sets normalization, exact governed bytes, and deterministic derived projections. It does not redefine source catalogs.\n\n### **Current surfaces**\n\n* `tools/generate_registry_report.py` — sole producer of `artifacts/registry/registry_report.json`; loads through the current registry loader, requires closed rails, hashes its consumed catalog bytes, and emits canonical JSON.  \n* `tests/config/test_registry_report_determinism.py` — current registry-report two-run coverage in the default `pytest.ini` discovery scope.  \n* `tests/compare/test_arrays_as_sets.py` and `tools/evidence/generate_arrays_as_sets_report.py` — explicit-target normalization proof for Channel `centers` and `domains`; `tests/compare` is not in default `pytest.ini` discovery.\n\n### **Required integrity contract**\n\nAfter §8.1 passes, integrity validation MUST prove all of the following:\n\n* every Channel has two distinct Gates;  \n* its `NN-NN` identity is the zero-padded min-first projection of those Gates;  \n* its declared center set is exactly the set derived from the two Gate rows, and the two centers are distinct;  \n* arrays declared as sets are deduplicated and deterministically sorted before storage, comparison, and emission;  \n* every governed JSON file required by §4 already equals the canonical serializer’s bytes on disk, including exactly one trailing LF;  \n* registry-report input paths, counts, and SHA-256 values match current source bytes;  \n* the report’s Channel IDs, Gate-center map, center/domain sets, domain counts, Magic-10 projection, and alias policy equal a fresh loader-derived projection; and  \n* two regenerations from identical governed inputs are byte-identical.\n\nManifest completeness and `release_id` remain owned by §§5–6. Human Index, Machine Mirror, and path-proof coherence remain owned by §§8.3 and 8.6. A failure MUST make the invoking workflow fail. This section does not assign CI job names and MUST NOT present `integrity_topology`, `integrity_arrays_as_sets`, or `integrity_canonicalization_compare` as existing workflow/job names.\n\n### **Current-to-required gaps**\n\nAt the pinned repository baseline:\n\n* runtime loading rejects duplicate or non-distinct Channel endpoints;  \n* Channel IDs are checked against their ascending Gate pairs;  \n* declared Channel centers are checked against the exact set projected from the Gate catalog;  \n* `catalog/gates_v1.json`, `catalog/channels_v1.json`, `catalog/magic10_caps.json`, and `catalog/magic10_seeds.json` are canonical JSON with exactly one final LF; and  \n* `artifacts/canonical/arrays_as_sets_report.log` is promoted under a matching Human Evidence Index row, Machine Evidence Mirror row, and sibling path proof.\n\nThe earlier endpoint, center-projection, catalog-byte, and unindexed arrays-as-sets defects are not current gaps.\n\nMagic-10 v1 still requires one coherent integrity cut covering the corrected scoring-bound Channel classifications, the authoritative mechanics configuration, its three new owning schemas, exact source hashes, manifest membership, generated configuration identity, and deterministic golden identity. Those future bytes MUST satisfy the canonical, declared-set, topology, loader, manifest, and release rules in this document before conformance is claimed.\n\nThese names remain reserved target outputs unless and until their owning checks generate and govern them:\n\n* `artifacts/topology/topology_coherence_report.log`; and  \n* `audit/gates/json_gate/canonical/json_gate_compare_log.ndjson`.\n\nDo not treat the current promoted arrays-as-sets report, static file presence, or canonical source bytes as proof of the unimplemented Magic-10 v1 contract or whole-release PASS.\n\n### **Acceptance hints (names-only)**\n\n`TOPOLOGY_NO_ORPHANS_OK`, `TOPOLOGY_CHANNEL_DEGREE_2_OK`, `TOPOLOGY_GATE_CENTER_OK`, `TOPOLOGY_CENTER_MULTIPLICITY_OK`, `ARR_SET_NO_CONFLICTS_OK`, `ARR_SET_ASCII_SORT_OK`, `FILE_EQ_CANON_BYTES_OK`, `TWO_RUN_IDENTITY_OK`, `ENV_LC_ALL_C_OK`.\n\n## **8.3 Machine Evidence Index — JSONL mirror (records-only) \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n### **Single home and path**\n\n#### **Path (fixed)**\n\n* artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl (there must be exactly one mirror file in the repo).\n\nThe mirror has a governed checksum sidecar at `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl.sha256`. The mirror file and its checksum sidecar MUST each have a sibling `.path_proof.txt` transcript (co-located), including `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl.path_proof.txt` and `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl.sha256.path_proof.txt`.\n\n#### **Governed locations only.**\n\nEvery evidence file referenced by the mirror MUST live under governed repo paths (for example, artifacts/, docs/). Transient generator paths (scratch/temp) are disallowed; mirror entries pointing to non-governed paths fail CI.\n\n#### **Evidence-path safety invariants (mirror discovered\\_physical\\_path).**\n\nFor every mirror record:\n\n* `discovered_physical_path` MUST be a repo-relative path (no absolute paths).  \n* `discovered_physical_path` MUST NOT contain parent-directory segments (`..`) and MUST NOT escape the repository root after normalization and resolution.  \n* `discovered_physical_path` MUST resolve to an existing file at validation time.  \n* Mirror entries that violate these invariants MUST fail CI.\n\nImplementation notes (titles-only; mechanics live outside PF12).\n\n* Evidence path validation: `tools/evidence/validate_evidence_paths.py`  \n* Final-LF endings check wrapper: `tools/evidence/check_lf_endings.py`\n\n#### **Tracked files (no .gitignore for governed artifacts).**\n\nGoverned evidence artifacts and their sibling path-proof transcripts (\\\\.path\\_proof.txt) MUST NOT be ignored by .gitignore. Governed locations are expected to be tracked; using .gitignore to hide governed artifacts or their path-proofs is invalid and should be treated as a QA failure.\n\n### **Format (canonical JSONL)**\n\nOne JSON object per line.\n\nCanonical JSON per §4 for each line:\n\n* UTF-8 (no BOM).  \n* Sorted keys.  \n* Compact separators.  \n* Exactly one trailing \\\\n per line.  \n* No blank lines; no trailing spaces.  \n* Unknown keys are rejected (CI-blocking).\n\n### **Minimum record schema (reject unknown keys)**\n\nEach Mirror record MUST contain the following required core keys. Optional keys are limited to the extension below; all other keys are rejected:\n\n* artifact\\_key — string.  \n* role — string. The Machine Mirror self-record MUST use self\\_record.  \n* sha256 — lowercase 64-hex string.  \n* size\\_bytes — non-negative integer.  \n* produced\\_at\\_utc — UTC ISO-8601 string.  \n* discovered\\_physical\\_path — governed repo-relative path.  \n* proof\\_anchor — governed repo-relative sibling path-proof path.\n\n### **Bundle-aware extension (evidence bundles, manifests, and change-container metadata)**\n\nThe minimum record schema above remains normative for all Mirror records. This section extends it to cover bundle artifacts, their manifests, and Epic or CRD metadata without changing the core field set or canonical JSONL discipline.\n\n#### **Allowed top-level keys and unknown-key rejection**\n\nThe Mirror still rejects unknown keys. The only allowed top-level keys for any record are:\n\nCore keys (required for every record):\n\n* artifact\\_key  \n* role  \n* sha256  \n* size\\_bytes  \n* produced\\_at\\_utc  \n* discovered\\_physical\\_path  \n* proof\\_anchor\n\nMetadata keys (optional; may appear on any record):\n\n* epic\\_id — a short identifier for the owning Epic (for example, \"HDE-EPIC020\"), bound to its actual approved Epic Specification/Implementation Plan and PF09 lineage under §8.18; HDE-Phased Epics remains historical context.  \n* crd\\_id — the stable identifier for the owning CRD, bound to its controlled source and approved class-specific Specification/Implementation Plan lineage under §8.18; historical PF30 references remain historical only.  \n* record\\_type — a short type label for this record (for example, \"epic020\\_bundle\" or \"epic020\\_bundle\\_manifest\"); names are governed by local schemas and tests.  \n* schema\\_version — a version string for the record schema (for example, \"1.0\").  \n* notes — free-form, names-only commentary to aid audits; contents are out of scope for PF12 beyond canonical JSON constraints.  \n* tokens — an optional non-empty array-as-set of acceptance-token names. Values MUST be deduplicated and ASCII-sorted. For HDE-EPIC020 records, every value MUST be drawn from the EPIC020 acceptance roster.\n\nA record MAY contain epic\\_id or crd\\_id, but MUST NOT contain both. Existing historical and active epic records retain epic\\_id and MUST NOT be migrated merely to add CRD compatibility.\n\nA selected family that uses optional crd\\_id metadata MUST have compatible schema/serializer/validator support, enforce epic\\_id/crd\\_id mutual exclusion, and preserve valid historical and active Epic records. This optional-field contract does not require those fields on every CRD row or make broad schema migration a prerequisite to ordinary local QA. The bounded §8.17.6 publisher emits only its approved existing row fields and omits unapproved identity/status metadata.\n\nBundle records use only the required core keys plus applicable metadata keys above. No additional bundle-specific top-level keys are allowed.\n\n#### **Bundle artifacts and manifests**\n\nA bundle artifact is a textual JSON or JSONL file that groups multiple logical evidence members. Its Mirror record’s artifact\\_key identifies the governed bundle family, and discovered\\_physical\\_path points to the bundle file.\n\nA bundle manifest enumerates the bundle’s members and is a separate governed artifact with its own Mirror record, artifact\\_key, and discovered\\_physical\\_path.\n\nFor selected bundle-based families, the Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror track the bundle file and its manifest instead of listing every internal member as a separate row. Internal member content is addressed by the manifest.\n\n#### **EPIC-scale example (EPIC020 Candidate 1 bundles)**\n\nEPIC020 Candidate 1 evidence bundles follow this pattern:\n\n* Each EPIC020 bundle and manifest has a Mirror record whose artifact\\_key is the relevant EPIC020 token (for example, \"EPIC020.D1.HTTP\\_COMPAT\\_MALFORMED\\_JSON\" or CLI\\_SHOWCOMPAT\\_CANON\\_OK).  \n* record\\_type is \"epic020\\_bundle\" for bundle artifacts and \"epic020\\_bundle\\_manifest\" for manifests.  \n* epic\\_id is \"HDE-EPIC020\".  \n* tokens is a non-empty array of token names tied to the EPIC020 acceptance roster; schema and ownership of token names live in HDE-Governance and Glow QA Guide.\n\nOther epics or CRDs may introduce similar bundle and manifest patterns with different record\\_type values and the applicable epic\\_id or crd\\_id value only under their owning approved contract. PF12 remains the single home for the allowed key set and canonical JSONL constraints. Change-container authority follows the approved class-specific Specification and class-bound Implementation Plan under §8.18, with titles-only routing to HDE-Governance, Change Process Guide, and Glow QA Guide; HDE-Phased Epics and HDE CRD Records remain historical/reference homes.\n\n#### **Path-proof semantics for bundles**\n\nEach bundle artifact and its manifest MUST have governed sibling path-proof transcripts (\\\\.path\\_proof.txt and \\\\.path\\_proof.txt) stored alongside each file, whose path, sha256, and size\\_bytes match the bundle/manifest file and the corresponding Mirror record values.\n\nFor bundle-based families, “per-artifact path proofs” in PF12 are interpreted as “per governed artifact,” where a governed artifact may be either:\n\n* a single artifact file (e.g., a log or JSON snapshot), or  \n* a bundle artifact or bundle manifest file.\n\nThis extension does not introduce hash-only or index-only families. Any future move toward hash-only evidence without on-disk member payloads remains a Future-Promotion and requires an explicit reconciliation Doc-Delta.\n\nAll other Mirror rules remain unchanged: canonical JSONL per §4, single mirror file at artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl, sort-before-write by (artifact\\_key, discovered\\_physical\\_path), uniqueness of that pair, strict governed-paths rule, and 1:1 parity with the Human Evidence Index.\n\n### **Self-record semantics (index.machine\\_mirror)**\n\nThe mirror MUST contain exactly one self-record with:\n\n* artifact\\_key equal to `index.machine_mirror`;  \n* role equal to `self_record`;  \n* discovered\\_physical\\_path equal to `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`; and  \n* proof\\_anchor equal to `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl.path_proof.txt`.\n\nFor this self-record:\n\n* sha256 MUST equal the SHA-256 digest of the canonical JSONL body excluding the self-record line.  \n* size\\_bytes MUST equal the byte length of the complete mirror file including the self-record line.\n\nThe sibling path-proof MUST record:\n\n* path equal to `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`;  \n* sha256 equal to the SHA-256 digest of the complete mirror file;  \n* size\\_bytes equal to the complete mirror byte length; and  \n* mirror\\_body\\_sha256 equal to the self-record’s sha256.\n\nThe path-proof sha256 therefore differs from the self-record sha256: the former proves the complete file, while the latter proves the non-self body.\n\nAll non-self records continue to bind sha256 and size\\_bytes to the referenced artifact at discovered\\_physical\\_path, with matching sibling path-proofs.\n\n### **Field order and write discipline (merge-blocking)**\n\nEvery record MUST serialize all present keys in ASCII ascending order. For a record containing only the required core keys, the order is exactly: artifact\\_key, discovered\\_physical\\_path, produced\\_at\\_utc, proof\\_anchor, role, sha256, size\\_bytes. Optional metadata keys appear at their ASCII-sorted positions.\n\nSort-before-write by the tuple (artifact\\_key, discovered\\_physical\\_path).\n\nUniqueness: the pair (artifact\\_key, discovered\\_physical\\_path) is unique; duplicates fail CI.\n\nSingle mirror file: only one artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl may exist in the repo.\n\n### **produced\\_at\\_utc vs mtime\\_utc**\n\nproduced\\_at\\_utc records when the evidence was logically produced. It is part of the Mirror record and sibling path-proof and is the primary evidence-ordering timestamp.\n\nmtime\\_utc is capture-time provenance stored in the sibling path-proof. A newly produced proof may seed it from the artifact’s observed filesystem modification time. A later clone, cache restore, or CI checkout MUST NOT compare it with that checkout’s local filesystem mtime.\n\nBoth timestamps MUST use the governed UTC shape. Their values provide provenance context and do not replace path, hash, size, canonical-field, or companion-linkage integrity.\n\n### **Path-proof transcript schema (governed artifacts)**\n\nNaming (MUST). The sibling path-proof transcript for a governed artifact MUST be named \\\\.path\\_proof.txt, where \\\\ includes the artifact’s full filename including extension. Example: audit/gates/determinism/env\\_pins.log → audit/gates/determinism/env\\_pins.log.path\\_proof.txt (not env\\_pins.path\\_proof.txt).\n\nFor every governed artifact in §8.6, the path-proof transcript MUST be a co-located sibling file named \\\\.path\\_proof.txt. It MUST describe exactly one artifact and follow a stable, line-oriented schema.\n\n#### **Required fields (exactly one record per file)**\n\nEach path-proof MUST contain exactly one record for the artifact it describes, with the following required fields:\n\n* path — repo-relative path to the artifact (for example artifacts/engine/order/channels\\_sorted.snapshot.json).  \n* sha256 — lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 digest of the artifact’s canonical bytes.  \n* size\\_bytes — non-negative integer byte length of the artifact’s canonical bytes.  \n* mtime\\_utc — UTC ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g. YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ) recording capture-time provenance (see “mtime\\_utc semantics” below).  \n* produced\\_at\\_utc — UTC ISO-8601 time when the evidence for this artifact was logically produced.\n\nThese fields MUST appear exactly once per file; path-proofs MUST NOT contain multiple or conflicting sha256/size\\_bytes pairs, nor multiple mtime\\_utc or produced\\_at\\_utc values for the same artifact.\n\n#### **Optional fields**\n\nPath-proof transcripts MAY include additional informational fields beyond the required set above, but those fields:\n\n* MUST NOT change acceptance semantics, and  \n* MUST NOT conflict with the required record for path, sha256, size\\_bytes, mtime\\_utc, or produced\\_at\\_utc.\n\nThe authoritative truth remains the match between:\n\n* the artifact’s canonical bytes,  \n* the mirror record’s sha256 and size\\_bytes, and  \n* the path-proof’s single sha256/size\\_bytes triple for that artifact.\n\n#### **Relationship to proof\\_anchor**\n\nEach mirror record’s proof\\_anchor field MUST equal the path to the corresponding .path\\_proof.txt for that artifact.\n\nCI MUST verify that:\n\n* the file referenced by proof\\_anchor exists under governed paths,  \n* the transcript’s path field matches the mirror’s discovered\\_physical\\_path,  \n* its sha256/size\\_bytes match the mirror record’s sha256/size\\_bytes, and  \n* there are no duplicate or conflicting sha256/size\\_bytes entries within the path-proof.\n\nFailure of any of these conditions is a hard error under the mirror/index tokens declared in §8.3 and §0.2.\n\n### **mtime\\_utc semantics (normative)**\n\n#### **Capture-time provenance**\n\nmtime\\_utc records the artifact filesystem modification time observed when the path-proof is first produced or materially refreshed. It MUST use `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` with no fractional seconds.\n\nA later clone, cache restore, archive extraction, or CI checkout MUST NOT compare mtime\\_utc with clone-local `stat().st_mtime`. Git does not preserve that metadata. An unchanged valid proof MUST NOT be rewritten or re-timestamped solely to match local filesystem metadata.\n\n#### **Interaction with produced\\_at\\_utc**\n\nproduced\\_at\\_utc records when the evidence was logically produced. It MUST use the same governed UTC shape. Family-specific generated\\_at\\_utc or non-backdating rules remain additive where expressly defined.\n\n#### **Integrity semantics**\n\nThe primary integrity proof is the coherent match among:\n\n* the governed repo-relative path;  \n* the artifact’s canonical bytes;  \n* sha256 and size\\_bytes in the Machine Mirror;  \n* sha256 and size\\_bytes in the sibling path-proof;  \n* the required canonical fields; and  \n* the proof\\_anchor and companion linkage.\n\nmtime\\_utc and produced\\_at\\_utc provide provenance context; they do not replace those integrity bindings.\n\n#### **Alignment with tools and QA**\n\nEvidence tooling and CI MUST:\n\n* recompute sha256 and size\\_bytes from canonical artifact bytes;  \n* preserve valid existing timestamps when the governed artifact and proof fields are unchanged;  \n* seed a newly produced mtime\\_utc from the observed filesystem time;  \n* validate UTC shape, path, hash, size, required fields, and companion linkage; and  \n* never use later-checkout filesystem metadata as evidence input.\n\nTests MUST enforce these same portable semantics.\n\n#### **Change control**\n\nAny change to mtime\\_utc or produced\\_at\\_utc semantics requires:\n\n* a PF12 Doc-Delta (§9);  \n* synchronized updates to PF19 and PF10; and  \n* synchronized updates to the evidence tooling and tests.\n\n### **Join to the human index (parity, proofs, same-PR rule)**\n\n#### **1:1 parity.**\n\nEvery §8.6 Evidence Index entry has exactly one mirror record, and every mirror record has a corresponding human entry:\n\n* artifact\\_key equals the Human Index artifact\\_key.  \n* discovered\\_physical\\_path equals the Human Index discovered\\_physical\\_path.\n\n#### **Path-proofs.**\n\nEach artifact’s directory contains a stored path-proof (for example, path\\_proof.txt with a stat transcript). The mirror record’s proof\\_anchor must exactly match the stored path-proof for that artifact.\n\n#### **Same-PR rule.**\n\nFor every governed artifact in §8.6, any change to the artifact MUST update, in the same PR:\n\n* The artifact bytes on disk under a governed path.  \n* Its sibling \\\\.path\\_proof.txt path-proof transcript (the proof\\_anchor target).  \n* The corresponding machine mirror record in artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl.  \n* The Human Evidence Index entry in docs/evidence/INDEX.json and its hash sentinel docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256.\n\nMirror or index entries that refer to non-existent artifacts or stale path-proofs are invalid and must be corrected, not ignored.\n\n#### **Troubleshooting (common failure mode): governed artifact drift**\n\nA governed artifact is considered drifted when any of the following disagree:\n\n* the artifact’s on-disk bytes  \n* its sibling \\*.path\\_proof.txt (sha256 and size\\_bytes)  \n* the corresponding Machine Mirror record (sha256 and size\\_bytes for the same discovered\\_physical\\_path)\n\nThis is a hard evidence integrity failure. Do not hand-edit proofs or mirror records to “make the check pass”.\n\nCorrect remediation (single writer):\n\nRe-generate the evidence skeleton using the canonical evidence tooling so all three surfaces realign:\n\n* Ensure docs/evidence/INDEX.json reflects the intended titles and paths.  \n* Run tools/evidence/update\\_evidence\\_index.py in write mode to regenerate:  \n  * docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256  \n  * artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl  \n  * all governed \\*.path\\_proof.txt transcripts  \n* Re-run the tool in \\--check mode and fix any remaining mismatches before merge.\n\n### **Determinism**\n\nAll checks run with LC\\_ALL=C, LANG=C, TZ=UTC.\n\nJSONL records are canonical and LF-terminated (exactly one \\\\n per record).\n\n### **Header snapshots in artifacts (normative)**\n\nFor artifacts that capture headers, header names MUST be lower-case and values MUST be verbatim; exact checks apply to values.\n\n#### **Capture hygiene (normative).**\n\nHeader snapshot artifacts MUST contain header lines only.\n\nTool warnings or stderr output (for example, curl warnings) MUST NOT be mixed into header snapshot bytes.\n\nIf the capture command can emit warnings, capture stderr separately (for example, to a sibling \\*.stderr.txt or a step log) or filter non-header lines before writing the governed artifact.\n\nWire casing may differ and is validated by transport owners.\n\nAcceptance hint (names-only): SNAPSHOT\\_HEADER\\_LOWERCASE\\_OK.\n\n### **Refusal proofs (policy note)**\n\nRefusal proofs are error/ops evidence (not JSON success). They must:\n\n* Not set ETag, Vary, or compression headers.  \n* Use Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8.\n\nThe refusal log allow-list for JSON body fields is exactly:\n\n* {at, route, status, duration\\_ms, idempotence\\_hash, release\\_id}\n\nRecords with any additional fields fail policy checks.\n\nRate-limit (429) evidence uses a different allow-list and is governed by HDE-Governance. Do not mix refusal and 429 fields in the mirror.\n\n### **Refresh sequence (normative)**\n\nWhen governed evidence artifacts change, the canonical refresh sequence is:\n\n* Update docs/evidence/INDEX.json with the new or changed titles and paths.  \n* Run python tools/evidence/update\\_evidence\\_index.py in write mode to regenerate:  \n  * docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256  \n  * artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl  \n  * all governed \\*.path\\_proof.txt transcripts  \n* Run the mirror schema/shape check job (canonical CI invocation: ci/checks/check\\_mirror\\_schema.sh artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl) and fix any discrepancies before merge.\n\n#### **Operator note (invocation; avoid bash drift).**\n\nci/checks/check\\_mirror\\_schema.sh is a Python entrypoint (script file with a Python shebang) and CI invokes it directly. When an acceptance artifact or runbook needs an explicit command, the canonical invocation is:\n\n* ci/checks/check\\_mirror\\_schema.sh artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl\n\nAcceptance artifacts may list either:\n\n* the script path (ci/checks/check\\_mirror\\_schema.sh) as a tool reference, or  \n* the explicit direct command above as an invocation.\n\nbash ci/checks/check\\_mirror\\_schema.sh is invalid and MUST NOT appear in approved acceptance artifacts or operator instructions.\n\nProcess and PR workflow (who runs which command and when) remains single-homed in Change Process Guide; this section pins file-level ordering and artifacts that MUST be updated together.\n\n### **Artifacts with generated\\_at\\_utc (provenance discipline, including sampler and Engine Core evidence)**\n\nSome governed artifacts (for example, sampler evidence artifacts under artifacts/sampler/\\*\\* and Engine Core evidence artifacts under artifacts/core/\\*\\*) include a generated\\_at\\_utc field in their own JSON payloads. For these artifact families, provenance discipline tightens the relationship between the payload timestamp and the evidence timestamps recorded in the Machine Mirror and path-proofs.\n\n#### **Normative rules (in addition to the general rules in this section)**\n\nWhen an artifact carries a generated\\_at\\_utc field in its payload, the evidence tooling MUST treat that field as the artifact’s self-reported generation time for the current refresh and enforce all of the following:\n\n* produced\\_at\\_utc in the Machine Evidence Mirror record for that artifact MUST NOT be earlier than the artifact’s generated\\_at\\_utc value. Backdating Mirror produced\\_at\\_utc relative to generated\\_at\\_utc is not allowed.  \n* produced\\_at\\_utc in the Machine Evidence Mirror record and produced\\_at\\_utc in the artifact’s path-proof transcript MUST be identical strings (same UTC ISO-8601 representation). Mirror and path-proof timestamps MUST stay in lockstep for a given artifact.  \n* mtime\\_utc in the path-proof remains capture-time provenance and MUST have valid UTC shape. It is not compared with a later checkout’s filesystem mtime. mtime\\_utc may be earlier than generated\\_at\\_utc, but the governed path, sha256, size\\_bytes, canonical fields, and companion linkage MUST still match.\n\nFor governed families that include both generated\\_at\\_utc and produced\\_at\\_utc, provenance correctness for a refresh requires:\n\n* Mirror produced\\_at\\_utc to be no earlier than payload generated\\_at\\_utc; and  \n* path-proof produced\\_at\\_utc to match Mirror produced\\_at\\_utc exactly.\n\nIntegrity gates continue to rely primarily on governed-path, sha256, size\\_bytes, canonical-field, and companion-linkage equality. Timestamp checks are additive: valid UTC shape, Mirror/path-proof produced\\_at\\_utc equality, and the explicit non-backdating rule relative to payload generated\\_at\\_utc.\n\n#### **Example — sampler and Engine Core evidence fixes (HDE-EPIC019)**\n\nIn earlier EPIC019 work, sampler Mirror records and path-proofs for sampler\\_pool\\_snapshots, sampler\\_two\\_run\\_logs, sampler\\_abba\\_logs, sampler\\_diversity\\_artifacts, and sampler\\_seed\\_replay\\_logs carried produced\\_at\\_utc values copied from an older skeleton baseline even after the artifacts themselves were regenerated with later generated\\_at\\_utc timestamps. Engine Core evidence families added in PR7 (engine\\_core\\_purity\\_report, engine\\_core\\_two\\_run\\_logs, engine\\_core\\_abba\\_logs, engine\\_core\\_json\\_compare\\_logs) were wired with generated\\_at\\_utc and closed-rails env metadata from the start.\n\nThe EPIC019 bugfix refreshed Mirror records and path-proofs so that:\n\n* sampler artifacts under artifacts/sampler/\\*\\* and Engine Core artifacts under artifacts/core/\\*\\* retain canonical bytes (sha256 and size\\_bytes unchanged when content is unchanged)  \n* their payload generated\\_at\\_utc values reflect the actual regeneration time for the latest evidence run, and  \n* produced\\_at\\_utc in both Mirror and path-proofs is updated to the later refresh time, satisfying the non-backdating rule above and restoring consistency between payload generation timestamps and evidence timestamps for all families that carry generated\\_at\\_utc.\n\n#### **Tools and tests**\n\nEvidence tooling (for example, tools/evidence/update\\_evidence\\_index.py and any Engine Core/sampler-specific generators) and Mirror schema checks MUST implement these provenance rules whenever an artifact family introduces a payload-level generated\\_at\\_utc field.\n\nTests that exercise those families (for example, sampler evidence tests under tests/evidence/ and Engine Core evidence tests under tests/evidence/test\\_engine\\_core\\_evidence.py) SHOULD assert that:\n\n* produced\\_at\\_utc in Mirror and path-proofs matches for each artifact instance, and  \n* where generated\\_at\\_utc is present, Mirror produced\\_at\\_utc is not earlier than payload generated\\_at\\_utc.\n\n#### **Change control**\n\nAny change to the relationship between payload generated\\_at\\_utc and evidence produced\\_at\\_utc semantics is a normative change and MUST land with:\n\n* a PF12 Doc-Delta (§9),  \n* synchronized updates to the relevant Mechanics/QA specs that describe Engine Core and sampler evidence behavior, and  \n* synchronized changes to the evidence tools and tests that enforce these semantics before the change is considered accepted.\n\n### **8.3.1 Refusal proof (single-file canonical) \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n#### **Path (fixed)**\n\n`artifacts/proofs/ops_refusal_proof.txt`\n\nThe artifact contains a header block, exactly one blank line, and one LF-terminated canonical JSON refusal body.\n\nIndex it in both `docs/evidence/INDEX.json` and `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl` in the same PR. Its required sibling path-proof is `artifacts/proofs/ops_refusal_proof.txt.path_proof.txt`, and the Mirror proof\\_anchor MUST equal that exact path.\n\nPolicy and token semantics live in HDE-Governance.\n\n#### **File format (exact)**\n\n##### **Header block**\n\nOne header per line in the form `<lower-case-name>: <verbatim-value>`. No blank lines may occur inside the header block.\n\nRequired headers:\n\n* `cache-control: no-store`  \n* `content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8`\n\nForbidden headers: `etag`, `vary`, `content-encoding`.\n\nOther headers may appear only when permitted by the owning transport policy. Header order is preserved as captured.\n\n##### **Separator**\n\nExactly one blank line separates headers from the body.\n\n##### **Body**\n\nThe body is one deterministic, numeric-free typed-refusal JSON object serialized canonically under §4 and terminated by exactly one LF. Exact refusal-envelope semantics remain owned by HDE-Governance and HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref.\n\nThe refusal-log six-key allow-list applies to logs, not to this captured response body.\n\n#### **Mirror linkage**\n\nThe Mirror record uses artifact\\_key `ops.rails_refusal`, role `proof`, discovered\\_physical\\_path `artifacts/proofs/ops_refusal_proof.txt`, and proof\\_anchor `artifacts/proofs/ops_refusal_proof.txt.path_proof.txt`.\n\n#### **Validation checks (CI)**\n\n* Required headers are present and lower-case.  \n* Forbidden headers are absent.  \n* Exactly one blank line separates header block and body.  \n* Body is one canonical, numeric-free typed-refusal JSON object.  \n* File ends with exactly one LF.  \n* Checks run under `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, and `TZ=UTC`.\n\n#### **Example (illustrative)**\n\n```\ncache-control: no-store\ncontent-type: application/json; charset=utf-8\nx-rails-mode: closed\n\n{\"code\":\"rails_closed\",\"error\":\"rails remain closed\",\"ok\":false,\"schema\":\"rails_closed\"}\n```\n\n#### **Acceptance hints (names-only)**\n\nOPS\\_REFUSAL\\_FILE\\_FORMAT\\_OK OPS\\_REFUSAL\\_HEADERS\\_OK OPS\\_REFUSAL\\_BODY\\_OK OPS\\_REFUSAL\\_MIRROR\\_LINK\\_OK\n\n## **8.4 Reserved \\[Tracking\\]**\n\nNo recoverable or current normative §8.4 contract is asserted. The number is reserved so §8.6 onward retains stable identities and cross-references. Future use of §8.4 requires a Doc-Delta that identifies the owner, paths, schemas, producer, tests, evidence/indexing posture, migration impact, and every affected cross-reference. Reserved numbering is not evidence that missing prose exists.\n\n## **8.5 Registry report \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n### **Single home and identity**\n\nThe governed registry report lives at exactly `artifacts/registry/registry_report.json`.\n\nIts Human Evidence Index and Machine Mirror identity is `registry.registry_report`; its `record_type` is `registry_report`, its `schema_version` is `1.0`, and its Mirror role is `snapshot`. PF09 phase checklists consistently require this file to be canonical JSON, kept in sync, and mirrored.\n\n### **Producer and execution boundary**\n\n`tools/generate_registry_report.py` is the sole producer. Generation MUST pass through `engine/config/registry_loader.py`, MUST require closed rails, and MUST write canonical JSON. A hand-edited report is not authoritative.\n\n### **Input contract**\n\n`inputs.catalogs` describes only current producer inputs:\n\n* `channels_v1` — path, row count, and SHA-256 for `catalog/channels_v1.json`;  \n* `gates_v1` — path, row count, and SHA-256 for `catalog/gates_v1.json`;  \n* `magic10_order` — path, SHA-256, and ordered keys for `catalog/magic10.json`;  \n* `magic10_caps` — path and SHA-256 for `catalog/magic10_caps.json`; and  \n* `magic10_seeds` — path and SHA-256 for `catalog/magic10_seeds.json`.\n\nMagic-10 seeds are a validated subset of the Magic-10 domain. The report MUST NOT claim all ten seed entries unless a later source contract actually requires and supplies them.\n\n### **Output contract**\n\nThe top-level object contains exactly `schema`, `generated_at_utc`, `inputs`, `artifacts`, and `notes`, with `schema: \"registry_report.v1\"`. `artifacts.registry` contains:\n\n* `channel_ids` — canonical sorted primary Channel IDs;  \n* `gate_centers` — Gate-number strings mapped to machine center IDs;  \n* `centers` — the closed sorted center set;  \n* `domains` — the closed sorted domain set derived from Channel rows;  \n* `domain_counts` — deterministic counts derived from Channel-domain membership;  \n* `magic10` — ordered keys, caps, and currently present seed metadata; and  \n* `alias_policy` — explicit mode and sorted alias map.\n\nThe producer serializes with recursive sorted keys, compact separators, and exactly one final LF. `generated_at_utc` is deterministic: use `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` when supplied; otherwise retain the existing report timestamp; if neither exists, use the producer’s fixed epoch fallback. Two regenerations from identical inputs MUST be byte-identical.\n\n### **Indexing and companions**\n\nThe same change that modifies report bytes updates `docs/evidence/INDEX.json`, `artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`, and `artifacts/registry/registry_report.json.path_proof.txt`, together with the hash and size bound by those records. The current family has no separate `.sha256` sidecar requirement. Preserve the existing `registry.registry_report` identity rather than minting a second key.\n\n### **Boundary and nonclaims**\n\nThe report is a registry projection, not a release manifest, not a source catalog, and not proof of a standalone UMS schema. It does not cover narrative-pack members or `math/thresholds.json`. Current generation is deterministic but inherits unresolved §8.1–§8.2 validation gaps; report presence is not proof those validations ran. Because the current Freeze-Pack Manifest omits topology and narratives inputs, the report MUST NOT be cited as proof of release completeness.\n\n## **8.6 Evidence Index entries (titles/paths only) \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n### **8.6.1 Discipline**\n\nUpdate both the Human Index and the Machine Mirror in the same PR:\n\n* Human Index: docs/evidence/INDEX.json  \n* Machine Mirror: artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl\n\nGoverned path-proof transcripts (required). The Human Index and its hash sentinel MUST each have a sibling `.path_proof.txt` transcript:\n\n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.json.path_proof.txt`  \n* `docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256.path_proof.txt`\n\nMachine Mirror discipline:\n\n* Records-only JSONL  \n* Canonical JSONL  \n* Exactly one LF per record  \n* Unknown-key rejection  \n* ASCII field order  \n* Sort-before-write  \n* Single mirror file  \n* proof\\_anchor present and valid for every record\n\nProcess and CI posture:\n\n* Detailed PR/workflow process is defined in Change Process Guide (titles-only).  \n* Acceptance sentinel gating behavior is defined in PF12 front-matter and Governance (titles-only).\n\nExact-source evidence-path binding validation (MUST).\n\nWhen a current acceptance or completion record relies on a PF12-governed artifact family, its binding MUST be traceable, as applicable, through:\n\n* repository identity and the exact Git commit SHA;  \n* base, candidate or head, merge, and post-merge identities when a PR is used;  \n* the PR number and immutable review or conversation record when a PR is used;  \n* the workflow name, run identifier or URL, exact tested SHA, conclusion, and applicable check set;  \n* stable PF, ADR, epic, CRD, task, acceptance-criterion, test, schema, or artifact identifiers;  \n* the exact governed artifact path and SHA-256 digest where artifact integrity is material;  \n* every required manifest, Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, path proof, tool version, and configuration reference;  \n* the applicable decision-maker, decision scope, and decision time; and  \n* any exception or waiver identity, owner, scope, reason, and expiry.\n\nThe record MUST NOT duplicate information that GitHub or an existing governed artifact already records reliably. A PR, commit, workflow run, or governed artifact may carry the evidence directly; PF12 creates no replacement token database, universal evidence form, or new approval mechanism.\n\nRecord the actual execution source and target environment, source/plan/task versions, commands and effective secret-safe configuration, results, evidence references, actor and time, and material limitations. Distinguish the tested commit/environment from later evidence-storage, review, or merge identities. Bounded authorized QA/Ops execution may use available repository PF documents under `docs/pfcanon` when the executor lacks Drive access; record the actual copies and known limitations without requiring a fresh Drive comparison or synchronization certificate. This execution exception does not extend to readiness, planning, review, governance, or independent editing authority.\n\nCurrentness is substantive. Assess changed requirements, implementation/proof-producing surfaces, dependencies, and evidence validity before reusing a result. An unavailable SHA is not by itself a blocker when the actual sources and decisive proof remain adequate; missing decisive proof remains unavailable or blocked. Unrelated repository movement, an evidence-only commit, or a prompt revision does not itself require a rerun or expire an approval. A present SHA alone does not prove that required work ran.\n\nOptional token compatibility.\n\nWhen a preserved historical record or an explicitly chosen bounded token cross-reference claims a token, every token-to-evidence binding MUST be validated against PF12’s Evidence Catalog and its fixed canonical paths. A binding to a non-canonical path is invalid and MUST be corrected before it supports acceptance. If a different path is genuinely required, route it through an explicit decision and drain it into the correct canonical home.\n\nThis conditional validation does not require a token, complete roster, token-evidence matrix, or token-aware acceptance map. Absence of those token surfaces MUST NOT block otherwise sufficient exact-source evidence.\n\nWhen a governed historical token-evidence matrix remains in use, it MUST agree with the Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, and governed path proof for every artifact it binds. The matrix remains optional compatibility metadata and is not an acceptance authority.\n\nPrimary evidence vs path-proof transcripts (clarification).\n\nExact-source records and optional token bindings MUST identify the primary governed artifact path listed in the Evidence Catalog. `*.path_proof.txt` files remain required integrity transcripts where PF12 requires them, but they are not primary evidence targets. The governed linkage to a path proof is through the Machine Evidence Mirror `proof_anchor` for the primary artifact.\n\nNo repository, commit, PR, workflow, hash, manifest, index, mirror, path proof, attestation, token, or decision record proves every other fact by itself. When required exact-source metadata or governed evidence is unavailable, the affected acceptance or completion claim remains unavailable or blocked.\n\nShared/global evidence dependencies (do not assume implicit).\n\nSome governed evidence surfaces are shared across many deliverables and may live outside a deliverable’s “local bundle” directory. When a deliverable’s acceptance depends on shared/global evidence surfaces, they must be explicitly listed and bound by canonical path rather than assumed to be “implicitly available.” PF12’s role is to define canonical paths and evidence families; workflow enforcement and review gates are routed by title to the Change Process Guide and Glow QA Guide.\n\nRemediation-only artifacts (MUST).\n\nRemediation-only repository diagnostics and manifests MUST NOT enter the Human Evidence Index or Machine Evidence Mirror unless their owning PF12 contract explicitly catalogs them. Existing repository remediation staging retains its scoped paths and non-admission posture. New off-repository repair proposals, plans, versioned remediation records, reports, and exports belong in ChatGPT Library under §8.18; their existence does not promote a repository evidence family.\n\nExample remediation subtree (current-state; EPIC024 dev acceptance artifacts):\n\n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/remediation/s2_dev_acceptance_artifacts/acceptance_map_viability.json`: Remediation JSON report (current-state EPIC024 schema: `epic024.acceptance_map_viability.v1`).  \n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/remediation/s2_dev_acceptance_artifacts/token_evidence_matrix_scope.md`: Remediation markdown scope note containing a canonicalized acceptance tokens table.\n\nIndex and mirror fixed filenames (for plans/tasks that touch governed indices/mirrors).\n\nEvidence index (human-readable):\n\n* docs/evidence/INDEX.json  \n* docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256  \n* docs/evidence/INDEX.json.path\\_proof.txt  \n* docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256.path\\_proof.txt\n\nEvidence index mirror (machine-readable):\n\n* artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl  \n* artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl.sha256  \n* artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl.path\\_proof.txt  \n* artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl.sha256.path\\_proof.txt\n\nPlans and tasks that touch any file above MUST treat the mirror checksum sidecar and both sibling .path\\_proof.txt transcripts as first-class deliverables. If a plan proposes a new file under governed roots, it MUST state whether the file is intended to appear in the indices/mirror; absence of that statement is a mechanical blocker.\n\nEvidence-output naming discipline (plans and token claims; normative).\n\nPlans and acceptance artifacts MUST name the primary governed evidence outputs that will be committed and indexed for the epic or PR.\n\nToken-claim evidence outputs MUST be concrete, filename-specific, and indexable. Therefore, acceptance artifacts MUST NOT bind tokens to directory families, wildcard patterns, or vague family phrases such as “plus step logs”.\n\nPlans SHOULD avoid wildcards in required-evidence lines even when a canon-defined path-pattern exists for discovery. If a path-pattern exists for discovery or enumeration, the plan SHOULD still bind the token to the concrete primary artifact instance(s) (exact path and filename) that will appear as records in the Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror for the PR or QA run.\n\nIf a tool produces a high-churn set of member logs, the plan MAY treat the governed output as a single primary artifact (for example, a manifest or bundle) and state that member files are referenced by that primary artifact, provided the plan names the primary governed artifact by exact path and filename and keeps evidence binding deterministic. Member files SHOULD be referenced by the manifest/bundle rather than being individually required in the plan’s evidence-output lines unless the Evidence Catalog explicitly promotes them as primary governed evidence surfaces.\n\nAcceptance map — legacy token compatibility shape (clarification).\n\nThese rules apply only when an existing token-aware acceptance map is preserved or a future explicitly bounded token cross-reference uses one. They do not require a new acceptance map, top-level token array, token roster, token-evidence matrix, or universal replacement form for tokenless work.\n\nAn existing token-aware acceptance-map artifact MUST preserve its governing schema. If that schema requires a top-level `tokens` array, retain the field. An empty array remains valid wherever the governing schema already permits it or requires the field to exist with a valid empty value.\n\nFor each token entry that is present:\n\n* the entry MUST be an object;  \n* `tokens[].name` MUST be a non-empty string and remains the case-sensitive authoritative token identity;  \n* `tokens[].token_name` MAY remain as a compatibility alias or display label, but validators MUST NOT require it or use it as token identity; and  \n* validators MUST NOT guess token field keys or treat matrix or table headers as token identities.\n\n---\n\n### **8.6.2 Parity rule (MUST)**\n\nIn any PR that changes governed evidence artifacts or their indexing, you MUST update all of the following together:\n\n* docs/evidence/INDEX.json (Human Index)  \n* docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256 (hash sentinel)  \n* artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl (Machine Evidence Mirror)  \n* artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl.sha256 (Machine Evidence Mirror checksum sidecar)  \n* The governed sibling \\*.path\\_proof.txt transcripts for every changed index/mirror file above\n\nProve each parity update through the exact repository and commit identity, exact governed paths and SHA-256 digests, and the applicable current validator or workflow result. No mirror or index acceptance-token assertion is required. A preserved historical or explicitly scoped token claim MAY reference registered mirror or index token names, but that optional metadata does not replace the exact-source proof.\n\nWhole-family same-change closeout rule (MUST).\n\nFor evidence-indexing closeout claims, success MUST be evaluated across the whole set of governed evidence families whose bytes changed in the scoped run.\n\nIf the same scoped run changes more than one governed evidence family, closeout is satisfied only when every changed family is refreshed in that same run, indexed and mirrored coherently, and backed by current sibling `.path_proof.txt` transcripts where PF12 requires them.\n\nA green result for one changed subfamily MUST NOT be used as a proxy for whole-family coherence. “Authoritative family fixed” is not equivalent to “whole changed family coherent.”\n\nPath-proof churn review grouping.\n\nBroad path-proof churn across governed artifacts is review load, not scope drift by itself.\n\nWhen a scoped run refreshes many path-proof companions or mirror rows, review SHOULD group the changes by governed evidence family and verify:\n\n* the changed payload artifact  \n* the changed path-proof companion  \n* the Human Evidence Index entry  \n* the Machine Evidence Mirror row  \n* any required checksum sidecar  \n* the cause of the refresh\n\nA broad refresh MAY be classified as non-blocking scope churn only when every changed governed artifact remains cataloged in PF12 or another owning PF home, every changed path-proof validates against its target artifact, and the Human Index, Machine Mirror, checksum sidecars, and path-proof records remain coherent for the same change.\n\nDuplicate or repeated evidence-refresh hunks SHOULD be consolidated or summarized for review, but consolidation MUST NOT hide any changed governed artifact, proof anchor, sha256, size\\_bytes, or discovered\\_physical\\_path.\n\n### **8.6.3 Entries (authoritative list; titles/paths only)**\n\n#### **8.6.3.1 Catalog governance and root discipline**\n\n**Multi-root evidence catalog rule (normative).** The Evidence Catalog is intentionally multi-root: governed evidence artifacts are expected to exist under multiple repo roots, for example `audit/`, `artifacts/`, `docs/`, `catalog/`, and `narratives/`. In evidence terms, the single-home constraint means PF12 is the single authoritative home for evidence family naming, canonical path bindings, and the Index and Mirror discipline that binds those paths. It does not mean evidence must live under a single directory.\n\nMulti-root storage is not, by itself, evidence drift. Drift occurs when a root or artifact is treated as governed evidence or a truth-home output but is not cataloged here and is not indexed and mirrored with exactly one governed `*.path_proof.txt` transcript.\n\n**Root classification rule (normative).** If any additional top-level root is treated as governed evidence, for example `scripts/` or `tools/`, its evidence outputs MUST either:\n\n* be cataloged in §8.6 as explicit evidence families with titles and canonical paths, and indexed and mirrored per §8.3; or  \n* be treated as non-governed tooling outputs and excluded from truth-home claims, meaning not indexed, not mirrored, and not accepted as evidence.\n\nObserved multi-root distribution across existing governed roots does not, by itself, expand the Evidence Catalog or create a new governed root.\n\nRevisit evidence-root classification or root proliferation only when future work proposes either:\n\n* a new governed root; or  \n* a second truth home for an existing governed evidence family.\n\nAbsent one of those proposals, observed multi-root distribution is handled under the classification rule above and is not, by itself, a canon-change trigger.\n\nHuman Index entries are titles and paths only. Machine Mirror records include at least `artifact_key`, `role`, `sha256`, `size_bytes`, `produced_at_utc`, `discovered_physical_path`, and `proof_anchor`. Unless a family-specific note narrows the rule, every artifact listed below MUST have exactly one Human Index entry, one Machine Mirror record, and one governed sibling `*.path_proof.txt` transcript, all kept in lockstep.\n\n#### **8.6.3.2 Core pack, canonical JSON, topology, and deterministic order**\n\n##### **Freeze-pack and math**\n\n* `artifacts/math/freeze_pack_manifest.json`  \n* `artifacts/math/release_id.txt`  \n* `artifacts/math/release_id_recompute.log`  \n* `artifacts/math/checksums_audit.log`  \n* `artifacts/math/manifest_snapshot.json`\n\n##### **Canonical JSON and topology**\n\n* `artifacts/canonical/arrays_as_sets_report.log`  \n* `audit/gates/json_gate/canonical/json_gate_check_log.ndjson`  \n* `audit/gates/json_gate/canonical/json_gate_compare_log.ndjson`  \n* `audit/gates/json_gate/canonical/json_gate_structured_record.json` (optional)  \n* `audit/gates/canonical_json/canonical_json.gate.json`  \n* `audit/gates/canonical_json/json_canon_compare.log`  \n* `audit/gates/canonical_json/json_canonical_check.log` The audit/gates/canonical\\_json/ family is a supplemental legacy canonical-JSON gate family. ChartSimpleResult MAY support bounded live smoke, authentication proof, geocode-key proof, provider availability proof, or minimal route-family confirmation. It MUST NOT be treated as sufficient for full BodyGraph, person, cache, compatibility, or compute input unless a governed adapter/schema proof demonstrates that it contains every required field for that contract. The preferred future v2 payload candidate is the richest relevant v2 chart response, currently the full chart route / ChartResult family, unless a future vendor-route policy or ADR proves another source. If full ChartResult does not contain all required BodyGraph details, the proof MUST record the exact field gap and either define a sanctioned adapter strategy, identify the correct vendor route for full BodyGraph detail, retain explicit legacy fallback, or route a new ADR before runtime compatibility is claimed. The proof MUST NOT persist raw secrets, uncontrolled raw vendor payloads, public Reader payload changes, new HTTP-home claims, app-side vendor credential ownership, or AI scope. Recording an adapter/schema gap is acceptable as gap evidence only; it MUST NOT be reused as proof of runtime compatibility. **Future `bg:resolve --source vendor` route-policy evidence.** A future proof or implementation that claims bg:resolve \\--source vendor resolves BodyGraph detail MUST be a governed, secret-safe evidence family. It MUST distinguish the selected route policy as exactly one of: v2 chart-backed BodyGraph resolution, explicit legacy BodyGraph fallback, dual-route policy, or unsupported runtime nonclaim. The evidence MUST record:  \n* the configured base-url posture  \n* the selected runtime resource path family  \n* the request shape used by bg:resolve \\--source vendor  \n* whether the route is v2 chart-backed, legacy BodyGraph, dual-route, or unsupported  \n* the redacted auth-header family and geocode-key posture where applicable  \n* whether the selected response contains the required BodyGraph detail  \n* the normalized internal BodyGraph/person/cache output contract when compatibility is claimed  \n* any legacy fallback or vendor-route gap that remains  \n* the nonclaims preserved by the proof. The evidence MUST distinguish simple route availability from full BodyGraph-detail resolution. A successful charts/simple observation MAY prove provider availability, auth posture, geocode-key posture, or route-family availability. It MUST NOT prove that bg:resolve \\--source vendor resolves complete BodyGraph detail unless the route-policy and adapter/schema proof also establish the required internal contract. `audit/qa/hde-epic037/00_meta/pr05_parent_binding_doc_deltas.md`.\n\n##### **Source precedence and quarantine**\n\nThe source-precedence posture for this family is:\n\n* validated v2 and v1 YAML specs first  \n* rendered endpoint pages second  \n* high-level guide pages third  \n* suspect artifacts quarantined until validated\n\n`api-reference/openapi.json` MUST NOT define vendor bytes, schemas, endpoint routes, request shaping, response mapping, or architecture conformance unless its HumanDesignAPI domain, title, server, and path-family ownership are validated and recorded in the governed validation artifacts. Documentation-discovery files such as `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` MAY be recorded only as source-inventory entries. They MUST NOT create:\n\n* AI product scope  \n* AI runtime scope  \n* AI evidence families  \n* AI-provider config keys  \n* AI rails  \n* AI tokens  \n* AI QA obligations\n\n**Path-proofs and indexing.**\n\nEach primary artifact above MUST have a sibling .path\\_proof.txt transcript stored alongside the artifact when the artifact is promoted into governed evidence, indexed, mirrored, or used as acceptance-support evidence. Each source-cache support input above MUST have a sibling .path\\_proof.txt transcript when the source-cache input is promoted into governed evidence, indexed, mirrored, or used as acceptance-support evidence. Canonical JSON artifacts in this family MUST follow PF12 canonical JSON rules:\n\n* UTF-8  \n* no BOM  \n* ASCII-sorted keys  \n* compact separators  \n* exactly one trailing LF\n\nYAML, text, Markdown, CSV, body, and log artifacts in this family MUST be UTF-8 and LF-terminated. The Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror MUST each carry exactly one binding for every promoted path. Mirror records MUST use the defined artifact\\_key and point proof\\_anchor to the sibling path-proof. When this family changes, the following MUST be refreshed coherently in the same change:\n\n* changed primary artifacts  \n* promoted source-cache inputs  \n* sibling path-proofs  \n* Human Index  \n* Human Index hash sentinel  \n* Machine Mirror  \n* Machine Mirror checksum sidecar  \n* required Index and Mirror sibling path-proofs\n\n#### **8.6.3.11 Lifecycle, admin QA, and runbooks**\n\n* `artifacts/db/backup_manifest.json`  \n* `artifacts/db/restore_verify.log`  \n* `artifacts/db/retention_run.log`\n\n##### **Admin QA and runbooks**\n\n* `docs/run/PROD_ENDPOINTS.json`  \n* `docs/run/RUN_PROD_QA.md`  \n* `docs/run/EPIC011_TEST_IDENTITIES.md`  \n* `artifacts/ops/admin_vendor_calls.jsonl`\n\n#### **8.6.3.12 Epic QA harness ledger artifacts**\n\nThese entries register repository QA harness ledger files that summarize Live QA results as current-state evidence. The invariant machine-output pair is the per-check primary log and step-logs manifest with their required governed companions; optional auxiliary ledgers are not closure requirements by default. This minimum does not remove the separate substantive final QA Report and RCA required for every completed current QA run under §8.18. Historical attempt records remain preserved without becoming a second current-state evidence root.\n\n**Production-affecting open-rails Live QA evidence.**\n\nWhen a Live QA plan includes a bounded open-rails step for production-affecting behavior, the evidence MUST remain redacted, bounded, and governed. It MAY record header names, redacted header-shape posture, endpoint or route family, environment label, rails posture, request class, result class, and safe status or error classification. It MUST NOT record raw secrets, raw bearer tokens, raw API keys, uncontrolled production data, full private payloads, or full vendor payload bodies unless a later owning canon explicitly permits that payload and the evidence is still secret-safe. Open-rails Live QA evidence proves only the behavior actually exercised. It MUST preserve nonclaim boundaries for full runtime conformance, parent-task completion, public Reader expansion, new public routes, new public flags, public payload changes, new HTTP homes, AI scope, PO closeout, and epic closure unless those claims are separately bound by their owning canon and governed evidence.\n\n**Open-rails QA evidence-family distinction.**\n\nWhen an epic requires open-rails QA, PF12-governed artifacts MUST keep the open-rails QA proof family distinguishable from closed-rails proof, OPS evidence, implementation evidence, repo inspection, static validation, schema validation, Evidence Index validation, Machine Mirror validation, and path-proof validation. The Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror SHOULD preserve the distinction through artifact keys, roles, paths, notes, record types, or equivalent governed metadata emitted by the evidence tooling. A prior OPS observation may be referenced only when it is explicitly bound into QA evidence or accepted under QA posture by the owning QA plan and evidence artifacts.\n\n**QA\\_PLAN\\_UPDATE routing for non-QA-root governed evidence.**\n\nWhen final PASS-grade QA proof relies on a refreshed or newly bound governed evidence surface outside the QA root, the QA package MUST include a QA\\_PLAN\\_UPDATE routing receipt before the post-routing proof is accepted. The receipt MUST be a governed QA evidence artifact under the QA checks root, MUST have a sibling path-proof transcript when promoted, and MUST name the routing type, source or trigger, affected check or closeout proof, non-QA-root artifacts being bound, allowed action, required post-routing receipt, rails posture, and nonclaims. A QA\\_PLAN\\_UPDATE routing receipt does not by itself claim product behavior, token satisfaction, PF09 drainage, PO closeout, or epic closure. It records the provenance route that allows the later proof to rely on the named non-QA-root governed evidence.\n\nThis receipt is evidence provenance, not a separate approval object or a new Product Owner confirmation. Its trigger is the actual refreshed or newly bound governed surface, not merely a changed, different, or unavailable SHA. Preserve the true tested state, later storage/review identities, actual authorizations, and source limits under §8.18. Existing governed receipt families remain intact; native remediation records do not create a new receipt or document for every handoff.\n\n##### **Canonical epic QA root**\n\n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/`\n\n##### **Invariant required outputs (current-state; canonical paths)**\n\n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/primary.log`: Required per-check canonical step receipt and primary evidence log. It records the closure-support binding posture for the EPIC029 dev-harness family and MUST preserve any accepted environment state that remains not yet closed while separately recording QA-log coverage as present and bound.\n\n##### **Per-run retention and appendix copies (non-canonical; not binding)**\n\nCurrent Live QA bindings MUST NOT use run-id directories, timestamped roots, or appendix-only copies as evidence roots. `run_id` or `RUN_ID` MUST NOT be required as an operator input, step-log header field, governed manifest field, correctness key, or root selector. Preserve prior actual attempts and their source/result lineage before an authorized current-state replacement. Retained history is not another current result, must not reset retry accounting, and does not enter the Index/Mirror unless an owning contract expressly admits it. Off-repository historical copies belong in ChatGPT Library under §8.18; the manifest continues to bind the current check-scoped primary.\n\n##### **Indexing discipline (governed artifacts)**\n\nIndexing follows the standard §8.6 rule set: exactly one Human Evidence Index entry per concrete file path, exactly one Machine Evidence Mirror record per concrete file path, and exactly one governed path-proof transcript per concrete file path, kept in lockstep. Acceptance hints (titles-only; evidence is via per-check primary.log under the epic QA root). EVIDENCE\\_INDEX\\_UPDATED\\_OK EVIDENCE\\_INDEX\\_HASH\\_OK EVIDENCE\\_INDEX\\_MIRROR\\_OK EVIDENCE\\_PATHS\\_VALIDATED\\_OK CI\\_CHECK\\_MIRROR\\_SCHEMA\\_OK CI\\_CHECK\\_FINAL\\_LF\\_OK JSON\\_CANONICAL\\_CHECK\\_OK\n\n#### **8.6.3.13 Epic token/evidence matrix**\n\nThese entries register per-epic Token/Evidence Matrix artifacts as governed members of the Evidence Catalog. Each matrix provides a single, reviewable ledger mapping QA tokens to evidence and execution surfaces for one epic.\n\n##### **Family description**\n\nEach epic MAY define exactly one Token/Evidence Matrix artifact under its epic QA root. The matrix is current-state; it is updated in place as the epic’s closure posture evolves.\n\n##### **Path pattern (single home per epic; choose exactly one format per epic)**\n\nMarkdown: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/token_evidence_matrix.md`\n\nJSON: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/token_evidence_matrix.json`\n\nJSONL: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/token_evidence_matrix.jsonl`\n\nThe `<epic-id>` segment is the canonical identifier used in §8.17: lower-case ASCII and hyphenated, for example `hde-epic021`. A differing semantic identifier, for example `HDE-EPIC021`, MAY be recorded in Machine Mirror metadata via epic\\_id. The matrix MUST contain no secrets.\n\n##### **Row set (binding discipline; names-only)**\n\nMatrix rows are reserved for the set of QA tokens that this epic explicitly claims as in-scope. Tokens explicitly deferred or out of scope for this epic MUST NOT appear as matrix rows.\n\n##### **Minimum content (names-only)**\n\nFor each token row in the matrix, the artifact MUST record at least: token\\_name: the QA token’s canonical name, as defined in HDE-Governance and or Glow QA Guide or an approved doc delta (titles-only). owner\\_pf: the PF document (and optionally section) that owns the token’s semantics (titles-only). evidence\\_artifacts: one or more governed artifacts associated with the token (artifact\\_keys and or discovered\\_physical\\_path entries), drawn from families listed in §8.6 and other PF12 sections. `qa_root_logs`: QA log paths under `audit/qa/<epic-id>/` that demonstrate QA harness runs relevant to this token (current-state preferred; retained history optional). ci\\_tests\\_jobs: CI test modules and or jobs that enforce this token under closed rails (names only). Additional columns such as Status or Notes MAY be present for human use; their contents are not governed by PF12 beyond canonical text formatting and governed-path rules.\n\n##### **Canonical format**\n\nWhen the matrix is Markdown, it MUST remain plain UTF-8 text with LF line endings and no ANSI sequences. When JSON or JSONL is used instead of Markdown, canonical JSON rules from §4 apply (UTF-8, no BOM; ASCII-sorted keys; compact; exactly one trailing LF; arrays-as-sets deduped and ASCII-sorted when treated as sets).\n\n##### **Indexing (titles/paths only)**\n\nLet MATRIX\\_PATH be the chosen single-home Token/Evidence Matrix path for this epic (one of the three paths listed above). Human Evidence Index (docs/evidence/INDEX.json). For each epic that defines a Token/Evidence Matrix, there MUST be exactly one Index entry with artifact\\_key set to a stable, epic-scoped key (for example epic021.token\\_matrix) and discovered\\_physical\\_path pointing to MATRIX\\_PATH. docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256 MUST be updated in the same change-set whenever a new epic matrix is added or its path changes. Machine Evidence Mirror (artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl). Each epic Token/Evidence Matrix MUST have a corresponding Mirror record with artifact\\_key equal to the key used in the Human Index entry, role: \"snapshot\", discovered\\_physical\\_path pointing to MATRIX\\_PATH, and sha256, size\\_bytes, produced\\_at\\_utc, and proof\\_anchor matching the governed path-proof transcript for this artifact. If additional labeling is needed, use §8.3 metadata keys (for example epic\\_id and record\\_type:\"token\\_evidence\\_matrix\"). Unknown keys remain rejected. Exactly one Mirror record per epic is allowed for this family; additional QA tables or notes under the same directory are separate artifacts and MUST NOT reuse the same artifact\\_key. Path-proofs. Each matrix artifact MUST have a sibling path-proof transcript (for example token\\_evidence\\_matrix.md.path\\_proof.txt) that satisfies the path-proof schema in §8.3 and is referenced from the Mirror record via proof\\_anchor.\n\n##### **Acceptance hints (names-only)**\n\nPF12 does not own token semantics. For epic Token/Evidence Matrices, PF12 binds the matrix family to existing QA tokens by name and path only. Epics and QA plans use the matrix as a ledger; PF12 governs only its existence, location, and indexing.\n\n### **8.6.4 Discipline reminder (current-state; unchanged)**\n\nEvery entry above must have:\n\n* Exactly one Human Index entry in docs/evidence/INDEX.json.  \n* Exactly one Mirror record in artifacts/evidence\\_index.jsonl.  \n* Exactly one governed path-proof transcript (\\*.path\\_proof.txt), referenced by proof\\_anchor.\n\nMirror records must follow §8.3:\n\n* Canonical JSONL  \n* Single mirror file  \n* Sorted field order and sorted records  \n* LF-terminated  \n* Unknown-key rejection  \n* proof\\_anchor pointing to a stored path-proof transcript for the same artifact\n\n### **8.6.5 Acceptance impact**\n\nThis section is a names-only catalog of governed artifact families and paths. Enforcement rests on the applicable substantive predicates and direct schema, canonical-byte, Index/Mirror, checksum, and path-proof validation. Existing token identifiers remain optional, scoped legacy cross-references under §0.2; their presence or absence is not a substitute for the decisive evidence and does not authorize new token issuance.\n\n## **8.7 DB fingerprint & smoke artifacts \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nPurpose. Capture database posture and minimal activity proofs as records-only governed evidence for EPIC-011 and future epics.\n\n### **Artifacts (titles and paths only)**\n\n* DB fingerprint — normalized DDL \\+ sha256: `artifacts/db/ddl_fingerprint.json`  \n* Roles and grants snapshot: `artifacts/db/grants.txt`  \n* Schema/search\\_path echo: `artifacts/db/check_schema.txt`  \n* Constraints check: `artifacts/db/check_constraints.txt`  \n* Partition plan (summary): `artifacts/db/partition_plan.txt`  \n* RW smoke (optional): `artifacts/db/db_rw_smoke.log`  \n* Retained historical runtime-connectivity snapshot: `artifacts/runtime/env_connectivity.snapshot.json`  \n* Env posture (names-only): `artifacts/runtime/env_matrix.snapshot.json`  \n* Current direct-selection snapshot: `artifacts/runtime/direct_db_selection.snapshot.json`  \n* Current direct-selection schema: `schemas/hde_epic038_direct_db_selection.v1.json`  \n* Current direct read-only OPS packet: `audit/ops/hde-epic038/ops-03/`\n\n### **Shared DDL identity projection**\n\n`engine/db/ddl_identity_projection.py` is the sole shared implementation of `hde.ddl_identity_projection.v1`.\n\nThe included projection fields are exactly:\n\n* `projection[].kind`  \n* `projection[].name`  \n* `projection[].columns[].name`  \n* `projection[].columns[].type`\n\nThe explicitly unexamined fields are:\n\n* `source[].columns[].nullable`  \n* `source[].columns[].default`  \n* `source[].constraints`  \n* `source[kind=view].definition`\n\nThe projector accepts only `table` and `view`, rejects malformed or duplicate objects and columns, sorts objects by `(kind, name)`, sorts columns by `(name, type)`, and emits only the governed projection fields. Equality proves only `projection_match`; it MUST be accompanied by `full_ddl_semantic_parity_claimed: false` and MUST NOT be represented as full DDL semantic parity.\n\n### **Current direct-only selection evidence**\n\nThe current family is `epic038.pr06r.direct_db_selection` at `artifacts/runtime/direct_db_selection.snapshot.json`, validated by `hde_epic038.direct_db_selection.v1` at `schemas/hde_epic038_direct_db_selection.v1.json`.\n\nThe primary contains exactly `schema`, `retired_keys`, `cases`, `predicates`, `result`, and `failure`. They MUST fail closed on an absent, invalid, ambiguous, or hash-mismatched active mechanics configuration and MUST NOT activate a candidate configuration.\n\nThe governed Magic-10 v1 golden identity is `tests/fixtures/magic10/v1/goldens.json`. It is a deterministic verification input, not a second formula authority, generated `config.magic10` payload, Human Index or Machine Mirror entry by implication, or release-manifest member outside the exact promoted roster.\n\nGeneration and env rails (titles-only):\n\n* Generated by tools/config/generate\\_config\\_artifacts.py under closed rails: LC\\_ALL=C, LANG=C, TZ=UTC, SAFE\\_MODE=1, ALLOW\\_NETWORK=0.  \n* Uses the hardened registry loader and the shared canonical serializer (per §4) to ensure deterministic bytes and two-run identity.\n\nCanonical JSON and schema tag:\n\n* MUST be canonical JSON per §4 (UTF-8, no BOM; sorted keys; compact; exactly one trailing LF).  \n* MUST contain a top-level schema field whose value MUST equal \"magic10\\_config.v1\".  \n* MUST use field shapes and types pinned by the owning JSON Schema for this artifact (names-only; the schema file is referenced here by title, not path).\n\nContent (names-only, from Addendum 6):\n\nAt minimum, the Magic-10 config JSON MUST:\n\n* Capture the normative Magic-10 order as a closed list matching the Magic-10 catalog (§2.6): ten category IDs in the pinned order.  \n* Record per-category caps as integer bounds for all categories (inputs \\+ integer limits); details of the cap object shape are governed by the config schema and tests, not restated here.  \n* Include seed metadata for each category currently present in `catalog/magic10_seeds.json`. Present keys MUST be a subset of the closed Magic-10 domain. Each present row contains:  \n  * `template_id` — string.  \n  * `seed_version` — integer or string version identifier.  \n  * `updated_at_utc` — UTC ISO-8601 timestamp string.  \n  * `checksum_sha256` — lowercase 64-hex identity for the referenced seed content.\n\nThe config MUST preserve subset semantics and MUST NOT synthesize missing category rows. A future full-ten requirement must first change §2.7 and the owning implementation through Doc-Delta.\n\n### **8.14.2 Band-edges config artifact (config.band\\_edges)**\n\nPath (fixed): artifacts/thresholds/band\\_edges.json\n\nRole and artifact\\_key:\n\n* Mirror artifact\\_key: \"config.band\\_edges\" (names-only).  \n* Mirror role: \"snapshot\".\n\nGeneration and env rails (titles-only):\n\n* Generated by tools/config/generate\\_config\\_artifacts.py under the same closed-rails profile as config.magic10 (LC\\_ALL=C, LANG=C, TZ=UTC, SAFE\\_MODE=1, ALLOW\\_NETWORK=0).  \n* Uses the shared canonical serializer; arithmetic remains in Math).  \n* Encode clamp behavior and rounding mode (for example, how values at or beyond the defined edges are handled and how intermediate values are rounded) in explicit fields governed by the schema.  \n* Include a version identifier for the band-edges config itself and a pointer back to math/thresholds.json indicating which thresholds source this config was derived from.\n\nAny mismatch between band edges and math/thresholds.json (for example, missing bands, unsorted edges, or incompatible ranges) is a hard error in the config tests and should be treated as a spec violation.\n\n### **8.14.3 EPIC-018 config acceptance map (epic018.config.acceptance\\_map)**\n\nPath (fixed): audit/EPIC-018\\_config\\_acceptance\\_map.json\n\nRole and artifact\\_key:\n\n* Mirror artifact\\_key: \"epic018.config.acceptance\\_map\" (names-only).  \n* Mirror role: \"snapshot\".\n\nPurpose.
