Each of the three artifacts MUST have a sibling path-proof transcript:\n\n* artifacts/thresholds/magic10\\_config.json.path\\_proof.txt  \n* artifacts/thresholds/band\\_edges.json.path\\_proof.txt  \n* audit/EPIC-018\\_config\\_acceptance\\_map.json.path\\_proof.txt\n\nEach transcript MUST follow the path-proof schema in §8.3 (exactly one record with path, sha256, size\\_bytes, mtime\\_utc, produced\\_at\\_utc) and MUST match the mirror record and the artifact bytes exactly.\n\n## **8.15 Config bundles (typed FE/BE) \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nPurpose. Exact filenames are owned by the bundle generator and tests; PF12 governs the family, not per-file naming.\n\n### **8.15.1 Backend config bundle (config\\_bundle.be)**\n\nArtifact family:\n\n* Artifact key (mirror / Evidence Index): \"config\\_bundle.be\".  \n* Role: \"snapshot\" (typed backend bundle).  \n* Directory: artifacts/config\\_bundles/ (filenames owned by the generator; tests and Evidence Index entries pin the exact paths).\n\nGeneration and env rails (titles-only):\n\n* Generated by engine/config/bundles.py and tools/config/generate\\_bundles.py.  \n* Generation MUST run under the same closed-rails profile used for D5 config artifacts: LC\\_ALL=C, LANG=C, TZ=UTC, SAFE\\_MODE=1, ALLOW\\_NETWORK=0.  \n* Bundles are built exclusively from:  \n  * governed Magic-10 config (config.magic10)  \n  * governed band-edges config (config.band\\_edges)  \n  * the registry report (registry.registry\\_report)  \n* via the hardened registry loader (titles-only to Mechanics/Registry).\n\nCanonical JSON and schema tag:\n\n* Each backend bundle JSON MUST be canonical JSON per §4 (UTF-8, no BOM; schema files live under docs/schemas/ and are not PF12-canonical yet).\n\nContent (names-only, from Addendum 7):\n\nAt minimum, the backend bundle MUST contain:\n\n* A Magic-10 section that matches the governed config.magic10 artifact semantically:  \n  * normative Magic-10 order  \n  * per-category caps for all ten categories  \n  * seed metadata (template\\_id, seed\\_version, updated\\_at\\_utc, checksum\\_sha256)  \n* A band-edges section that matches config.band\\_edges semantically:  \n  * band names and edges  \n  * clamp policy  \n  * rounding mode  \n  * version and a pointer to the source thresholds (names-only)  \n* Full topology slices aligned with the registry report:  \n  * channel objects with at least the fields id, gates, centers, circuit\\_primary, substream, primary\\_domain, domains, flags (exact field set pinned by schema/tests), where:  \n    * id MUST be a canonical channel ID (NN-NN or multi-pair string) consistent with the Channels catalog  \n    * center/domain/circuit values MUST be consistent with the registry report and catalogs (titles-only to §2.1/§3.2)  \n* center records and domain lists consistent with the registry report  \n* an alias\\_policy block whose semantics match the registry’s alias policy (titles-only; schema lives under docs/schemas/).\n\nContent (names-only, from Addendum 7):\n\nAt minimum, the frontend bundle MUST contain:\n\n* Magic-10 content sufficient for client usage:  \n  * Magic-10 order and per-category caps consistent with the backend bundle and config.magic10  \n* Band-edges content sufficient for client usage:  \n  * band names, edges, clamp behavior, rounding mode, version, and a pointer to the thresholds source, consistent with config.band\\_edges  \n* A trimmed topology view:  \n  * channel identifiers (IDs) with associated center/domain information such that:  \n    * the set of channel IDs MUST equal the channel\\_ids recorded in the registry report’s artifacts.registry section  \n    * centers/domains/alias policy information is consistent with the backend bundle and registry report  \n* An alias\\_policy section aligned with the registry report  \n* A sources object with the same structure and constraints as the backend bundle’s sources block (entries for Magic-10 config, band-edges config, and registry report, each with path, sha256, size\\_bytes matching the governed artifacts)\n\nTwo-run identity. record.  \n* The same requirement applies to backend bundle files.\n\nAcceptance hints (names-only):\n\nPF12 does not own token semantics, but these bundles are the governed surface for bundle-related tokens, including:\n\n* CONFIG\\_BUNDLES\\_DETERMINISTIC\\_OK — typed frontend and backend bundles are generated under closed rails from governed config artifacts and registry report, are canonical JSON, satisfy two-run identity, and contain a sources block whose path/sha256/size\\_bytes entries match the current governed artifacts.\n\nTokens and detailed CI policy live in Glow QA Guide and HDE-Governance; PF12 binds these tokens to the config\\_bundle.fe and config\\_bundle.be families by artifact key, directory, and sources linkage, not by test names.\n\n## **8.16 Repo implementation following constraints:\n\nNon-canonical status:\n\n* Repo docs (README.md, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/INDEX.md, docs/RUN.md, docs/config\\_and\\_bundles.md, docs/evidence/EPIC018\\_evidence.md, and related ./docs/\\*\\* files) are not part of PF-Canon.  \n* When they conflict with PF12 or other PF documents, the PF documents win; the drift is a bug in the repo docs and must be fixed with PF12 or removed.\n\nNo token ownership:\n\n* Repo docs MUST NOT introduce new acceptance token names, redefine token semantics, or change which artifacts a token covers.  \n* Token names and lists are illustrative and must match the authoritative lists in PF12 §8.5, §8.6, §8.14, §8.15 and Appendix C.  \n* If a path appears in repo docs but not in PF12’s Evidence Catalog, treat it as non-governed until a PF12 Doc-Delta adds it.\n\n### **8.16.3 Doc-Delta expectations**\n\nRepo docs themselves do not require a Doc-Delta when they change wording or flow, but:\n\n* Any change to \n* If a change relies on a new repo doc (for example, adding docs/config\\_and\\_bundles.md as the implementation crib for D5/D6 config/bundles) and that change also adjusts governed artifacts or Evidence Index entries, the Doc-Delta MUST name both:  \n  * the PF12 sections it affects (for example, §8.5, §8.14, §8.15, §8.6, Appendix C)  \n  * the new or updated repo docs (by path) as implementation references only.\n\n## **8.17 Live QA evidence layout (audit/qa/\\\\/) \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\nPurpose.\n\nStandardize the layout and naming of Live QA evidence under the governed audit/\\*\\* root so that:\n\n* Live QA artifacts are easy to locate and reason about across epics, CRDs, and attempts.  \n* Evidence promoted to governed status can be indexed and mirrored consistently.  \n* The QA process can rely on predictable naming without re-specifying it per governed change container.\n\nChange-container identity (normative).\n\nThis layout supports actual Epic or CRD identity without converting one class into the other.\n\n* Epic inputs retain their existing identity and `EPIC_QA_ROOT` at `audit/qa/<epic-id>/`.  \n* Local CRD identity uses `HDE-CRD-[0-9]{4,}`: at least four ASCII decimal digits, with no four-digit ceiling. Its root is `audit/qa/<lowercase-crd-id>/`; the source is the controlled CRD identity and approved class-bound lineage, not an active PF30 gate.  \n* Configuration selects exactly one Epic or CRD identity. CRD mode has no fabricated Epic-only derived identity, acceptance map, roster, token matrix, or viability requirement. Generic `<epic-id>`/`EPIC_QA_ROOT` wording refers to the corresponding CRD root only where the actual contract supports that substitution.  \n* Named Epic families, strict legacy predicates, and existing historical bytes retain their own scope. Do not extend the closed Codespaces snapshot schema or another Epic-only schema by analogy.\n\nLocal recording and governed publication are distinct capabilities. Validate the selected family's actual producers and consumers before admission; do not make every future CRD result or migration of every Epic-only tool a prerequisite to unrelated QA. The bounded admitted CRD family and its fail-closed rules are specified in §8.17.6; the local grammar alone allocates no identity and admits no additional CRD. Path provenance (normative).\n\nLive QA plans and runbooks MUST NOT list a file path as “required” unless the path is one of:\n\n* Canon-defined — the path (or path-pattern) is explicitly defined by PF canon (including this section and the Evidence Index entries catalog).  \n* Audit-proven — the path’s existence is already proven by an existing governed artifact family.  \n* QA-created — the plan includes inline creation instructions and validation for the path.\n\nProven or created, otherwise forbidden (MUST).\n\nIf a path is not canon-defined and not audit-proven, it MUST either be created under QA with explicit instructions and justification, or it MUST NOT appear in the plan.\n\nQA-created path requirements (MUST).\n\nWhen a plan requires QA to create a file that has no prior canonical existence, the relevant step MUST include:\n\n* exact mkdir / write instructions (no placeholders)  \n* a one-line purpose (what the file proves and why it exists)  \n* explicit PASS and FAIL predicates tied to the file’s contents\n\nQA write scope (MUST).\n\nRepository QA capture creates files only within its authorized `audit/**` or `artifacts/**` scope. Required canonical companions outside that capture root are updated only through their separately authorized governed writer; QA capture itself grants no such mutation authority. New off-repository QA plans, audits, reports, RCA, recovery records, and exported evidence are native change-process artifacts stored in ChatGPT Library under §8.18.\n\nPre-existing vs QA-run artifacts (MUST).\n\nPlans MUST separate pre-existing artifacts (expected to exist before execution) from QA-run artifacts (created during execution).\n\nPreflight presence gating (MUST).\n\nPreflight “presence” checks MUST only gate on pre-existing artifacts. A QA-run artifact MUST NOT be required in preflight unless the plan also creates it in that same preflight step.\n\nNew standardized evidence families (MUST).\n\nIf a new recurring QA evidence family/path is needed, it MUST be introduced via Glow HD Engine Build Notes addendum (or the owning PF canon home) before plans may require it.\n\nIf the live truth is introduced first via Glow HD Engine Build Notes addendum, drain into the owning PF document later under the normal canon-maintenance workflow. The absence of later drainage is not, by itself, an execution, acceptance, or closeout blocker once the live truth is recorded.\n\nClass-specific Specification and Implementation Plan evidence-family reference posture.\n\n* A high-level evidence-family reference in an Epic or CRD Specification or class-bound Implementation Plan is planning context, not a produced artifact. Concrete QA evidence production belongs to the actual downstream QA Guide/Plan and governing family. A Specification does not contain executable QA or implementation instructions; the Implementation Plan does not replace the detailed QA Plan.  \n* A high-level evidence-family reference MUST NOT be treated as a required QA evidence artifact, close-pack evidence inventory item, Human Index entry, Machine Mirror row, path-proof obligation, or close-stage deliverable by itself.  \n* QA evidence production requirements require concrete paths, creation or discovery posture, PASS/FAIL predicates, and the applicable Evidence Index / Machine Mirror / path-proof posture.  \n* Close-pack evidence inventories require the close-pack baseline artifacts and key\\_outputs binding posture defined in this section or a later owning PF canon update.\n\nLive QA Plan approval evidence identity vs later byte-shape validation.\n\n* Live QA Plan approval requires evidence identity: proof target, governed evidence family or class, decisive receipt, PASS and FAIL predicate, rails posture, and token non-claim posture when applicable.  \n* Live QA Plan approval does not require every final byte-shape detail to be specified in advance when evidence identity, safe execution, and verdictability are clear.  \n* Byte-shape details may still fail QA execution, evidence indexing, or closeout validation. Closeout-time validation remains responsible for canonical JSON compactness, field order, path-proof transcript shape, step-log header shape, mirror-record shape, checksum sidecars, zero-byte prohibition, and Human Index / Machine Mirror parity.  \n* Plan approval MUST NOT be treated as a waiver of later PF12 evidence-discipline failures.\n\nGoverned evidence planning posture.\n\n* Evidence family identity and governed proof intent matter at plan approval.  \n* Byte-perfect generation mechanics, helper syntax, and command literalness are execution details unless they change evidence identity.  \n* Path-proof or evidence-index planning MUST NOT be blocked because a plan’s helper syntax is not paste-ready.  \n* Plan approval MUST distinguish evidence identity from execution syntax.  \n* These plan-approval rules do not waive execution-time or closeout-time PF12 evidence discipline.\n\nScope / root.\n\nThe canonical root for Live QA evidence is:\n\n* EPIC\\_QA\\_ROOT \\\\= audit/qa/\\\\/\n\nWithin the actual Epic or CRD QA root, evidence is organized primarily by check\\_id (current state), with a stable root-level manifest. The generic Epic variants below retain their selected contracts; the flat exact-three-field CRD manifest in §8.17.6 is narrower and does not accept their optional extra fields or check-scoped alternate binding.\n\n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/qa_step_logs_manifest.json`: Per-epic manifest acting as a current-state index keyed by check\\_id. Each manifest entry MUST carry, at minimum, `check_id`, `status`, and `log_path`; `log_path` MUST point to that check’s canonical primary log under the epic QA root. Additional fields such as `check_name`, `fail_status`, and `timestamp_utc` MAY appear when the producing plan or harness records them. Records-only canonical JSON (UTF-8, ASCII-sorted keys, compact, exactly one trailing LF).  \n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/po-000/qa_step_logs_manifest.json`: Optional step-0, check-scoped current-state copy of the QA step logs manifest. When a Live QA plan explicitly names this check-scoped manifest as a required deliverable, it is the binding surface for that run.\n\nThis section does not define:\n\n* Live QA rails posture, D-goal semantics, or QA verdict policy (titles-only routing to Glow QA Guide and HDE-Governance). Actual scope comes from the approved class-specific Specification and class-bound Implementation Plan; HDE-Phased Epics remains historical context.  \n* Which specific artifacts the approved QA Plan requires, subject to PF12's owning family and admission rules. A plan cannot extend a closed schema or admit unlisted files by assertion.\n\nCurrent-state evidence (normative).\n\nUnder audit/qa/\\\\/:\n\n* Current-state evidence is the set of results bound by the canonical root manifest for each check\\_id.  \n* An authorized rerun reuses its stable check-scoped current path, preserving the previous actual attempt and attributable result before replacement. Do not create a new current run root, rewrite the earlier attempt into PASS, or fabricate an execution that did not occur.\n\nTools MUST NOT infer run state by enumerating subdirectories under audit/qa/\\\\/. The manifest is the authoritative index of current-state step evidence.\n\n### **8.17.1 Root and step directories**\n\nEpic QA root (per epic).\n\nEach epic’s Live QA area lives under:\n\nEPIC\\_QA\\_ROOT \\\\= audit/qa/\\\\/\n\nEPIC\\_QA\\_ROOT MUST use lower-case ASCII directory names for fixed directory slugs (for example 00\\_meta/, checks/, results/). Per-check directories under checks/ are named by the check\\_id token and are exempt from the lower-case rule (see Directory name rules).\n\nEPIC\\_QA\\_ROOT MAY contain:\n\n* 00\\_meta/ — stable, mechanically produced epic-level QA metadata (for example, baseline rails/env pins capture, optional debugging captures).  \n* checks/ — current-state per-check directories (one directory per check\\_id). Each check directory contains primary.log and MAY contain auxiliary tmp\\_\\* supporting files or plan-owned outputs.  \n* results/ — current-state step outputs and verdict artifacts (names-only; plan-owned).  \n* snapshots/ — run-local convenience copies of governed artifacts and headers (names-only; non-canon).  \n* closeout/ — current-state closeout summaries (names-only; plan-owned).  \n* remediation/ — remediation-only staging (if present); excluded from governed Evidence Index/Mirror unless explicitly governed elsewhere.\n\nPlanning-trace deliverables (hard rule).\n\nLive QA Plans MUST NOT include any required deliverable whose sole purpose is “PF23 consult capture.” Planning consult capture is planning-time only and is not a governed member of the audit/qa/\\\\/ evidence layout.\n\nChecks-only evidence layout (hard rule).\n\nPer-run directory nesting is disallowed for Live QA evidence. Live QA Plans, QA prompts, and QA reviews MUST NOT introduce or depend on run-id directories, timestamped run roots, or operator-selected fresh evidence roots.\n\nPlan-created Live QA deliverables are allowed, but they MUST live under stable `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/` directories. Re-running a check MUST reuse the same check-scoped path rather than creating a new root for that run.\n\nDirectory name rules.\n\n* The `EPIC_QA_ROOT` directory name and all structural child directories, including `00_meta/`, `checks/`, `results/`, `snapshots/`, `closeout/`, and `remediation/`, MUST use lower-case ASCII.  \n* Per-check directories under checks/ MUST be named by the check\\_id slug used for manifest keying, and that slug MUST be lower-case ASCII.  \n* Use `-` as the default separator for new plan-owned directory slugs. Use `_` only if matching an existing canon slug (example: po-017\\_lowercase\\_naming).\n\nScope note (directory-only).\n\n* This rail applies to directory names only. Filenames MAY contain uppercase characters unless separately forbidden by canon.  \n* When validating this rail mechanically, scan directories, not file paths. Example: `find <root> -type d -print | grep -n -E '[A-Z]'`.\n\n### **8.17.2 Primary step logs and emptiness rules**\n\nMechanical, not hand-edited (governed evidence rule).\n\nMachine-produced Live QA primaries, manifests, captures, and governed integrity companions MUST reflect the actual commands, observations, and validated bytes. Do not manually fill, edit, or invent outcomes in these machine artifacts. This rule does not prohibit substantive analysis in the native QA Audit, QA Plan, final QA Report, or RCA: their responsible authors produce complete evidence-grounded records under §8.18 without falsifying underlying machine evidence.\n\nPlaceholders that imply later human fill (for example, (fill PASS/FAIL) or “fill manually as run proceeds”) are non-conforming in approved QA evidence templates.\n\nEvery completed current QA run requires a distinct final QA Report and RCA authored by Kronos under §8.18, on success as well as failure. Machine-readable results support those substantive analyses; mechanically derived counts alone do not substitute for them. Optional historical repository summary artifacts retain their own capture and indexing contracts.\n\nPrimary log per check\\_id (current-state).\n\nEach Live QA check that produces evidence MUST have exactly one current-state primary log file referenced by qa\\_step\\_logs\\_manifest.json for that check\\_id.\n\nPrimary log location (canonical).\n\nPrimary logs MUST live at:\n\naudit/qa/\\\\/checks/\\\\/primary.log\n\nThe directory checks/\\\\/ is the check-scoped home for the check. The \\\\ directory name MUST match the check\\_id used for manifest keying (see §8.17.1).\n\nPrimary log filename (normative constraints).\n\nThe primary log filename is fixed: primary.log.\n\nThe log’s header (format owned by QA source-of-truth documents) MUST include the true check\\_id used for manifest keying.\n\nJSON header posture (current-state).\n\n* `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/primary.log` MUST begin with exactly one machine-readable JSON object header line (first line), followed by the transcript body.  \n* Header regeneration or Moon Loop header repair MUST result in exactly one header line. If a prior header line exists, it MUST be removed before writing the corrected header.  \n* The header line SHOULD include a schema\\_version value to support validation and downstream parsing.\n\nPlan-scoped header writer inputs (names-only).\n\nIf a Live QA plan uses a step-log header writer that reads per-check metadata from environment variables, the plan MUST export the complete required set immediately before header generation for each check and MUST NOT rely on prior step state. Minimum per-check exports (names must match the header writer contract):\n\n* CHECK\\_ID  \n* CHECK\\_NAME  \n* PASS\\_FAIL  \n* COMMANDS\\_JSON  \n* ARTIFACTS\\_JSON  \n* PF\\_REFS\\_JSON\n\nArtifact list invariants (normative).\n\n* The per-check artifacts list (exported via `ARTIFACTS_JSON` and recorded in the `primary.log` JSON header) MUST include the canonical primary log path for the current `check_id`: `audit/qa/<epic-id>/checks/<check_id>/primary.log`.  \n* For PASS results (`PASS_FAIL=PASS`), omission of the primary log path from that artifacts list is an evidence hygiene defect and MUST be remediated (header repair or rerun) before the step can be treated as closed PASS.\n\nLive QA handling (discovered mid-run).\n\nIf a check ran successfully but primary.log is missing or has a wrong JSON header due to missing exports, a minimal header-only remediation MAY:\n\n* export the required header env vars for the check, and  \n* regenerate the JSON header and reassemble primary.log by writing the corrected header plus the existing body bytes verbatim\n\nThis remediation is evidence-capture only and MUST NOT modify product behavior, test assertions, or acceptance criteria.\n\nNon-empty requirement.\n\nThe primary log for a check MUST be a non-empty, LF-terminated text file. It MUST NOT be zero bytes.\n\nIf a step fails to complete or tooling fails, the primary log MUST STILL be written and MUST contain at least:\n\n* a short summary of what the check attempted  \n* a terse failure description and/or final status line consistent with Live QA status semantics (for example, PASS/FAIL\\_BEHAVIOR/FAIL\\_TOOLING/TOOLING\\_BLOCKED)\n\nAn attempted check or check that reaches a governed result requires its truthful primary, including failure or tooling interruption. A merely planned, deferred, cancelled-before-execution, or not-run item is recorded honestly in the substantive coverage inventory; do not invent a primary, execution, PASS, or failed attempt for it. `NOT RUN` and `DEFERRED` are inventory states, not additions to the closed five-status step-log domain. A flat current-result manifest binds only actual validated primary logs; it does not replace the complete planned-versus-executed coverage inventory.\n\nMinimum command transcript capture (current-state).\n\nEach per-check primary log MUST include an execution transcript sufficient to reconstruct what actually ran. At minimum, it MUST capture:\n\n* the exact command line(s) invoked (as executed)  \n* an explicit exit code (per-command or final)  \n* stdout/stderr output, or explicit references to captured output files\n\nIf a Live QA executor corrects a plan-command syntax defect during execution while preserving the approved command identity and proof target, the per-check primary log or equivalent governed evidence MUST also record:\n\n* the command provenance, such as `Plan + QA syntax correction`  \n* a brief reason for the correction  \n* the produced evidence artifacts  \n* the final PASS, FAIL, or TOOLING classification\n\nThe correction MUST NOT silently alter the acceptance target, command identity, artifact output, or PASS/FAIL predicate.\n\nDiscovery-resolved loci (runtime evidence).\n\nIf a check first discovers a repo-resident locus during execution and then uses it, the primary log MUST record the discovered locus string verbatim before the first command that depends on it.\n\nThe primary log SHOULD also record the discovery proof used (for example, an existence check, file listing, or route probe) so the executor’s locus choice remains auditable without guesswork.\n\nGoverned Live QA evidence files under audit/qa/\\\\/ MUST NOT be empty:\n\n* If a planned artifact is not produced, the file MUST be absent rather than present with size 0\\.  \n* Path-proofs and Machine Mirror records MUST NOT point to zero-byte QA artifacts.\n\nException: Sentinel files MAY be empty if clearly marked as sentinel and MUST NOT be referenced by the Human Evidence Index, Machine Mirror, or acceptance binding surfaces.\n\n### **8.17.3 Supporting files and tmp\\_\\* naming**\n\nSupporting files (auxiliary; not canonical per-step).\n\nA Live QA check MAY produce additional supporting files (for example, JSON request bodies, sorted ID lists, raw CLI outputs). These files are auxiliary and do not replace the primary log.\n\nAny supporting file SHOULD:\n\n* live under audit/qa/\\\\/results/ or a check-scoped subdirectory  \n* use a tmp\\_ prefix (for example, tmp\\_http\\_request.json, tmp\\_sorted\\_ids.txt, tmp\\_cli\\_output.txt)\n\nWhere a supporting file materially contributes to proof, the primary log SHOULD:\n\n* mention the filename explicitly  \n* briefly describe how it is used\n\nCanonical per-check surface.\n\nFor acceptance and audit purposes, the primary log remains the canonical per-check artifact. Supporting files are auxiliary unless separately promoted to governed evidence by the owning evidence catalog and indexed/mirrored accordingly.\n\n### **8.17.4 Env/rails snapshots and D-goal linkage**\n\nEnv/rails snapshots (current-state).\n\nEnv/rails snapshot data MUST be captured mechanically for the Live QA run. To preserve a minimal required output set, the required capture surface is the per-check primary.log (see §8.17.2): the primary log SHOULD include the relevant rails/env pins in a machine-grep-friendly header block.\n\nSeparate snapshot files under audit/qa/\\\\/ MAY be produced (recommended: under 00\\_meta/ for baseline and under results/ for per-check snapshots), but they are optional and MUST NOT be required for closure unless explicitly promoted as acceptance-decisive governed evidence.\n\nEach snapshot (whether embedded in a primary log header or stored as a standalone text artifact) MUST clearly record, at minimum, values of:\n\n* SAFE\\_MODE  \n* ALLOW\\_NETWORK  \n* APP\\_ENV  \n* LC\\_ALL  \n* LANG  \n* TZ\n\nin a machine-parsable form consistent with the QA rails pins.\n\nEnvironment variable discipline (governed interface; QA-time minting prohibited).\n\n* Environment variable names used in Live QA plans and Live QA evidence artifacts are governed interface surfaces, not free text.  \n* The list above is the minimum required env/rails snapshot set. Plans MAY capture additional environment variables, but MUST NOT treat additional names as required correctness gates unless the names are explicitly canon-approved.  \n* No QA-time env var minting: new environment variable names MUST NOT be introduced during Live QA execution (including Moon Loop execution). If a plan/tooling flow would require a new environment variable name to function, that is a development change and the name MUST be defined and documented in canon before any plan relies on it.  \n* MODO\\_\\* variables are non-canonical and meaningless for Glow/HDE. Any environment variable name beginning with MODO\\_ MUST NOT be introduced, required, or depended on for PASS/FAIL or for required evidence structure (including required header fields, required manifest fields, or required evidence schema keys).  \n* EPIC025 exception (grandfathered; non-binding only): existing approved EPIC025 plan materials may contain MODO\\_\\* references due to iteration churn. These placeholders MUST be treated as inert and MUST NOT be replicated.\n\nD-goal/token references (titles-only).\n\nWhen a Live QA artifact is intended to satisfy or inform a specific D-goal or token:\n\n* the corresponding primary log SHOULD include a short, machine-grep-friendly header line stating the D-goal and token names (names-only)  \n* acceptance wiring documents SHOULD reference the check\\_id and primary log path by title only (titles-only routing)\n\nOwnership of semantics.\n\nPF12 standardizes layout and naming only. Semantics for:\n\n* rails posture and env pins  \n* D-goals and QA tokens  \n* Live QA workflows and status classifications (for example, PASS/FAIL\\_BEHAVIOR/FAIL\\_TOOLING/TOOLING\\_BLOCKED)\n\nremain owned by the QA source-of-truth documents and are referenced here by title only.\n\n### **8.17.5 Codespaces snapshot (Step-0; current-state) \\[Optional\\]**\n\nStatus (normative).\n\nThis artifact is OPTIONAL. Live QA Plans MUST NOT require it for closure by default.\n\nIf it is produced and treated as governed evidence, it MUST be generated by commands and MUST NOT be hand-edited (see §8.17.2), and it MUST conform to the canonical bytes and schema rules below.\n\nPurpose.\n\nIf produced, provide a single, mechanically generated snapshot of the Codespaces execution context at the start of Live QA so later review can see:\n\n* determinism and rails posture (pins and rails variables)  \n* tooling versions used for the run  \n* presence-only status for required secrets and env keys\n\nwithout leaking secret values.\n\nCanonical path (current-state; epic-level).\n\naudit/qa/\\\\/00\\_meta/codespaces\\_snapshot.json\n\nRun-id discipline note (normative).\n\n`run_id` MAY be retained as nullable provenance metadata inside governed records. It MUST NOT select directories, key evidence, change canonical paths, alter correctness, or create a second indexed copy. The epic-level current-state snapshot is the only governed Codespaces snapshot home.\n\nCanonical JSON (required).\n\n* UTF-8, no BOM.  \n* ASCII-sorted keys at every object level.  \n* Compact separators.  \n* Exactly one trailing LF.  \n* No ANSI sequences.\n\nSchema (minimum; reject unknown keys).\n\ncodespaces\\_snapshot.json MUST be a JSON object with exactly the keys below:\n\n* schema — string, MUST equal \"codespaces\\_snapshot.v1\".  \n* captured\\_at\\_utc — string, UTC ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ).  \n* epic\\_id — string (for example hde-epic022).  \n* run\\_id — string or null.  \n  * If present as a string, it MUST be a UTC timestamp label (for example 20251221T031045Z).  \n  * It MUST NOT be required for correctness and MUST NOT be used for keying.  \n* rails — object with exactly:  \n  * SAFE\\_MODE — integer or boolean (effective value).  \n  * ALLOW\\_NETWORK — integer or boolean (effective value).  \n  * APP\\_ENV — string or null (names-only).  \n  * LC\\_ALL — string.  \n  * LANG — string.  \n  * TZ — string.  \n* tool\\_versions — array of objects treated as a set (dedupe \\+ ASCII-sort by tool):  \n  * each item MUST be { \"tool\": \\\\, \"version\": \\\\ }  \n  * examples (non-normative): \"python\", \"pip\", \"poetry\", \"os\"  \n  * tool versions MUST be collected without invoking repository state (no VCS-derived identity).  \n* env\\_presence — array of objects treated as a set (dedupe \\+ ASCII-sort by name):  \n  * each item MUST be { \"name\": \\\\, \"present\": \\\\ }  \n  * Values MUST NOT be recorded. Only name and presence boolean.  \n  * The list of names to include is owned by the Live QA plan (titles-only routing to the QA source-of-truth).  \n* notes — array of strings (optional; names-only; no secrets).\n\nIndexing (when used as governed evidence).\n\nWhen the Codespaces snapshot is used as governed evidence (for example, referenced by acceptance artifacts), the indexed artifact MUST be the epic-level current-state snapshot:\n\naudit/qa/\\\\/00\\_meta/codespaces\\_snapshot.json\n\n### **8.17.6 CRD current-check family and bounded governed publication \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n#### **Scope, identity, and paths**\n\nThis subsection drains the accepted artifact contracts in HDE Build Notes addenda 2.10, “HDE-CRD-0001-PR-01 — Token Claim Semantics Lineage Acceptance”; 2.11, “HDE-CRD-0001-PR-02 — CRD Evidence Publication Acceptance and Plan-Wide CI Override Correction”; and 2.15, “HDE-CRD-0001 — QA Evidence Acceptance and Final Reporting Requirements.” It states required behavior, not a fresh assertion that current repository bytes conform or that any QA check passed.\n\nOrdinary local CRD recording accepts the real CRD grammar in §8.17 and confines outputs to the actual configured QA root. Governed admission is narrower: only the validated current manifest and current primary logs for `HDE-CRD-0001` are admitted by this contract. Other CRDs, arbitrary auxiliary files, and future allocations are not admitted by grammatical validity or local recording alone.\n\n| Artifact | Exact governed identity/path |\n| ----- | ----- |\n| Current manifest | `audit/qa/hde-crd-0001/qa_step_logs_manifest.json`; artifact key `audit.qa.hde_crd_0001.qa_step_logs_manifest` |\n| Current primary for an actual check | `audit/qa/hde-crd-0001/checks/<check_id>/primary.log`; artifact key `audit.qa.hde_crd_0001.checks.<check_id>.primary.log` |\n| Required primary/manifest integrity companions | Sibling `<artifact-path>.path_proof.txt` and the existing Human Index/Machine Mirror/sentinel relationships under §§8.3 and 8.6; no invented sibling checksum requirement |\n\nThe actual check\\_id is stable, nonempty, lowercase ASCII, and must match its plan check, header, manifest entry, lexical path, and artifact identity. Do not resolve aliases, traversal, another root, or a changing capture into a valid current primary. A record-count or path-existence check does not prove semantic validity.\n\n#### **Complete current v2 header and flat manifest**\n\nEach current primary begins with one compact, sorted UTF-8 JSON object line followed by the truthful transcript body. The complete v2 header has exactly these fourteen keys; the existing schema identifier remains `pf27.step_log_header.v2`. No `fail_status`, run identifier, approval object, or additional field is added to this closed header.\n\n| Key | Required meaning |\n| ----- | ----- |\n| `schema_version` | Exact `pf27.step_log_header.v2`. |\n| `timestamp_utc` | Actual finalization time in RFC 3339 UTC form ending in `Z`. |\n| `check_id` | Actual stable check identity matching the plan, manifest, and path. |\n| `check_name` | Actual nonempty plan-check name. |\n| `status` | Exactly `PASS`, `FAIL_BEHAVIOR`, `FAIL_TOOLING`, `TOOLING_BLOCKED`, or `PARKED`. |\n| `status_reason` | Empty string for `PASS`; nonempty causal explanation for every other status. |\n| `command` | Exact executed command sequence; empty only when no command executed. |\n| `command_provenance` | Truthful command source; `Not executed` corresponds to no executed command, not a guessed or planned command. |\n| `exit_code` | Actual integer when a command ran; `null` only when none ran; `PASS` requires `0`. |\n| `evidence_artifacts` | Nonempty array including the primary's own canonical path and all primary artifacts relied upon. |\n| `captured_env` | Actual secret-safe values for relevant canon-defined environment names; no invented environment keys. |\n| `pf_refs` | Array of exact in-document PF titles, not guessed filenames or new authority. |\n| `intended_tokens` | Explicit supported list of strings; `[]` is valid. |\n| `claimed_tokens` | Explicit supported list of strings; `[]` is valid and no claim is inferred. |\n\nThe header is compact JSON with ASCII-sorted keys, no BOM, and a single terminating LF before the transcript. The primary is nonempty LF-terminated UTF-8 text. `PASS` requires trustworthy decisive execution/proof, all applicable prerequisites and predicates, valid required evidence, and the complete status-specific contract; valid shape alone cannot establish it. Glow QA Guide owns substantive status classification. `WARN` is an annotation; `NOT RUN` and `DEFERRED` are coverage-inventory states, not extra header statuses. A `PARKED` result requires actual prior authorization for non-execution and cannot hide a failed attempt.\n\nThe current CRD manifest is a flat JSON array whose entries contain exactly `check_id`, `status`, and `log_path`. Entries bind actual validated current primaries; each check occurs once, status agrees with its primary, and log\\_path is the lexical canonical path under the active CRD root. Use compact sorted-key UTF-8 JSON, no BOM, and exactly one final LF. Wrapped manifests, extra entry keys, v1 headers, duplicate checks, conflicting identities/statuses, aliases, malformed paths, missing self-binding, and inputs changing during stable capture reject. Do not apply the broader optional-field or alternate step-0 binding allowances of historical Epic manifests to this family.\n\nOptional absence is different from incompleteness. An unrelated operation does not require a nonexistent future CRD family. A present, selected, or already indexed current CRD family must be validated completely; missing or invalid required members fail closed. Validate selected retained rows, including legacy aliases and collisions, before generic deduplication so deduplication cannot hide invalid evidence.\n\n#### **Explicit claims and interface separation**\n\nNew outcomes never infer claims from `PASS`, intentions, prose, prior dictionary state, or formatting. Nonempty claims require `PASS`, every claim must occur in intended\\_tokens, and non-PASS results have empty claims. Omitted, `None`, or empty claims create an empty new claim set, including PASS-to-PASS updates; they do not retain stale claims. Supported token inputs are lists of strings. Invalid containers or non-string elements reject before membership tests. Explicit aligned subsets, order, and duplicates at the reduced-helper compatibility interface remain preserved; do not convert these arrays to inferred sets. A PASS whose intentions differ from claims retains its causal nonclaim explanation in the log body.\n\nThe reduced seven-key `tools/qa/step_log_header.py` interface and its historical formatting functions are not the complete fourteen-key generic v2 producer or validator. Historical normalization/serialization may preserve old status, claims, caller extra fields, and malformed historical shapes for representation; that does not approve them for new publication. New creation, transition, and publication validate claims before state mutation, build and serialize a separate candidate before filesystem mutation, and preserve caller state and existing bytes on invalid input or serialization failure. Publication normalizes supported `None` token fields to `[]` without importing stale claims.\n\nThe reduced helper does not validate token predicates, registry authority, required body explanations, or the entire current v2 schema. Those duties remain with their actual callers and full-family validation. Its invalid-input protection is not crash-consistent rollback or atomic header-plus-body publication. The corrected claim behavior does not expand that interface's original environment capture, public signatures/defaults, in-place return convention, or closed-schema role. Strict selected legacy Epic predicate and viability behavior remains intact; CRD mode rejects Epic-only viability and migration before accessing Epic-only paths. Empty rosters do not create a vacuous PASS.\n\n#### **Governed writer, integrity graph, and recovery limits**\n\n`record_check`, `record_check_family`, `write_primary_log`, and `update_manifest` retain local-record roles. `tools.qa.qa_harness.validate_crd_check_family` validates the complete current family. Governed publication uses `tools.evidence.update_evidence_index.publish_crd_check_family` from the selected repository root and the existing canonical updater; a local write is not governed admission.\n\nAdmitted rows use the stated artifact keys, discovered\\_physical\\_path, and existing role values. The canonical writer derives required proof/Mirror fields and synchronized Human Index, Machine Mirror, hash sentinels, orientation proof, and Mirror self-proof relationships. Omit empty optional token metadata and do not inject new identity, status, or arbitrary metadata keys into closed Human Index/Mirror records. Local additional files stay inside the active QA root; the governed publisher accepts no arbitrary additional-file or index-metadata injection.\n\nComposed publication requires a nonempty coherent current family and a coherent existing graph, captures preimages for the planned writes in one outer single-writer transaction, records the local family, runs the existing rendering/convergence path, and completes final family/integrity verification before leaving the transaction. On a handled failure, restore the captured prior bytes, existence, parent/fixture state, and metadata within that transaction's scope; preserve the original-cause diagnostic if recovery also fails. Do not silently repair unrelated historical evidence as part of admission. Preserve the existing updater's separate recovery scope and six-pass convergence behavior. The composed Python interface is `publish_crd_check_family(config, results, *, captured_at_utc=None, coherence_verifier=None)`; it creates no CRD CLI or `--crd-id` flag.\n\nThese guarantees are exception-path and single-writer bounded. Stable reads detect observed identity/byte changes; they are not a global freeze or interprocess lock. The contract does not promise process-crash/kill recovery, atomic simultaneous visibility of every file, or concurrent-writer safety. Controlled negative tests and isolated fixtures do not become failed operative QA attempts. A final verification auxiliary remains auxiliary unless separately admitted; a primary cannot certify its own later write or future integrity state. Physical graph validity does not establish domain QA acceptance, hosted CI PASS, approval, or change closure.\n\n## **8.18 Native change-process artifacts: identity, content, lineage, and storage \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n### **8.18.1 Ownership and representation boundary**\n\nPF12 owns the following artifact identities, minimum substantive content, lineage, and evidence-reference boundaries. Change Process Guide owns sequence and role handoffs; HDE-Governance owns authority; Plan Templates owns reusable profiles; Glow QA Guide owns QA methods and verdicts; Reality Audits supplies historical observations and the applicable audit method, not an automatic current product requirement. Explicit active HDE Build Notes decisions control their stated overrides, including addenda 2.1, “Epic/CRD Specification and Implementation-Plan authority; PF20/PF30 historical status”; 2.2, “End-to-End Change Flow, Approval Ownership, and Prompt-Map Control”; and 2.13, “QA-10 Integrated Audit, Readiness and Repeatable Remediation.”\n\nThese are native substantive records, not new mandatory JSON schemas, repository file paths, ledgers, or approval wrappers. Keep required content in the actual existing artifacts and reference reliable records directly rather than duplicating them. A substantive artifact identifies its actual class/change, exact version or durable identity, source and predecessor lineage, author/decision owner where applicable, state and time, outputs/evidence, limits, and downstream use. An audit-only proof establishes provenance/validation; it does not replace a substantive Specification, Implementation Audit, Plan, execution result, or decision.\n\nCreate, revise, and approve stages retain the substantive artifact and the separate audit-only proof where their controlling contract requires that pair. A revision is a complete successor, not redlines alone or a silent patch to approved history. Approval applies to the exact reviewed artifact. Exact durable references replace ambient conversation assumptions. An unknown historical field is disclosed, not reconstructed into a fabricated approval or execution record.\n\n### **8.18.2 Class-specific authority and minimum content**\n\nEach change has two substantive authorities: its approved class-specific Specification and its separately approved class-bound whole-change Implementation Plan. The concrete types are `EPIC_SPECIFICATION`, `CRD_SPECIFICATION`, `EPIC_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN`, and `CRD_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN`. There is no third active Epic Plan, CRD Plan, Implementation Guide, generic class-optional Specification authority, or active PF20/PF30 copy.\n\n| Artifact | Source and minimum substantive content | Boundary |\n| ----- | ----- | ----- |\n| Epic kickoff handoff | Product Owner's Epic class selection; exact authoritative HDE Build Checklist phase, eligible task/subtask inventory and source statuses; compatible phase-bounded formation and scope. Master Scrum produces the handoff. | No imported phase work, invented inventory, Specification/IP, planned PR/Ops structure, active PF20 entry, or execution/approval claim. |\n| CRD kickoff handoff | Product Owner-controlled CRD identity, exact primary source, bounded PO context, observed condition/current-state findings, and CRD-lane rationale. Master Scrum produces the handoff. | Separate CRD formation; no manufactured PF09 inventory, active PF30 entry, Specification/IP, planned work units, or execution claim. Genuine PF09 intersections remain references only. |\n| Epic Specification | Exact kickoff and PF09 phase/inventory lineage; problem or approved objective, intended outcomes and acceptance boundaries, scope/exclusions, constraints, dependencies, risks, unresolved decisions, phase/capability guidance, and high-level QA/evidence/migration/rollback/Ops posture. | Isis authors; the same continuing Thoth session approves or returns exact redlines to Isis. Preserve class-specific source/status identities. |\n| CRD Specification | Exact CRD kickoff, controlled identity and primary-source lineage, observed-change basis and lane rationale, plus the substantive scope/outcome/constraint content applicable to the observed change. | Isis authors; the same continuing Thoth session approves or returns exact redlines to Isis. Do not manufacture Epic work or a PF30 gate. |\n| Implementation Audit | Exact approved Specification, class and version; substantive evidence-grounded whole-change implementation analysis, findings, dependencies, limitations, and inputs needed for deterministic planning; separate audit-only proof. | IA's first substantive artifact after Specification receipt; mandatory input to IP creation and resolvable by IP revision/approval. Proof or “Implementation Analysis” is not a substitute. |\n| Epic or CRD Implementation Plan | Exact approved same-class Specification and Implementation Audit; complete change-wide method, planned PR work units and Ops tasks, each unit's purpose, bounded scope, outcome, ordering, dependencies and handoffs, plus change-wide validation/evidence/migration/rollback and execution-critical inputs. | IA authors; Isis approves or returns exact redlines to IA. Preserve one coherent approved baseline. Unit planning does not create an actual PR, commit, merge, deployment, or Ops action. |\n\nA Specification has scope and acceptance boundaries, not atomic implementation tasks, file-by-file edits, executable commands/scripts, deterministic PR IDs/work units, detailed PR plans, implementation receipts, or actual execution/QA/closure claims. Naming an anticipated system for scope does not plan or authorize a work unit. An incomplete or contradictory approved source returns to its actual Specification revision owner; the Audit or IP must not silently repair or expand it.\n\nThe class-visible review holds and approved labels remain unambiguous: `ASK OK? — EPIC SPECIFICATION`, `ASK OK? — CRD SPECIFICATION`, `APPROVED — EPIC SPECIFICATION`, `APPROVED — CRD SPECIFICATION`, and their corresponding `EPIC IMPLEMENTATION PLAN`/`CRD IMPLEMENTATION PLAN` forms. A review hold is not approval. Specification approval permits the Audit/IP cycle, not implementation; IP approval does not replace actual downstream execution authorization.\n\n### **8.18.3 Downstream lineage and evidence references**\n\n| Artifact or event | Required lineage and attribution |\n| ----- | ----- |\n| PR Instruction and audit-only proof | Exact approved class-bound IP/version, selected planned PR\\_ID/work unit, scope, dependencies, handoffs, and evidence expectations; IA authors. |\n| Detailed PR Implementation Plan and proof | Exact PR Instruction and IP unit; repository-validated coding, files, tests, and executable plan within that unit. The dedicated PR session authors; it must not backfill scope into the Specification/IP. |\n| Product Owner PR Implementation Proceed | Actual invocation identifying the reviewed detailed plan is approval and bounded execution authorization. Retain its native reference. No second approval artifact, receipt, token, signature, hash, object, ID, or confirmation is required. |\n| PR implementation/review result | Actual dedicated-session execution, PR or ordered lineage, affected source and commit identities, commands/tests, review evidence, outcomes, constraints, exceptions, and remaining work. Planned, opened, reviewed, merged, and later storage states are separate facts. |\n| Ops Task and result | Exact IP task and separately authorized target/scope, safety and rollback posture, actual authorized DevOps/environment executor, evidence, and return to the responsible review chain. Ops is not PR implementation; Kronos has no Ops execution/approval role. |\n| Final repository documentation | Actual completed documentation work and acceptance evidence for the implemented change before QA, not assumed completion from a plan or document title. Reusable prompt bodies are not repository documentation outputs. |\n| Live QA Guide | Exact supported readiness result and its fresh audit/triage, approved change and accepted delivery lineage; Isis/QA-20 produces the Guide. |\n| QA Audit and QA Plan | Kronos's distinct substantive Audit then executable QA Plan grounded in the Guide and exact change/evidence; Isis's exact Plan review and any author-return/revision lineage. |\n| QA execution and review | Actual authorized environment/DevOps results for every selected QA ID, returned to Kronos with dependencies and attempt lineage. Preserve finite QA collections without an arbitrary identity/count cap. |\n| Final QA Report and RCA | Two distinct substantive artifacts for every completed QA run, including PASS; Kronos authors. Bind exact Plan/Guide, individual results/attempts, coverage, evidence, limitations, findings, causes, remediation and recurrence follow-ups. Do not infer completion from a primary-log count alone. |\n| Retrospective and closure decision | Isis's actual exact-source retrospective/decision, completed QA Report and RCA, accepted delivery and relevant Ops evidence, remaining caveats/deferrals and distinct maintenance actions. Neither QA PASS nor repository presence supplies Isis's closure decision. |\n| Post-closure maintenance records | Actual proposed/applied PF10 drainage, prepared/delivered closure memos to Thoth and Master Scrum, and actual board update, each with exact destination and available receipt. Preparation is not delivery/publication; an unresolved board row is not an invented update. |\n\nRetain approved planned state separately from actual execution, acceptance, and closure. A historical `AWAITING_PO_PROCEED`, `PLAN_PENDING`, or `MERGE_PENDING` checkpoint is not silently rewritten when a later event occurs. Capture the actual later event and scope. A scoped CI exception preserves actual failure/unavailability and the exact owner decision; it does not transform failure into PASS, waive substantive defects, or propagate outside its approved scope. Post-closure documentation and administrative actions do not reopen an already-evidenced closure merely because those actions remain pending.\n\n### **8.18.4 Integrated readiness and remediation records**\n\nContinuing Isis's QA-10 produces three distinct substantive outputs: a fresh Reality Audit Markdown, a separate Change Audit Triage Markdown, and QA\\_READINESS. Resolve the exact approved Specification/IP and amendments, accepted PR/Ops/documentation evidence, applicable current technical authority and audit/triage methods, relevant repository/environment sources, and prior PF23 observations. Prior READY is optional history, not an input gate.\n\nThe fresh audit retains complete applicable positive/negative coverage, current evidence, unknowns/limits, and a dated historical comparison distinguishing new, persistent, resolved, changed/equivalent, and unverifiable observations. Old paths/findings do not independently establish current requirements. Triage preserves every finding's identity, evidence, objective/scope relationship, disposition, proposed action and owner, and known existing-entry references. Its efficient PF10-addendum format distinguishes proposals from actual approved or published records; grouping cannot erase membership.\n\nQA\\_READINESS binds the exact approved lineage, complete readiness reconciliation, audit/triage references, decision, unresolved dependencies, and next handoff. An evidenced failure of an applicable approved objective is `NOT_READY`, with expected outcome, actual shortfall, decisive evidence, and required recovery proof. Missing decisive evidence is an incomplete assessment, not an invented objective failure or READY. Runtime QA still owed goes into the Guide/Plan without being preclaimed or mislabeled as a failure. Supported complete readiness is `READY_FOR_QA`, permitting QA-20 Guide creation and the independent Kronos Audit/Plan; there is no mandatory QA-15 intermediary or second readiness gate. Readiness is not QA PASS or closure.\n\nA conditional remediation handoff normally remains in the readiness result unless the receiving contract requires a separate substantive artifact. It identifies the failed objective/prerequisite, exact approved source, evidence, actual stage, affected scope, owner and return point. Early remediation requires no nonexistent QA Plan, fabricated execution attempt, or invented Kronos decision.\n\nMaintain one compact versioned remediation record carrying the source finding, failed objectives, approved baseline, repair changes, work items/owners, dependencies/risks, verification, exact decision references, actual results, and return point. Thoth supplies evidenced diagnosis and bounded advice; IA conditionally supplies missing implementation detail and any complete successor IP before Isis's substantive review of the exact repair and incorporated Plan changes. Preserve previous versions and unaffected approved content; do not retain conflicting parallel work authorities or require a duplicate review of the same completed design. IA owns delivery through the actual PR/Ops/documentation owners and permissions. Return proof to the originating decision owner; a QA-10 repair returns to QA-10 for affected readiness/audit/triage reassessment.\n\nSubstantive remediation has no fixed cycle count, but a repeated failure without new evidence requires diagnostic reassessment, not blind retries. Material changes to remedy/scope/dependencies/risk/acceptance return for review; changed objectives/exclusions require the actual Product Owner scope decision and applicable Specification approval. Ordinary bounded QA rerun rules remain bounded and cannot be reset by relabeling a rerun as remediation. Cancellation or interruption is incomplete work, not a fabricated failed QA attempt. Resume preserves valid completed phases and exact source/result/attempt lineage. Manual PF10/PF23 publication of informational proposals is not an additional readiness gate.\n\n### **8.18.5 Prompt-use provenance and substantive currentness**\n\nFor implemented components, retain the exact source Specification ID/version and component/requirement/work-unit reference; selected ecosystem/release and prompt ID/version; authoritative Notion page/revision or available content identity; actual stage and use time; and resulting artifact, PR, or commit references as applicable. Preserve multiple actual prompt uses and transitions. Unknown historical provenance stays explicitly unknown rather than guessed.\n\nThis provenance belongs in the existing substantive instruction, implementation result, review, audit, or closure records that need it. HDE Build Notes addendum 2.9, “Deferral of the Repository Prompt-Use Provenance Helper,” defers the proposed repository helper: no mandatory helper command, new registry/ledger, historical backfill, synchronization procedure, or new gate follows from the traceability duty. Reconsideration is separately owned. Canonical reusable prompt bodies remain in Notion; repository metadata, when separately authorized, records pointers/identity rather than duplicating those bodies. A proposed ecosystem release, completed publication, selected active release, and observed runtime result remain distinct states.\n\nUse actual source/task/plan versions, executed commands and effective secret-safe configuration, results, evidence, actor/time and limitations. Distinguish the tested implementation/environment from subsequent storage/review/merge references. Currentness depends on material requirements, implementation, dependencies, and proof, not SHA equality alone. A source or evidence-only commit does not automatically expire valid work; changed substantive proof targets require affected revalidation. Missing decisive evidence remains a real blocker. No artifact title, hash, mirror row, review label, or provenance pointer proves all other dimensions.\n\n### **8.18.6 Storage classes and prospective enforcement**\n\nHDE Build Notes addendum 2.6, “Ephemeral Change-Process Artifact Storage,” controls new, copied, exported, and materially revised off-repository change-process artifacts. Classify each expected output before writing:\n\n| Class | Storage and meaning |\n| ----- | ----- |\n| `EPHEMERAL_LIBRARY` | Every off-repository file created because change work is considered or processed; ChatGPT Library is its home, even if approved, controlling, accepted, or retained permanently. |\n| `REPOSITORY_CONTROLLED` | Intended implementation outputs at their governed repository paths: code, tests, migrations, configuration, executable assets, and repository-native canonical documentation/evidence under the actual authorized contract. |\n| `CONTROL_NOTION` | Concise operational state, registry data, decisions and pointers; not full change-process file bodies. Independently governed canonical reusable prompts retain their designated Notion authority. |\n| `DURABLE_DRIVE` | Separately authorized ongoing authorities/business documents independent of one change, expressly designated to that persistent surface; not a workflow plan, Specification, QA artifact, receipt, or working file promoted merely because approved. |\n| `TRANSIENT_SCRATCH` | Reproducible active working data that need not survive the session; surviving handoff/recovery work is retained as an artifact. |\n\nThe inclusive Library classes are EA-01 intake/scope/authority and handoff packets; EA-02 all plans, Specifications, work breakdowns, matrices and revisions; EA-03 drafts, redlines, proposed successors, changesets, exports and execution notes; EA-04 QA/audit/review reports, findings, snapshots, tests, verification, hashes/manifests/logs and receipts; EA-05 coordination, approvals, session identities, checkpoints, escalation and recovery; and EA-06 publication, registry/reconciliation evidence, drainage, retrospective, closure, and preserved historical artifacts. These are storage classifications, not mandatory extra documents or a short-retention policy.\n\nRepository-controlled outputs remain in their governed repository homes. An exported/review copy, report, plan, bundle or snapshot about those outputs is an off-repository artifact and belongs in Library. A Library copy is not a new repository path-of-record, governed admission, or substitute for required repository evidence integrity. Conversely, native workflow records do not require Index/Mirror/path-proof bindings merely because they support a review.\n\nWhen classification is uncertain, use EPHEMERAL\\_LIBRARY unless controlling authority establishes otherwise. If the required Library artifact route is unavailable, stop that write and report the missing capability; do not fall back to Drive or Notion full-body storage. The rule is prospective: preserve legacy records and their provenance; do not bulk migrate, delete, or silently rewrite them. The current PFCanon authority/version-matched Markdown and repository exact-byte mirror relationship remains separately governed. A generated redline or revised download is not publication to those authorities.\n\n# **9\\) Change Log & Doc-Delta Hooks \\[Required-Now\\]**\n\n## **9.1 What requires a Doc-Delta**\n\nSection 0.4 is the single home for Doc-Delta triggers. A change requires a Doc-Delta when it changes any current catalog or closed-domain contract, promotes a Future-Promotion surface, changes a schema or executable validation contract, changes canonical bytes or serialization, changes a frozen input or Freeze-Pack Manifest contract, changes governed evidence or parity rules, or changes release identity under §0.4.\n\nAn editorial-only reorganization does not require a Doc-Delta when it changes no governed catalog, schema, domain posture, validation rule, canonical-byte rule, artifact identity, canonical path, release contract, or normative requirement.\n\n### **Required record content**\n\nEvery Doc-Delta MUST state:\n\n* a stable Doc-Delta ID, date, and author;  \n* its scope and every affected catalog, schema, and governed artifact by title and repository-relative path;  \n* the change summary and rationale;  \n* the current-domain or Future-Promotion impact;  \n* whether frozen inputs or `catalog/manifest.json` bytes change;  \n* the prior and computed `release_id`, or an explicit statement that the prior `release_id` remains valid;  \n* the required Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, checksum, sentinel, and path-proof updates;  \n* any preserved legacy or explicitly scoped token impact, when applicable, using names registered by HDE-Governance and without redefining token semantics; absence of such an active scoped token cross-reference requires no token declaration, roster, claim, or matrix, and backward-compatible token arrays retained in the template remain empty;  \n* each required validation behavior, its verified executable entrypoint, its result, and its evidence path;  \n* each unresolved decision as `[OPEN]`, with an owner and next step; and  \n* the pull request and commit identifier when available.\n\n### **Same-change coupling**\n\nThe Doc-Delta MUST accompany the change that creates the governed effect. Every required artifact, validation, release-identity, Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, checksum, sentinel, and path-proof update MUST land in the same finalized change.\n\nThe Doc-Delta records intended and observed change state. Its presence does not by itself prove that implementation exists, validation passed, evidence is coherent, a new `release_id` was computed, or the change landed.\n\n---\n\n## **9.2 Doc-Delta template**\n\n### **How to use**\n\nComplete every applicable field and attach the Doc-Delta to the same change that introduces the governed effect. Reference other PF specifications by title only.\n\nKeep the Human Evidence Index (`docs/evidence/INDEX.json`) and the Machine Evidence Mirror (`artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl`) in the same change. Update the Human Evidence Index hash sentinel and Machine Evidence Mirror checksum whenever their governed bytes change.\n\n### **Fill-in template**\n\n```\ndoc_delta:\n  id: \"DOCDELTA-YYYYMMDD-<slug>\"\n  date: \"YYYY-MM-DD\"\n  author: \"<name>\"\n  scope:\n    catalogs: \"<true|false>\"\n    schemas: \"<true|false>\"\n    manifest_checksums: \"<true|false>\"\n    validation: \"<true|false>\"\n    evidence_index: \"<true|false>\"\n    routing_only: \"<true|false>\"\n\n  targets:\n    catalogs_changed:\n      - title: \"<catalog title>\"\n        path: \"<repository-relative path>\"\n        operation: \"<add|remove|rename|move|modify>\"\n    schemas_changed:\n      - title: \"<schema title>\"\n        path: \"<repository-relative path>\"\n        operation: \"<add|remove|rename|move|modify>\"\n    other_artifacts_changed:\n      - title: \"<artifact title>\"\n        path: \"<repository-relative path>\"\n        operation: \"<add|remove|rename|move|modify>\"\n\n  summary: |\n    <What changed and why.>\n\n  domain_impact:\n    current_domains_changed: []\n    future_promotions: []\n\n  release_identity:\n    frozen_input_changed: \"<true|false>\"\n    manifest_changed: \"<true|false>\"\n    release_id_expected_change: \"<true|false>\"\n    prior_release_id: \"<value|not-applicable>\"\n    computed_release_id: \"<value|[OPEN]|not-applicable>\"\n\n  acceptance_impact:\n    tokens_added: []\n    tokens_removed: []\n    tokens_unchanged: []\n\n  validation:\n    - behavior: \"<required behavior>\"\n      entrypoint: \"<verified command or workflow check>\"\n      result: \"<pass|fail|not-run|blocked>\"\n      evidence_path: \"<repository-relative path>\"\n\n  evidence_updates:\n    - title: \"<evidence title>\"\n      path: \"<repository-relative path>\"\n      operation: \"<add|refresh|move|remove>\"\n\n  index_and_mirror:\n    human_index: \"docs/evidence/INDEX.json\"\n    human_index_sentinel: \"docs/evidence/INDEX.sha256\"\n    machine_mirror: \"artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl\"\n    machine_mirror_checksum: \"artifacts/evidence_index.jsonl.sha256\"\n    parity_status: \"<pass|fail|not-run|blocked>\"\n\n  routing_titles_only:\n    math: \"HDE-Math-Spec\"\n    governance: \"HDE-Governance\"\n    cli_api_vendor: \"HDE-CLI-API-Vendor-Ref\"\n    architecture: \"HDE Architecture\"\n\n  open_decisions:\n    - id: \"<decision id>\"\n      description: \"<smallest unresolved decision>\"\n      owner: \"<owner>\"\n      next_step: \"<next step>\"\n      status: \"open\"\n\n  traceability:\n    pull_request: \"<URL|not-applicable>\"\n    commit: \"<SHA|not-applicable>\"\n\n  change_log_entry: |\n    <Summarize the landed change, affected titles and paths, release_id impact,\n    validation evidence, and Human Evidence Index/Machine Evidence Mirror status.>\n```\n\n### **Submission checklist**\n\n* Every changed target is listed by title, path, and operation.  \n* Current-domain and Future-Promotion effects are distinguished.  \n* Frozen-input, manifest, and `release_id` impact is explicit.  \n* Every required behavior names a verified executable entrypoint, result, and evidence path.  \n* Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, checksum, sentinel, and path-proof updates are synchronized where required.  \n* Acceptance-token names come from HDE-Governance; no token semantics or CI job names are invented locally.  \n* Every unresolved item is `[OPEN]` and includes an owner and next step.  \n* The change-log entry reports only the state proven by the landing change.\n\n## **9.3 Acceptance to land**\n\nAll required behaviors MUST pass through verified executable entrypoints on the same finalized change. The Human Evidence Index and Machine Evidence Mirror MUST be synchronized. A new `release_id` MUST be recorded when frozen inputs or manifest bytes change.\n\n### **Preconditions**\n\nThe landing change MUST bind its concrete commands, workflow checks, results, and evidence to every applicable requirement in:\n\n* §3 for catalog schemas, executable validation, topology, and domain closure;  \n* §4 for canonical serialization, arrays-as-sets normalization, locale, and determinism;  \n* §§5–6 for the Freeze-Pack Manifest, exact-byte bindings, and `release_id`;  \n* §§8.1–8.2 for schema, topology, set, canonical-byte, and Registry Report integrity; and  \n* §§8.3 and 8.6 for Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, parity, checksum, sentinel, and path-proof coherence.\n\nThe landing change MUST also prove that both current topology schemas validate their current catalogs, governed negative fixtures fail closed, required Channel and closed-domain checks pass, the Registry Report regenerates identically twice from finalized inputs, and every required check is included in the actual default CI or test discovery used by the landing workflow.\n\nPF12 does not treat an illustrative token, behavior label, script name, or prose label as an existing CI job. The Doc-Delta and validation report MUST identify the executable entrypoints that establish each required behavior.\n\n### **Release handling**\n\nIf a frozen input or manifest byte changes, recompute `release_id` under §6.2 and record the new value in the governed Manifest Snapshot evidence and the change-log entry.\n\nIf no frozen input or manifest byte changes, verify and record that the prior `release_id` remains valid. Do not infer unchanged release identity from an editorial label or an unchanged version string.\n\n### **Environment and determinism**\n\nRun generation and validation with `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, and `TZ=UTC` as required by §4.3. Required two-run identity checks MUST use the same finalized inputs.\n\n### **Acceptance-token binding**\n\nWhen a landing change claims acceptance tokens, every name MUST match HDE-Governance and every claim MUST bind to the governed evidence that establishes its registered semantics. PF12 does not redefine token semantics or maintain a speculative minimum-token roster in this section.\n\n### **Failure policy**\n\nA failed, blocked, or unexecuted required behavior; an invalid or inconsistent manifest; a missing required Doc-Delta; unsynchronized Human Evidence Index or Machine Evidence Mirror bytes; a missing required checksum, sentinel, or path-proof; or an inconsistent `release_id` blocks the governed change from landing.\n\n## **9.4 Refresh landing record \\[Required-When-Landed\\]**\n\nThe change that lands the complete catalog, schema, validation, manifest, evidence, and legacy-reference refresh MUST include a refresh record. The record MUST NOT state or imply that the refresh or its companion remediation has landed until the finalized change supplies the required implementation, validation, evidence, and release-identity proof.\n\nThe landed record MUST identify:\n\n* the completed Doc-Delta;  \n* every affected catalog, schema, manifest, evidence, and reference artifact by title and path;  \n* the validation report and verified executable entrypoints;  \n* the prior and new `release_id` when frozen inputs or manifest bytes changed;  \n* the synchronized Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, checksum, sentinel, and path-proof updates;  \n* proof that the legacy UMS enrichment source was preserved as a reference-only artifact before its embedded canonical copy was removed; and  \n* the landing pull request and commit.\n\nUntil all of these conditions are proven for the same finalized change, the refresh contract remains required but not repository-conformant and MUST NOT be represented as PASS or landed.\n\n# **Appendix A: UMS Schemas**\n\nThis appendix contains no embedded catalog or schema bytes. It indexes the current PF12-owned authorities and preserves a boundary for possible future enrichment. It does not establish implementation, validation, QA, acceptance, or landing state.\n\nBefore this replacement is applied, the finalized change MUST satisfy §9.4 by preserving the designated legacy UMS enrichment source in a reference-only artifact and proving exact-byte preservation. Until that proof exists, the replacement MUST NOT be represented as landed. The preserved material is historical design input only. It MUST NOT be loaded, treated as a current catalog or schema, included as a Freeze-Pack Manifest input, or cited as current implementation or conformance evidence.\n\n## **A.1 Current authorities and boundaries**\n\n| Surface | Current source or executable home | Boundary |\n| :---- | :---- | :---- |\n| Centers and Gates | `catalog/gates_v1.json`; `schemas/gates_v1.schema.json`; `engine/config/registry_loader.py` | Centers are derived from Gate rows. PF12 defines no separate current Centers catalog or schema. Canonical machine IDs include `g` and `ego`, not `g_center` or `ego_heart`. |\n| Channels | `catalog/channels_v1.json`; `schemas/channels_v1.schema.json`; `engine/config/registry_loader.py` | Canonical Channel identity is the zero-padded, numeric-minimum-first `NN-NN` form defined in §2.1. Topology, set, and canonical-byte requirements remain owned by §§3.2 and 8.2. |\n| Magic-10 order | `catalog/magic10.json`; `engine/categories/registry.py`; `engine/config/registry_loader.py` | The catalog owns the ordered closed set. |\n| Magic-10 caps | `catalog/magic10_caps.json`; `engine/config/registry_loader.py` | Caps are separate from the Magic-10 order catalog. |\n| Magic-10 seed metadata | `catalog/magic10_seeds.json`; `engine/config/registry_loader.py` | Present keys are a subset of the closed Magic-10 domain. Full-ten coverage is not implied. |\n| Score thresholds | `math/thresholds.json` | Threshold arithmetic remains owned by HDE-Math-Spec. |\n| Viewer preferences | `engine/validation/viewer_prefs.py` | PF12 defines no current Viewer Preferences or Presets catalog. |\n| Narratives pack | `catalog/narratives/manifest.json` and its governed members | The narratives contract remains owned by §2.8 and HDE-Narratives-Guide. |\n| Registry projection | `artifacts/registry/registry_report.json`; §8.5 | The report is derived evidence, not a source catalog or release manifest. |\n| Authorities, Profiles, and Presets | §§2.2 and 2.5 | These remain Future-Promotion surfaces. This appendix assigns no current catalog, schema, manifest, or consumer to them. |\n\nThe former embedded `Ums.catalog.*` and `ums.schema.*` payloads are not current authorities. Do not cite legacy paths, inferred values, incomplete rows, generated timestamps, or embedded examples as current catalog, schema, runtime, or validation truth. Structural schemas, executable validation, topology integrity, canonical bytes, and derived evidence retain their separate owning sections. A pointer to an owning surface is not proof that its requirements passed.\n\n## **A.2 Future enrichment promotion boundary**\n\nThe reference-only legacy source MAY inform future design, but every promoted value and relationship MUST be reverified against current authoritative sources.\n\n| Future surface | Preserved design intent | Promotion boundary |\n| :---- | :---- | :---- |\n| Enriched Channels | Names, keynotes, circuit or stream labels, and notes | Retain current canonical IDs and centers; verify every enrichment value; define the owning schema and consumer; add validation, tests, manifest treatment, evidence, and a Doc-Delta. |\n| Enriched Gates | Rave and I Ching names, harmonics, Channel membership, astrological spans, crosses, and notes | Replace incomplete or inferred values only with source-proven data; model one-to-many relationships explicitly; validate all rows and provenance. |\n| Unified wheel or bundle | Zodiac and hexagram constants with a combined Gate and Channel view | Derive the surface from current single-home catalogs; do not create an independently editable duplicate; define generation and identity. |\n| Enriched UMS schemas | Standalone Gate, Channel, and aggregate contracts | Start from current canonical machine IDs and current schemas; use JSON Schema 2020-12, stable identity, exact fields, current-byte fixtures, and same-change executable wiring. |\n| Authorities, Profiles, and Presets | Reserved domain and personalization catalogs | Establish the exact source, consumer, schema, manifest scope, migration, tests, and evidence before promotion. |\n\nNothing in this promotion map is a current implementation or release claim. Promotion is additive and governed. The historical source remains non-authoritative after any promoted replacement lands.\n\n# **Appendix B — Channel ID normalization (informative)**\n\nThis appendix provides examples of the Channel identity projection defined in §2.1 and the topology and set rules defined in §3.2. It contains no schema or catalog payload bytes and creates no second normative home.\n\n## **B.1 Before → After normalization examples**\n\n| Input | Canonical `channel_id` |\n| :---- | :---- |\n| `57-20` | `20-57` |\n| `8-1` | `01-08` |\n| `34-10` | `10-34` |\n| `43-23` | `23-43` |\n| `3-60` | `03-60` |\n| `12-22` | `12-22` |\n| `10-10` | Invalid: both endpoints identify the same Gate. |\n\nThese examples illustrate the canonical projection. The owning contract requires malformed or noncanonical stored catalog identities to fail closed. The examples do not authorize silent repair and do not claim that the checked-in validator enforces every required failure case.\n\n## **B.2 Arrays-as-sets example**\n\nInput: `[\"57-20\",\"01-08\",\"10-34\",\"23-43\",\"10-34\"]`\n\nAfter Channel-ID projection, deduplication, and ASCII sorting: `[\"01-08\",\"10-34\",\"20-57\",\"23-43\"]`\n\n## **B.3 Evidence hooks**\n\nWhen these hooks are produced as governed evidence, register them in the Human Evidence Index at `docs/evidence/INDEX.json`:\n\n* `audit/gates/topology/orientation_demo.txt` — before-and-after orientation examples.  \n* `audit/gates/topology/degree_check.log` — observed Gate degrees and result.  \n* `audit/gates/topology/multiplicity_vector.log` — observed center-pair multiplicities and result.\n\nThis list names evidence hooks only. It does not assert that an artifact exists, that a check ran, or that a result passed. The Evidence Catalog in §§8.3 and 8.6 governs record identities, current paths, parity, and proof requirements.\n\n# **Appendix C — Governed artifact record types (records-only)**\n\nThis appendix is a navigation aid, not a second schema or evidence inventory. Repository families remain governed by their exact owning sections. Native off-repository change-process artifact identities, minimum content, lineage, and storage are defined in §8.18; their retention does not make them repository Evidence Catalog members.\n\n## **C.1 Canonical homes**\n\n* §8.3 owns the Machine Evidence Mirror record contract, allowed metadata, ordering, self-record, parity, and path-proof rules.  \n* §8.6 owns the authoritative governed artifact identities and paths recorded by the Human Evidence Index.  \n* The applicable family section under §8 owns each payload contract, producer boundary, current or historical posture, and required companions.  \n* HDE-Governance owns acceptance-token semantics.\n\n## **C.2 Boundary and change routing**\n\nThe former parallel record list is withdrawn. It MUST NOT be used to establish an artifact path, schema, sidecar requirement, implementation state, validation result, QA or OPS state, acceptance-token posture, or evidence completeness.\n\nAdd or change a governed record type only in its owning §8 section and synchronize the Human Evidence Index, Machine Evidence Mirror, checksum, sentinel, and path-proof surfaces when the owning contract requires them. A record or path reference does not prove that the artifact exists, was generated, passed validation, or supports acceptance.\n\n# **Appendix D — Stateless JSON QA artifacts \\[Speculative\\]**\n\nThis appendix is a non-normative locator only.
